summary: HKGAI、科大讯飞、杜小满推出自我进化金融AI模型轩辕4.5 |中国劳工布告栏 星期二, 3 Nov 2026 · 香港 香港和中国劳工英文新闻 HKGAI、科大和杜小满推出自进化金融人工智能模型轩辕4.5 HKGAI、科大和杜小满在香港金融科技周推出首个自进化金融大语言模型轩辕4.5。该模型采用递归自我改进技术，核心财务任务的性能提升了30%，而成本仅为一般模型的10% 香港生成式人工智能研究
content:
HKGAI、科大讯飞、杜小满推出自我进化金融AI模型轩辕4.5 |中国劳工公告栏
星期二, 3 十一月 2026 · 香港 香港和中国劳工新闻（英文）
HKGAI、科大讯飞、杜小满推出自主进化金融AI模型轩辕4.5
HKGAI、科大讯飞、杜小满在香港金融科技周上推出首个自进化金融大语言模型轩辕4.5。该模型采用递归自我改进技术，核心财务任务的性能提升了30%，而成本仅为一般财务任务的10%
香港生成人工智能研究发展中心（HKGAI）、香港科技大学（HKUST）和金融科技公司度小满于2026年11月2日在香港金融科技周上推出了首个自进化金融大语言模型轩辕4.5。该倡议旨在支持人工智能（AI）在金融技术领域的全球扩张。
据HKGAI介绍，轩辕4.5利用尖端的递归自我改进（RSI）技术，在核心金融应用场景（包括获客、风险管理和客户关系管理）方面的性能提升了30%。该中心表示，其计算成本仅为通用模型的 10%。
杜小满集团行政总裁朱光表示：“三方共同推动人工智能在金融领域的深度应用，助力香港金融业智能化升级。香港作为杜小满集团的国际总部，我们将继续深化与科大的科研合作，携手HKGAI开拓国际市场。”
在杜小满的实际业务运营中，大模型已构建了千余个AI代理和5000多个技能，每日代币消耗超过1000亿。该公司报告称，短期逾期风险下降了约50%，总体年化信贷逾期风险下降了12%。在信贷审批流程中，人工智能审批人员的性能超过了80%的人类审批人员，客户等待时间从10分钟缩短到2分钟。
杜小曼表示，企业微信AI坐席可以为客户经理提供精准的沟通策略和应对建议，将单个客户经理的服务能力提升一倍，达到2万人，相当于传统模式下10名经理的工作量。
HKGAI表示，通过未来的战略合作，将与杜小满共同将这项金融AI技术推向国际市场，继续展示香港在生成人工智能领域的研发实力。

HKGAI, HKUST and Du Xiaoman launched XuanYuan 4.5, the first self-evolving financial large language model, at Hong Kong FinTech Week. The model uses recursive self-improvement technology, showing a 30 per cent performance improvement in core financial tasks while costing only 10 per cent of general
The Hong Kong Generative AI Research and Development Center (HKGAI), Hong Kong University of Science and Technology (HKUST) and financial technology firm Du Xiaoman on 2 November 2026 launched the first self-evolving financial large language model, named XuanYuan 4.5, at Hong Kong FinTech Week. The initiative aims to support the global expansion of artificial intelligence (AI) in financial technology.
According to HKGAI, XuanYuan 4.5 leverages cutting-edge Recursive Self-Improvement (RSI) technology and has demonstrated a 30 per cent improvement in performance across core financial application scenarios, including customer acquisition, risk management and customer relationship management. Its computing cost is only 10 per cent of that of general-purpose models, the centre said.
Guang Zhu, chief executive of Du Xiaoman, said: “The three parties are jointly promoting the deep application of AI in the financial sector, assisting the intelligent upgrade of Hong Kong's financial industry. Hong Kong serves as the international headquarters of Du Xiaoman Group, and we will continue to deepen our scientific research collaboration with HKUST, joining hands with HKGAI to explore international markets.”
In Du Xiaoman's actual business operations, the large model has built over a thousand AI agents and more than 5,000 skills, with daily token consumption exceeding 100 billion. The company reported that short-term overdue risks have dropped by around 50 per cent, and the overall annualised credit overdue risk has decreased by 12 per cent. In the credit approval process, the performance of AI approvers surpasses that of 80 per cent of human approvers, and customer waiting times have been reduced from 10 minutes to 2 minutes.
Enterprise WeChat AI agents can provide relationship managers with precise communication strategies and response suggestions, doubling the service capacity of a single relationship manager to 20,000 people, a workload equivalent to ten managers under the traditional model, Du Xiaoman said.
HKGAI said that through future strategic cooperation, it and Du Xiaoman will jointly promote this financial AI technology to the international market, continuing to showcase Hong Kong's research and development strength in the field of generative artificial intelligence.

content:
数码港推出50万港元区块链资助计划2.0及tConnect平台 |中国劳工公告栏
星期二, 3 十一月 2026 · 香港 香港和中国劳工新闻（英文）
数码港推出50万港元区块链资助计划2.0及tConnect平台
数码港周一推出区块链及数字资产试点补贴计划2.0，为每个试点项目提供高达50万港元的资助，并推出tConnect Launchpad平台。这些举措旨在加速香港金融领域的代币化和数字资产部署。
数码港周一推出两项战略举措，以加速香港金融领域的代币化和数字资产部署。该数字技术中心推出了区块链和数字资产试点补贴计划 2.0 以及 tConnect Launchpad 平台。这两项举措旨在促进数字资产解决方案的实际应用并促进行业合作。
计划2.0受财经事务及库务局委托，为测试区块链解决方案的企业提供财务支持。合资格的试点项目可获高达80%的资助，最高资助额为50万港元。申请者可在2026年12月31日申请截止日期前提交最多三个项目建议书。去年推出的首个计划吸引了超过200份申请，九个入围试点项目中有一半以上成功商业化。
财经事务及库务局局长许正宇表示，政府推出计划2.0是因为业界反应热烈，市场效益丰厚。许补充说，香港继续在全球金融科技产品方面处于领先地位，同时加强监管制度以促进可持续增长。
在香港金融管理局的支持下，tConnect Launchpad 为机构提供了专用的技术环境。参与者可以在结构化框架内验证代币化和数字资产解决方案。该平台有助于测试代币化基金、支付解决方案、现实世界资产代币化和结算基础设施。金管局总裁余伟文表示，代币化是金管局金融科技 2030 愿景的基石。 Yue指出，该平台将区块链创新与实际金融应用联系起来，并将金融机构与代币化社区连接起来。
数码港行政总裁郑忠岩表示，香港数字资产发展正进入新阶段。 Cheng指出，市场正在从创新探索走向大规模采用。新举措针对高影响力领域，包括机构去中心化金融、链上金融和代理经济。数码港拥有香港最大的金融科技和区块链社区以及人工智能超级计算中心。该中心继续通过孵化、融资和跨境扩张来支持初创企业。

Cyberport launches HK$500,000 blockchain subsidy scheme 2.0 and tConnect platform | China Labour Bulletin Board
Tuesday, 3 Nov 2026 · Hong Kong Hong Kong and China labour news in English
Cyberport launches HK$500,000 blockchain subsidy scheme 2.0 and tConnect platform
Cyberport on Monday unveiled the Blockchain and Digital Asset Pilot Subsidy Scheme 2.0, offering up to HK$500,000 per pilot project, and the tConnect Launchpad platform. The initiatives aim to accelerate tokenisation and digital asset deployment in Hong Kong's financial sector.
Cyberport launched two strategic initiatives on Monday to accelerate tokenisation and digital asset deployment across Hong Kong's financial sector. The digital tech hub introduced the Blockchain and Digital Asset Pilot Subsidy Scheme 2.0 alongside the tConnect Launchpad platform. The twin moves aim to boost real-world applications of digital asset solutions and foster industry collaboration.
Commissioned by the Financial Services and the Treasury Bureau, Scheme 2.0 provides financial support for enterprises testing blockchain solutions. Eligible pilot projects can receive up to 80 per cent funding with a maximum subsidy of HK$500,000. Applicants may submit up to three project proposals before the application deadline on 31 December 2026. The inaugural scheme launched last year attracted over 200 applications, with more than half of the nine shortlisted pilot projects successfully commercialising.
Secretary for Financial Services and the Treasury Christopher Hui Ching-yu said the government is rolling out Scheme 2.0 due to enthusiastic industry response and substantial market benefits. Hui added that Hong Kong continues to top global fintech offerings while enhancing regulatory regimes for sustainable growth.
Supported by the Hong Kong Monetary Authority, tConnect Launchpad provides a dedicated technical environment for institutions. Participants can validate tokenisation and digital asset solutions within a structured framework. The platform facilitates testing for tokenised funds, payment solutions, real-world asset tokenisation, and settlement infrastructure. HKMA chief executive Eddie Yue Wai-man said tokenisation forms a cornerstone of the authority's Fintech 2030 vision. Yue noted that the platform bridges blockchain innovations with practical financial applications and connects financial institutions to the tokenisation community.
Cyberport chief executive Rocky Cheng Chung-ngam said Hong Kong's digital asset development is entering a new stage. Cheng noted the market is progressing from innovation exploration to large-scale adoption. The new initiatives target high-impact areas including institutional decentralised finance, on-chain finance, and the agentic economy. Cyberport houses Hong Kong's largest fintech and blockchain community alongside its AI Supercomputing Centre. The hub continues to support start-ups through incubation, funding, and cross-border expansion.

summary: 内地女子香港假结婚假生育罪被判无罪中国劳工布告栏 星期二, 2026 年 11 月 3 日 · 香港 香港和中国劳工英文新闻 内地女子香港假结婚及假生育罪名被判无罪 控方未提供任何证据，一名 42 岁的内地女子周芙蓉因串谋诈骗及以欺骗手段获取服务罪被判无罪。这些指控涉及涉嫌假结婚以获得香港入境权和私立医院产科服务。一名42岁中国内地女子被控入境
content:
内地女子香港假结婚假生育罪被判无罪中国劳工公告栏
星期二, 3 十一月 2026 · 香港 香港和中国劳工新闻（英文）
内地女子香港假结婚及诈骗生育罪被判无罪
在检方没有提供证据的情况下，42岁的中国内地女子周芙蓉因串谋诈骗和以欺骗手段获取服务罪被宣告无罪。这些指控涉及涉嫌假结婚以获得香港入境权和私立医院产科服务。
一名42岁的中国大陆女子被控通过假结婚获得香港入境许可和私人医院产科服务，在检方没有提供对她不利的证据后，她被无罪释放。
被告人周芙蓉面临串谋诈骗和串谋以欺骗手段获取服务两项罪名。她周一在沙田裁判法院出庭受审，由高级大律师蔡伟邦代表出庭。
审判原定于今年六月举行，但因涉及线人证人的问题而推迟。当案件重新审理时，检方宣布不会提供对周不利的证据，促使地方法官正式驳回两项指控并宣告她无罪。
随着诉讼程序开始，检方告知法庭，虽然周此前对两项罪名均表示不认罪，但司法部上周提交了一份备忘录，表明他们不会继续起诉。检方表示，撤回证据的决定是经过深思熟虑的。作为回应，辩方要求地方法官正式宣布周无罪释放所有指控。陈批准了该申请，并裁定两项指控均不成立，而辩方没有提出额外的费用或命令申请。
这些指控源于据称在 2018 年至 2018 年 4 月 20 日期间在香港或其他地方发生的事件，具体日期不详。检方指控周与一名李姓男子和一名名叫艾伦的人串谋诈骗入境事务处处长和部门人员。当局声称，她与李缔结了婚姻，并向边境管制官员不诚实地表示，她来港的主要目的是与配偶团聚，从而诱使官员批准她入境，否则他们会拒绝。
此外，周某还被指控在同一时期与同一两人合谋，以欺骗手段在协和医院获得产科和产后服务。指控指出，她谎称李是她未出生孩子的亲生父亲，以确保在私人机构进行医疗预约和分娩安排。

Mainland woman acquitted of Hong Kong sham marriage and maternity fraud charges | China Labour Bulletin Board
Tuesday, 3 Nov 2026 · Hong Kong Hong Kong and China labour news in English
Mainland woman acquitted of Hong Kong sham marriage and maternity fraud charges
A 42-year-old mainland Chinese woman, Zhou Furong, was acquitted of conspiracy to defraud and obtain services by deception after the prosecution offered no evidence. The charges involved an alleged sham marriage to obtain Hong Kong entry and private hospital maternity services.
A 42-year-old mainland Chinese woman accused of entering into a sham marriage to obtain Hong Kong entry clearance and private hospital maternity services has been acquitted of all charges after the prosecution offered no evidence against her.
The defendant, Zhou Furong, faced two counts of conspiracy to defraud and conspiracy to obtain services by deception. She appeared before Deputy Magistrate Chan Yue-chow at Sha Tin Magistrates' Courts on Monday, represented by Senior Counsel Edwin Choy Wai-bond.
The trial had originally been scheduled for June this year but was adjourned to address issues regarding an informant witness. When the case resumed, the prosecution announced it would not offer evidence against Zhou, prompting the magistrate to formally dismiss both charges and acquit her.
As proceedings commenced, the prosecution informed the court that while Zhou had previously pleaded not guilty to both counts, the Department of Justice had submitted a memorandum last week indicating that they would not pursue the prosecution. The prosecution remarked that arriving at the decision to withdraw evidence had taken some deliberation. In response, the defence requested that the magistrate officially declare Zhou acquitted of all allegations. Chan granted the application and ruled that neither charge stood, while the defence made no additional applications for costs or orders.
The charges stemmed from events that allegedly took place between an unspecified date in 2018 and 20 April 2018, in Hong Kong or elsewhere. Prosecutors had alleged that Zhou conspired with a man surnamed Li and an individual known as Alan to defraud the Director of Immigration and departmental officers. Authorities claimed that she contracted a marriage with Li and dishonestly represented to border control officers that her primary purpose for visiting Hong Kong was to reunite with her spouse, thereby inducing officials to approve her entry when they would have otherwise refused.
In addition, Zhou was accused of conspiring with the same two individuals during the identical period to obtain obstetric and postnatal delivery services at Union Hospital by deception. The charge specified that she had falsely claimed Li was the biological father of her unborn child to secure medical booking and delivery arrangements at the private facility.

content:
香港金融峰会以人工智能欢迎晚宴开幕 |中国劳工公告栏
星期二, 3 十一月 2026 · 香港 香港和中国劳工新闻（英文）
香港金融峰会以人工智能欢迎晚宴拉开帷幕
香港2026年国际金融领袖投资峰会于11月2日以欢迎晚宴拉开帷幕，主题讨论涉及人工智能和机器人技术。财政司司长陈茂波和金管局总裁余伟文在周二的主要峰会和周三的峰会之前的活动上致辞
香港金融管理局（金管局）宣布，香港2026年国际金融领袖投资峰会于11月2日星期一以欢迎晚宴拉开帷幕。主要峰会将于周二上午举行，周三将举行题为“与国际投资者对话”的研讨会。
金管局在社交媒体上发帖称，今年峰会的主题是“拥抱变革，开辟新路”。晚宴以“科技向善”为主题，重点讨论香港和中国大陆蓬勃发展的科技生态系统。参与者探讨了人工智能 (AI) 和机器人技术如何重塑工作模式、创造新商机并改善日常生活。讨论还涵盖香港的研究能力以及下一波技术突破和投资机会的前景。
财政司司长陈茂波和金管局总裁余伟文在欢迎晚宴上致辞。圆桌讨论由红杉中国创始人兼管理合伙人沉南鹏主持。演讲嘉宾包括Moonshot AI创始人兼首席执行官杨志林和致远创新联合创始人、联席总裁兼中心研究负责人熊岩。
此次峰会汇聚了全球金融领袖，旨在讨论快速发展的技术领域的新兴趋势和投​​资前景。

Hong Kong's 2026 International Financial Leaders Investment Summit commenced with a welcome dinner on Monday 2 November, the Hong Kong Monetary Authority (HKMA) announced. The main summit will be held on Tuesday morning, followed by a seminar titled “Dialogue with International Investors” on Wednesday.
According to a social-media post by the HKMA, this year's summit is themed “Embrace Change, Forge a New Path”. The dinner featured a “Tech for Good” panel discussion focusing on the thriving technology ecosystems in Hong Kong and mainland China. Participants explored how artificial intelligence (AI) and robotics are reshaping work patterns, creating new business opportunities and improving daily life. The discussion also covered Hong Kong's research capabilities and prospects for the next wave of technological breakthroughs and investment opportunities.
Financial Secretary Paul Chan and HKMA Chief Executive Eddie Yue delivered addresses at the welcome dinner. The panel was moderated by Shen Nanpeng, founder and managing partner of Sequoia China. Speakers included Yang Zhilin, founder and chief executive of Moonshot AI, and Xiong Yan, co-founder, co-president and head of central research at Zhiyuan Innovation.
The summit, which brings together global financial leaders, aims to discuss emerging trends and investment prospects in the rapidly evolving technological landscape.

香港发展局向行政长官提交玛丽医院电梯调查报告 |中国劳工公告栏
星期二, 3 十一月 2026 · 香港 香港和中国劳工新闻（英文）
香港发展局向行政长官提交玛丽医院电梯调查报告
香港发展局已就玛丽医院新门诊大楼电梯问题向行政长官提交调查报告。十七部电梯已修复，其中七部现已开放供公众使用。该局会尽快向立法会发展事务委员会汇报。
香港发展局表示，已就玛丽医院新临床大楼多部升降机早前因工程问题无法运作一事向行政长官提交调查报告。该局现正遵照行政长官指示，提供进一步的补救工作及跟进行动的资料，并会尽快向立法会发展事务委员会汇报调查结果，并作出公开解释。
过去数月，该局表示重点督促建筑署及机电工程署尽快完成玛丽医院新临床大楼的修缮工程。截至目前，已有17部电梯进行了修复工程。根据目前的进展，剩余电梯的修复工作预计将在第四季度内完成。已修复的17部电梯中，有7部已通过检验，并根据医院需要开放供员工和公众使用。有关承建商自费为新启用的升降机提供操作人员，以改善与乘客的沟通。
自今年9月起，该局对玛丽医院一期临床大楼的电梯工程进行独立调查，旨在找出该工程在施工、验收和监督方面的不足之处，并探讨类似工程项目的监督制度是否有改进的空间。

Tuesday, 3 Nov 2026 · Hong Kong Hong Kong and China labour news in English
Hong Kong development bureau submits Mary Hospital lift probe report to chief executive
Hong Kong's Development Bureau has submitted an investigation report to the chief executive on lift issues at Mary Hospital's new clinical block. Seventeen lifts have been repaired, with seven now open for public use. The bureau will report to LegCo's development panel soon.
The Development Bureau of Hong Kong said it has submitted an investigation report to the Chief Executive regarding multiple lifts at the new clinical block of Mary Hospital that earlier could not operate due to engineering problems. The bureau is now following the Chief Executive's instructions by providing further information on remedial works and follow-up actions, and will report the investigation findings to the Legislative Council's Development Panel as soon as possible, making a public explanation.
Over the past few months, the bureau said it had focused on urging the Architectural Services Department and the Electrical and Mechanical Services Department to complete remedial works at Mary Hospital's new clinical block as quickly as possible. So far, 17 lifts have undergone remedial works. Based on current progress, remedial work on the remaining lifts is expected to be completed within the fourth quarter. Among the 17 lifts that have been repaired, seven have passed inspection and, in accordance with hospital needs, have been opened for use by staff and the public. The contractor concerned has, at its own expense, provided operators for the newly commissioned lifts to improve communication with passengers.
Since September this year, the bureau has been conducting an independent investigation into the lift works at Mary Hospital's Clinical Block 1. The investigation aims to identify any shortcomings in the construction, acceptance inspection and supervision of the works, and to explore whether there is room to improve the oversight system for similar engineering projects.

香港在维也纳工发组织论坛上推动绿色转型 |中国劳工公告栏
星期二, 3 十一月 2026 · 香港 香港和中国劳工新闻（英文）
香港在维也纳工发组织论坛上推动绿色转型
香港驻柏林贸易办事处于 10 月 28 日至 30 日在维也纳举行的工发组织论坛上展示了香港的绿色转型战略。黄文忠局长概述了香港在“一带一路”倡议下作为超级联系人的角色及其2050年气候行动计划的目标，包括逐步淘汰
香港驻柏林经济贸易办事处于10月28日至30日在奥地利维也纳举行的联合国工业发展组织（工发组织）论坛上推广香港的绿色转型经验。此次活动汇聚了来自世界各地的政策制定者、行业领袖和城市发展专家，分享关于可持续城市发展和绿色转型的见解。
10月29日（维也纳时间），香港驻柏林经济贸易办事处处长黄文忠参加小组讨论。他强调香港在“一带一路”倡议下的“超级联系人”和“超级增值者”角色。他还介绍了香港在《香港气候行动计划2050》下的低碳经济策略和进展。
黄先生表示：“我们设定了在2035年或之前逐步淘汰燃煤发电，并停止注册新的汽油动力私家车的目标。这些目标表明香港追求绿色转型和实现碳中和的决心。作为全球领先的国际金融中心和国际创新科技中心，香港在金融和创新方面的优势可以促进跨界别合作，从而加速绿色转型。”
访问期间，黄大使会见了中华人民共和国常驻联合国维也纳办事处等国际组织大使兼代表李松以及临时代办王涛。中国驻奥地利大使馆.他们就加强香港与奥地利的合作交换意见。
香港驻柏林经济贸易办事处是香港特别行政区政府在德国、奥地利、捷克共和国、匈牙利、波兰、斯洛伐克共和国、斯洛文尼亚和瑞士处理商业及其他经济贸易事宜的官方代表。

Tuesday, 3 Nov 2026 · Hong Kong Hong Kong and China labour news in English
Hong Kong promotes green transition at UNIDO forum in Vienna
Hong Kong’s trade office in Berlin showcased the city’s green transition strategy at a UNIDO forum in Vienna from 28-30 October. Director Wong Man-chung outlined Hong Kong’s role as a super-connector under the Belt and Road Initiative and its Climate Action Plan 2050 targets, including phasing out c
The Hong Kong Economic and Trade Office in Berlin promoted the city’s green transition experience at a United Nations Industrial Development Organization (UNIDO) forum in Vienna, Austria, from 28 to 30 October. The event brought together policymakers, industry leaders and urban development experts from around the world to share insights on sustainable urban development and green transition.
On 29 October (Vienna time), Hong Kong Economic and Trade Office in Berlin Director Wong Man-chung took part in a panel discussion. He highlighted Hong Kong’s role as a “super-connector” and “super-value-adder” under the Belt and Road Initiative. He also introduced the city’s strategy and progress towards a low-carbon economy under the Hong Kong’s Climate Action Plan 2050.
Wong said: “We have set targets to phase out coal-fired power generation by or before 2035, and to stop registering new petrol-powered private cars. These targets demonstrate Hong Kong’s determination to pursue green transition and achieve carbon neutrality. As a leading global international financial centre and international innovation and technology hub, Hong Kong’s strengths in finance and innovation can facilitate cross-sector collaboration, thereby accelerating the green transition.”
During his visit, Wong met with Li Song, Ambassador and Permanent Representative of the People’s Republic of China to the United Nations Office at Vienna and other international organisations, as well as Wang Tao, Chargé d’Affaires a.i. of the Chinese Embassy in Austria. They exchanged views on strengthening cooperation between Hong Kong and Austria.
The Hong Kong Economic and Trade Office in Berlin is the official representative of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region Government in commercial and other economic and trade matters in Germany, Austria, the Czech Republic, Hungary, Poland, the Slovak Republic, Slovenia and Switzerland.

高金素梅列“共谍案”被告 复讯后限制出境出海(图) 立委 | 張俊傑 | 調查局 | 國安 | 原住民 | 北京 | 奧運 | 时政聚焦 || 看中国网
无党籍立委高金素梅助理张俊杰涉共谍案，高金素梅2日以被告身分被调查局国安站约谈，经台湾高等检察署复讯，获无保请回，并限制出境、出海，准备离开高检署时，她接受媒体访问。(图片来源:中央社/李念庭摄)
【看中国2026年11月2日讯】（看中国记者立明综合报导）无党籍立委高金素梅办公室接连有3名幕僚卷入共谍案，前办公室主任张俊杰涉嫌遭中国情工单位吸收，在台发展组织、收受中方资金，另有2名助理遭检方声押禁见获准。台湾高等检察署2日指挥调查局国安站，以涉嫌违反《国家安全法》等罪嫌，首度以被告身分约谈高金素梅。高金经检察官复讯近2小时后，获无保请回，但遭限制出境、出海。 看中国网站 禁止建立鏡像網站。返回正版看中国网站。
检调调查，张俊杰涉嫌于2008年受邀参加北京奥运开幕式期间，遭中国情工单位吸收，返台后协助发展组织，并透过“原住民多族群文化交流协会”等民间团体，涉嫌收受中方资金、安排赴中交流活动。此外，张俊杰也被指利用立委助理身分，在立法院配合推动反军购相关事务。 看中国网站 禁止建立鏡像網站。返回正版看中国网站。
专案小组进一步追查发现，另一名幕僚林怡君涉嫌负责随团赴北京、安排行程及对外联系，并向高金素梅转达中方接见安排。张俊杰则在检调发动约谈前疑似闻风潜逃，甚至破坏电子脚镮、弃保逃亡。高检署日前已将助理林怡君及办公室主任陈智葟声请羁押禁见，获法院裁准。
检调2日首度以被告身分约谈高金素梅，下午4时30分许将她移送高检署复讯，经近2小时侦讯后，检察官谕令无保请回，但限制出境、出海。据了解，高金素梅否认涉入共谍案，表示张俊杰虽担任办公室主任，负责人事及行政事务，但她已充分授权对方处理相关工作，对于张俊杰涉嫌违反国安法一事并不知情，也未曾收受中国资金。
高金素梅晚间步出侦查庭时表示，全案仍在侦查阶段，许多细节不便说明。她指出，2008年正值两岸交流开放时期，当时不论民间团体、政府机关或各政党，都曾进行教育、文化、经济、农业、渔业及产业等各领域交流，对于检调针对相关活动进行大规模调查，她感到不解，甚至直言“毛骨悚然”。
高金素梅并呼吁台湾不要回到戒严及独裁时代，还以“你可以压垮一个玫瑰、两个玫瑰，甚至上百朵玫瑰，但是你无法阻挡春天的百花齐放”表达立场。媒体追问张俊杰目前下落，以及是否会呼吁对方尽速投案，高金素梅均未正面回应。
检调目前持续追查张俊杰涉嫌发展组织的过程、中方资金流向，以及相关人员在案件中的角色，并将进一步厘清高金素梅是否知悉或涉及相关行为，全案仍待司法调查。

content:
没招了！又提民主集中制 还要再上一次当吗？(图) 文革 | 大躍進 | 毛澤東 | 劉少奇 | 鄧小平 | 江澤民 | 七千人大會 | 集體領導 | 谈古论今 |傅龙山 编辑整理| 看中国网
2018年3月19日，在北京人民大会堂召开第十三届全国人大第七次全体会议，当时新当选的中共副总理韩正（前排右一）领衔，时任副总理孙春兰、胡春华、刘鹤，时任国务委员魏凤和等人，准备宣誓就职。（图片来源：Etienne Oliveau/Getty Images） 看中国网站 禁止建立鏡像網站。返回正版看中国网站。
每当中共政权岌岌可危时，高层就会重提“集体领导”与“民主集中制”——这套政治话术既能安抚党内官僚的不安、调动技术官僚挽救危局的积极性，也能向外界释放“体制具备自我纠错能力”的讯号；然而一旦危机解除，为防止派系坐大威胁核心权威，权力便往往再次收紧。对照过去七十余年的四次历史循环便能看清，这不过是中共欺骗剧本的第五次重演。 看中国网站 禁止建立鏡像網站。返回正版看中国网站。
1956年苏共二十大赫鲁雪夫发表批判史达林个人崇拜的秘密报告后，中共于同年9月召开“八大”。当时刘少奇、邓小平等人主导在党章中删除了“毛泽东思想作为指导思想”的表述，并明确强调“党的集体领导原则”与反对个人崇拜。
毛泽东当时对“八大”路线的容忍仅是迫于国际共运大气候的暂时妥协。1957年毛泽东发动“整风运动”号召党外人士帮助党整风，随后迅速转为“反右运动”，并于1958年南宁会议与成都会议上严厉批评周恩来等人的“反冒进”，公开提出“正确的个人崇拜必须崇拜”，彻底瓦解了八大确立的集体领导框架。
虽然八大确立的“一线、二线”分工原本旨在建立常态化的党务运作机制，但由于党内缺乏对最高领袖权力的刚性宪政约束，当政策分歧上升为路线斗争时，常务机构便无法抵御中共党国最高领袖的政治动员，文革爆发后家家见血的惨烈就是明证。
“大跃进”与人民公社化运动导致严重的大饥荒与经济崩溃后，中共于1962年初召开扩大的中央工作会议（即“七千人大会”）。毛泽东在会上作了有限度的自我批评，并重申“民主集中制”，将经济恢复的日常工作交由刘少奇、周恩来、陈云、邓小平等人主持。
此次又重提“集体领导”实为典型的危机控管与缓兵之计。一方面透过强调“中央集体负责”来分摊大跃进失败的政治责任；另一方面则让一线官僚收拾经济残局。一旦1965年前后经济稍有起色，毛泽东便以刘少奇等人推行“修正主义”为由发动文化大革命，将当年参与集体领导的高层干部逐一清洗。
刘少奇等人在此期间确实透过务实政策扭转了经济颓势，熟悉中共黑帮政治的读者应该也想得到，这想必是导致刘少奇被整死的主因之一。
文革结束后，邓小平在1978年十一届三中全会前后高举“解放思想、发扬党内民主”与“集体领导”的旗帜，借此批判华国锋的“两个凡是”，并在1980年发表《党和国家领导制度的改革》讲话，批评权力过分集中之弊端，废除了领导职务终身制。
“集体领导”在此阶段首先被用作夺取华国锋最高权力的政治工具。在进入八十年代后，名义上由胡耀邦、赵紫阳先后担任党的总书记主持中央政治局工作，但实际最高决策权仍掌握在以邓小平、陈云为首的“八大大佬”手中。当胡耀邦与赵紫阳试图真正落实政治局常务委员会的多数决原则或推动政治体制改革时，便分别于1987年“党内生活会”与1989年政治风波中被大佬以非正式程序罢黜。
虽然，八十年代的制度改革确实打破了毛泽东时代的个人极权，确立了任期制、退休制与党政分开的初步框架，为经济改革提供了相对宽松的空间，但在面对危及中共政权稳定的重大冲击时，非正式的大佬政治仍然凌驾于民主的谎言口号之下，胡锦涛、赵紫阳相继被罢黜、六四大开杀戒就是明证。
邓小平南方谈话与中共十四大后，逐渐形成了政治局常委会各管一摊的“集体领导”模式（至胡锦涛时期发展为九名常委分工的“九龙治水”格局），同时伴随着隔代指定接班人与“七上八下”等内部潜规则。
这一时期的集体领导本质上是各派系与权贵家族为了瓜分经济利益、避免内部火拚而达成的“寡头共治”妥协，并非真正的民主制衡。由于缺乏独立司法与社会监督，这种分权反而导致了派系山头林立（如周永康掌控政法系、徐才厚与郭伯雄掌控军委）与江泽民领头的系统性腐败，“反腐”最终又成为下一阶段高度集权的借口。
学者黎安友（ Andrew Nathan）早年曾提出的“威权韧性”理论；他指出，这套集体接班与常委分工机制在一定时期内实现了权力交接的可预测性，维持了统治集团的内部稳定与经济高速增长，直到外部环境与内部结构矛盾超越了寡头协商所能负荷的极限。回顾中共党史，也可以发现每每当中共最高领导人的决策遭遇重大挫败时，党内高层便会重申“民主集中制”与“集体领导”。简言之，就是没招了的时候，才会主动重提“集体领导”，这既能缓解党内“躺平”官僚的恐惧，还能诱使技术官僚出来替烂摊子献策背锅，又能让国际资本与外界再次产生“中共体制能够自我纠错、温和派即将抬头”的错觉。这种做法在政治功能上主要用于缓和党内派系矛盾、平息基层与社会的不满，并将决策失误的政治责任由个人转嫁为“集体承担”，以借此度过执政危机。
综述以上史实，重点反不在于中共这次怎么骗、喊了哪些响亮口号，真正的关键在于前车之鉴已经这么多了，我们为什么还要再上一次当呢？

title: 美中期选举在即 北京媒体影响力或存两大“盲区”(图)
summary: 美中期选举在即 北京媒体影响力或存两大“盲区”(图) 美国 | 中共 | 微信 | AI模型 | 新闻 美国 - 看中国新闻网 - 海外华人 历史秘闻 时事 || 看中国网 2026年10月24日，美国中期选举提前投票首日，纽约民众投票。（图片来源：Ryan MURPHY/AFP via Getty Images） 看中国网站 禁止建立鏡像網站。返回正版看中国网站。 【看中国2026年11月3日讯】（看中国记者肖然综合报道）明天（11月3日）就是美国中期选举投票日。前自由之家
content:
美中期选举在即 北京媒体影响力或存两大“盲区”(图) 美国 | 中共 | 微信 | AI模型 | 新闻 美国 - 看中国新闻网 - 海外华人 历史秘闻 时事 || 看中国网
2026年10月24日，美国中期选举提前投票首日，纽约民众投票。（图片来源：Ryan MURPHY/AFP via Getty Images） 看中国网站 禁止建立鏡像網站。返回正版看中国网站。
【看中国2026年11月3日讯】（看中国记者肖然综合报道）明天（11月3日）就是美国中期选举投票日。前自由之家中国、香港和台湾研究主任、独立研究员莎拉·库克（Sarah Cook）近日撰文指出，目前尚无公开证据显示北京正以可见方式干预2026年选举，但这一判断存在明显的研究盲区。 看中国网站 禁止建立鏡像網站。返回正版看中国网站。
库克提出，北京一贯被记录在案的媒体影响力行动，是否也在本轮选举中试图左右美国政治？乍看之下似乎没有：公开报道尚未发现与中国相关的明显影响力活动，与俄罗斯更为激进的做法相比尤其如此。但她强调，这一结论受制于重大研究盲区。
她认为，北京在两个领域具有特殊的信息塑造能力，却几乎没有受到系统性审视：一是华裔美国人广泛使用的微信，二是被美国开发者日益采用的中国人工智能模型。
库克同时指出，北京未必有意改变参众两院的控制权，但“意图”或许比“能力”更次要。即便不以改变权力格局为目标，党的相关机构仍可能设法削弱那些对中共政权人权侵害直言不讳的候选人，例如国会“美中战略竞争特别委员会”或“国会及行政当局中国委员会”（CECC）的成员。
微信集通讯、支付和新闻推送于一体，在与中国保持联系的第一代移民中尤为普及。据估计，其美国月活跃用户约150万，集中在纽约、新泽西、加州和得州。
其中，德州参议院选举备受关注：共和党人肯・帕克斯顿（Ken Paxton）对阵民主党人詹姆斯・塔拉里科（James Talarico）。华裔约占得州人口1%，不少年长者通过微信公众号或亲友群获取新闻。
德克萨斯大学2025年一项研究访谈了20名得州华裔，聚焦2022年中期选举前的情况，发现三点：政治错误信息在平台上流传，例如有人转发亚裔女性数月前已“当选”波士顿市长的不实消息；文化压力使人不愿在家庭群里反驳长辈；部分用户因担心审查而回避政治话题。
库克指出，微信上的错误信息大多可能只是普通党派或不准确内容，与北京无关，但这些现象说明，北京偏好的针对特定候选人的叙事有可能被引入并难以反驳，加拿大以往就有类似案例。目前没有公开信息显示得州选战在微信上流传着什么内容，但影响选民的潜力依然存在。
库克指出，2026年是首次在AI聊天机器人普及环境中举行的选举。9月一项调查显示，约五分之一美国人打算借助AI了解候选人。多数人会用ChatGPT、Claude等模型，但DeepSeek和阿里巴巴的通义千问等中国模型也在悄然进入美国信息环境，主要是被用作其他应用和AI智能体的底层模型。
她只找到一项系统考察中国AI模型回答美国选举问题的研究，由欧洲一家机构上周发布。该研究测试了七个模型（五个美国、两个中国），反复提出20个选项有限的民调式问题。结果显示，各模型表现相对一致，党派倾向好坏参半：多数在经济、移民等议题上更常选共和党，在医疗议题及“支持哪个党候选人”“哪个党应控制国会”等问题上偏向民主党。
中国模型与美国模型并无明显差异，两者之间却彼此不同。DeepSeek在两道国会相关问题上100次全选民主党，Claude和Perplexity同样如此；通义千问则分别为55%和75%。
库克认为，值得注意的是中国模型在评论美国政治时享有的空间：DeepSeek能直接批评美国总统施政；若就习近平或全国人大提出同类问题，几乎必然遭到拒答或得到一边倒的赞美。她据此呼吁，研究者和选举监督者应在2028年前弥补这一认知缺口。
库克指出，北京在美国的影响力行动通常着眼于长期辩论、放大极化和抹黑受迫害群体，不太可能优先谋求改变两院控制权。更现实的目标，可能是减少国会中已知的中共批评者。她特别声明，这并不意味着这些批评者的对手与北京有关联，担忧的只是批评者可能被噤声。
除德州参议院选战外，另有五场被“库克政治报告”评为“toss-up”（竞争激烈）、且候选人为上述两个机构现任或前任成员的选举，被视为潜在目标。
库克称这是一次“思想实验”，她对其中暴露的知识空白感到不安：美国面对北京影响力时最严重的脆弱性，潜藏于休眠的网络与渠道之中，一旦北京决定动用便唾手可得。她呼吁在选举日前夕更加关注这些渠道。

title: Iran engages US in 'intensive' negotiations to avert fresh war outbreak

summary: [伊朗](https://www.france24.com/en/tag/iran/)周一证实，它已与华盛顿进行“密集”交流，并提出在严格的条件下重新开放[霍尔木兹海峡](https://www.france24.com/en/tag/strait-of-hormuz/)，因为努力升级[以避免重返战争](https://www.france24.com/en/middle-east/20261102-iran-warns-renewed-war-with-us-could-outlast-previous-conflict)。外交部长阿巴斯·阿拉格奇表示，间接谈判正在通过调解人进行。 [中国](https://www.france24.com/en/tag/china/)也敦促重返谈判，而伊朗安全负责人
content:
[伊朗](https://www.france24.com/en/tag/iran/)周一证实，它已与华盛顿进行“密集”交流，并提出在严格的条件下重新开放[霍尔木兹海峡](https://www.france24.com/en/tag/strait-of-hormuz/)，因为努力升级[以避免重返战争](https://www.france24.com/en/middle-east/20261102-iran-warns-renewed-war-with-us-could-outlast-previous-conflict)。

外交部长阿巴斯·阿拉格奇表示，间接谈判正在通过调解人进行。 [中国](https://www.france24.com/en/tag/china/)也敦促重返谈判，而伊朗安全负责人则与俄罗斯总统[弗拉基米尔·普京](https://www.france24.com/en/tag/vladimir-putin/)讨论了冲突。

因伊朗封锁霍尔木兹海峡能源走廊而导致油价飙升的油价周一下跌逾 6%，原因是人们对结束八个月冲突的措施持乐观态度。

阿拉格奇在接受官方伊斯兰通讯社的视频采访时表示：“鉴于当前局势的敏感性和严重性，磋商和审议非常密集。”

“[卡塔尔](https://www.france24.com/en/tag/qatar/) 和[巴基斯坦](https://www.france24.com/en/tag/pakistan/) 在这些谈判中发挥着非常积极的调解作用。”
据 Axios 新闻媒体报道，美国副总统 JD 万斯 (JD Vance)(https://www.france24.com/en/tag/jd-vance/) 已致函最高国家安全委员会秘书 Mohsen Rezaei，讨论可能举行的新会谈，这是数月来最高级别的举动。

阅读更多[特朗普称美国可能对伊朗发动“另一次小型史诗般的愤怒”攻击](https://www.france24.com/en/americas/20261023-trump-says-us-may-launch-another-little-epic-fury-attack-iran)

在周二的[美国中期选举](https://www.france24.com/en/tag/us-midterm-elections/)之前，加倍外交努力，对战争和燃油价格上涨的不满正在给美国总统[唐纳德·特朗普](https://www.france24.com/en/tag/donald-trump/)的共和党人带来压力。

民主党预计将赢得至少部分国会控制权，并在两年内首次对特朗普施加政治限制。

伊朗第一副总统穆罕默德·礼萨·阿雷夫表示，从美国收到的信息是“对我们胜利的认可”。

据伊朗伊斯兰通讯社报道，他说：“我们的敌人在过去两场战争中都未能实现其任何目标。即使在今天，尽管美国出于自身目标和国内舆论的担忧，正在采取各种行动，但通过中间人向伊朗传达的信息表明我们承认我们的胜利。”

但特朗普继续对伊朗发出威胁，他在一次竞选集会上表示，“在某个时候，我们将不得不向他们敲击”。
##“善意的方法”

一名伊朗高级官员表示，德黑兰准备在两天内开放霍尔木兹海峡，这是能源丰富的海湾地区的出口高速公路——只要华盛顿同意其要求清单。

9月，如果美国同意包括结束所有战线的战争、解冻伊朗资产、解除石油供应等要求，伊朗提出了[为期七天的重新开放海峡计划](https://www.france24.com/en/middle-east/20260927-trump-expects-iran-talks-next-week-after-rejecting-seven-day-truce-proposal) [制裁](https://www.france24.com/en/tag/sanctions/)并结束对伊朗港口的反封锁。

外交部表示：“两天内实施该计划的可能性再次表明了伊朗的诚意。”

[Iran](https://www.france24.com/en/tag/iran/) on Monday confirmed it has engaged Washington in "intensive" exchanges and has offered to reopen the [Strait of Hormuz](https://www.france24.com/en/tag/strait-of-hormuz/) under strict conditions, as efforts escalate[to avert a return to war](https://www.france24.com/en/middle-east/20261102-iran-warns-renewed-war-with-us-could-outlast-previous-conflict).

Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said indirect talks were taking place via mediators. [China](https://www.france24.com/en/tag/china/) also urged a return to negotiations, while Iran's security chief discussed the conflict with Russian President [Vladimir Putin](https://www.france24.com/en/tag/vladimir-putin/).

Oil prices– sent rocketing by Iran's blockade of the Strait of Hormuz energy corridor– dropped more than six percent on Monday, optimistic over steps to halt the eight-month-old conflict.

"Given the sensitivity and gravity of the current situation, consultations and deliberations are very intensive," Araghchi said in a video interview with the official IRNA news agency.

"[Qatar](https://www.france24.com/en/tag/qatar/) and [Pakistan](https://www.france24.com/en/tag/pakistan/) are playing a very active mediating role in these negotiations."

The Axios news outlet reported that US Vice President [JD Vance](https://www.france24.com/en/tag/jd-vance/) had sent a letter to Secretary of the Supreme National Security Council Mohsen Rezaei about possible new talks, marking the highest-level move in months.

The redoubled diplomatic push comes ahead of Tuesday's [US midterm elections](https://www.france24.com/en/tag/us-midterm-elections/), where dissatisfaction over the war and higher fuel prices are weighing on US President [Donald Trump](https://www.france24.com/en/tag/donald-trump/)'s Republicans.

Democrats expect to win at least partial control of Congress and impose political constraints on Trump for the first time in two years.

Iran's First Vice President Mohammad Reza Aref said the messages received from the US were "an acknowledgement of our victory".

"Our enemy failed to achieve any of its objectives in the last two wars. Even today, although the United States, driven by its own goals and concerns regarding domestic public opinion, is engaging in various manoeuvres, the messages conveyed to Iran through intermediaries point to an acknowledgment of our victory," he said, according to IRNA.

But Trump kept up his threats against Iran, telling a campaign rally that at "some point we're going to have to give them the hammer".

## 'Good-faith approach'

A senior Iranian official said Tehran was ready to open Hormuz, the export highway for the energy-rich Gulf, within two days– as long as Washington agrees to its list of demands.

In September, Iran proposed [a seven-day plan to reopen the strait](https://www.france24.com/en/middle-east/20260927-trump-expects-iran-talks-next-week-after-rejecting-seven-day-truce-proposal) if the US agreed to demands including ending the war on all fronts, unfreezing Iranian assets, lifting oil [sanctions](https://www.france24.com/en/tag/sanctions/) and ending its counter-blockade of Iranian ports.

"The possibility of implementing this plan in two days is another indication of Iran's good-faith approach," foreign ministry spokesman Esmaeil Baghaei told reporters at a briefing.

"We have stated that, if Iran's demands are met, it would be possible to restore security to the Strait of Hormuz and resume the negotiating process within a short period."

Baghaei said "everything depends" on the US side accepting the Iranian demands.

"Only then can we discuss the subsequent stages," he added.

American and Israeli threats to Iran rose in the run-up to the midterms and last week's elections in [Israel](https://www.france24.com/en/tag/israel/), where Prime Minister [Benjamin Netanyahu](https://www.france24.com/en/tag/benjamin-netanyahu/)[failed to secure a majority](https://www.france24.com/en/middle-east/20261026-israeli-candidate-eisenkot-pledges-to-unite-israelis-as-netanyahu-deems-him-soft-on-iran).

title: 仅发电邮邀请出席APEC峰会，台湾抗议中国“歧视性待遇”
source: 美国之音中文网 您可靠的信息来源
summary: 资料照片：台湾外交部长林佳龙在台北举行的新闻发布会上讲话。(2024年7月19日) 台湾外交部长林佳龙星期一(11月2日)表示，即将在深圳举行的亚太经合组织(APEC)峰会，主办方中国仅以电子邮件而不是正式信函邀请台湾，台湾已经向中国发出正式抗议；但台湾不会因为遭到歧视性待遇，就放弃参与的权利。 中国将在这个月18日-19日于广东深圳主办2026年APEC第33次领导人非正式会议，包括美国总统唐纳德·特朗普(Donald Trump)，俄罗斯总统弗拉基米尔·普京(Vladim
content:
资料照片：台湾外交部长林佳龙在台北举行的新闻发布会上讲话。(2024年7月19日)
台湾外交部长林佳龙星期一(11月2日)表示，即将在深圳举行的亚太经合组织(APEC)峰会，主办方中国仅以电子邮件而不是正式信函邀请台湾，台湾已经向中国发出正式抗议；但台湾不会因为遭到歧视性待遇，就放弃参与的权利。
中国将在这个月18日-19日于广东深圳主办2026年APEC第33次领导人非正式会议，包括美国总统唐纳德·特朗普(Donald Trump)，俄罗斯总统弗拉基米尔·普京(Vladimir Putin)以及全球商界领袖和国际组织负责人都将出席。
台湾外交部长林佳龙星期一表示，今年中国并未循例亲自递交邀请函，而是以电子邮件寄送，林佳龙表示，台湾已经在第一时间向中国表达抗议。
依照惯例，APEC主办国会派特使亲自递送邀请函。林佳龙表示，今年中方没有采取亲自递交的方式，而是以“电子邮件”联系台湾外交部，称谓则维持台湾的参与名称“Chinese Taipei”(中华台北)。
台湾中央社报道，林佳龙星期一在接受记者访问时表示，台湾作为APEC正式会员，过去平等参与领导人峰会，中国在争取这次主办时也承诺，会遵守APEC规章、惯例，并确保出席国家代表有平等地位和安全。
林佳龙指出，今年各种APEC相关会议，中国对台湾有一些差别待遇，台湾外交部都立即表达抗议，并争取台湾的参与权益，也与APEC所有会员经济体保持良好沟通，获得支持。
林佳龙强调，台湾不会因为中国企图施加差别待遇，就放弃参与APEC的权益，也希望中国就邀请函递送、称谓和程序，都能遵守相关规定。
台湾在1991年11月以“ Chinese Taipei”名义，与中国大陆、香港一同加入APEC，是APEC正式成员。
APEC领导人峰会从1993年开始，由于北京反对台湾总统出席，台湾通常由总统指派一名“领袖代表”参加。长期以来，APEC峰会主办国派特使到台北，向台湾总统递交邀请函，台湾总统再指派代表出席。不过具体做法随主办国不同和两岸关系发展而有变化。
2001年中国在上海主办APEC峰会，北京向台北发出传真通知，而不是派特使递交正式邀请，随后北京拒绝了时任台湾总统陈水扁选定的代表，卸任副总统李元簇，台湾因此没有派代表出席当年的领导人峰会。
2014年中国再次主办峰会，时任台湾总统为马英九。中国派出国台办副主任龚清概到台北，向时任台湾陆委会主委王郁琦递交邀请。
今年，台湾外交部长林佳龙证实已经收到中方邀请，但邀请函是以“电子邮件”发出，台湾已经向主办方提出抗议。但表示不会因此放弃参与。
过去几个月，两岸关系因中国的灰色地带侵扰持续紧张。中国加大在台湾附近海域的军事与海警活动，台湾方面10月底也报告侦测到多批中国军机和舰船。
台湾中央社报道，台湾陆委会副主委沈有忠星期一在台北出席亚洲政经与和平交流协会举行的一场研讨会上表示，预计中国在五中全会后，可能加大对台湾的灰色地带施压，频繁使用海警船、科研船、民兵船等非正规军事力量，在不引发全面军事冲突的前提下，挑战台日菲等区域民主国家在这片海域的管辖权和执法权，企图逐步改变国际航行自由的现状。
上个月20日，中国海警船进入东沙海域限制水域，台湾派出海巡舰艇监控并进行驱离。
美国国务院对此向美国之音表示，中国的行为是蓄意的胁迫和破坏稳定的(intentionally coercive and destabilizing)。国务院发言人指出，中国在台湾和平管辖了70多年的海域周边宣示权威，只会加剧紧张局势，破坏地区和平与安全。

我是主持人，Reg 记者 Brandon Vigliarolo，本周我们的重点是我认为我们的撰稿人 Carly Page 恰当地描述了过去几年我们所处的人工智能炒作周期的顶峰，这就是 Anthropic 首次公开募股文件的公开发布。与我一起谈论这个问题的是我们的系统编辑 Tobias Mann 和高级记者 Tom Claburn，我相信他们对此事都有很多话要说。欢迎大家。托比亚斯·曼 (00:34) 很高兴来到这里。汤姆·克拉伯恩 (00:34) 很高兴来到这里。 Brandon (00:36) 所以，我确信我们有很多内容需要讨论。 614 页的内容实在是太多了。托拜厄斯，我知道你正在用细齿梳子梳理这件事。在我们讨论本次 IPO 中一些更不稳定的部分之前，请先告诉我们具体的数据。托比亚斯·曼 (00:56) 当然。从表面上看，进入任何 S-1 文件，这都是一种风险缓解的混乱，有点掩盖你的屁股。它们读起来几乎就像是世界末日预言。布兰登 (01:18) 对。 Tobias Mann (01:18) S-1 确实做到了这一点。但在数字方面，市场的收获有点有趣，因为有些人看着这些数字，然后说：“好吧，这实际上看起来很合理。”他们的营业亏损仅约7亿美元。 Brandon (01:40) 我认为净 [收入] 为 163 亿，对吧？这就是他们的报告。托拜厄斯·曼 (01:46) 对。
Brandon (01:47) 现在他们还提到，我想，我本来想问你这个问题，807 亿美元的总损失，但我知道这是某种会计调整。他们在 IPO 中提到了这具体意味着什么吗？托比亚斯·曼 (Tobias Mann) (02:01) 没有具体的。有点模糊，而且总是这样。布兰登 (02:07) 当然是，对吧？ Tobias Mann (02:09) Anthropic 的业务需要大量现金，因此他们必须向合作伙伴说：“嘿，我们需要资金来支付训练这些模型的计算费用。我们可以借债，也可以通过估值（我们的股权）获得回报。”所以我相信损失的很大一部分是他们试图冲销他们必须偿还的大量股本

【原文 English Original】
It's official: Anthropic is going public, and boy, are our eyebrows tired from poring over hundreds and hundreds of pages of questionable claims. You can listen to the latest episode of The Kettle right here on this page, as well as on Spotify , Apple Music , or YouTube . Those platforms also let you subscribe to The Kettle, so you are always notified when the latest episode goes live. Anthropic is going to need to do a lot to make its massive IPO more than just a flash in the pan, as systems editor Tobias Man n and senior reporter Tom Claburn tell host Brandon Vigliarolo on this week's episode. For one, the company has nearly a trillion dollars in compute commitments to pay for, which is going to mean it'll be burning through more cash than a datacenter gas turbine turned up to 11. In addition to its massive spending for the foreseeable future, there's also the fact that much of its computing power relies on customers who are also competitors. In short, we're skeptical, but you probably already knew that. It's El Reg, after all, and we're not just taking what the AI industry claims at face value - if it looks like a house of cards, it probably is. A lightly edited transcript is below: Brandon (00:03) Hey everyone, and welcome to the latest episode of The Register 's Kettle podcast. I'm your host, Reg reporter Brandon Vigliarolo, and this week we're focusing on what I think our contributor Carly Page aptly described as the peak of the AI hype cycle we've been in for the past few years, and that's the public release of Anthropic's initial public offering filing. With me to talk this over is our systems editor Tobias Mann and senior reporter Tom Claburn, both of whom I'm sure have plenty to say about this matter. Welcome guys. Tobias Mann (00:34) Good to be here. Tom Claburn (00:34) Good to be here. Brandon (00:36) So, I'm sure we've got a lot to cover. 614 pages is a lot to go through. Tobias, I understand you were combing through this thing with a fine-toothed comb . Talk us through the hard numbers before we get into some of the more wobbly parts of this IPO. Tobias Mann (00:56) Sure. At face value, going into any S-1 filing, it is a kind of mess of risk mitigation, kind of covering your butt. They all pretty much read like a doomsday prophecy. Brandon (01:18) Right. Tobias Mann (01:18) The S-1 definitely did that. But on the numbers side of things, the takeaway for the market was kind of interesting because there were some people looking at the numbers and going, "OK, this actually seems reasonable." Their operating losses were only about 700 million dollars. Brandon (01:40) I think on 16.3 billion net [revenues], right? That was what they reported. Tobias Mann (01:46) Right. Brandon (01:47) Now they also mentioned, I think, and I was going to ask you about this, $80.7 billion total losses, but I understand that was an accounting adjustment of some kind. Did they mention in the IPO what that meant specifically? Tobias Mann (02:01) Not specifically. It's a little fuzzy, and it's always kind of like this. Brandon (02:07) Of course it is, right? Tobias Mann (02:09) Anthropic's business is extremely cash heavy, and so they had to go to partners and say, "Hey, we need capital in order to pay for compute to train these models. We can either take it in debt or you could also get repaid in valuation, our equity." And so I believe a large part of that loss is they're trying to write off a lot of the equity that they're going to have to pay off when they do go public. And so I do believe that's the lion's share of that loss. Because it does look huge, but when you think about how companies go public and how they raise capital as startups, it's not really that surprising. It's just a huge number because Anthropic is arguably the largest IPO in US history at this point. Brandon (03:02) Right. But bottom line is their actual day-to-day business losses were $693 million....It was $1.2 billion, I think, for the first half of the year or same time last year or something like that. So it's gone down. Tobias Mann (03:17) Yes. Tom Claburn (03:17) And they're trying to go out at two trillion now? Is that the number? Tobias Mann (03:25) Well, the number kind of depends on whether they're going to be able to sustain this. I was going to mention for the first time ever, their revenues outpaced their compute expenses two to one. This has never been true in the company's history, and it's one of the reasons that people are feeling more confident about this. The issue that really comes from all of this, and what has gotten missed somewhat in the more rosy interpretations of the S-1, is that they also are signed up to have to repay upwards of 800 billion dollars and counting of compute commitments out through the next two decades or so. Brandon (04:12) You outlined in your story just a whole host of people they owed billions of dollars to for compute. Like you said, it would be great. That $16.3 billion in [revenue] would be great if those compute costs were going to hold steady, right? But they're not. They're going to keep climbing and there are a lot of bills that are going to be due. So, profitability is relying on making more than that nearly trillion dollars in compute obligations, and that's a big if. Tom Claburn (04:43) I mean, the big question mark is in terms of what the technology does for inference costs, because I think a lot of this is betting on being able to get the same hardware that is much more efficient down the road and maybe not drop your prices proportionately and profit on the difference. But it remains to be seen whether there will be enough competition to just have the price go do with the increasing cost. And you see that a lot. I think the inference costs have dropped pretty significantly over the year, on average. I mean, it's really hard to calculate inference costs because there are so many different factors and it's really situational depending on the workload and how much caching is going on and things like that. But overall it's a lot cheaper to do inference now than it was a few months ago. Tobias Mann (05:34) Per token, yeah. Brandon (05:36) But again, I feel like if you're betting this $2 trillion IPO on the fact that we're going to keep getting better and cheaper at inference, right? I mean, I know Moore's Law is kind of a thing of the past, but at this point, what if we run up against another compute bottleneck and inference stops getting cheaper before they need it to? Obviously any IPO prospectus is one big document about risk, right? Like, "Hey, you might make a ton of money investing in this company, or we might go complete belly up and you lose everything," right? That's always a possibility. Tom Claburn (06:15) Right. And they still haven't demonstrated that the use case for AI is wide enough at volume that they claim it is. I mean, in certain sectors it's pretty obvious now there's going to be AI for a long time. Coding, everyone kind of agrees that works and we know how to manage that. And then there will be adjacent fields to that. But once you start getting into more general office work and regular business tasks that are not super-compute heavy, I don't know. It's a good question. We'll see if people are going to use it that broadly, but I just see it being overly optimistic. Tobias Mann (06:59) The big question I have right now is: Is there enough user demand to support even a $200 billion a year revenue stream? Because even going off just commitments that they can't get out of made in the first half of this year, that's $417 billion running out through about 2033 to 2036. Brandon (07:32) I think the upper end of your estimate was a total, including newer commitments, of about $807 billion. At the lower end, $782 billion at the lower end. That's not that much of a difference when you're looking at hundreds of billions of dollars. Tobias Mann (07:46) But if they can't make a profit with a two to one revenue-to-compute ratio — if they have to make twice as much in revenue in order to pay for their compute and still not break even — you extrapolate this out and they're going to have to be making $200 billion plus, assuming no additional compute contracts are made during that period over the next year, which is definitely not going to happen. They've already said they're going to keep making compute contracts. So this number just keeps getting more absurd the further out you go, unless inference magically gets dirt cheap, which we haven't seen. Brandon (08:33) Right. And it could cap. You know, I think also you made a really good point in your story, Tobias, when you mentioned that some of their biggest customers are also some of their biggest competitors. They're leasing space from hyperscalers, they're making deals with people to host their compute. But these are also companies that are operating their own AI models. And you might end up in a situation where they're like an MVNO, which, if anyone's not familiar with a mobile virtual network operator, is cell phone companies that are not T-Mobile, Verizon, or AT&T. Anyone who's not those big three in the United States is operating a virtual network that piggybacks on someone else's infrastructure. And when that infrastructure is busy, you get less priority. So we could see them run into a similar situation there, I imagine. Tom Claburn (09:26) There's an interesting trend that another piece I'm working on later today touches on. Some of the AI gateways like OpenRouter are now starting to move away from just focusing on price metering and looking towards things like fastest time to tokens and all the quality of service metrics in terms of the way that they price and deliver the models, because inference pricing has become very commoditized in terms of what they're dealing with. They're not necessarily serving all the frontier models at very high prices. They're dealing with a lot of open weight models. And if you just focus on the lower end of the market, there's not a lot of margin there. So it makes sense to go, "Well, maybe if we deliver this faster or have better reliability or service, we can move up the price and get a little profit." And I think everyone in the industry is starting to realize that the music is stopping and they have to take a seat at some point and make the business model work. So there's going to be a lot of pressure on that. And that's also showing up in things like the licensing of models. A lot of those open weight models have seen their licenses get more restrictive over time as companies realize, "Well, maybe we don't want someone competing with us with this thing that we've made." So I think there's a lot.. Brandon (10:48) That reminds me of Mistral just releasing the open weight version of Large 4, " Le Chonk ". And the licensing model basically said if you intend to use this for any down-market purposes, you've got to sign a fairly restrictive agreement with us so that you're not just using this open weight model without us benefiting from it, right? Tobias Mann (11:15) A lot of the big Chinese models, like Kimi K3, I believe were among the first to move back in this direction, basically saying, "Hey, if you're just going to deploy this internally, we don't care." If this is just for your enterprise, fine, but if you're going to be selling an API service like OpenRouter around it, you gotta cut us in. So there is definitely that. And Anthropic in their S-1 – again, every S-1 reads like a doomsday prophecy. And this S-1 of the things that they raise: open models are a threat on multiple levels, one of them being that a lot of their customers are startups sensitive to economic downturn. So those customers will likely be the first to jump ship to cheaper alternatives that are maybe not as good, but they can afford if the economy runs into any issues. Brandon (12:25) I wonder if that'll happen or not, right? Tom Claburn (12:28) Was it Elon Musk who was tweeting about the end of the neoclouds recently? With financing getting tighter, a lot of the neoclouds living on borrowed money are going to find it harder to sustain their loans and are not going to survive this. So there will be a shakeout at some point. Does it hit the big companies? I don't know. All the cloud providers look pretty happy because they get business regardless. Even if Google's AI models are not first in people's minds, they're still serving all of this stuff. Brandon (13:08) We've said that on multiple episodes, and in multiple articles we've written, right? Basically, if the AI industry does implode, Google's going to be fine, Amazon's going to be fine, Microsoft's going to be fine; these guys have other businesses. Anthropic and OpenAI, not so much. That's all they do. And in many cases they're renting compute space from these other providers. So they might take a bit of a hit there, but by and large, they're going to be okay. They've got compute, they'll turn it around, they'll find other people to use it. Which is interesting, from your article, Tobias, you kind of summarize that the entire pitch this IPO makes is that bigger is better, right? But as we were just talking about, there are a lot of reasons to say that's probably not the case. It makes me wonder if they're still living in the token-maxxing era, whereas I just wrote a story this week about AWS telling its engineers to back off, stop using so many tokens, be more judicious, use AI well, don't just use it. And Microsoft said this months ago in August – they were saying tokenmaxxing doesn't factor into how they want to do business. So you've got two very big consumers of AI basically saying, "Y'all need to slow it down and be more purposeful." So, bigger isn't necessarily... Tobias Mann (14:33) Anthropic's business is predicated on the idea that more compute means more revenue. However, the disconnect is: Can revenue scale fast enough? Is there enough user base? Is there enough token demand to support the scale they need to cash the checks they've already written? And it really looks like a house of cards. They warn about this in the S-1 – they have to – that if their revenue can't keep up with their compute commitments, they could default. And that default could turn into a cascade where if they can't pay one bill, they can't get enough compute to generate revenue necessary to pay the next bill, and it all falls apart. Brandon (15:28) If it happens to Anthropic, the other AI frontier labs are not far behind, because that's going to be a symptom of a larger problem. And that's that people are basically saying what a lot of non-AI companies or companies that do AI along with other things, like AWS, are saying: We don't need these massive frontier models for the vast majority of business purposes. They're not necessary. Tom Claburn (15:54) Right. A lot of the enterprise AI products you see now are about trying to figure out ways to reduce that cost, too.You have some sort of gateway or harness system that looks at your jobs and routes them to an appropriately cheap model so that most of the time you're not using top-tier intelligence; maybe you're using a decision model, a regular classifier, or something like Gemma to do language translation. You don't always have to use that expensive model, and that price pressure is going to hit them, too. Tobias Mann (16:37) To Tom's point, Cadence System s , which does a lot of electronic design automation and circuit board layout, just rolled out a new product line called Maestro that's built around Nvidia's Nemotron open-weights models. The idea is that they had been using proprietary APIs to power their agents that assist engineers with PCB layout and chip design, but those agents generate a ton of data that could be used to train and fine-tune open weight models. So their latest pitch is, "Hey, we know our customers like this, but it's getting expensive to continue using these proprietary models from OpenAI, Anthropic, or Google. So we're going to give you a way to take an inexpensive model, use the proprietary model to generate training data that we can use to fine-tune this open model, and then you can decide how much of the work you want done on the expensive proprietary models versus the cheap open models. You can deploy those models on-prem, in our cloud, or on your preferred cloud. Just use our agent platform and pay the subscription fee." Brandon (18:03) I can't imagine most businesses are going to fork over all this money to proprietary model providers when they don't need those resources. It really makes me wonder how much of this IPO is forecasting the bursting of the bubble. I feel sometimes like we talk about the AI bubble bursting like doomsday prophecies: "It's happening now!" But there have been more signs recently. Chinese AI stocks have been hammered recently. There have been recent earnings reports from American companies that have not looked Yeah. Tom Claburn (18:57) Google was hammered ; they lost like $500 billion in stock value based on the fact that their search was underperforming Brandon (19:07) That's that one I wasn't able to think of, that minor little blip, right? Tom Claburn (19:11) AI overviews not monetizing as well. So there's a lot, yeah. Tobias Mann (19:15) A problem they created for themselves. Brandon (19:18) Google creating its own problems? What? Tobias Mann (19:24) I would agree that Anthropic's survival depends fairly heavily on pushing the frontier forward. In order to do that, it needs a disproportionate amount of compute that it may not be able to afford on a continuing basis, especially if Microsoft, Google, and all of these cloud CSPs that provide compute for them and are among their biggest customers decide, "We don't really need cloud for this. We've reached a point where our own open-weights models or small proprietary models are good enough for drafting emails or generating code bases for our customers." So they're going to start buying fewer tokens from Anthropic or OpenAI when they eventually IPO. They're likely to go through very similar challenges because they're also getting most of their compute from companies like Oracle and Microsoft at this point. Brandon (20:38) Which was one of the questions I wanted to ask as we wrapped up: Do you think OpenAI is going to be in any better position once their IPO comes out? Because neither of them owns a lot of their compute, and OpenAI's attempts to build its own compute seem to have fizzled out a bit. Could they be in a better position or is it going to be more of the same? Tobias Mann (21:05) I don't know with OpenAI whether they're going to be able to overcome the same risks that Anthropic has. It does feel like Anthropic is sidestepping a lot of hard questions by pushing forward with their IPO now. Tobias Mann (21:24) With Anthropic going public this year, if OpenAI goes public next year, I don't think they can avoid the scrutiny, because the world is going to have woken up to the risk factors associated with these giant model houses. And I think they're going to face a much harder time with this, even before they get there. Tom Claburn (21:52) OpenAI has the distribution of ChatGPT, which is demonstrating itself to be a useful tool that people like to use. But that's not where their monetization gold mine is going to be, unless they become the Google of AI search, and Google is already trying to get to that space, too. So I don't know how they're going to make it into the enterprise business and get the margins they need to pay back all the money they've taken. Tobias Mann (22:31) OpenAI also has a different business model than Anthropic, and to a pretty hilarious degree, if you recall the advertisements during the Super Bowl about injecting advertisements into GPT.... The point being that OpenAI's revenue streams may be sufficiently different to insulate them from this. They have been trying to position themselves as an AI advertising company as another revenue stream, which Anthropic has flatly rejected. So it's possible that OpenAI's business model is sufficiently different by next year. 12 months is a long time in this industry. If Altman takes them public this time next year, the conversation might be very different. Having said that, Wall Street's eyes are going to be open to a lot of the risk factors in a way that Anthropic is sort of sidestepping right now by being the first really big model house to go public. Brandon (23:54) Which is honestly kind of surprising to see OpenAI press the brakes while Anthropic presses the gas. I'm assuming they saw an opportunity to get out the gate first and avoid answering the hard questions. Because OpenAI basically said, "Hey, we're going to pause our IPO while we assess these risks," given they've been in the doghouse regarding AI behaving badly this year, giving Anthropic that opportunity to scoot past and not have to deal with these things. Tobias Mann (24:26) I think the other tell with Anthropic is actually that two-to-one compute ratio, because that's the first time that's ever happened. And it will be very telling if in their first or second public quarter that just disappears. So the timing might be related to the fact that they can now claim their cash flows are on a positive trajectory towards being cash flow positive and moving towards profitability. OpenAI delaying their IPO, I suspect, is largely because they need to get to a similar point. Otherwise, people are going to look at this and go, "This has no possibility of ever being profitable." At least with Anthropic's S-1, halfway through 2026, it looks like they could be profitable. Whether that's true in in their first public quarter is another matter until Brandon (25:23) To close us out here, I think this statement from your article, Tobias: "The only way to justify this kind of spend and risk is if you believe the upside is enormous, like the biggest economic transformation in the history of humankind enormous." And that raises my final question for you both: Is it going to be worth it? And what's the chance that Anthropic is going to flame out spectacularly in the next year or two? Tobias Mann (25:49) Tom, I'll let you take the first crack at that one. Brandon (25:51) Ha ha ha. Tom Claburn (25:51) Yeah. I mean, I don't know how spectacular it will be. I think it's gotten to the point where it's sort of too big to fail, but I could certainly see some desperation moves where one of these big AI companies strikes a deal with Apple for distribution, because they really need the kind of money that Google was paying Apple for, or sorry, that Google is paying Apple for for distribution. And I can see something like that happening because they really need revenue. I don't really see it blowing up because it's everybody. So they're going to figure out a way to do the least harm if things go downhill. And that may mean parting out part of their businesses. Who knows? Tobias Mann (26:35) I would tend to agree with Tom. I think about what happened with the dot-com boom as an indicator. The situation is quite a bit different because the AI industry has wormed its way so deep that it's not the surface-level situation we saw with the dot-com boom. There was a ton of fiber laid during the dot-com boom that didn't get utilized until much more recently, but it did get utilized. So I think AI is probably bigger than the internet and going to go down in the history books as the next industrial revolution, in much the same way the internet felt like that. After the dot-com boom, it was big, but it wasn't as big as people prescribed the value to. It took another 10 years for it to actually become the thing everybody wanted it to become. It eventually rose to that valuation, but it took much longer than the market could sustain. And I think we're probably in for that. Brandon (27:57) So in other words, don't buy during the IPO. Don't buy high and hope to sell higher, because you might have 10 years to wait before you get back to that IPO valuation or above. Who knows? Maybe it'll go faster. No matter what happens, there's a good chance we're going to be right here to talk about it because this sure can fill a lot of podcasts and articles. Digital ink is going to be spilled on this topic for years to come. We hope you'll join us to hear all about it on the Kettle. Thanks for listening. ®

title: “The greater good”: Why Canadian editors censored Iran’s anti-regime voices
zh_title: “更大的利益”：为什么加拿大编辑审查伊朗的反政权声音
source: 总部设于伦敦的国际知名言论自由机构“查禁目录”
summary: 在 2026 年的前 140 天里，伊朗公民只能限制访问互联网，而且只有 20 天。国际特赦组织的艾格尼丝·卡拉玛德表示，在数字封锁的掩护下，伊斯兰共和国对抗议者进行了史无前例的屠杀。它还加快了逮捕、监禁、酷刑、逼供和处决的速度，成为目前中国以外世界上已知的首屈一指的刽子手。在伊朗之外，文学和出版界似乎正在​​暗中组织起来压制对该政权的批评，这些人的行动是由那些人进行的。
content:
在 2026 年的前 140 天里，伊朗公民只能限制访问互联网，而且只有 20 天。国际特赦组织的艾格尼丝·卡拉玛德表示，在数字封锁的掩护下，伊斯兰共和国对抗议者进行了史无前例的屠杀。它还加快了逮捕、监禁、酷刑、逼供和处决的速度，成为目前中国以外世界上已知的首屈一指的刽子手。在伊朗之外，文学和出版界似乎有一种暗中有组织的行动，旨在压制对该政权的批评，而这些行动的发起者自然应该是持不同政见的伊朗人的盟友：学者、编辑和出版商。作为一名伊朗裔加拿大诗人和翻译家，我最近与编辑和学者发生了令人震惊的遭遇。我粗略地浏览了我在文学期刊和杂志上发表的出版物清单（超过 300 种），以确认我批评伊斯兰共和国的政治诗歌没有出现在加拿大公认的杂志上。这些诗歌已在美国、英国、孟加拉国和澳大利亚出版。我与拒绝我作品的编辑进行的几次交流证明，他们的决定与诗歌的质量无关，而与诗歌的内容有关。
一家位于美国的诗歌媒体犹豫是否接受我的诗歌，因为这些诗“将大屠杀归咎于伊朗当局” 2026 年 1 月伊朗大屠杀之后，一家美国诗歌媒体犹豫是否接受我的诗歌，因为这些诗“将大屠杀归咎于伊朗当局”。这些诗后来被接受，因为编辑从他信任的消息来源那里听到了消息，而他恰好同意我的评估。 2026 年 7 月，同一位编辑拒绝了我受伊朗活动家启发的诗。他称，在美国和以色列发动的战争中，对伊斯兰共和国的批评是煽动性和叛国性的。这位活动家反对战争和国内暴政并不重要。用他的话来说，“更大的利益”是“犹太复国主义和帝国主义的失败”。在最近的另一次遭遇中，加拿大的一家杂志最初接受了我对伊朗持不同政见诗人西娜·贝马内什 (Sina Behmanesh) 的翻译，但后来又拒绝了。小编解释说，他因为以色列美伊战争而改变了主意。就背景而言，战争始于2026年2月28日，直到2026年5月12日，编辑仍在计划出版这些诗歌。为了证明自己的决定合理，他写道：“现在是保持沉默并寻求和解的时候了。说话对任何人都没有帮助。”他写道，他意识到该政权正在变得“极其暴力和镇压”。但他的结论是不出版他的作品，以“保护”诗人和他的亲人。
尽管这位诗人在自己的社交媒体上发表了波斯语原文，而且是加拿大一位直言不讳的活动家，但这并不重要。编辑建议诗人向他发送“恳求爱与和解的诗歌”。用他的话说，“更大的利益是犹太复国主义和帝国主义的失败”。我曾担任文学评审团成员，并目睹了我的加拿大出生的评审员同胞更喜欢不批评南半球政治和宗教制度的作品。其中一些陪审员在大学教授英语和创意写作。许多是加拿大创意写作项目的产物，并且是由这些项目厌恶带有明确政治立场的写作而形成的。杂志读者、文学大赛评委，

【原文 English Original】
In the first 140 days of 2026, Iranian citizens had only restricted access to the internet, and that for only 20 days. Under the cover of a digital blackout, the Islamic Republic committed an unprecedented massacre of protesters, according to Agnes Callamard of Amnesty International. It also accelerated the rate of arrests, jailings, tortures, forced confessions and executions, becoming the world’s leading known current executioner outside of China. Outside Iran, there seems to be a tacit organised effort to silence critics of the regime on the literary and publishing scene, conducted by those who should naturally be allies to dissident Iranians: academics, editors, and publishers. As an Iranian-Canadian poet and translator, I have recently had alarming encounters with editors and academics. I took a cursory look at the list of my publications in literary journals and magazines (over 300), to confirm that none of my political poems critical of the Islamic Republic have appeared in recognised Canadian magazines. These poems have been published in the US, the UK, Bangladesh and Australia. The few exchanges I’ve had with editors who rejected my work prove that their decisions had nothing to do with the quality of the poems and everything to do with their content. One poetry outlet based in the US hesitated to accept my poems because the poems “placed blame for the massacre on the authorities in Iran” After the January 2026 massacre in Iran, one poetry outlet based in the US hesitated to accept my poems because the poems “placed blame for the massacre on the authorities in Iran.” The poems were later accepted because the editor heard from his trusted source, who happened to agree with my assessment. In July 2026, the same editor rejected my poem inspired by an Iranian activist. He described the critique of the Islamic Republic, in the middle of a war launched by the US and Israel, as seditious and treasonous. It did not matter that the activist was against war and domestic tyranny. “The greater good” in his words “is the defeat of Zionism and imperialism”. In another recent encounter, a magazine in Canada initially accepted my translations of a dissident Iranian poet, Sina Behmanesh, only to reject them later. The editor explained that he changed his mind because of the Israel-US-Iran war. For context, the war started on 28 February 2026, and as late as 12 May 2026, the editor was still planning to publish the poems. To justify his decision, he wrote: “Now, it is time to stay silent and search for reconciliation. Speaking won’t help anyone.” He wrote that he was aware that the regime was becoming “extremely violent and repressive.” But his conclusion was to “protect” the poet and his loved ones by not publishing him. And it didn’t matter that the poet had published the original Persian texts on his social media and is an outspoken activist in Canada. The editor advised the poet to send him “poems pleading for love and reconciliation.” “The greater good” in his words “is the defeat of Zionism and imperialism” I have been on literary juries and have witnessed that my fellow Canadian-born jurors prefer works that do not critique political and religious systems in the global South. Some of these jurors teach English and creative writing at universities. Many are products of creative writing programmes in Canada and have been shaped by these programmes’ aversion to writing with a clear political stance. Magazine readers, literary contest judges, editors, and publishers are products of this noncommittal aesthetic. The African American poet and civil rights activist Audre Lorde spoke words that are true: “Your silence will not protect you.” It is also true that silencing others does not protect them. Silencing writers, journalists and activists exposes them to greater danger. It empowers dictators and perpetrators of crimes against humanity and allows them to continue their violent actions with impunity. Censorship is collaboration with criminals, not protection of victims. The poems of Sina Behmanesh have been published in the latest issue of Index on Censorship’s magazine, “Death by a thousand bots”. The post “The greater good”: Why Canadian editors censored Iran’s anti-regime voices appeared first on Index on Censorship .

title: Friedland takes aim at China’s scandium grip with US-backed mine
zh_title: 弗里德兰瞄准中国对美国支持的钪矿的控制
summary: 罗伯特·弗里德兰 (Robert Friedland) 支持的 Sunrise Energy Metals (ASX) 已批准在澳大利亚建设 Syerston 钪项目，推进在中国以外建立世界上第一个重要矿物主要来源的计划。该公司预计将于 2028 年下半年开始在新南威尔士州的矿山和炼油厂生产高纯度氧化钪，年产量将增至 60 吨。该项目预计开发成本为 3.22 亿美元，建设和调试预计需要 24 个月。 “我们决定继续开发 Syerston Scandiu
content:
罗伯特·弗里德兰 (Robert Friedland) 支持的 Sunrise Energy Metals (ASX) 已批准在澳大利亚建设 Syerston 钪项目，推进在中国以外建立世界上第一个重要矿物主要来源的计划。该公司预计将于 2028 年下半年开始在新南威尔士州的矿山和炼油厂生产高纯度氧化钪，年产量将增至 60 吨。该项目预计开发成本为 3.22 亿美元，建设和调试预计需要 24 个月。 Sunrise 董事长弗里德兰在声明中表示：“我们决定继续开发 Syerston 钪项目，这是在广泛的技术开发、工程、许可和商业参与之后做出的，反映了董事会对 Syerston 资源质量以及我们面前的重大市场机会的信心。”这一决定是在西方经济体寻求中国钪供应的替代品之际作出的。Sunrise 表示，自北京于 2025 年实施严格的矿产出口管制以来，钪实际上已经停止进入主要市场。随着这种金属在航空航天、国防、为人工智能数据中心和先进半导体提供动力的燃料电池等领域得到更广泛的应用，预计需求将在未来十年内增长。施工进展 早期施工工作已经开始，其中一条输水管道已于 10 月 9 日破土动工。
公司还提前采购了长周期设备，完成了二期管道设计，并开始建设用于加工的高压釜。Syerston预计每年加工矿石6.4万吨，生产纯度超过99.9%的氧化钪。该矿床预计在其运营的第一个十年中平均含有 690 ppm 的钪。 Syerston 钪项目。 （图片由 Sunrise Energy Metals 提供。）该项目的计划运营寿命为 32 年，其中包括 21 年的露天开采和 11 年的库存矿石加工。 Sunrise 还在研究扩大产能，使其超出最初的每年 60 吨。时间和规模将取决于客户承诺、需求增长、工程结果、融资和董事会批准。美国资助的 Sunrise 已获得美国战争部战略资本办公室的有条件承诺，提供高达 4 亿美元的长期债务融资。该公司还报告称，截至 9 月 30 日，其可用现金为 1.481 亿澳元。该矿业公司正在寻求通过拟议的迁址和纳斯达克上市将其公司总部迁至美国，以使其资本市场存在与潜在客户和战略融资保持一致。根据该提案，一家新成立的特拉华州公司将成为 Sunrise 的母公司，股东将获得新实体的股份或在澳大利亚证券交易所上市的存托权益。
该公司计划很快分发一份概述交易的计划手册。融资仍然是有条件的，而任何超出初始开发的扩张都需要单独的投资决定。

【原文 English Original】
Robert Friedland-backed Sunrise Energy Metals (ASX) has approved construction of its Syerston scandium project in Australia, advancing plans to establish the world’s first major primary source of the critical mineral outside China. The company expects to begin producing high-purity scandium oxide at the mine and refinery in New South Wales in the second half of 2028, ramping up to 60 tonnes annually. The project carries an estimated development cost of $322 million, with construction and commissioning expected to take 24 months. “Our decision to proceed with development of the Syerston Scandium Project follows extensive technical development, engineering, permitting and commercial engagement, and reflects the Board’s confidence in the quality of the Syerston resource, and the significant market opportunity ahead of us,” Friedland, Sunrise’s chairman, said in the statement . The decision comes as Western economies seek alternatives to Chinese scandium supplies, which Sunrise says have virtually stopped reaching key markets since Beijing imposed critical mineral export controls in 2025. Demand is expected to grow through the decade as the metal finds wider use in aerospace, defence, fuel cells powering AI data centres and advanced semiconductors. Construction advances Early construction work is already underway, including a water pipeline that broke ground on Oct. 9. The company has also advanced procurement of long-lead equipment, completed the second-stage pipeline design and begun construction of an autoclave for processing. Syerston is expected to process 64,000 tonnes of ore annually, producing scandium oxide with purity exceeding 99.9%. The deposit is forecast to average 690 parts per million scandium during its first decade of operations. The Syerston scandium project. ( Image courtesy of Sunrise Energy Metals. ) The project has a planned operating life of 32 years, comprising 21 years of open-pit mining followed by 11 years of processing stockpiled ore. Sunrise is also studying an expansion of production capacity beyond the initial 60 tonnes annually. The timing and scale will depend on customer commitments, demand growth, engineering results, financing and board approval. US funding Sunrise has received a conditional commitment for up to $400 million in long-term debt financing from the US Department of War’s Office of Strategic Capital. The company also reported A$148.1 million in available cash as of Sept. 30. The miner is pursuing a move of its corporate headquarters to the US through a proposed redomiciliation and Nasdaq listing, aligning its capital markets presence with prospective customers and strategic financing. Under the proposal, a newly incorporated Delaware company would become Sunrise’s parent, with shareholders receiving shares in the new entity or ASX-listed depositary interests. The company plans to distribute a scheme booklet outlining the transaction shortly. The financing remains conditional, while any expansion beyond the initial development would require a separate investment decision.

content:

【原文 English Original】
Ontario has added Mayfair Gold’s (TSXV: MFG; NYSE-A: MINE) Fenn-Gib gold project to its accelerated permitting program, making the proposed development near Timmins the fourth selected under the province’s One Project, One Process framework. The designation puts provincial approvals and Indigenous consultation under a coordinated review led by the Ministry of Energy and Mines. Mayfair is targeting a construction start in 2028 and first production in 2030, while Ontario estimates the project would support 450 construction jobs and 250 long-term positions. “For too long, permitting delays stood in the way of getting Ontario’s resources to market,” Energy and Mines Minister Stephen Lecce said in a statement Monday. “To compete, we must be the best, which is why our government is planning to further accelerate permitting this fall, to get mines built faster, unlocking billions in investment to create more good-paying jobs right here at home.” The decision advances Mayfair’s effort to develop a smaller, higher-grade starter operation within Fenn-Gib’s much larger gold resource. It also adds another gold development to a provincial program initially launched with lithium and nickel projects, as Ontario seeks to demonstrate that coordinating reviews can translate into construction. Financing takes shape Mayfair lined up financing of up to C$310 million ($218 million at the time) from Australia’s Macquarie Bank in October. The proposed package comprises a C$300-million project loan and a C$10-million equity investment, compared with Fenn-Gib’s estimated C$450-million initial development cost. Macquarie completed the investment on Oct. 14, buying about 2.35 million shares at C$4.26 apiece. The proposed debt financing remains subject to due diligence, definitive agreements and closing conditions, Mayfair said. The loan proposal includes an early C$25-million drawdown to support work ahead of full construction financing, including engineering, equipment orders and preliminary construction activities. The proposed debt would cover about two-thirds of initial capital costs, leaving Mayfair to arrange the balance. Fenn-Gib, about 80 km east of Timmins, hosts 181.3 million indicated tonnes grading 0.74 gram gold per tonne for 4.3 million oz. contained metal, and 8.9 million inferred tonnes at 0.49 gram for 141,000 oz., according to its September 2024 resource estimate. January’s prefeasibility study focused on probable reserves of 25.1 million tonnes grading 1.29 grams gold per tonne for about 1 million oz. contained metal. The development plan envisions processing 4,800 tonnes daily over a 14.3-year operating life, producing an average of about 64,100 oz. annually, including 71,300 oz. a year during the first six years. Coordinated reviews Fenn-Gib joins Frontier Lithium’s (TSXV: FL; US-OTC: LITOF) PAK lithium project, Canada Nickel’s (TSXV: CNC; US-OTC: CNIKF) Crawford nickel project and Kinross Gold’s (TSX: K; NYSE: KGC) Great Bear gold project under the framework, launched in October 2025. Ontario aims to halve government review times by giving developers a single provincial contact to coordinate approvals across ministries. The designation does not itself grant the permits needed for construction, and the Crown’s duty to consult Indigenous communities remains in place, the province said. Lecce previously told TNM that Ontario was targeting permitting timelines of about two years. He later outlined plans to extend the reforms to early exploration, advanced exploration and expansions at operating mines. Mayfair shares finished Friday at $3.10 in Toronto, 6.6% weaker on the day, ahead of Monday’s announcement. “The One Project, One Process designation is an important milestone for the Fenn-Gib Gold Project and reinforces Ontario’s commitment to responsible, investment-ready mining development,” Mayfair CEO Drew Anwyll said in the provincial statement. “This framework provides greater coordination and predictability as we advance Fenn-Gib through permitting and development, helping move the project closer to construction and the significant employment and economic opportunities it can create for the region.”

title: Marine Force-Southeast Asia Will Maintain Continuous Presence in the Philippines
zh_title: 东南亚海军陆战队将继续在菲律宾保持存在
summary: 美国海军陆战队下士2026 年 8 月 25 日，在菲律宾博赫多尔举行的群岛海岸防御连续体 26.4 期间，第一海军陆战队远征军东南亚海军陆战队轮换部队北方空海军炮火联络连分遣队的一名火力支援海军陆战队员与菲律宾海军陆战队第四海军旅一起进行火力支援小组训练。该服务上周宣布，东南亚轮换力量目前正在第二次连续轮换到菲律宾。 MRF-SEA 于 10 月 26 日进行了轮换营业额。 MR
content:
美国海军陆战队下士2026 年 8 月 25 日，在菲律宾博赫多尔举行的群岛海岸防御连续体 26.4 期间，第一海军陆战队远征军东南亚海军陆战队轮换部队北方空海军炮火联络连分遣队的一名火力支援海军陆战队员与菲律宾海军陆战队第四海军旅一起进行火力支援小组训练。该服务上周宣布，东南亚轮换力量目前正在第二次连续轮换到菲律宾。 MRF-SEA 于 10 月 26 日进行了轮换。MRF-SEA 最初是一支为期六个月的轮换部队，从 10 月到 3 月部署到该地区，但其任务在 4 月延长。应菲律宾政府邀请，该部队目前在菲律宾持续驻扎，以继续与菲律宾军方合作。 MRF-SEA 是在第一海军陆战队远征军支持下作战的两支轮换部队之一，另一支是海军陆战队轮换部队-达尔文。与作为海军陆战队空地特遣部队部署的 MRF-D 不同，MRF-SEA 部署为可扩展的特遣部队，其指挥总部是常设组成部分。其他海军陆战队单位将根据需要进行分配。我们。
2026 年 6 月 24 日，为支持 MRF-SEA 而部署的第三濒海战斗队、海军陆战队第三临海团、海军陆战队第三师的海军陆战队士兵和海军陆战队第四旅的菲律宾海军陆战队士兵，在菲律宾巴丹群岛伊特巴亚特的海上关键地形安全行动期间，在地形巡逻的同时参加城市地形军事行动，以支持 KAMANDAG 10。美国海军陆战队照片轮换前延期后，MRF-SEA 的指挥部门将根据预定活动的地点在东南亚国家之间移动。自四月份以来，指挥部门一直驻扎在菲律宾。目前的部署是 MRF-SEA 的第六次迭代。轮换部署于 2022 年开始。根据海军陆战队的一份新闻稿，该部队的存在旨在加强联合战备和美菲联盟，每次轮换都建立在之前部队的关系和经验教训的基础上，MRF-SEA 称之为“有目的的存在”。 “我们的目标从来都不是简单地出现在菲律宾，”即将卸任的 MRF-SEA 轮换指挥官罗伯特·邦恩 (Robert Bunn) 上校说。 “存在必须有目的。与我们的菲律宾盟友一起进行的每一次演习、计划会议和重复都是一个机会，让我们变得更加具有互操作性、响应能力和能力，并在每次活动中逐渐变得更好。
下一次轮换现在有机会吸取这些教训和关系，推动联盟向前迈进一步。”之前的 MRF-SEA 轮换中，该部队在“肩并肩 26”演习、“卡曼达格 10”演习以及通过群岛海岸防御连续体 (ACDC) 进行的一系列双边活动期间与菲律宾军队一起进行了训练。该连续体在主要演习之间提供了反复训练，使美国和菲律宾部队能够将一次活动中的经验教训应用到下一次活动中。 ACDC是一系列双边训练活动和主题专家交流，支持菲律宾海军陆战队的现代化努力和菲律宾海军陆战队的群岛海岸防御概念，同时加强美国和菲律宾军队之间的联合战备。
