summary: Zambia: Widespread Repression in Post-Election Crackdown - allAfrica.com Zambia: Widespread Repression in Post-Election Crackdown A Patriotic Front supporter proudly displays his identification and voter cards, Lusaka, Zambia (file photo).
content:
Zambia: Widespread Repression in Post-Election Crackdown - allAfrica.com
Zambia: Widespread Repression in Post-Election Crackdown
A Patriotic Front supporter proudly displays his identification and voter cards, Lusaka, Zambia (file photo).
Human Rights Watch (Washington, DC)
Opposition and Critics Forcibly Disappeared, Arbitrary Detained, Beaten
Zambian police and military forcibly disappeared, arbitrarily detained, beat, and threatened opposition members, lawyers, journalists, and government critics in the days before and after general elections in August.
The post-election climate of intimidation, harassment, and repression has had a chilling effect on civic and political organizations, particularly on dissenting voices.
The authorities should immediately halt the crackdown, allow access to lawyers and medical care to detainees, release everyone arbitrarily detained, and ensure accountability for abuses.
(Johannesburg) - The Zambian police and military forcibly disappeared, arbitrarily detained, beat, and threatened opposition members and supporters as well as lawyers, journalists, and government critics in the days before and after general elections in August 2026, Human Rights Watch said today. The authorities have also yet to credibly explain or investigate the killing of an opposition leader in contested circumstances.
"Zambia's government should break this dangerous cycle of repression," said Ashwanee Budoo-Scholtz, deputy Africa director at Human Rights Watch. "The authorities should immediately halt the ongoing post-election crackdown, allow access to lawyers and provide medical care for those in detention, release everyone arbitrarily detained, and ensure accountability for abuses by security forces."
Follow us on WhatsApp | LinkedIn for the latest headlines
President Hakainde Hichilema was reelected in the August 13 election, which observers said was marred by irregularities such as a suspension of counting and limited fundamental freedoms. From August 24 to 28, the authorities suspended judicial services and prevented legal challenges to the presidential election results, closing and cordoning off court premises. Zambian police stated that the closures were an "intelligence-led and preventive measure," without providing details.
Human Rights Watch documented 14 cases in August that appear to have been enforced disappearances, in which the authorities refused to reveal the situation and whereabouts of a detained person. Several of these people were initially forcibly disappeared for days. Victims, family members, and lawyers said that the military held some of them.
Human Rights Watch also documented 61 cases in which detainees or their lawyers and relatives allege that they were beaten or otherwise violently abused during their arrest, in detention, or both. Eighteen have been charged with treason, with two also facing sedition charges. In many cases, the people detained were never charged with a crime while in others, the charges against them appear to be politically motivated. The government has not disclosed how many people were arrested during the crackdown or the charges against them, prompting concerns that the number of people detained is higher than presently known.
Human Rights Watch has also documented two cases in which the Zambia-based relatives of government critics living abroad say government authorities harassed and threatened them.
The post-election climate of intimidation, harassment, and repression has had a chilling effect on civic and political organizations, particularly on dissenting voices, Human Rights Watch said. On September 11, the government announced the cancellation of six government critics' passports, including that of an academic, Sishuwa Sishuwa, for "security reasons."
On August 14, security forces raided the home of the Tonse Alliance opposition leader, Brian Mundubile, in a suburb of Lusaka, the capital. Opposition members present allege that security forces killed a former government minister, Mutotwe Kafwaya, during the raid. Inspector General of the Zambia Police Service Graphel Musamba said members of a "joint intelligence-led operation" were met with "gunfire and resistance from unknown individuals" that "prompted officers to return fire," and that Kafwaya had been killed in the process. Kafwaya's fate was not known until August 19, after his wife filed a habeas corpus petition to compel authorities to disclose his whereabouts, bring him before court, and show sufficient and lawful cause for his continued detention.
Public officials made contradictory statements about the raid and who was responsible for it. On August 15, the Zambia Information and Communications Technology Authority (ZICTA) sent out a text message to all registered phones in Zambia stating: "Beware of false reports of shootings and abductions. Stay calm and peaceful." The Ministry of Information and Media dismissed reports of the raid and shooting as "disinformation intended to alarm and mislead the public."
The police also issued a media statement denying that there had been a raid and that Mundubile was in police custody. Police Inspector General Musamba later admitted that there had been a "joint security-led intelligence operation" at Mundubile's home.
Mundubile, who was later arrested and charged with treason, stated in a High Court petition that Human Rights Watch has seen that he saw a member of the military fatally shoot Kafwaya.
Given the conflicting statements by government officials about who was responsible for the raid on Mundubile's home and the circumstances surrounding Kafwaya's killing, Zambian authorities should institute an independent, impartial, and thorough investigation into the matter, Human Rights Watch said.
Detainees have implicated Zambia's military in arbitrary detention and enforced disappearance. Forty-three opposition members acting as election monitors were detained on August 14. Their lawyer said their whereabouts had been unknown for eight days and that the police had denied holding them. When a lawyer finally saw them, he told Human Rights Watch that "most of them were swollen and had terrible injuries, including broken bones. They said they had been brutalized by the military." Their lawyers filed a habeas corpus application and, on September 10, a court in Lusaka ordered their immediate release.
Under Zambian law and international human rights law, all detainees have the right to due process, including to be promptly informed of the charges against them, to have access to counsel if charged with a crime, to have their detention reviewed by a judge, and to be presumed innocent. They should also have access to adequate medical care and be able to communicate with their families.
In a September 2 call, the United Nations special rapporteur on the rights to freedom of assembly and of association said that the authorities should "release all political detainees, respect fundamental freedoms, and restore democratic accountability." The Ministry of Foreign Affairs and International Cooperation said in response that the call was "inaccurate, undiplomatic and falling short of the standards of objectivity, moderation and discretion expected of UN mandate holders."
The ministry said that being a member of opposition party "does not place a person beyond the reach of the law, nor does it convert a criminal suspect into a political detainee... The government is committed to ensuring that these protections are respected in every case, and Zambia's courts are open to test them."
Zambia will serve as a member of the UN Human Rights Council for the 2027-2029 term. As a council member, Zambia is expected to "uphold the highest standards in the promotion and protection of human rights."
"The Zambian government's needs to end its brazen human rights crackdown," Budoo-Scholtz said. "Leaders in Southern Africa and Zambia's development partners should encourage President Hichilema to restore the rule of law and ensure that civic and political spaces are protected."
Enforced Disappearances, Including by Military Personnel
Human Rights Watch documented 14 cases of apparent enforced disappearances of opposition members and supporters, including some in which the authorities denied holding people who were later produced after habeas corpus applications.
The authorities claimed to have arrested 11 men during the August 14 raid on Mundubile's home.
Lawyers and family members of seven of the men said that they were made to lie down and were beaten using fists, rifle butts, and sticks, kicked by men in military uniform, then blindfolded and driven away in military vehicles. Victims and witnesses identified members of Zambia's military through their uniforms and military vehicles.
During the same raid, security forces picked up several opposition members and supporters and forcibly disappeared them for days before family members or their lawyers found them. They included Bishop Trevor Mwamba, an opposition leader; Patrick Mwansa, a leading opposition campaigner; and security aides Jackson Mutyoka, Bernard Chewe, Brazil Soko, Francis Mulenga, and Richard Banda.
According to their lawyers and court documents seen by Human Rights Watch, the men were taken to a "military command center" where they were "screened and processed" then detained in "various police stations around Lusaka." Lawyers and family members said they went around police stations in Lusaka looking for the detainees, but authorities denied holding the men. However, some were found days later at the same stations where the police had denied holding them.
Mwansa's family said he had a broken finger and swollen face when they finally located him four days later in Lusaka's Central Police Station. On September 6, Mwansa was moved to a maximum security prison in Kabwe, 150 kilometers from Lusaka, and has not yet received medical treatment, a family member said.
The family of Bishop Mwamba, president of the opposition United National Independence Party, who was also picked up during the raid at Mundubile's home, said they searched for him in police stations in and around Lusaka for four days before locating him at Matero Police Station. Earlier, including on the day he was located, officers at Matero Police Station had denied holding Mwamba.
"He had spent days without food and without taking his prescription medication," the relative said. "The police had first denied [holding him] but we insisted to see him, because we had received an anonymous tip informing us that he was at Matero. When they brought him out and we asked what he was arrested for, police said they had no charge for him 'because he was brought in by the military who asked us to keep him in the cells for them."'
On August 30, when the family took food and pain killers to Benard Chewe at Kabwata Police Station, where he had been detained, officers there told them that he had been moved but claimed that they did not know where. When the family traced him two days later to Mwembeshi Correctional Facility on the outskirts of Lusaka, they were denied access.
Men in unmarked vehicles who introduced themselves as "state intelligence officers" picked up Harry Findlay, a Lusaka businessman and opposition supporter, from his residence on August 4, a family member said. Neither his lawyer nor family had access to him, and the authorities did not inform them of his whereabouts. Findlay's lawyers sent two letters to Zambian authorities, on August 7 and August 17, requesting his whereabouts and calling for his immediate release and access to doctors, lawyers, and family.
On August 20, Findlay was taken to court under a judge's order to inquire into the legality of his detention. On August 29, he was charged with treason and moved to Mukobeko Maximum Security Prison, where he remains without trial.
All the men detained in the August 14 raid were eventually charged with treason and remain in detention without having appeared in court. Human Rights Watch believes that in these cases, Zambian authorities are using treason charges, which are nonbailable, and sedition, which carries a heavy penalty, to stifle dissent and political opposition.
On August 27, police arrested Mundubile and his running mate, Makebi Zulu, and subsequently also charged them with treason and seditious practices. The charge sheet, which Human Rights Watch has seen, alleges that Mundubile and Zulu went on Facebook live on August 14 stating that the opposition had won the election. The government alleges that this was meant to "raise discontent or disaffection among the people of Zambia."
On September 22, the Law Association of Zambia raised concerns about prolonged detentions without court appearances. Zambia's Human Rights Commission on September 3 said it was following 84 election-related detainees whose cases it cast as part of a "disturbing pattern of prolonged detention, delayed notification of charges, restricted access to family and legal representation and failure to bring detainees before a competent court without undue delay."
Human Rights Watch documented that 61 people had been mistreated in custody by reviewing court documents and interviewing family members.
Lawyers for the 43 opposition members acting as election monitors who were detained on August 14 said that state security agents kicked and beat them and denied them food during the first 8 days of their 21-day detention.
Lawyers representing 18 detainees accused of treason state in court documents that the detainees were abused and assaulted in custody and denied medical attention. The lawyers also said 10 of the 18--George Chisanga, Patrick Mwansa, Trevor Mwamba, Francis Mulenga, Brazil Soko, Jackson Mutyoka, Bernard Chewe, Richard Banda, Emmanuel Mulenga, and Darius Mwila--had been restricted from accessing their lawyers or family members.
In a court petition filed on September 11, Ezra Topola, Dickson Tembo, and Victor Muzyamba alleged that security personnel waterboarded them and suspended them from a metal bar and beat them. Findlay alleged that he was kept in solitary confinement in Mwembeshi Correctional Facility and denied access to his prescription medication. Mwansa alleged that he suffered serious injuries, including cuts to his face and a fracture on his hand, but was denied access to medical attention.
Family members told Human Rights Watch that when they found Mutyoka on August 17 at Lusaka's Central Police Station, three days after military detained him at Mundubile's home, he showed signs of having been physically abused. "When we saw him, his face was swollen, he was coughing blood and was limping," a relative said. "He said they had been made to lie down in the yard of Mundubile's home and beaten using rifle butts and whips by masked men in military unform. All he wanted was to see a doctor, but that request was denied and, to this day, he has not been seen by a doctor."
When Chewe's family members found him at Kabwata Police Station three days after he was taken from Mundubile's home, they said that he too showed signs of physical abuse. "He had a swollen forehead, busted lips, and complained of body pains," a relative said. "He said he had been assaulted by the military at their headquarters before they took him to the police station."
Lawyers for Chewe, Mutyoka, and Soko at Mwembeshi Correctional Facility said that Zambia Army Special Forces personnel interrogated them and that on September 10, authorities moved the three to Mukobeko Maximum Security Prison without informing family or lawyers.
On October 27, family members said medical doctors have not yet seen the three despite urgent letters written on September 9, seen by Human Rights Watch, to the commissioner of the Zambia Correctional Service and the officer-in-charge of Mwembeshi Correctional Facility.
Eight election monitors for the opposition, men aged 21 to 26, said a group of armed soldiers wearing uniforms and masks jumped over the perimeter wall into a house in Lusaka's Emmasdale township on August 15 around 8 p.m., where the monitors were meeting. They said the armed soldiers dragged them out of the house, kicked them with boots, and beat them with fists and sticks.
They were forced into a military truck and taken away but could not identify where they were held. For the next three days, security forces beat them several times a day, demanding confessions that they belonged to "Brian Mundubile's militia." All eight were released on August 18 without charge.
Human Rights Watch has also examined a petition filed on September 11 by lawyers for the 18 accused of treason that implicates the army in interrogations and abuse of detainees. In the petition, lawyers allege that special forces personnel led by Gen. Moses Shapwaya threatened and intimidated some of the detainees in prison to force them to incriminate Mundubile and Zulu.
From court records and interviews with victims, family, and lawyers, Human Rights Watch documented 71 cases in which opposition members and supporters, as well as government critics, were arrested on charges that may be politically motivated or held in prolonged detention without charge. These include the 43 election monitors and 17 musicians and comedians who were detained after performing at an opposition rally, among others.
The arrest of the 43 monitors came after the opposition leader stated that he planned to challenge the election result in court, while the government accused him of plotting an insurgency. In an electoral court challenge, the monitors would have been potential witnesses for the opposition's case. After their 21 days in detention without charge, the court ruled that their arrest was unjustified and ordered their immediate release.
Human Rights Watch interviewed a 44-year-old Lusaka mathematician who was hired to tally numbers for a potential court challenge to President Hichilema's election. He said that on August 15 at about 9:30 p.m., about eight armed men who identified themselves as intelligence and police officers broke into his house and harassed him. They demanded access to his phone and laptop, he said, and to know who was funding the court challenge.
He said they dragged him outside, put him into a vehicle, and took him to the police headquarters in Lusaka, where he was interrogated further about the election petition. The next day, he was transferred to Ridgeway Police Station, where he spent 18 days without being charged. On August 28, his lawyer filed a habeas corpus application in the Lusaka High Court, which Human Rights Watch has seen. Five days later, police charged him with a misdemeanor offense and released him the same day.
Before the election, on August 5, a group of 17 people were arrested after performing at an opposition rally in Mongu, Western province. Police detained them for over two weeks on what was initially said to be a traffic offense of travelling in a vehicle without numbered plates, a lawyer familiar with the case told Human Rights Watch.

The lawyer said that the group's arrest and prolonged detention were politically motivated because of their vocal and visible mobilization for the opposition. Police later charged and prosecuted the 17 for "riotous assembly or behavior." In a court document seen by Human Rights Watch, the state alleges that the 17 did "unlawfully assemble and begun to execute a common purpose by a breach of peace and the terror of the public." A court released them on bail on August 30, after over three weeks in detention.
Human Rights Watch interviewed seven people, including lawyers and a journalist, who said they had fled their homes because they believed they had been targeted for arrest in the days after the August 13 election. A lawyer and a journalist showed Human Rights Watch messages on their phones alerting them that they were on a "wanted list." Some left and others were in hiding within the country.
A statement by seven international lawyers' associations said some lawyers involved in preparing or lodging election-related legal challenges had fled Zambia due to threats to their safety.
A lawyer said that he went into hiding on August 15 after scores of security agents came to his home and office. The lawyer had been acting on behalf of Tonse Alliance, including working on a court petition to challenge President Hichilema's election. "There was no reason for the security agents to chase me in that manner," he said. "If the police wanted me for any reason, they should have alerted me, and I would have presented myself with my legal representatives."
Mulenga Kapwepwe, an opposition leader who worked closely with Mundubile and Zulu, said she went into hiding on August 15 after confidential sources alerted her that she was "on a wanted list." "I have had to rearrange my life," she said. "Many of my colleagues are in detention charged with treason, and I have been warned that the moment I come out of hiding, I will be targeted."
On August 17, a journalist who runs an investigative journalism website and has previously been detained for his journalism crossed the border into a neighboring country hours before security agents went to his house looking for him. "My website was following up on the raid at Mundubile's house," he said. "That is when I received messages on my phone saying: 'Stop what you are doing. We are coming after you.' I was once arrested and detained without charge for nearly two weeks. I know what these people are capable of. So, fearful for my life, I left."
While he was fleeing, the journalist said, he received a call from a family member that about five people who identified themselves as officers from Office of the President were at his house looking for him. They told his family that he was wanted for sedition.
Human Rights Watch documented two cases in which the authorities allegedly harassed and threatened the Zambia-based family members of government critics living abroad.
Police allegedly detained two siblings of a well-known diaspora critic of the government and harassed their 76-year-old father, demanding that their sibling abroad, who runs a popular social media page with hundreds of thousands of followers, take down material critical of the government.
One sibling was detained in a 3 a.m. raid on their home, in which armed police officers demanded access to their phones and laptop, a close source said, adding that one of the police officers "had a gun and said: 'This is a high security operation." The officers said the foreign-based sibling's "political commentary was 'a problem' and that they needed it to stop." The authorities allegedly demanded the removal of specific videos as a condition for their release. In one of these videos, the social media personality demanded an independent inquiry into the August 14 killing of Kafwaya.
In another case, a government critic in the United States with investments in Zambia said that three men who identified themselves as intelligence officers from the Office of the President approached family members in Zambia days after the election and threatened to "squeeze" her businesses if she continued to criticize President Hichilema's administration on social media. "They told my sister, a civil servant, that she risked losing her job if I did not tone down my criticism," the critic said.

content:
周六晚间，法兰克福商店橱窗遭到暴徒打砸图像来源: Andreas Arnold/dpa/picture alliance
（德国之声中文网）上周末“Z世代”抗议活动后法兰克福发生的暴力事件，持续在政治层面引发讨论。
德国内政部长亚历山大·多布林特（Alexander Dobrindt，基社盟）周日在接受《图片报》（Bild）在线版采访时表示：“左翼暴力团体和具有移民背景的滋事者绑架了当天早些时候进行的和平示威活动。我们将查明这些暴徒和抢劫者的身份，并追究其法律责任。这种破坏社会安宁的行为必须受到严厉惩处。”
德国教育部长卡琳·普里恩（ Karin Prien，基民盟）认为，这些事件也引出了一个问题：如何才能更成功地实现社会融合。她在接受德意志电台（Deutschlandfunk）采访时提到，极左团体以及“可能具有移民背景的人群”参与了“过激的暴力行为”。她强调，这不是煽动怨恨，而是要探究为何有人会采取此类手段。“如果他们确实有移民背景，那我们必须关注，必须审视其背后的根本原因”，卡琳·普里恩说。她指出，一个关键问题是， 为何某些群体在社会融合方面不如其他群体。这位部长明确表示，她并不支持“Z世代”提出的所有诉求，比如在兵役问题上，但她主张对话，尤其是倾听那些未参与暴力活动的年轻人的心声。
法兰克福所在的黑森州州长鲍里斯·莱茵（Boris Rhein，基民盟）对法兰克福发生的暴力事件感到震惊。黑森州内政部长罗曼·波塞克（Roman Poseck，基民盟）表示，法兰克福骚乱的肇事者有两类，先是左翼极端分子，随后是“有移民背景的年轻人”加入。他在通报中称，被捕者年龄在13至29岁之间，“其中绝大多数是德国公民”。波塞克还指出：“我们有理由认为，肇事者中只有极少数来自法兰克福本地；许多人是从周边地区赶来的，还有一些人来自更远的地方。这些人绝大多数具有移民背景。“
德国国防部长皮斯托里乌斯（Boris Pistorius，社民党）不同意联盟党（基民盟/基社盟）政治家的解读。在接受德国电视二台（ZDF）采访时，他反问道：“所谓的‘移民群体’究竟是指什么？是指那些已经在德国生活了三代、且身为德国公民的人吗？我们到底要在什么时候才能停止这种区分？我认为，这会引向错误的方向。”
科隆警察局长约翰内斯·赫尔曼斯（Johannes Hermanns）表示：“令人痛心且深感不安的是，那些本意是为自身未来进行和平示威的年轻人，今天却被一些一心只想制造暴力的极端分子渗透了。”
社民党联邦议院党团呼吁召开全国教育峰会。该党团副主席施密特（Schmidt）指出，有权获得良好教育和职业培训的权利是此次示威活动的核心诉求之一。她主张德国发起一场由联邦、州和地方各级政府共同参与的教育峰会。
在周六晚间法兰克福的骚乱中，暴徒向安全部队投掷燃烧瓶和鞭炮，并砸碎了多家商店，包括一家枪支商店的橱窗。安全部队动用了水炮车、装甲车、直升机和无人机。大量人员被暂时拘留。超过100名警员在冲突中受伤。柏林、汉堡和科隆等德国其他城市也发生了暴力事件。德国内政部长多布林特对安全部队的表现给予了肯定。他表示：“多亏了我们尽职尽责的警员，才避免了像巴黎那样严重的暴力失控局面。警方保持大规模警力在场并分散部署的行动策略被证明是成功的。”
此前号召在德国30多个城市举行和平示威的“Z世代做主”（Gen Z regelt）倡议组织的发言人表示，集会结束后所发生的一切，我们无法施加任何影响。该组织在Instagram上发文，明确与“任何形式的暴力，以及由非示威参与者的其他团体或个人所实施的暴力行为”划清界限。声明写道：“我们主张和平抗议、民主价值观以及自由表达意见的权利。暴力从来不是、也永远不会是我们运动的一部分。”
“Z世代做主”倡议组织提出的诉求包括增加学校经费、促进社会正义、采取措施应对不断上涨的生活成本，以及加强气候保护。这个由年轻人组成的松散联盟主要通过社交媒体进行协调，其具体组织架构及参与人员尚不明确。一个名叫阿克拉姆·塞洛（Akram Selo）的人被列为抗议活动的主要平台——“Z世代做主”网站的运营者。此人自称是一名18岁的高中生，其登记地址位于瑞士。他在接受《明星周刊》（Stern）采访时表示，这一倡议背后是一群“想要做出改变的年轻人”，通过TikTok建立联系。在接受《法兰克福汇报》（FAZ）采访时，塞洛称自己正在准备参加德国高中毕业考试，目前的组织团队由五人组成，其中三人选择保持匿名。他们居住在不同的城市，且并非所有成员彼此都相识。从《法兰克福汇报》的采访中可以看出，他对自己的人身安全感到担忧。
汉堡等地10月31日下午的“Z世代”抗议活动在和平的气氛中进行图像来源: Jonas Walzberg/REUTERS
该倡议组织计划在三周内再次在全国范围内动员大规模人群，并在“Z世代做主”的网站上呼吁人们为了教育、健康、气候保护，以及负担得起的生活，11月20日在34个德国城市参加全欧洲范围内抗议活动。
一个广泛的联盟号召人们参与11月20日的“国际青年罢工日”（International Youth Strike）。该联盟成员包括“联邦学生大会”（BSK）——此前，该组织曾与“Z世代做主”（Gen Z regelt）这一倡议活动保持距离。

2015年的夏末秋初，大量中东难民涌向欧洲、涌向德国。重压之下，时任德国总理Merkel做出了一个影响深远的决定：向难民敞开大门。当时的民意也支持这项决定。然而，十年后的今天，陆续接纳了数百万难民的德国，其民意早已逆转；反对移民和难民的右翼民粹政党获得的选票越来越多，主流政党也纷纷开始收紧相关政策。德国，是否能弥合因难民问题而撕裂的社会？德国，又能否通过吸纳移民来填补劳动力不足的缺口？
最新研究显示，德国孩子的受教育机会和家庭背景高度相关，其中父母受教育程度、收入水平的影响尤其明显。此外，所有家庭背景群体中，男孩能上文理中学的几率都低于女孩。研究报告建议，为弱势儿童比例较高的学校配备更好师资。
最新一次对中学生的水平测试显示，德国学生在阅读、数学和自然科学领域均滑落至历史最低水平。前五名均为亚洲国家，中国排名第一。专家认为，在德国，社会经济地位仍在很大程度上决定教育成就。
在欧盟释放信号，表示愿意让加拿大以“准成员”身份成为其特殊伙伴后，美国总统特朗普对此发出嘲讽，并表示，这一设想属于“敌对行为”。
北京香山论坛多国代表对军用人工智能的潜在风险深表担忧。在美中两国准备举行高层会晤之际，武器自主化正急剧压缩决策时间，大国在此类技术管控上的分歧再度引发广泛讨论。
周一，中共为前总书记江泽民举行百岁冥诞纪念大会。周二，前总理朱镕基的遗体在八宝山公墓火化，天安门等地降半旗致哀。江泽民与朱镕基留给习近平怎样的遗产？习近平能否借助已经逝去的时代安抚当下的民心，进一步巩固自己的权力？
10月30日，刚刚与欧盟领导人进行会谈的加拿大总理卡尼接受了德国之声专访。他表示，加拿大对美国的依赖度过高，现在亟需深化与志同道合国家的多样化伙伴关系。
德国总理默茨在首尔与韩国总统李在明共同举行了联合新闻发布会，默茨表示，两国关系将提升至“深层战略伙伴关系”的水平。他说，在全球动荡时期，“我们现在加深伙伴关系是理所应当”。
德国车商奥迪计划斥40亿美元在美国建厂，预计创造约4500个就业岗位。特朗普将此归功于关税政策，但德国国内批评声不断。在德国车企面临中国竞争、利润承压和裁员风险之际，奥迪押注美国市场及大型燃油SUV，也引发了有关德国就业和电动化转型的讨论。

content:
朝鲜和韩国继续隔着非军事区相互戒备图像来源: Kay Nietfeld/dpa/picture alliance
（德国之声中文网）朝鲜和韩国两个拥有共同历史、语言以及大量文化遗产，却彼此对立的国家，这故事在德国人听来并不陌生。
德国自己也曾在对立政权下分裂数十年，直到地缘政治局势发生变化，东西德才得以在1990年和平统一。
仅仅两年后，时任德国总理科尔（Helmut Kohl）访问朝鲜半岛非军事区（DMZ），表达了希望朝韩也能在本世纪90年代末实现统一的愿望。
但这一愿望最终未能实现。德国实现统一约35年后，朝韩依然在政治制度、经济发展以及地缘政治阵营上严重对立。
周五，德国总理默茨站在俯瞰朝鲜半岛非军事区的地方，所表达的愿望与科尔1993年提出的几乎如出一辙。
默茨在社交媒体上写道：“我们德国人知道国家分裂有多痛苦。我们也知道，只要坚守自己的价值观，并拥有对话的勇气，就有可能推倒高墙。”
默茨还表示：“我们祝愿朝鲜半岛人民能够在自由中实现统一。”
在长期关注朝韩政治动态的分析人士看来，这听起来更像是一个遥不可及的梦想。
朝鲜和韩国继续隔着非军事区相互戒备，双方在财富水平和政治自由方面的巨大差异也一览无余。
但最大的问题或许在于：朝韩双方似乎都没有表现出实现统一的意愿。
庆熙大学外交政策教授朱宰佑（Choo Jae-woo）表示：“过去二十年来，人们的心态已经发生了变化。在韩国年轻人眼中，朝鲜不过是邻近的一个国家，既贫穷又充满威胁。他们对朝鲜并没有像老一辈人那样怀有某种情感上的羁绊。”
首尔大学和平与统一研究所今年9月公布的一项调查显示，39.1%的韩国受访者认为统一已不可能实现。这是该调查开展约二十年以来的最高比例。
许多人担心，为朝鲜建设基础设施将耗费巨额资金，包括修建道路、医院和学校，以及现代社会正常运转所需的各项配套。
从官方立场来看，韩国政府并未放弃将国家统一作为目标。韩国宪法仍然主张以自由和民主为基础实现和平统一。但朱宰佑指出，近几届韩国政府对这一理念的宣传力度已经远不如过去。
To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video
朱宰佑说：“2023年12月，金正恩宣布将修宪，和平统一已不再可能。相反，朝鲜将韩国视为敌对国家，且金正恩已无意推动双方走向统一。”
朝鲜修订后的宪法于2026年3月他通过。此后，金正恩政权更加激进，清除了宪法中所有关于和解及民族统一的表述。
首尔韩国外国语大学政治学与国际关系教授梅森·里奇（Mason Richey）表示：“我认为，朝鲜已经把话说得很明白了：它根本无意与韩国拉近关系。”
他补充说，每当朝鲜半岛统一问题再次被提起，韩国的分析人士、官员乃至普通民众都会开始“翻白眼”。
里奇指出，除了朝韩双方缺乏统一意愿之外，还有诸多其他挑战亟待克服。
朝鲜政权希望维护自身权力和威望。如果统一后的国家引入民主制度，朝鲜现政权的权力和地位必然受到威胁。
里奇表示，弥合朝韩之间巨大的经济发展差距将是一项艰巨工程，即使能够获得外部援助，也会给韩国带来巨大压力。
他指出，统一后的德国如今在大多数领域已经实现了东西部之间的平衡，但值得注意的是，1990年的东德发展水平仍远高于今天的朝鲜。
根据韩国银行2024年的统计数据，朝鲜名义GDP每年为317亿美元，而韩国高达1.85万亿美元，是朝鲜的58倍。朝鲜人均GDP仅为1230美元，而韩国接近3.6万美元。
朱宰佑还指出，朝韩统一不仅是内部事务问题。两国在战略和安全领域分别依附于不同阵营：韩国与美国结盟，朝鲜则与中国保持紧密关系，并且越来越多地转向俄罗斯。
朱宰佑对德国之声表示：“这些大国不会愿意为了实现朝鲜半岛统一而放弃各自的盟友，因为统一对它们而言同样涉及重大的战略问题。美国不会希望出现一个倒向中国的统一朝鲜；如果统一意味着美国可能把军队部署到中国边境上、也就是今天的朝鲜境内,中国就会抵制统一。这是双方都无法想象的局面。”
他认为，归根结底，朝鲜半岛目前的现状或许并不完美，却是维持地区稳定的最佳方式。
不过，他补充说：“十年之后，经济、社会和安全局势可能会发生翻天覆地的变化。因此，我们永远不能把话说死。”

National Center for Education Statistics (NCES), Institute of Education Sciences (IES), Department of Education (ED).
On October 29, 2026, the U.S. Department of Education published a notice in the Federal Register announcing a Request for Information (RFI) for NCES with FR DOC# 2026- 22047 (91 FR 68118, pages 68118-68120). ED is issuing this correction notice to ensure that NCES can properly receive the requested information from the field ( printed page 68953) and more effectively carry out requirements laid out in 20 U.S.C. 9543.

On September 25, 2025, based on timely requests for review, in accordance with 19 CFR 351.221(c)(1)(i), we initiated an administrative review of the antidumping duty order on large power transformers from the Republic of Korea (Korea).[1] On January 29, 2026, Commerce selected Hyundai and Iljin as the mandatory respondents in this review.[2]
Due to the lapse in appropriations and Federal Government shutdown, on November 14, 2025, Commerce tolled all deadlines in administrative proceedings by 47 days.[3] Additionally, due to a backlog of documents that were electronically filed via Enforcement and Compliance's Antidumping and Countervailing Duty Centralized Electronic Service System (ACCESS) during the Federal Government shutdown, on November 24, 2025, Commerce tolled all deadlines in administrative proceedings by an additional 21 days.[4] On July 9, 2026, we extended the preliminary results of this review to no later than October 30, 2026.[5]
For a complete description of the events that followed the initiation of this review, see the Preliminary Decision Memorandum.[6] A list of the topics discussed in the Preliminary Decision Memorandum is attached as an appendix to this notice. The Preliminary Decision Memorandum is a public document and is on file electronically via Enforcement and Compliance's Antidumping and Countervailing Duty Centralized Electronic Service System (ACCESS). ACCESS is available to registered users at https://access.trade.gov. In addition, a complete version of the Preliminary Decision Memorandum can be accessed directly at https://access.trade.gov/​frnotices.
The merchandise subject to the Order is large power transformers from Korea. For a complete description of the scope of the Order, see the Preliminary Decision Memorandum.
Commerce is conducting this review in accordance with section 751(a) of the Tariff Act of 1930, as amended (the Act). Constructed export prices have been calculated in accordance with section 772 of the Act. NV is calculated in accordance with section 773 of the Act. For a full description of the methodology underlying our conclusions, see the Preliminary Decision Memorandum.
Rate for Non-Individually Examined Companies
The Act and Commerce's regulations do not address the establishment of a rate to apply to companies not selected for individual examination when Commerce limits its examination in an administrative review pursuant to section 777A(c)(2) of the Act. Generally, Commerce looks to section 735(c)(5) of the Act, which provides instructions for calculating the all-others rate in a market economy investigation, for guidance when calculating the rate for companies which were not selected for individual examination in an administrative review.
Under section 735(c)(5)(A) of the Act, the all-others rate is normally an amount equal to the weighted average of the estimated weighted-average dumping margins established for exporters and producers individually investigated, excluding any rates that are zero, de minimis ( i.e., less than 0.5 percent), or determined entirely on the basis of facts available. Where the weighted-average dumping margin for each of the individually examined companies is zero, de minimis, or based entirely on facts available, section 735(c)(5)(B) of the Act provides that Commerce may use “any reasonable method to establish the estimated all-others rate for exporters and producers not individually investigated, including averaging the estimated weighted-average dumping margins determined for the exporters and producers individually investigated.” In this review, Commerce preliminarily calculated weighted-average dumping margins of zero percent for Hyundai and Iljin. Therefore, we have preliminarily determined to continue to assign the estimated weighted-average dumping margins currently in effect to the non-selected companies subject to review. For a full discussion of the rates for non-selected companies, see the Preliminary Decision Memorandum.
As a result of this review, we preliminarily determine the following estimated weighted-average dumping margin exists for the period August 1, 2024, through July 31, 2025:
Producer/exporter Weighted- average dumping margin (percent) HD Hyundai Electric Co., Ltd 0.00 Iljin Electric Co., Ltd 0.00 LS Electric Co., Ltd 4.32 Hyosung Heavy Industries Corporation 4.32
Commerce intends to disclose its calculations and analysis performed to interested parties for these preliminary results within five days of any public announcement or, if there is no public announcement, within five days of the date of publication of this notice in accordance with 19 CFR 351.224(b).
As provided in section 782(i)(3) of the Act, Commerce intends to verify the information relied upon in making its final results.
Case briefs or other written comments may be submitted to the Assistant Secretary for Enforcement and Compliance no later than seven days after the date on which the last verification report is issued in this review. Rebuttal briefs, limited to issues raised in the case briefs, may be filed not later than five days after the date for filing case briefs.[7] Interested parties who submit case briefs or rebuttal briefs in this proceeding must submit: (1) a table of contents listing each issue; and (2) a table of authorities.[8] All briefs must be filed electronically using ACCESS. An electronically filed document must be received successfully in its entirety ( printed page 68942) in ACCESS by 5:00 p.m. Eastern Time on the established deadline.
As provided under 19 CFR 351.309(c)(2)(iii) and (d)(2)(iii), we request that interested parties provide at the beginning of their briefs a public executive summary for each issue raised in their briefs.[9] Further, we request that interested parties limit their public executive summary of each issue to no more than 450 words, not including citations. We intend to use the public executive summaries as the basis of the comment summaries included in the issues and decision memorandum that will accompany the final results in this administrative review. We request that interested parties include footnotes for relevant citations in the public executive summary of each issue. Note that Commerce has amended certain of its requirements pertaining to the service of documents in 19 CFR 351.303(f).[10]
Pursuant to 19 CFR 351.310(c), interested parties who wish to request a hearing must submit a written request to the Assistant Secretary for Enforcement and Compliance, filed electronically via ACCESS by 5:00 p.m. Eastern Time within 30 days after the date of publication of this notice. Requests should contain: (1) the party's name, address, and telephone number; (2) the number of participants; and (3) a list of issues to be discussed. Oral presentations at the hearing will be limited to issues raised in the briefs. If a request for a hearing is made, Commerce will inform parties of the scheduled date for the hearing.[11]
Pursuant to section 751(a)(2)(A) of the Act and 19 CFR 351.212(b)(1), Commerce will determine, and U.S. Customs and Border Protection (CBP) shall assess, antidumping duties on all appropriate entries of subject merchandise in accordance with the final results of this review.
If any individually examined respondent's weighted-average dumping margin is not zero or de minimis ( i.e., less than 0.50 percent) in the final results of this review, Commerce intends to calculate importer-specific assessment rates on the basis of the ratio of the total amount of dumping calculated for each importer's examined sales to the total entered value of those sales. Where we do not have entered values for all U.S. sales to a particular importer, we will calculate an importer-specific, per-unit assessment rate on the basis of the ratio of the total amount of dumping calculated for the importer's examined sales to the total quantity of those sales.[12] To determine whether an importer-specific, per-unit assessment rate is de minimis, in accordance with 19 CFR 351.106(c)(2), we also will calculate an importer-specific ad valorem ratio based on estimated entered values. If any respondent's weighted-average dumping margin is zero or de minimis or where an importer-specific ad valorem assessment rate is zero or de minimis, we will instruct CBP to liquidate appropriate entries without regard to antidumping duties.[13]
In accordance with Commerce's “automatic assessment” practice, for entries of subject merchandise during the POR produced by each respondent for which it did not know that the merchandise was destined for the United States, we intend to instruct CBP to liquidate those entries at the all-others rate calculated in the less-than-fair-value (LTFV) investigation if there is no rate for the intermediate company(ies) involved in the transaction.[14]
For LS Electric Co., Ltd. and Hyosung Heavy Industries Corporation, the companies that were not selected for individual review, we will assign an assessment rate based on the review-specific rate, calculated as noted in the “Rate for Non-Individually Examined Companies” section, above. The final results of this review shall be the basis for the assessment of antidumping duties on entries of merchandise covered by the final results of this review and for future deposits of estimated duties, where applicable.[15]
Commerce intends to issue assessment instructions to CBP no earlier than 35 days after the date of publication of the final results of this review in the Federal Register . If a timely summons is filed at the U.S. Court of International Trade, the assessment instructions will direct CBP not to liquidate relevant entries until the time for parties to file a request for a statutory injunction has expired ( i.e., within 90 days of publication).
The following deposit requirements will be effective for all shipments of the subject merchandise entered, or withdrawn from warehouse, for consumption on or after the publication date of the final results of this administrative review, as provided by section 751(a)(2)(C) of the Act: (1) the cash deposit rate for the companies listed above will be that established in the final results of this review, except if the rate is less than 0.50 percent and, therefore, de minimis within the meaning of 19 CFR 351.106(c)(1), in which case the cash deposit rate will be zero; (2) for previously investigated or reviewed companies not covered by this review, the cash deposit rate will continue to be the company-specific cash deposit rate published for the most recently completed segment of this proceeding in which the company participated; (3) if the exporter is not a firm covered in this review, or the LTFV investigation, but the manufacturer is, then the cash deposit rate will be the rate established for the most recent segment for the manufacturer of the merchandise; and (4) the cash deposit rate for all other manufacturers or exporters will continue to be 22.00 percent, the all-others rate established in the LTFV investigation.[16] These cash deposit requirements, when imposed, shall remain in effect until further notice.
This notice also serves as a preliminary reminder to importers of their responsibility under 19 CFR 351.402(f)(2) to file a certificate regarding the reimbursement of antidumping duties prior to liquidation of the relevant entries during this review period. Failure to comply with this requirement could result in Commerce's presumption that reimbursement of antidumping duties occurred and the subsequent assessment of double antidumping duties.
We are issuing and publishing these preliminary results of review in accordance with sections 751(a)(1) and 777(i)(1) of the Act, and 19 CFR 351.221(b)(4).
Acting Deputy Assistant Secretary for Antidumping and Countervailing Duty Operations.

[Investigation No. 701-TA-665 and 731-TA-1557 (Review)]
United States International Trade Commission.
The Commission hereby gives notice that it has instituted reviews pursuant to the Tariff Act of 1930, as amended, to determine whether revocation of the antidumping and countervailing duty orders on certain mobile access equipment (“MAE”) and subassemblies thereof from China would be likely to lead to continuation or recurrence of material injury. Pursuant to the Act, interested parties are requested to respond to this notice by submitting the information specified below to the Commission.
Instituted November 2, 2026. To be assured of consideration, the deadline for responses is December 2, 2026. Comments on the adequacy of responses may be filed with the Commission by January 12, 2027.
Richard Whiting (202-205-2039), Office of Investigations, U.S. International Trade Commission, 500 E Street SW, Washington, DC 20436. Hearing-impaired persons can obtain information on this matter by contacting the Commission's TDD terminal on 202-205-1810. Persons with mobility impairments who will need special assistance in gaining access to the Commission should contact the Office of the Secretary at 202-205-2000. General information concerning the Commission may also be obtained by accessing its internet server ( https://www.usitc.gov). The public record for this proceeding may be viewed on the Commission's electronic docket (EDIS) at https://edis.usitc.gov.
Background. —On December 10, 2021, the Department of Commerce (“Commerce”) issued a countervailing duty order on imports of MAE and subassemblies from China (86 FR 70439). Additionally, on April 14, 2022, Commerce issued an antidumping duty order on imports of MAE and subassemblies from China (87 FR 22190). The Commission is conducting reviews pursuant to section 751(c) of the Act, as amended (19 U.S.C. 1675(c)), to determine whether revocation of the orders would be likely to lead to continuation or recurrence of material injury to the domestic industry within a reasonably foreseeable time. Provisions concerning the conduct of this proceeding may be found in the Commission's Rules of Practice and Procedure at 19 CFR part 201, subparts A and B, and 19 CFR part 207, subparts A and F. The Commission will assess the adequacy of interested party responses to this notice of institution to determine whether to conduct full or expedited reviews. The Commission's determinations in any expedited reviews will be based on the facts available, which may include information provided in response to this notice.
Definitions. —The following definitions apply to these reviews:
(1) Subject Merchandise is the class or kind of merchandise that is within the scope of the five-year reviews, as defined by Commerce.
(2) The Subject Country in these reviews is China.
(3) The Domestic Like Product is the domestically produced product or products which are like, or in the absence of like, most similar in characteristics and uses with, the Subject Merchandise. In its original determinations, the Commission defined a single Domestic Like Product as finished MAE and MAE subassemblies coextensive with the scope of the investigation.
(4) The Domestic Industry is the U.S. producers as a whole of the Domestic Like Product, or those producers whose collective output of the Domestic Like Product constitutes a major proportion of the total domestic production of the product. In its original determinations, the Commission defined the Domestic Industry as all producers of finished MAE and subassemblies and firms that conducted activities involved in the assembly of MAE subassemblies into finished MAE.
(5) The Order Dates are the dates that the orders under review became effective. In the review concerning the countervailing duty order on imports of MAE from China, the Order Date is December 10, 2021. In the review concerning the antidumping duty order on imports of MAE from China, the Order Date is April 14, 2022.
(6) An Importer is any person or firm engaged, either directly or through a parent company or subsidiary, in importing the Subject Merchandise into the United States from a foreign manufacturer or through its selling agent.
Participation in the proceeding and public service list. —Persons, including industrial users of the Subject Merchandise and, if the merchandise is sold at the retail level, representative consumer organizations, wishing to participate in the proceeding as parties must file an entry of appearance with the Secretary to the Commission, as provided in § 201.11(b)(4) of the Commission's rules, no later than 21 days after publication of this notice in the Federal Register . The Secretary will maintain a public service list containing the names and addresses of all persons, or their representatives, who are parties to the proceeding.
Former Commission employees who are seeking to appear in Commission five-year reviews are advised that they may appear in a review even if they participated personally and substantially in the corresponding underlying original investigation or an earlier review of the same underlying investigation. The Commission's designated agency ethics official has advised that a five-year review is not the same particular matter as the underlying original investigation, and a five-year review is not the same particular matter as an earlier review of the same underlying investigation for purposes of 18 U.S.C. 207, the post-employment statute for Federal employees, and Commission rule 201.15(b) (19 CFR 201.15(b)), 79 FR 3246 (Jan. 17, 2014), 73 FR 24609 (May 5, 2008). Consequently, former employees are not required to seek Commission approval to appear in a review under Commission rule 19 CFR 201.15, even if the corresponding underlying original investigation or an earlier review of the same underlying investigation was pending when they were Commission employees. For further ethics advice on this matter, contact Charles Smith, Office of the General Counsel, at 202-205-3408.
Limited disclosure of business proprietary information (BPI) under an administrative protective order (APO) and APO service list. —Pursuant to § 207.7(a) of the Commission's rules, the Secretary will make BPI submitted in this proceeding available to authorized applicants under the APO issued in the proceeding, provided that the application is made no later than 21 days after publication of this notice in the Federal Register . Authorized applicants must represent interested parties, as defined in 19 U.S.C. 1677(9), who are parties to the proceeding. A separate service list will be maintained by the Secretary for those parties authorized to receive BPI under the APO.
Certification. —Pursuant to § 207.3 of the Commission's rules, any person ( printed page 68975) submitting information to the Commission in connection with this proceeding must certify that the information is accurate and complete to the best of the submitter's knowledge. In making the certification, the submitter will acknowledge that information submitted in response to this request for information and throughout this proceeding or other proceeding may be disclosed to and used: (i) by the Commission, its employees and Offices, and contract personnel (a) for developing or maintaining the records of this or a related proceeding, or (b) in internal investigations, audits, reviews, and evaluations relating to the programs, personnel, and operations of the Commission including under 5 U.S.C. Appendix 3; or (ii) by U.S. government employees and contract personnel, solely for cybersecurity purposes. All contract personnel will sign appropriate nondisclosure agreements.
Written submissions. —Pursuant to § 207.61 of the Commission's rules, each interested party response to this notice must provide the information specified below. The deadline for filing such responses is on or before 5:15 p.m. on December 2, 2026. Pursuant to § 207.62(b) of the Commission's rules, eligible parties (as specified in Commission rule 207.62(b)(1)) may also file comments concerning the adequacy of responses to the notice of institution and whether the Commission should conduct expedited or full reviews. The deadline for filing such comments is on or before 5:15 p.m. on January 12, 2027. All written submissions must conform with the provisions of § 201.8 of the Commission's rules; any submissions that contain BPI must also conform with the requirements of §§ 201.6, 207.3, and 207.7 of the Commission's rules. The Commission's Handbook on Filing Procedures, available on the Commission's website at https://www.usitc.gov/​documents/​handbook_​on_​filing_​procedures.pdf, elaborates upon the Commission's procedures with respect to filings. Also, in accordance with §§ 201.16(c) and 207.3 of the Commission's rules, each document filed by a party to the proceeding must be served on all other parties to the proceeding (as identified by either the public or APO service list as appropriate), and a certificate of service must accompany the document (if you are not a party to the proceeding you do not need to serve your response).
Please note the Secretary's Office will accept only electronic filings at this time. Filings must be made through the Commission's Electronic Document Information System (EDIS, https://edis.usitc.gov). No in-person paper-based filings or paper copies of any electronic filings will be accepted until further notice.
No response to this request for information is required if a currently valid Office of Management and Budget (“OMB”) number is not displayed; the OMB number is 3117 0016/USITC No. 26-5-709, expiration date July 31, 2029. Public reporting burden for the request is estimated to average 15 hours per response. Please send comments regarding the accuracy of this burden estimate to the Office of Investigations, U.S. International Trade Commission, 500 E Street SW, Washington, DC 20436.
Inability to provide requested information. —Pursuant to § 207.61(c) of the Commission's rules, any interested party that cannot furnish the information requested by this notice in the requested form and manner shall notify the Commission at the earliest possible time, provide a full explanation of why it cannot provide the requested information, and indicate alternative forms in which it can provide equivalent information. If an interested party does not provide this notification (or the Commission finds the explanation provided in the notification inadequate) and fails to provide a complete response to this notice, the Commission may take an adverse inference against the party pursuant to § 776(b) of the Act (19 U.S.C. 1677e(b)) in making its determinations in these reviews.
Information To Be Provided in Response to This Notice of Institution: As used below, the term “firm” includes any related firms.
Those responding to this notice of institution are encouraged, but not required, to visit the USITC's website at https://usitc.gov/​reports/​response_​noi_​worksheet, where one can download and complete the “NOI worksheet” Excel form for the subject proceeding, to be included as attachment/exhibit 1 of your overall response.
(1) The name and address of your firm or entity (including World Wide Web address) and name, telephone number, fax number, and Email address of the certifying official.
(2) A statement indicating whether your firm/entity is an interested party under 19 U.S.C. 1677(9) and if so, how, including whether your firm/entity is a U.S. producer of the Domestic Like Product, a U.S. union or worker group, a U.S. importer of the Subject Merchandise, a foreign producer or exporter of the Subject Merchandise, a U.S. or foreign trade or business association (a majority of whose members are interested parties under the statute), or another interested party (including an explanation). If you are a union/worker group or trade/business association, identify the firms in which your workers are employed or which are members of your association.
(3) A statement indicating whether your firm/entity is willing to participate in this proceeding by providing information requested by the Commission.
(4) A statement of the likely effects of the revocation of the antidumping and countervailing duty orders on the Domestic Industry in general and/or your firm/entity specifically. In your response, please discuss the various factors specified in § 752(a) of the Act (19 U.S.C. 1675a(a)) including the likely volume of subject imports, likely price effects of subject imports, and likely impact of imports of Subject Merchandise on the Domestic Industry.
(5) A list of all known and currently operating U.S. producers of the Domestic Like Product. Identify any known related parties and the nature of the relationship as defined in § 771(4)(B) of the Act (19 U.S.C. 1677(4)(B)).
(6) A list of all known and currently operating U.S. importers of the Merchandise and producers of the Subject Merchandise in the Subject Country that currently export or have exported Subject Merchandise to the United States or other countries since the Order Dates.
(7) A list of 3-5 leading purchasers in the U.S. market for the Domestic Like Product and the Subject Merchandise (including street address, World Wide Web address, and the name, telephone number, fax number, and Email address of a responsible official at each firm).
(8) A list of known sources of information on national or regional prices for the Domestic Like Product or the Subject Merchandise in the U.S. or other markets.
(9) If you are a U.S. producer of the Domestic Like Product, provide the following information on your firm's operations on that product during calendar year 2025, except as noted (report quantity data in short tons and value data in U.S. dollars, f.o.b. plant). If you are a union/worker group or trade/business association, provide the information, on an aggregate basis, for the firms in which your workers are employed/which are members of your association.
(a) Production (quantity) and, if known, an estimate of the percentage of total U.S. production of the Domestic Like Product accounted for by your firm's(s') production; ( printed page 68976)
(b) Capacity (quantity) of your firm to produce the Domestic Like Product (that is, the level of production that your establishment(s) could reasonably have expected to attain during the year, assuming normal operating conditions (using equipment and machinery in place and ready to operate), normal operating levels (hours per week/weeks per year), time for downtime, maintenance, repair, and cleanup, and a typical or representative product mix);
(c) the quantity and value of U.S. commercial shipments of the Domestic Like Product produced in your U.S. plant(s);
(d) the quantity and value of U.S. internal consumption/company transfers of the Domestic Like Product produced in your U.S. plant(s); and
(e) the value of (i) net sales, (ii) cost of goods sold (COGS), (iii) gross profit, (iv) selling, general and administrative (SG&A) expenses, and (v) operating income of the Domestic Like Product produced in your U.S. plant(s) (include both U.S. and export commercial sales, internal consumption, and company transfers) for your most recently completed fiscal year (identify the date on which your fiscal year ends).
(10) If you are a U.S. importer or a trade/business association of U.S. importers of the Subject Merchandise from the Subject Country, provide the following information on your firm's(s') operations on that product during calendar year 2025 (report quantity data in short tons and value data in U.S. dollars). If you are a trade/business association, provide the information, on an aggregate basis, for the firms which are members of your association.
(a) The quantity and value (landed, duty-paid but not including antidumping and/or countervailing duties) of U.S. imports and, if known, an estimate of the percentage of total U.S. imports of Subject Merchandise from the Subject Country accounted for by your firm's(s') imports;
(b) the quantity and value (f.o.b. U.S. port, including antidumping and/or countervailing duties) of U.S. commercial shipments of Subject Merchandise imported from the Subject Country; and
(c) the quantity and value (f.o.b. U.S. port, including antidumping and/or countervailing duties) of U.S. internal consumption/company transfers of Subject Merchandise imported from the Subject Country.
(11) If you are a producer, an exporter, or a trade/business association of producers or exporters of the Subject Merchandise in the Subject Country, provide the following information on your firm's(s') operations on that product during calendar year 2025 (report quantity data in short tons and value data in U.S. dollars, landed and duty-paid at the U.S. port but not including antidumping and/or countervailing duties). If you are a trade/business association, provide the information, on an aggregate basis, for the firms which are members of your association.
(a) Production (quantity) and, if known, an estimate of the percentage of total production of Subject Merchandise in the Subject Country accounted for by your firm's(s') production;
(b) Capacity (quantity) of your firm(s) to produce the Subject Merchandise in the Subject Country (that is, the level of production that your establishment(s) could reasonably have expected to attain during the year, assuming normal operating conditions (using equipment and machinery in place and ready to operate), normal operating levels (hours per week/weeks per year), time for downtime, maintenance, repair, and cleanup, and a typical or representative product mix); and
(c) the quantity and value of your firm's(s') exports to the United States of Subject Merchandise and, if known, an estimate of the percentage of total exports to the United States of Subject Merchandise from the Subject Country accounted for by your firm's(s') exports.
(12) Identify significant changes, if any, in the supply and demand conditions or business cycle for the Domestic Like Product that have occurred in the United States or in the market for the Subject Merchandise in the Subject Country since the Order Dates, and significant changes, if any, that are likely to occur within a reasonably foreseeable time. Supply conditions to consider include technology; production methods; development efforts; ability to increase production (including the shift of production facilities used for other products and the use, cost, or availability of major inputs into production); and factors related to the ability to shift supply among different national markets (including barriers to importation in foreign markets or changes in market demand abroad). Demand conditions to consider include end uses and applications; the existence and availability of substitute products; and the level of competition among the Domestic Like Product produced in the United States, Subject Merchandise produced in the Subject Country, and such merchandise from other countries.
(13) (OPTIONAL) A statement of whether you agree with the above definitions of the Domestic Like Product and Domestic Industry; if you disagree with either or both of these definitions, please explain why and provide alternative definitions.

2026 年 10 月 19 日，澳大利亚国防工业部长帕特·康罗伊 (Pat Conroy) 在悉尼安杜里尔 (Anduril) 工厂的自动海底航行器 Ghost Shark 前向媒体发表讲话。（Saeed Khan / 法新社，盖蒂图片社）
新西兰基督城——澳大利亚军方官员一直对如何使用 Anduril 开发的 Ghost Shark 超大型自主水下航行器（XLAUV）守口如瓶。然而，他们最近揭开了澳大利亚皇家海军正在部署的一些有效载荷的神秘面纱。
10 月 19 日，在澳大利亚悉尼 Anduril 制造中心举行的正式揭幕仪式上，展示了三枚“幽灵鲨”有效载荷。
其中一个是水雷，另一个是一群 Altius-600 徘徊弹药，第三个是后勤补给库。
换句话说：三个有效载荷中的两个包含动能效应器，可以为幽灵鲨提供更大的咬合力。
这意味着一艘 XLAUV 可以秘密部署十几个水雷，也许是在冲突期间的海上咽喉要道。
与此同时，安杜里尔的 Altius 武器可以执行监视和打击任务。
关于补给储备，一位官员表示，“这么说吧，人们可以发挥自己的想象力，想象哪些部队会在部署时使用这些补给储备。”
国防部在一份新闻稿中表示：“这些平台的模块化设计使它们能够操作一系列不同的有效载荷，并根据所需的任务进行定制。”
幽灵鲨正在开发其他有效载荷，可能涉及轻型和重型鱼雷以及电子战。
国防工业部长帕特·康罗伊解释说，“幽灵鲨”可以从集装箱、相对较小的船只的船尾或码头部署。
“这给对手留下了问号，”他说。
由于澳大利亚必须等待数年才能获得核动力潜艇，像“幽灵鲨鱼”这样的自主水下系统可以填补六艘老化的柯林斯级柴电潜艇继续缓慢前进的能力差距。
安杜里尔澳大利亚工厂不到一年前开业，“能够在远离我们海岸执行一系列复杂任务的‘幽灵鲨鱼’现在正以越来越快的速度下线，落入澳大利亚海军手中，”康罗伊说。
堪培拉为其幽灵鲨舰队花费了 17 亿澳元（12 亿美元）。这相当于“数十艘”XLAUV，但澳大利亚并未透露具体数量。
澳大利亚皇家海军还部署了澳大利亚 C2 Robotics 公司生产的小型 Speartooth XLAUV。
海军首席副上将马特·巴克利表示：“就我们的平台本身而言，它们当然必须继续发展，而我们可以安装到像“幽灵鲨”这样的无人舰艇上的模块化有效载荷的发展……为我们创造了巨大的灵活性，并使我们能够使这些系统适应未来的任务和未来的要求。”
他补充道：“我们的目标很明确——我们需要以相关的速度提供能力，加强我们进行水下作战和海底行动的能力，为海上拒止做出贡献，

Australia’s Minister for Defence Industry, Pat Conroy, speaks to the media in front of the autonomous undersea vehicle Ghost Shark at an Anduril facility in Sydney on Oct. 19, 2026. (Saeed Khan / AFP via Getty Images)
CHRISTCHURCH, New Zealand — Australian military officials have been furtive about how they will use Anduril-developed Ghost Shark extra-large autonomous underwater vehicles – or XLAUVs. However, they recently lifted the lid on some payloads the Royal Australian Navy is fielding.
In an official unveiling at Anduril Australia’s manufacturing center in Sydney on Oct. 19, three Ghost Shark payloads were revealed.
One entailed sea mines, another was a swarm of Altius-600 loitering munitions, and the third was logistics supply caches.
In other words: Two of the three payloads comprise kinetic effectors to give the Ghost Shark greater bite.
This means a single XLAUV can clandestinely deploy a dozen sea mines, perhaps in maritime chokepoints during a conflict.
Meanwhile, Anduril’s Altius weapons can perform both surveillance and strike.
Regarding the supply caches, an official said, “Let’s just say, people can use their imagination about the sort of forces that would use these on deployment.”
The Department of Defence said in a press release: “The modular design of these platforms allows them to operate a range of different payloads, customized to the required mission.”
Other payloads are being developed for the Ghost Shark, likely involving lightweight and heavyweight torpedoes, as well as electronic warfare.
Ghost Sharks can deploy from shipping containers, off the stern of relatively small ships or from wharves, Minister for Defence Industry Pat Conroy explained.
“It places question marks in adversaries’ minds,” he said.
With Australia having to wait years for nuclear-powered submarines to arrive, autonomous underwater systems like the Ghost Shark can fill capability gaps as six aging Collins-class diesel-electric submarines continue to plod along.
Anduril Australia opened its factory less than a year ago, and “Ghost Sharks capable of a range of complex missions operating far from our shores are now rolling off the line at an increasing rate into the hands of the Australian navy,” Conroy said.
Canberra is spending A$1.7 billion (US$1.2 billion) on its fleet of Ghost Sharks. This amounts to “dozens and dozens” of XLAUVs, but Australia is not saying how many exactly.
The Royal Australian Navy is also fielding the smaller Speartooth XLAUV from Australian firm C2 Robotics.
Navy Chief Vice Adm. Matt Buckley said: “In terms of our platforms themselves, of course they must continue to evolve, and the evolution of modular payloads that we can fit to uncrewed vessels like the Ghost Shark … creates enormous flexibility for us and allows us to adapt these systems to future missions and future requirements.”
He added: “Our purpose is clear – we need to deliver capability at the speed of relevance, strengthen our ability to conduct undersea warfare and seabed operations, contribute to sea denial and help protect our critical undersea infrastructure.”
The Ghost Shark and its payloads have participated in the past few Maritime Big Play Pacific events, including one in San Diego in October.
The first Ghost Shark was handed over to the Australian Navy for testing and acceptance in early 2026.
Gordon Arthur is an Asia correspondent for Defense News. After a 20-year stint working in Hong Kong, he now resides in New Zealand. He has attended military exercises and defense exhibitions in about 20 countries around the Asia-Pacific region.

content:
日媒报道称，中国大陆科考船数月来在台湾附近海域异常活动，航迹与海底电缆重叠。图为今年4月20日，“同济”号在南中国海执行春季航次任务。 （新华社）
（东京/北京综合讯）日媒报道称，中国大陆科考船数月来在台湾附近海域异常活动，航迹与海底电缆重叠，可能是为台海紧张局势下可能出现的突发事件做准备。
《读卖新闻》星期天（11月1日）引述地理空间情报分析公司ingeniSPACE称，今年5月以来，四艘大陆科考船在台湾附近特定海域多次出现异常活动，包括隶属于大陆自然资源部的“向阳红22”号、上海和福建高校运行的“同济”号和“嘉庚”号，以及一艘在船舶自动识别系统（AIS）中显示为“MUSHANZI”的船只。
数据显示，向阳红22号多次在台湾北部特定海域航行，期间出现减速、停船和不规则变向等行为；嘉庚号在东部海域、MUSHANZI号在南部巴士海峡也出现类似行为；同济号则多次绕台湾本岛航行，并在多个特定地点停船或减速。
ingeniSPACE透过AIS等数据分析发现，这些船舶减速或停船的区域，均与连接台湾及其他海外地区的海底电缆铺设区域重叠，认为大陆船只正在大范围区域内收集海底光缆信息。
《读卖新闻》引述一名台湾官员称，ingeniSPACE的数据和分析与台湾当局了解的情况相符。
日本九州大学教授益尾知佐子分析，大陆船只似乎在为可能出现的台湾冲突或陆美争端做准备。她认为，北京在必要情形下，可能会切断太平洋沿岸海底电缆，以扰乱日本社会并阻碍日美间通讯。
ingeniSPACE首席运营官杰森·王（音译，Jason Wang）则指出，类似行动也在日本和菲律宾附近海域出现，“中方正为第一岛链沿线大片区域可能发生的突发事件做准备，以应对灰色地带的行动”。
针对上述报道，《环球时报》前总编辑胡锡进星期天在微博发文称，台湾海域地处东亚—太平洋数据走廊的关键节点，其周边海缆共24条，包括14条国际线路，连接着日本、美国、新加坡、菲律宾等国，“这些海缆一旦同时断掉或大部分同时断掉，对台湾的影响肯定是‘瘫痪’级的”。
胡锡进说，美日掌握的所有水文资料、海底地形情况以及其他相关信息，中国大陆都应该掌握，“至于我们要用那些资料做什么，我认为它们的作用应该是全面的，其中当然包括支持我们的国防”。

content:
中国A股连续遭重挫后，央行星期一（11月2日）宣布，将推动证券、基金、保险公司互换便利操作，以及将股票回购增持再贷款政策转为长期制度性安排。 （路透社）
中国A股上月连续遭重挫后，央行宣布开展证券、基金、保险公司互换便利操作，股票回购增持再贷款政策则转为长期制度性安排，以支持资本市场健康稳定发展。上证指数星期一（11月2日）上涨1.1%，创下8月27日以来最大单日涨幅。
分析指出，上述政策主要是为加大流动性、托底稳预期，但不太可能复制2024年首次使用上述政策工具后的反弹行情。
中国央行和金融监管总局、中国证监会等部门星期一召开座谈会，研究部署用好用足政策工具的有关工作。央行同日闭市后作出上述宣布。
其中，互换便利操作将于星期二（3日）展开。目前有31家证券、基金公司申报，申请额度超过1000亿元（人民币，约192亿新元）。此外，股票回购增持再贷款政策由阶段性安排转为长期制度性安排，再贷款利率由1.25%降至1%。
中金公司、国泰海通证券、中信证券以及工商银行、建设银行、中信银行等23家证券和基金公司以及26家银行参加了会议。
中国金融监管机构2024年9月首次推出互换便利操作和股票回购增持再贷款两项政策工具，前者通过向证券、基金和保险机构提供流动性，增强入市投资能力；后者则通过低成本贷款，鼓励上市公司回购股票及主要股东增持股份。政策当时推出后，股市随即迎来强劲反弹。
今年6月以来，A股进入震荡期。A股基准指数沪深300指数上月下跌8.5%，创2016年以来最大单月跌幅；上证指数则在10月最后一个交易日收报3599点，时隔一年多再次失守3600点关口；创业板指10月份累计重挫23.02%，创2016年2月以来最大单月跌幅。
股市低迷、信心受挫之际，央行第三次推出上述两项政策工具。中国证监会指出，此次推出的工具扩大了互换便利业务的参与机构范围和资金额度；同时提高上市公司股票回购增持专项再贷款的覆盖率；证监会将引导推出更多权重指数公司、龙头科技股等具有较强市场影响的标志性案例。
受政策预期带动，沪深300指数当日收高0.8%，科创50指数收盘涨幅超过3%。
华侨银行亚洲宏观经济主管谢栋铭告诉《联合早报》，这次重点是降低使用门槛和成本，把已有额度真正用起来，解决现有资本市场支持工具“有额度、但使用不足；有资金、但传导不畅”的问题。
他同时指出，央行可以改善金融机构融资能力，但无法直接消除机构对股票市场下跌的担忧。“机构是否愿意增加股票配置，仍取决于融资成本、预期投资回报、市场波动及自身风险管理要求。”
谢栋铭和香颂资本执行董事沈萌均认为，此轮政策支持不太可能复制2024年的强反弹行情。沈萌认为，相关政策工具可能会达到预期管理和稳定市场情绪的目的，但对股市总体来说是“治标不治本”。
他解释：“如果只是支持资本市场，而没有改善实体经济基本面，就会让市场跟基本面脱节。这也会鼓励更多人短线投机操作，导致整个资本市场基础更加脆弱，陷入恶性循环。”
银河证券原首席经济学家左小蕾也说，中国股市容易受非理性情绪驱动，靠注入资金或许会有短期效应，但更需要长期的资本市场建设，包括提高上市公司的质量和业绩等。“如果没有这种公司给市场提供信心，股民就更容易选择短期套利的方式炒股。”

title: 东京专栏 - 泄露个人信息2.6亿件 日本为什么成网络攻击重灾区？

content:
据日本个人信息保护委员会透露，自2026年4月以来，该委员会接到企业报告的因非法访问而导致的个人信息泄露事件，累计涉及人次约达2.6亿人次，约是日本人口的两倍。根据IBM网络安全部门发布的报告《X-Force威胁情报指数2022》，2021年遭受网络攻击最多的国家是日本，而在新的一轮网络攻击中，日本也是重灾区。

市场调查咨询机构MM综合研究所（总部位于东京都港区）的调查显示，今年1月至9月，因网络攻击导致的信息泄露事件共发生454起，较去年同期的304起增加了49%。截至10月13日，全年累计已达485起，超过2025年全年的432起，创近5年来最高纪录。

9月，共享汽车服务“Times Car”被曝发生信息泄露事件，约660万条会员信息（包括已退会会员）遭到泄露，其中包括驾驶证图像等个人资料；10月，烤肉连锁店“烤肉之王”（焼肉きんぐ）和汉堡连锁店“汉堡王”（Burger King）等企业接连发生数据泄露事件，受影响数据超过1000万条。佐川急便则宣布，最多可能有约5323万条数据外泄，其中包括货物配送运单数据等信息。

野村综合研究所网页10月28日刊登了野村综合研究所研究员木内登英在时事解读专栏发表的文章《日本企业遭受网络攻击的经济损失——补充报告：受害范围从单个企业扩大至社会基础设施 英国政府估算：网络攻击造成的成本相当于GDP的0.5%》，对日本企业遭受网络攻击造成的经济损失进行了进一步分析。

在10月13日发表的专栏中，笔者曾对近年来日本企业遭受网络攻击给日本经济造成的损失进行了估算（专栏：《日本企业遭受网络攻击的经济损失：受害企业销售额减少1542亿日元，GDP损失估计为557亿日元》，2026年10月13日）。

当时，通过企业公开信息和媒体报道，已经能够确认网络攻击对销售额造成影响的，仅限于KADOKAWA、朝日集团控股（Asahi Group Holdings）、ASKUL（雅虎购物旗下企业）和日冷（Nichirei）4家主要企业，因此，相关估算也是以这4家企业的数据为基础进行的。估算结果显示，4家企业销售额减少总计1542.0亿日元，由此推算出的GDP损失额为556.8亿日元。

为什么日本成为网络攻击受害的重灾区，首先是日本在网络安全在世界上属于最差一级的。

TBS电视台2026年10月8日【news23】在网络刊登题为《日本的网络安全水平全球最差”——国际黑客组织Qilin在独家采访中指出日本的脆弱性：如果“失控AI”发动黑客攻击……》的文章指出：国际黑客组织“麒麟”（Qilin）对日本作出了这样的评价：“日本是世界上计算机安全防护最薄弱的国家之一。”

《Courrier Japon》10月18日刊登题为《美国媒体报道：“日本为何成为网络攻击的绝佳目标”》指出：

日本企业和地方自治体频繁遭受网络攻击，个人信息泄露事件接连发生。美国《纽约时报》也关注到这一系列网络攻击，在报道受害情况的同时，对“日本为何成为攻击目标”进行了如下分析。

文章指出日本“网络能力处于世界最低水平”，日本是全球第四大经济体，也是机器人、汽车和电子设备的重要生产国，长期以来一直是黑客眼中的绝佳攻击目标。专家指出，尽管日本是较早引进新技术的国家，但其网络安全基础设施仍处于发展阶段。微软的一份报告显示，2026年，在亚洲地区，日本是遭受网络攻击威胁最频繁的国家之一，仅次于中国台湾。

英国智库国际战略研究所（IISS）于2021年6月28日公布的一份报告也指出，从网络和数字领域的综合实力来看，日本明显落后于其他主要国家，被列入排名最低的第三档国家。报告认为，日本尤其在网络防御领域存在明显滞后。

该报告分析了包括日本、美国和欧洲主要国家，以及中国和东南亚国家在内的15个国家的数字经济与安全保障能力。根据IISS的评估，美国位居第一档；中国、俄罗斯、以色列、英国和法国等国被列入第二档。另一方面，日本则与伊朗、印度、印度尼西亚和朝鲜等国同处第三档。报告指出，日本“在若干领域存在严重的脆弱性”。

根据日本总务省公布的《令和7年度通信利用动向调查》（2026年5月29日公布，调查对象为员工人数100人以上的企业，样本数n=2488），采取某种网络安全应对措施的企业比例达到98.0%。

具体措施的实施比例如下：

在终端设备上安装防病毒程序 82.0%

通过ID和密码进行访问控制 60.4%

在服务器上安装防病毒程序 60.2%

对员工进行安全教育 54.7%

设置或安装防火墙 51.9%

制定信息安全政策 48.2%

为操作系统安装安全补丁 43.5%

记录访问日志 41.0%

虽然98%的企业表示已经采取了某种网络安全措施，但安全补丁的安装和访问日志的记录比例仍只有四成左右。由此可以看出，日本企业的网络安全防护存在一种值得注意的现象：虽然安装了防病毒软件，但在系统更新和安全记录等方面的措施仍很不足，依赖防毒软件自身的功能的较多，常备不懈人为点检的比例较低。

日本的网络安全和防御能力处于较差水平，一方面与日本的网络技术基本处于较为落后的水平之外，另一个就是日本的社会安全系数较高，使人们的防范意识很差，这种“和平天真”也延伸到了网络领域。现在在日本各地，还到处可以看到的无人售货的蔬菜摊床等，菜可以随便拿走，付钱不付钱全靠你的自觉，没有人看管。最近许多商店实行客人自行扫码自助结账，软银株式会社的子公司SB支付服务株式会社面向消费者和商家双方，就2025年自助结账机的使用情况实施了一项问卷调查。调查显示，消费者使用过自助结账机的比例为94.1%；商店引进自助结账机的比例为55.5%。但是在大多数商店里客人究竟是不是把拿到手的商品全部扫码付款似乎很难全面把握，要靠客人的高度自觉。

根据总部设在澳大利亚的国际性智库和平经济研究所（IEP）2026年版《全球和平指数》（Global Peace Index），日本在163个国家和地区中排名第10位，较上一年的第13位上升了3位。在“社会安全与治安”领域，日本在163个国家和地区中排名第4位。

而如今网络已经连接到全世界各个角落的今天，日本人这种极度缺乏预防和防卫意识的状态已经完全不适用了，无论从技术上还是从意识上都需要彻底革新。

title: Taiwanese man arrested in Manila over alleged scam, illegal detention
zh_title: 台湾男子因涉嫌诈骗和非法拘留在马尼拉被捕
summary: 台湾男子因涉嫌诈骗、非法拘禁在马尼拉被捕 - 焦点台湾 台湾男子因涉嫌诈骗、非法拘禁在马尼拉被捕 要启动文字转语音服务，请首先同意以下隐私政策。马尼拉11月2日电（中央社）菲律宾警方称，一名台湾男子因涉嫌非法拘留菲律宾公民并强迫他们进行网络恋爱和电信诈骗而在菲律宾首都被捕。菲律宾国家警察刑事调查和侦查组 (CIDG)
content:
台湾男子因涉嫌诈骗和非法拘留在马尼拉被捕 - 聚焦台湾
台湾男子因涉嫌诈骗和非法拘留在马尼拉被捕
要激活文字转语音服务，请首先同意以下隐私政策。
图片来自Pixabay，仅供说明之用
中新社马尼拉11月2日电 菲律宾警方称，一名台湾男子因涉嫌非法拘禁菲律宾公民并强迫他们进行网络恋爱和电信诈骗而在菲律宾首都被捕。
菲律宾国家警察刑事调查和侦查组（CIDG）表示，在收到一名妇女伴侣的投诉后，警方于10月28日突击搜查了马尼拉马拉特区的一个公寓单元，称她遭到非法限制和虐待。
此次行动营救了三名菲律宾受害者（两名女性和一名男性），并逮捕了一名 32 岁的彭姓台湾男子和一名 38 岁的马来西亚李姓男子。
据刑事调查小组称，两名嫌疑人面临人口贩运、非法拘留和胁迫等指控。
初步调查发现，嫌疑人招募菲律宾国民担任所谓的“虚拟助理”职位，提供月薪400美元至500美元，外加100美元的全勤奖金。
然而，在接受工作后，三名受害者据称从 10 月 23 日起被限制在公寓内，手机被没收。据报道，他们被迫从上午 9 点工作到晚上 9 点。每天，背诵爱情和电信诈骗的剧本。
警方表示，受害者在被转移到菲律宾中部的保和岛之前已获救。
CIDG 表示，警方在突袭中查获了笔记本电脑、手机、身份证和含有可疑诈骗脚本的文件。
据台湾刑侦局驻菲律宾联络官透露，彭来自南投县，有多次诈骗前科，经常前往菲律宾和柬埔寨。
台北驻菲律宾经济文化办事处周一表示，将于周二在万灵节假期后政府办公室重新开放后派人员探访彭，以核实他的身份并监督调查。

Taiwanese man arrested in Manila over alleged scam, illegal detention

Image from Pixabay for illustrative purpose only
Manila, Nov. 2 (CNA) A Taiwanese man has been arrested in the Philippine capital on suspicion of unlawfully detaining Filipino nationals and forcing them to carry out online romance and telecom scams, Philippine police said.
The Philippine National Police Criminal Investigation and Detection Group (CIDG) said officers raided a condominium unit in Manila's Malate district on Oct. 28 after receiving a complaint from a woman's partner that she had been unlawfully confined and abused.
The operation led to the rescue of three Filipino victims -- two women and one man -- and the arrest of a 32-year-old Taiwanese man surnamed Peng (彭) and a 38-year-old Malaysian man surnamed Lee.
The two suspects face charges including human trafficking, illegal detention and coercion, according to the CIDG.
A preliminary investigation found that the suspects recruited Filipino nationals for purported "virtual assistant" positions, offering monthly salaries of US$400-US$500 plus a US$100 attendance bonus.
However, after accepting the jobs, the three victims were allegedly confined in the condominium from Oct. 23, with their mobile phones confiscated. They were reportedly forced to work from 9 a.m. to 9 p.m. each day, memorizing scripts for romance and telecom scams.
Police said the victims were rescued before they could be transferred to Bohol in the central Philippines.
Officers seized laptops, mobile phones, identification cards and documents containing suspected scam scripts during the raid, the CIDG said.
According to Taiwan's Criminal Investigation Bureau liaison officer in the Philippines, Peng is from Nantou County, has multiple prior fraud convictions and frequently traveled to the Philippines and Cambodia.
The Taipei Economic and Cultural Office in the Philippines said Monday it will send personnel to visit Peng on Tuesday, after government offices reopen following the All Souls' Day holiday, to verify his identity and monitor the investigation.

调查显示公众对台湾金融服务信心升至64.1%
要激活文字转语音服务，请首先同意以下隐私政策。
台湾银行金融学院。 CNA档案照片
中新社台北11月2日电 台湾金融学院(TABF)周一表示，最新调查显示，64.1%的受访者对使用金融产品和服务有信心，而大学生越来越多地将投资视为省钱或对冲通胀的一种方式。
TABF 召开新闻发布会，发布两年一度的调查结果，今年的调查结合了公共金融行为的定量调查和探讨大学生如何进行投资的深度访谈。
调查发现，公众对金融产品和服务的信心从2024年的38.9%上升到今年的64.1%。调查还显示，86.5%的受访者可以轻松支付日常家庭开支，而51.6%的受访者有足够的储蓄来支付紧急情况下至少六个月的基本生活费用。
TABF主席雷仲达表示，公众信心的改善得益于人工智能需求的增长、台湾股市创历史新高以及实际GDP的高增长。
在财务风险方面，调查发现，72%的受访者会在紧急情况下向个人储蓄、家人或朋友寻求经济支持，低于之前调查的约80%。与此同时，更多受访者表示将出售股票或共同基金、以保单借款或申请银行贷款，利率分别上升3.8、5.2和10.6个百分点。
TABF管理团队成员郑翰表示，调查结果表明，人们对股票投资风险的警惕性降低，越来越多地将股票视为稳定的收入来源。
他建议人们保持足够的现金储蓄，以支付三到六个月的生活费用，并警告说，市场波动或低迷可能会迫使投资者低价出售股票并蒙受损失。
调查还发现，公众对避免金融诈骗的信心从2024年的65.7%上升到今年的73.8%。然而，70岁及以上的老年人仍然特别脆弱，与其他年龄组相比，他们对使用金融服务的信心较低，电子支付使用年龄也较低。
这张 CNA 档案照片中的一名银行员工协助客户操作 ATM 机（仅供说明）
对于年轻人，程说，许多大学生的投资动机是担心通货膨胀会侵蚀他们银行储蓄的价值，而家人、朋友和在线平台帮助塑造了他们的投资习惯和信心。
调查还警告说，虽然零碎股票交易降低了投资门槛，但它可能会鼓励资本有限的年轻人投资高风险产品。报告称，那些拥有财务安全网的人可能能够在损失后继续投资，而那些没有这种支持的人可能会被迫退出市场。
自 2020 年以来每两年进行一次，今年的调查涵盖了台湾各地 1,070 名 18 岁及以上的人，通过固定电话和手机进行。在 95% 的置信水平下，其误差幅度为正负 3 个百分点。

Public confidence in Taiwan financial services rises to 64.1%: Survey
To activate the text-to-speech service, please first agree to the privacy policy below.
The Taiwan Academy of Banking and Finance. CNA file photo
Taipei, Nov. 2 (CNA) The Taiwan Academy of Banking and Finance (TABF) said Monday that 64.1 percent of respondents to its latest survey expressed confidence in using financial products and services, while university students increasingly viewed investing as a way to save money or hedge against inflation.
TABF held a press conference to release the results of its biennial survey, which this year combined a quantitative survey of public financial behavior with in-depth interviews exploring how university students approach investing.
The survey found that public confidence in financial products and services rose from 38.9 percent in 2024 to 64.1 percent this year. It also showed that 86.5 percent of respondents could comfortably cover their daily household expenses, while 51.6 percent had enough savings to cover at least six months of basic living costs in an emergency.
TABF Chairman Paul Lei (雷仲達) said the improvement in public confidence came amid growing demand for artificial intelligence, record highs on Taiwan's stock market and high real GDP growth.
On financial risks, the survey found that 72 percent of respondents would turn to personal savings, family or friends for financial support in an emergency, down from about 80 percent in previous surveys. Meanwhile, more respondents said they would sell stocks or mutual funds, borrow against insurance policies or take out bank loans, with the rates rising by 3.8, 5.2 and 10.6 percentage points, respectively.
Cheng Han (鄭翰), a member of TABF's management team, said the findings suggested that people are becoming less cautious about the risks of stock investment and increasingly view stocks as a stable source of income.
He advised people to maintain sufficient cash savings to cover three to six months of living expenses, warning that market volatility or a downturn could force investors to sell stocks at low prices and incur losses.
The survey also found that public confidence in avoiding financial scams rose from 65.7 percent in 2024 to 73.8 percent this year. However, people aged 70 and older remained particularly vulnerable, with lower confidence in using financial services and lower rates of electronic payment use age than other age groups.
A bank employee assists a customer in operating an ATM in this CNA file photo for illustrative purposes
Regarding younger people, Cheng said many university students are motivated to invest by concerns that inflation will erode the value of their bank savings, while family, friends and online platforms helped shape their investment habits and confidence.
The survey also cautioned that while fractional-share trading has lowered the barrier to investing, it could encourage young people with limited capital to invest in high-risk products. Those with a financial safety net may be able to continue investing after losses, while those without such support could be forced out of the market, it said.
Conducted every two years since 2020, this year's survey included 1,070 people aged 18 and older across Taiwan, undertaken by phone using landlines and mobile phones. It has a margin of error of plus or minus 3 percentage points at a 95 percent confidence level.
The qualitative research component by Chang Chih-yao (張志堯), head of Shih Hsin University's Department of Social Psychology, involved in-depth interviews with 36 university students aged 19-26 who had actual investment experience.

台湾10月制造业活动扩张但势头放缓 - 焦点台湾
台湾10月制造业活动扩张但势头减弱
要激活文字转语音服务，请首先同意以下隐私政策。
中新社台北11月2日电 中华经济研究院(CIER)周一表示，10月份台湾制造业活动仍处于扩张状态，但由于衡量该行业活动的指数环比下降，包括新订单、生产和就业在内的所有五个主要分项指数均下降，增长动力减弱。
台湾领先的经济智库之一CIER援引数据称，10月份制造业采购经理人指数(PMI)环比下降0.9点至62.5。与此同时，PMI 连续 13 个月保持扩张。
10月份服务业非制造业指数（NMI）也较上月下降1.5点至55.4，但连续第20个月保持扩张状态。
PMI和NMI读数高于50表明扩张，低于50则表明收缩。
CIER表示，10月份，新订单、生产、就业、供应商交货和库存分类指数均较9月份分别下降0.4、0.9、1.3、0.2和1.4点至63.2、64.7、56.3、68.4和60.0点。
CIER 补充称，新订单分类指数连续第二个月下降。
然而，CIER表示，未来六个月商业前景分类指数较9月上升0.3点至10月的61.7，标志着该分类指数连续10个月保持在60以上。
CIER总裁连贤明告诉记者，全球人工智能发展出现放缓迹象，很大程度上是由于缺乏关键零部件，特别是存储芯片和基板，导致交付推迟。
此外，连恩表示，市场密切关注大规模的人工智能投资能否产生足够的回报。
他指出，尽管台湾 10 月份 PMI 较 9 月份有所下降，但这可归因于势头放缓，而不是经济气候逆转。
CIER副院长陈信宏回应连连表示，人工智能和其他行业一样，有起有落。
六大行业中，仅电力电气设备、交通运输设备等行业分类指数上涨，化工/生物、电子/光电、食品/纺织、基础原材料等行业分类指数均下跌。六大产业均在扩张。
CIER表示，虽然第四季度国内消费保持强劲，提振了零售销售和旅游业，但由于全球股市波动，金融业的势头放缓，给10月份更广泛的服务业带来压力。
CIER补充称，10月份，NMI四大分项指数中的三个——商业活动、就业和供应商交付——分别较上月下降3.0、2.3和0.7点至54.7、54.1和56.0，而只有新订单分项指数保持不变。
未来六个月商业前景分类指数也较 9 月下降 1.6 点，至 10 月的 56.2，但连续 10 个月保持扩张。
