摘要 中国的安全目标包括剥夺美国在北极冰层和通往中国本土水域的北部通道上不受挑战的机动自由。中国正在系统地、灵活地利用国家权力工具来获得科学条约成员资格、通过科学任务进入被禁止的区域，并通过海底采矿、商业海底电缆企业和秘密测绘任务获取全面的海底地形数据。中国可能会利用任何情报优势来确保，当它选择冲突时，它的海底存在既技术先进，又拥有对海底地形、传感器阵列、水流和北约/美国战术的广泛了解。中华人民共和国于 2014 年宣布其近北极国家地位，表明中国有意成为该地区的经济和安全存在。科学研究为中国系统性扩展其在北极的业务提供了一种手段，并通过经济机会和科学发现证明了这一点。这些相同的实验和探险为中国的军事冒险创造了机会。中国已迅速采取行动，在北极建立存在，同时进行全球海底勘探和测绘。
对中国进行实验的地点和所涉及设备的性质的分析表明了一种具有直接军事适用性的数据收集模式。中国的目标和战略目标很明确：北极存在、获取资源、使用商业航道以及对地下威胁的预警。科学将为中华人民共和国的探险、测试和海底数据收集扫描提供看似合理、可否认的理由，从而为中华人民共和国提供实现这些战略目标的数据。普拉宁和科普拉表示，自习近平主席于 ​​2014 年宣布中国近北极国家地位以来，中国的官方战略一直是将北极地区视为“‘新型安全领域’或‘战略新疆域’的一部分，预计在不久的将来，大国竞争将在其中扩大。” 2015年颁布的中国国家安全法提升了北极的安全地位，强调了其对中国经济和整体国家安全利益的重要性。 2020 年出版的《军事战略科学》延续了这一趋势，其中中华人民共和国传达了其军队的北极未来。中国战略将极地视为与海底或太空同等的战略地形。此外，北极是“国家利益拓展的主要方向”，中国军队肩负着新的使命。
获得北极的资源和安全存在具有总体战略成果，中国正在努力通过控制北极表面和地下领域（包括海底和位于其上的水下电缆）来确保这一成果。中国正在推进一项安全议程，如果实现，将挑战美国和北约通过白令海峡咽喉要道进入太平洋和北极地区的表面和地下机动走廊并进入北冰洋，同时允许中国进入该走廊。海峡水浅，以及穿越该海峡的船只和水下船只的脆弱性，使其成为通过网络发现和拦截船只的天然咽喉要道

【原文 English Original】
Abstract The PRC’s security goals include denying the United States unchallenged freedom of maneuver under the Arctic ice and the northern approaches to the PRC’s home waters. The PRC is systematically using instruments of national power flexibly to gain access to scientific treaty memberships, enter denied areas via scientific missions, and obtain comprehensive seafloor topographic data through undersea mining, commercial undersea cable ventures, and clandestine mapping missions. The PRC will probably use any intelligence advantage to ensure that, when it chooses conflict, it does so with an undersea presence that is both technologically advanced and informed by extensive knowledge of undersea topography, sensor arrays, currents, and NATO/US tactics. The People’s Republic of China’s declaration of its near-Arctic state status in 2014 signaled the PRC’s intentions to become an economic and security presence in the region. Scientific research provides a means by which the PRC pursues the systematic expansion of its operations in the Arctic, which it justifies by economic opportunity and scientific discovery. These same experiments and expeditions create openings for PRC military ventures. The PRC has moved rapidly to establish a presence in the Arctic, in conjunction with its global seafloor exploration and mapping. An analysis of where the PRC performs experiments and the nature of the equipment involved demonstrates a pattern of data collection with immediate military applicability. The PRC’s goals and strategic objectives are clear: an Arctic presence, access to resources, use of commercial sea lanes, and early warning of subsurface threats. Science will provide the PRC with data to achieve those strategic goals by offering a plausible, deniable rationale for PRC expeditions, tests, and seafloor data-gathering scans. According to Puranen and Kopra, the official PRC strategy since President Xi announced China’s near-Arctic state status in 2014 has been to regard the Arctic region as “part of the ‘new security domains’ (新型安全领域) or “new strategic frontiers” (战略新疆域), in which great power competition was projected to be expanding in the near future .” China’s National Security Law, enacted in 2015, elevated the Arctic’s security status and underscored its importance to China’s economic and overall national security interests . The trend continued with the 2020 publication of The Science of Military Strategy, in which the PRC communicated its military’s Arctic future. Chinese strategy considers the polar regions to be strategic terrain on par with the ocean seabed or space. Further, the Arctic is “the main direction in which national interests are expanding,” with new missions for the Chinese military . Gaining access to resources and a security presence in the Arctic has an overarching strategic outcome that the PRC is working to ensure by mastering the Arctic surface and subsurface domains, including the seabed and the underwater cables that lie on it. The PRC is advancing a security agenda that, if realized, will challenge United States and NATO access to the Pacific Ocean and the Arctic region’s surface and subsurface mobility corridors through the Bering Strait chokepoint and into the Arctic Ocean, while granting the PRC access to the same. The shallow waters of the strait and the vulnerability of ships and underwater vessels traversing the strait make it a natural choke point from which to detect and interdict vessels through a network of underwater sensors, unmanned underwater vehicles, unmanned surface vessels, and emplaced AI-enhanced seafloor weapons systems . Further, by leveraging data gathered by PRC research vessels and PLAN escorts, the PRC can use civil-military fusion to model potential engagement sites and locate vulnerable undersea cables for exploitation. Ultimately, Article 7 of China’s 2017 National Intelligence Law obligates every PRC citizen and research institution to provide information of intelligence value to the state. Data gathered in the name of science is subject to national security requirements, and the PRC uses it to advance in policy, intelligence, and military domains. Scientific Expeditions Translate into Military Strategy and Targeting Opportunities The Bering Strait chokepoint connects the Arctic Ocean and the Bering Sea. Averaging 30 to 50 meters deep with a maximum depth of 390 meters, the 53-mile-wide (44 nautical miles) strait is key terrain for any potential conflict between underwater naval forces in future conflict. Under the United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea (UNCLOS), the data that scientific research collects must be for peaceful purposes. The UNCLOS also specifies that that states must grant permission for research, resource prospecting,, or exploration in their Exclusive Economic Zones (EEZs) or continental shelves. However, the United States rejects this position and conducts military surveys and routine oceanographic data collection. This presents the PRC with a justification for its own surveys and exploration based on United States practice. Unlike the PRC the United States makes its scientific findings available in open-access public databases like the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration web site , and European Union states make their Polar and marine data available through networks like Copernicus or EMODnet . The PRC does not share data and retains its scientific findings behind a civil-military fusion system that classifies scientific data. PRC science survey results are used for territorial disputes and to claim resources in disputed areas. Further, the PRC conducts survey missions with a public justification that doesn’t match actual ship movements or locations . Chinese research vessels conduct surveys off the Alaskan coast inclusive of the U.S. Arctic Extended Continental Shelf, a seabed extending around 200 nautical miles from shore claimed by the United States. In August 2025, five PRC research ships simultaneously conducted research in the U.S. Arctic waters. Embedded in scientific crews are PRC People’s Liberation Army Navy (PLAN) personnel that are part of the ships’ complement . Scientific expeditions are also escorted by PLAN or PRC Coast Guard vessels. The same scientific expeditions that gather oceanographic data and conduct experiments provide the PLAN with opportunities to enhance the operational proficiency needed to employ nuclear submarines and icebreakers to project power in the Arctic Ocean. In 2025, as if to illustrate this point, the PRC deployed three icebreakers on Arctic expeditions. The surveys could provide the PRC with results to aid submarines and unmanned underwater vehicles. Acoustic and radar studies of sea ice can yield data that could inform the military’s AI-enhanced systems for study and planning . Very deep research can also provide the PRC with data to design manned or unmanned submersibles capable of operating at extreme depths. Submarines that operate at extreme depths can take advantage of subsea canyons and seamounts to mask their presence. A PRC expedition to the Gakkel Ridge in the Arctic depths has demonstrated the PRC’s ability to deploy deep-sea crewed submersibles beyond 5,000 meters depth to explore the Arctic seafloor. The deep-sea crewed submersible Fendouzhe conducted 40 dives in parallel with an icebreaker, which ensured the submersible was not trapped under sea ice . The PRC has taken deep dives with the Fendouzhe to greater depths (almost 11,000) in 2020 at Challenger Deep. The 2025 mission was accompanied by another submersible, Jiaolong , and a fleet of five scientific vessels, one of which was an icebreaker. Although exploration of thermal vents was the given explanation for the dives, sonar and cameras were employed to map the region with great detail. Curiously, the PRC science expedition declined to release its data for wider scientific inquiry. This undercuts PRC justifications for its wide-ranging seafloor scanning expeditions and oceanographic survey projects. Again, civil-military fusion shapes how data is retained or released. If there is a strategic military value information will not be shared. Climate Change and Economic Opportunities Will Create Opportunities and Increase Risks Passage through the Bering Strait is normally restricted to open-water travel between May and November, with some variations. Icebreakers can increase access, and the PRC is on an ambitious program of icebreaker construction with Russian assistance. Recent ship passages through the strait are nearly twice those of the prior decade even though monthly ship passages number fewer than ten per month. Although the International Maritime Organization (IMO) Code for Ships Operating in Polar Waters (the Polar Code) came into force in 2018, international signatories are responsible for enforcing it. This is an opening for PRC lawfare and an expanding role for its Coast Guard and PLAN forces. Dominating the Global Seafloor is a Key PRC Strategic Goal PRC efforts to establish control over seafloor resources, including rare earth and strategic mineral nodules, are more advanced than those of other global competitors. The PRC has the world’s largest fleet of civilian research ships, and underwater sensors that gather data on ocean temperatures and salinity and map the seafloor. PRC state-owned firms also control 86,900 square miles of seafloor through five contracts recognized by the United Nations-founded International Seabed Authority (ISA) . Only 31 ISA contracts have been released worldwide, and just 22 contractors have been awarded exploration rights. The PRC has taken its licenses and developed a mapping program with alacrity, systematically mapping areas with hundreds of underwater sensors and buoys. Notably, the PLAN-affiliated mapping ships reportedly regularly stray outside China’s approved waters, with over 94% of such violations occurring at strategic points in the Indian, Pacific, and Arctic Oceans . The PRC should continue surveys outside of legally approved areas, especially where there is seafloor wealth or strategic data, under the cover of economic or science-related experiments or surveys. Scenario One: Undersea Defenses and Irregular Warfare Weapon Systems Will be Employed by PRC Forces in the Arctic The PLA’s “Transparent Ocean” initiative is a strategic initiative that the PRC is using to create and link a five-layered network of early warning systems that span from space (satellites) to the seafloor, with unmanned surface ships, unmanned underwater vehicles, seabed sensors, and AI-enhanced data centers. PRC scientists from Zhejiang University and the China Academy of Sciences, two academic institutions with connections to Arctic projects and the PLA, are working on projects to support this network . Although the South China Sea is the most likely emplacement area for this effort, the Arctic could prove a rich operational environment for data systems. AI-enhanced data systems will collect data, test assumptions, and develop anti-submarine routines that could be transmitted to subsurface, surface, and mine threats capable of swarm operations . One example of climate data that is valuable to military observers embedded in PLA scientific expeditions is the impact of sea ice melt on warming. An Alaskan newspaper reported that changes in Arctic ice melt and freshwater influxes are creating noise that could affect United States military acoustic sensors. Scientific expeditions that gather information about salinity, currents, and undersea topography generate data that AI-intelligentized weapons can use for acoustic, magnetic, and optical targeting. The same techniques the PRC is employing in the Paracel Islands could be used in the Bering Strait or near the Alaskan Aleutian Islands. Seafloor maps would support a future combat scenario in which the PRC, for a short time, could impose losses and delays on forces seeking to use the Bering Strait and its adjoining waters. Still, they may not be able to sustain control of a chokepoint . PLA scientists have conducted oceanographic surveys of the Arctic over the last ten years, accumulating knowledge of the subsea domain that planners could use to site naval mines along likely approaches into the Pacific through the Bering Strait . Chinese maritime doctrine identifies mines as an effective means of denying an adversary freedom of movement and as a form of warfare well-suited to irregular forces or clandestine groups. AI-controlled advanced undersea mines could utilize acoustic signatures gathered by PRC scientific vessels to target military craft and submarines while avoiding attacks against civilian sea lane traffic. A disturbing component of PLAN minelaying is the prospect of civilian cooperation to supplement military assets. Each PLAN regional command has organized militia units for missions, and the PRC 2008 defense white paper explicitly mentions that reserve forces are likely to be involved in mine warfare . PLAN doctrine further confirms the militia’s role in the PLAN Mine Warfare /Mine Counter-Measure journal Sea Mine Warfare and Ship Self-Defense (水雷战与舰船防护), which provides a thirteen-point recommendation for how to employ mines. Among the guidance is the principle of 先制, or “First Control,” through clandestine mine-laying to gain a surprise advantage. Militia vessels could lay mines in areas where seafloor data scanning has confirmed as advantageous by civilian ships modified for this purpose, their unobtrusive shapes eliciting little interest. The exact composition of such units is unknown, but the influential Chinese book Unrestricted Warfare recommends a mix of units to change the tone and predictability of war. In addition, combining various forms of warfare is proposed to disrupt the advantages of a conventionally minded foe. The PRC defines national security as an integration of economic, legal, cyber, and diplomatic power alongside military forces. Utilizing economic (resource), scientific, and guerrilla (unconventional war) capabilities would bring the PRC’s scientifically garnered data into planning, targeting, and early warning plans and preparation . Another system that will likely be used in conjunction with subsurface sensors, mines, and unmanned vehicles is drones capable of Arctic operations. The drone programs that China and Russia are developing benefit from experience gained from Russia’s combat in Ukraine. Although China assists Russia with production and sanctions evasion, the PRC also benefits from its alliance with Russia through its own research and development programs that incorporate Russian lessons learned. China is learning how to use autonomous drones for ISR, logistics, casualty evacuation, and persistent patrol presence. PRC Arctic research can serve dual-use purposes and should be suspected of having direct government links to the PLAN, which may use any information of strategic value. This includes research conducted as part of an international team. The information on ice, sea salinity, and competing naval forces will be useful for China’s Shang 3 (Type 093B) Class Nuclear Attack Submarines, which were built for Arctic use. The data gathered from scientific missions could be used for wargames before submarine operations, or integrated into the research, development, and ultimate deployment of the Shang 3 attack submarine. Knowing the undersea topography and how to operate in areas where US sensors are degraded could provide PRC vessels with a tactical advantage during the open phases of conflict. Scenario Two: Economic ventures and scientific expeditions will become rationale for permanent PLAN and Coast Guard presence in the Arctic The PRC’s 14 th Five-Year Plan calls for significant research into the Arctic and its environment. The Ministry of Science and Technology has established guidelines for funding polar-capable unmanned amphibious vessels, deep-sea polar research projects, and projects directly related to Beijing’s Polar Silk Road ambitions. According to the Science of Military Strategy , the projection of military power towards the Arctic must progress with extreme caution and, at least initially, exploit the legitimate cover provided by military-civil fusion projects . Sensor emplacement could be part of the gradual buildup of military power and early-warning networks for the PRC and the PLAN. Sensors could be positioned during expeditions by unmanned undersea drones or deep-sea submersibles. PRC polar ambitions include integrating Arctic sensors with its BeiDou satellite system, especially those that can provide information on sea ice, navigation, and undersea conditions. The projects also mention “high resolution microwave sounding and aerial remote sensing,” in conjunction with “30 charts for the Northwest Passage and “nautical charts covering more than 80 percent of the Northwest Passage .” The PRC also plans to study and understand how the international conventions and regulations govern Arctic shipping routes. In the course of “building up Arctic expertise,” the PRC plans to form polar cooperation agreements with Arctic states. The PRC has already announced its intention to use the Northwest Passage for commercial traffic. Scientific expedition justifications anchored on claims of information gathering for the benefit of all or the PRC’s economic ambitions are not enough to give the PRC an enduring military presence in the Arctic. However, Coast Guard vessels and icebreakers blur the lines enough to provide the PLAN and PRC planners with information on pressure, temperature, salinity, and currents. At the same time, the PRC builds a submarine force capable of operating in the Arctic. A lack of US icebreakers hinders monitoring and contesting PRC efforts to increase its Arctic presence. The PRC’s deployment of five icebreaking research vessels near Alaska in 2025, including the PRC’s most powerful icebreaker, the Xue Long 2, alongside oceanographic research ships from China’s State Oceanic Administration, a deep-sea submersible deploying vessel, and the long-endurance icebreaker T an Suo San Hao signals the PRC’s intent to establish an enduring presence in the Arctic region. PRC ships have been tracked moving through Russian waters and visiting ports including Murmansk. It is unclear how many new icebreakers the PRC will build;. PRC and Russian designers have reportedly been developing nuclear-powered vessel designs similar to Russian types since 2019. The PRC’s push for nuclear icebreaker development bodes well for powerful ships capable of operating for long periods at sea without being tethered to refueling or resupply. As the PRC builds its fleet through cooperative programs with Russia, the US launch of its Arctic Security Cutter shipbuilding program, following the creation of the 2024 Icebreaker Collaboration Effort (ICE) Pact, promises 11 new Arctic vessels to enhance US maritime security in the Arctic. As of 2026,, the US icebreaker fleet for the Arctic consisted of a rotational group of two aging vessels and a new medium icebreaker. Although the deliveries of Arctic Security Cutters are not scheduled to be complete until 2025, new vessels are projected to begin joining the Arctic patrols by 2028. However, the new icebreakers will also be subject to a dual mission: Arctic icebreakers are programmed for Antarctic missions as well. The PRC’s possession of multiple icebreakers provides it the necessary tools to facilitate scientific exploration and freedom of maneuver in the Arctic year-round. However, the opening the PRC requires to establish a rotating and permanent presence in the Arctic could be the recently signed maritime law memorandum of understanding between the Federal Security Service of Russia and the Chinese Coast Guard. The Chinese Coast Guard could justify its presence as a law-enforcement body ensuring freedom of navigation, while also participating in the occasional naval exercise with Russia. In addition, the European Union’s plans to lay two new cables linking Europe to Asia could provide the PRC with opportunities to assist with the projects or monitor cable deployment while engaging in scientific research. The EU, in a 2026 report, identified new Arctic undersea cable connections as a high-demand initiative for Europe. The EU plans a Far North Fiber cable to link Europe and Japan via the North-West Passage, and a prioritized Polar Connect cable to follow a direct route through the North Pole towards North America and East Asia. Presently, the EU lacks the resources to quickly pursue a cable-laying program and a follow-up support program to have vessels available for repairs that sea ice may necessitate if it cuts cables. The PRC has the vessels to support a program of this magnitude, and if it chooses to lay its own cables, it could use its existing law enforcement agreements to claim rights of protection for its ships . Scenario Three: The PRC will make claims to undersea resources and territory in the Arctic and utilize existing laws and protocols to map the region illegally The PRC’s history of employing lawfare to justify its aggressive measures taken within other states’ maritime domains is well known. Ship movements, ostensibly to find fish or to conduct freedom-of-navigation exercises, have been used to explore training areas and sea lanes. Research vessels have also deployed drones, submersibles, buoys, and sonar to map the seabed and areas of questionable scientific value, despite PRC claims of lawful access under the United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea (UNCLOS). The results of the manipulation of UNCLOS and outright obfuscation of its goals will complicate efforts to prevent the PRC from illegally gaining data that its military can use to plan for future wars. The seafloor is economically strategic, and the resources located on its surface are vital to modern high-technology business. The potential for global power competition to play out on the seafloor is growing as resource concentrations are mapped. The seafloor’s irregular surface can also hide a plethora of irregularities . Mapping it will be the first step toward establishing control and territorial claims that extend beyond state EEZs. Mapping the seafloor and developing a highly detailed understanding of undersea currents, salinity, and temperature is valuable to commercial enterprises as well as future PRC nuclear submarine traffic. When companies employ remote mining vehicles and undersea drones, knowledge of these seabed environments will help determine where and when to commence mining operations. The PRC has invested heavily in the International Seabed Authority, and the US lack of support for the United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea gives the PRC a position to advocate for change in replacing the “outdated maritime order (落后时代的旧海洋规则) with a new one based on multilateralism and equality.” The National Deep Sea Centre (国家深海基地) under the PRC Ministry of Natural Resources (自然资源部) employs claims of scientific research to advance territorial claims, and research vessels have violated EEZs to conduct deep-sea exploration. The PRC uses its membership in international organizations to assert its claims, deny others’, and gain an advantage despite violating the same rules and norms it claims to champion. Taken in that sense, the simple act of planting a flag on the seafloor can be seen as a prelude to asserting authority on an area previously disputed or unclaimed by a sovereign nation . Despite not seeking an active seat at the ISA table, the Trump administration recognizes the economic viability of mining undersea resources. The April 2025 release of Executive Order 14285 declared that the US would develop capabilities in seabed mining , mapping, and deep-sea technology, and create partnerships to challenge PRC seabed mineral resource prospecting. In parallel with prospecting, the possibility of the PRC joining Russia as the second nation to reach the Arctic seabed would give it a claim to the disputed seabed and its mineral wealth. The PRC could leverage an event of this sort to justify its near-Arctic power claim and further justify its determination to gain access to oil and minerals in the Arctic. The pattern of PRC undersea mining and mapping indicates a systemic attempt to identify, exploit, and monopolize resources wherever and whenever possible, especially in areas where states lack the capacity or will to prevent PRC overreach. Scenario Four: PRC undersea drones and surface vessels will tap or cut submarine cables as a prelude to conflict The PRC has an advantage in the number of Chinese-flagged cable-laying ships and their potential to conduct espionage beneath the waves. Companies like the PRC-state-controlled S.B. Submarine Systems repair submarine cables and could clandestinely tap them for information. The same ships are reputedly engaged in questionable practices, such as hiding their locations from radio and satellite tracking services while operating in sensitive areas of the South China Sea. Such ships could aid in seabed cable location and cutting, or, in preparation for conflict, gather intelligence from cables carrying classified US military data. The frequency of PRC vessels implicated in cable incidents in the South China Sea (27 suspected incidents since 2018), serves as warning to PRC intentions for undersea cables in case of conflict. The implications for the US and allies are dire when such incidents are generalized to include the Arctic region. The implications for the US and allies are dire. Limited cable repair ship numbers and availability constrain worldwide cable repair capacity . In addition to anchor-dragging incidents, the PRC has been developing methods to cut cables and tap into them for intelligence purposes. The PRC is suspected of deploying underwater drones to surveil submarine cables and map maritime mobility corridors. Drones discovered in the Philippines are suspected to be tied to the passage of research and PLAN vessels over areas with cables . PRC research vessels have also allegedly employed remote-controlled cable-cutting machines to sever undersea cables at depths of up to 3,500 meters. Although the cable cutting machine is reputedly for oil and gas missions, similar PRC cable cutters have demonstrated the ability to sever 38-inch cables and with-inch pipes in twenty minutes. Underwater cables are the veins that carry the world’s internet and connect the world’s economies, carry classified information, and in the case of conflict, could be among the first targets of warring powers. Natural causes can damage underwater cables, but recently they have been damaged by dragging anchors. Submarines or surface ships could also target them. If cables are mapped before an attack and left unguarded, they are a likely target. The underwater cables in the Arctic and immediately adjoining regions are few in number and could be isolated and cut . Arctic cable cuts could affect communications across multiple regions because of the low density of cable and length of cable lines through the Arctic. Newer cables may also be at risk. The “Polar Connect Cable” will originate in Norway, pass through the North Pole, and continue to Japan, South Korea, and the Asia-Pacific region via the Bering Strait. The 10,000 km distance between Norway and Japan would reduce latency and provide greater network resilience. Another such cable, the 14,000 km-long “Far North Fiber Project,” runs from the Nordic Countries to Japan via Greenland, Canada, Alaska, and the West Coast of the U.S. The cable will run through the Northwest Passage —the sea lane running through the Arctic Archipelago of Canada and south of Greenland. Other submarine cables like the Quintillion are invaluable to the US northern Alaska coast and provide vital data services to the oil industry as well as US military users. A 2025 break in the Quintillion cable, caused by sea ice, cut service to over 20,000 users in western and northwestern Alaska and forced many to rely on satellite internet. In the Arctic, repairs to cables could take months due to sea ice, darkness, and a lack of available repair vessels. Latency slowdowns or complete loss of cable and satellite traffic could be a significant factor in a future conflict. PRC systems can interdict satellite systems, and in the event of a cable cut, the lack of information would be a military and a civil issue that the PRC could exploit. PRC doctrine does not demand the Bering Strait be barred. Holding the strait long enough to delay a US or NATO response could provide the PRC with a window of action in the Pacific. Although cutting a single cable would not stop submarines, it could reduce awareness of PRC teams operating from ground bases in the Arctic while they deploy sensors and targeting technologies. Conclusion The PRC will continue to use science, dual-use research and technologies, and international research agreements to aggregate data that will be militarily impactful for planners, weapons and ship designers, and undersea dominance. PRC scientific research in the Arctic has impacts that span from space to the deepest parts of the oceans. Applying new information and gaining strategic advantage are among the PRC’s goals for the many oceanographic surveys and hydrographic studies conducted in and around the Arctic. As a “strategic height,” the Arctic is being systematically explored, and its secrets incorporated into the PRC’s attempts to gain and maintain an Arctic presence that goes beyond observer status and into active participation with rights to resources and policy decisions. The Arctic region is a strategic window to NATO, Europe, and potential pathways to material wealth. The PRC has announced its goals in its five-year plans, strategic documents, and various economic ventures, revealing an unambiguous plan to master the seabed’s resources and contours. The PRC is preparing resources for surface and subsurface exploitation of the Arctic. The ambitious building programs spanning icebreakers, underwater unmanned vehicles, drones, and unmanned surface vessels show a concerted effort to build upon the data that science has gathered. The PRC is putting sensors in place, uniting its commercial and military capabilities, and ensuring that, when conditions demand preparations for conflict, the data to support operations are readily at hand. The post Trouble is Brewing Under the Ice: The PRC’s Use of Science to Gain Military Advantage in the Arctic appeared first on Small Wars Journal by Arizona State University .

title: After Vucic ouster, Serbia’s weapons-buying habits are under the microscope
zh_title: 武契奇下台后，塞尔维亚的武器购买习惯受到密切关注
summary: 塞尔维亚贝尔格莱德——欧洲主要军火购买国之一塞尔维亚可能会放慢采购速度，并调查近期购买的诚信度，此前学生领导的抗议运动在周日的选举中意外获胜，推翻了该国长期的强人领导人。一个由学生组成的反对塞尔维亚腐败指控的团体在民意调查中以 50 万票的优势击败了亚历山大·武契奇，这表明人们对武契奇长达 12 年且日益独裁的统治感到愤怒。武契奇试图在国际舞台上发挥自己的力量，通过寻求E来与俄罗斯对抗欧盟。
content:
塞尔维亚贝尔格莱德——欧洲主要军火购买国之一塞尔维亚可能会放慢采购速度，并调查近期购买的诚信度，此前学生领导的抗议运动在周日的选举中意外获胜，推翻了该国长期的强人领导人。一个由学生组成的反对塞尔维亚腐败指控的团体在民意调查中以 50 万票的优势击败了亚历山大·武契奇，这表明人们对武契奇长达 12 年且日益独裁的统治感到愤怒。武契奇试图在国际舞台上发挥自己的力量，通过寻求欧盟成员资格和向乌克兰提供武器来与俄罗斯对抗欧盟，但他也拒绝对俄罗斯实施制裁。他还充当中国进入巴尔干地区的桥头堡，与中国公司签署了重大基础设施协议。武契奇在向欧洲和中国进行大规模军购的同时，还购买了12架阵风战机，从法国购买了FK-3和HQ-17A防空系统，以及从北京购买了CH-92和CH-95无人机。塞尔维亚还从以色列购买了赫尔墨斯无人机，并与埃尔比特达成协议，在塞尔维亚组装无人机。据SIPRI称，塞尔维亚2025年在武器采购上花费了约11.2亿欧元，2021-25年期间花费了近36.5亿欧元。 2025 年 9 月 2 日，俄罗斯总统弗拉基米尔·普京（右）与塞尔维亚总统亚历山大·武契奇在北京钓鱼台国宾馆会面。
（Maxim Shemetov/POOL/AFP via Getty Images）一月份，武契奇宣布他将在 18 个月内将塞尔维亚的军事能力提高一倍。但周日，学生们将大学教授作为全国选举的候选人，组建了一个拥有巨大支持但没有指定领导人的政党，导致他在周日被投票下台。 SIPRI 研究员卡塔琳娜·德约基奇 (Katarina Djokic) 告诉《防务新闻》，新政府短期内将继续忙碌，重点是消除武契奇对国内商业和政治的牢牢控制，而国防将进一步推后待办事项清单。 “新政府将有其他优先事项，其中最突出的是落实反腐败政策和重建正常运作的政治机构，这将具有足够的挑战性。在这种情况下，重大国防项目的资源和政治共识可能会减少，”她说。 “可以合理预期的是，未来几年军备支出将会放缓，”她补充道。德约基奇指出，学生名单的宣言谈到了继续发展分层防空和现代化塞尔维亚空军，但她指出，重点是改善人员状况，并承诺加薪。宣言谈到要解决“合格人员短缺”的问题。该文件还表示，将开展一项调查，仔细研究武契奇武器协议的文件，寻找腐败交易。
宣言称：“一个新的委员会正在成立，一个独立的跨部门政府委员会，负责调查武器生产、采购和出口方面的违规行为、滥用职权和腐败行为，作为对前政权合同进行全面审计的一部分。”宣言补充道，“我们将实现国防工业工厂现代化，将其转变为智能工厂，与技术学院合作建立国家军事电子中心，并启动国防软件计划。”新政府可能不太愿意与以色列达成防务协议。宣言中关于外交政策的部分指出，“我们不会遵守

【原文 English Original】
BELGRADE, Serbia — One of Europe’s key arms purchasers, Serbia, is likely to slow down procurement and investigate the probity of recent buys after a student-led protest movement ousted the country’s long-time strongman leader in a surprise election win on Sunday. A group formed by students to battle alleged corruption in Serbia trounced Aleksandar Vucic at the polls by half a million votes, signaling exasperation with Vucic’s 12-year, increasingly authoritarian rule. Vucic sought to punch above his weight on the international stage by playing Russia off against the European Union by seeking EU membership and supplying arms to Ukraine, but also refusing to apply sanctions against Russia. He also acted as a bridgehead into the Balkans for China, signing major infrastructure deals with Chinese firms. Vucic accompanied his outreach to Europe and China with large arms purchases, including buying 12 Rafale jets from France and FK-3 and HQ-17A air defense systems as well as CH-92 and CH-95 drones from Beijing . Serbia also purchased Hermes drones from Israel and struck a deal with Elbit to assemble drones in Serbia. According to SIPRI, Serbia spent around 1.12 billion euros on arms procurement in 2025 and nearly 3.65 billion euros in the period 2021-25. Russian President Vladimir Putin (R) walks with Serbian President Aleksandar Vucic for a meeting at the Diaoyutai State Guesthouse in Beijing on Sept. 2, 2025. (Maxim Shemetov/POOL/AFP via Getty Images) In January, Vucic announced he would double Serbia’s military capabilities within 18 months. But on Sunday, he was voted out of office after students put up their university professors as candidates in a national election, forging a political party with huge support but no named leader. Katarina Djokic, a researcher at SIPRI, told Defense News the new government would stay busy in the short term focusing on expunging Vucic’s firm grip on business and politics at home, with defense pushed further down the to-do list. “The new government will have other priorities — prominently, delivering on anti-corruption policies and reestablishing functioning political institutions, which will be challenging enough. Under such conditions, there could be less resources and less political consensus for major defense projects,” she said. “What could reasonably be expected is a slowdown in armament expenditures in the couple of years to come,” she added. Djokic noted that the Student List’s manifesto talks of continuing to develop its layered air defense and modernizing Serbia’s air force, but she pointed to a stress on improving the lot of personnel, with a pay rise promised. The manifesto talks of remedying a “scarcity of qualified personnel.” The document also says an inquiry will be set up to pore over the paperwork of Vucic’s arms accords looking for corrupt deals. “A new commission is being formed – an independent, interdepartmental government commission for irregularities, abuses and corruption in the production, procurement and export of weapons, as part of a general audit of the previous regime’s contracts,” it states. The manifesto adds, “We will modernize defense industry factories and turn them into smart factories, establish a National Center for Military Electronics in cooperation with technical faculties, and launch a defense software program.” The new government may not be so well disposed to defense deals with Israel. In the manifesto’s section on foreign policy it states, “We will not be complicit in the systematic attempt to destroy the Palestinian people that Israel is carrying out in the Gaza Strip.” Vucic was adept at linking his arms build-up to tensions with neighboring Kosovo , which was formerly a part of Serbia and never acknowledged as an independent state by Serbia. “Depending on the new government’s regional relations, there may be less incentive to use regional tensions and “arms races” as a pretext for ordering more arms, and more advanced arms,” said Djokic. The Student List’s manifesto does however suggests the new government will keep up demands that Kosovo is reintegrated into Serbia. “We will fight for the preservation of Kosovo … as part of Serbia,” it states.

content:
家属发言：政治监禁的代价 zevans@freedom… 2026 年 10 月 29 日星期四 - 00:00 类型观点 页面区块 中国诺贝尔和平奖获得者刘晓波在最后的公开声明中写信给他的妻子：“我在有形的监狱里服刑，而你在无形的心灵监狱里等待。”他的话语反映了一些家庭经常被忽视的痛苦，这些家庭面临着情感上的痛苦、不断增加的法律费用以及对亲人健康和安全的担忧。许多人发现自己被迫扮演陌生的倡导者角色，争取正当程序、探视权，甚至了解有关被单独监禁者的基本信息。对政治犯的声援也必须延伸至遭受这些苦难的家庭。下面，他们用自己的话分享了自己的经历。塔利亚·卡塔克 (Talia Khattak) 是政治犯伊德里斯·卡塔克 (Idris Khattak) 的女儿，伊德里斯·卡塔克 (Idris Khattak) 自 2019 年以来一直在巴基斯坦被拘留，原因是他努力保护该国普什图族少数民族免遭迫害。每天早上我醒来，努力继续我的生活，而每天晚上，持续不断的忧虑又回来了，我的心在下降：我的父亲在一场假审判中被定罪，他正在变老，生病，而且他没有得到他的药物。我躺在床上，无法入睡，想知道他是否感到痛苦，是否知道我们为他而战有多努力。我现在应该照顾他，但我听不到他的声音告诉我一切都会好起来的。
当他应该宠爱他的孙子时，他却被关在牢房里。他独自抚养我和妹妹，而现在，当他最需要我们的时候，我们却无法在他身边。我想念他的故事、他的笑话、他的歌声。他还活着，却又那么遥不可及。没有他的每一天都是我们永远回不去的一天。我祈祷他早日回到我们身边。政治犯 Tsi Conrad 的妻子 Enita Meyeh Yambong Tsi 自 2016 年以来一直在喀麦隆被拘留，原因是他对该国长达十年的英语危机、法语国家政府与英语地区之间的暴力冲突进行了新闻报道。我的丈夫齐·康拉德 (Tsi Conrad) 的入狱让我们一家人的心都碎了。他不是因为犯罪而入狱，而是因为他的良心和记者的工作。自从他被关押在孔登吉中央监狱后，我和我的孩子们被迫离开我们在巴门达曾经幸福的家，流离失所到雅温得，只是为了与他保持亲近。我的孩子们失去了家园、学校和童年。我既成为母亲又成为父亲，承受着分离的创伤，对丈夫生命的持续恐惧，以及让他在监狱里活着所付出的难以承受的代价。每天晚上，我都面对着他空荡荡的床边。每天早上，我的孩子们都会问同样令人心碎的问题：“爸爸回家了吗？”我努力让我们的家人团结在一起，同时看着他们的童年悄然逝去。
他的监狱围墙可能关押着他，但他的监禁却囚禁了我们所有人。 高普，政治犯高全福牧师和庞宇牧师的儿子高全福牧师和庞宇牧师自2025年以来因行使宗教自由和信仰权利而在中国被拘留。我父母的拘留改变了我和我家人的一切。作为他们的儿子，我不得不忍受与抚养我、教导我信仰、并向我展示正直生活意味着什么的两个人分离的痛苦。我每天醒来都想知道他们的安全、健康，以及他们是否要度过余生

Family Members Speak: The Toll of Political Imprisonment zevans@freedom… Thu, 10/29/2026 - 00:00 Type Perspectives Page blocks In his final public statement, Chinese Nobel Peace Prize laureate  Liu Xiaobo wrote to his wife: “I am serving my sentence in a tangible prison, while you wait in the intangible prison of the heart.” His words capture the often-overlooked suffering of families who grapple with emotional anguish, mounting legal fees, and fears for their loved ones’ health and safety. Many find themselves thrust into the unfamiliar role of advocate, fighting for due process, visitation rights, and even basic information about those held incommunicado. Solidarity with political prisoners must also extend to the families who endure these hardships. Below, they share their experiences in their own words. Talia Khattak, daughter of political prisoner  Idris Khattak Idris Khattak has been detained in Pakistan since 2019 in connection with his efforts to defend the country’s Pashtun ethnic minority from persecution. Every morning I wake up and try to carry on with my life, and every night the constant worry returns, and my heart drops: my father was convicted in a fake trial, he is getting old and sick, and he is not receiving his medicine. I lie awake wondering if he is in pain, if he knows how hard we are fighting for him. I should be caring for him now, yet I can’t hear his voice telling me it’s going to be okay.  When he should be spoiling his grandchildren, he is in a prison cell. He raised my sister and me on his own, and now, when he needs us the most, we cannot be there for him. I miss his stories, his jokes, the sound of him singing. He is alive, yet so out of reach. Every day without him is a day we will never get back. I pray he comes back home to us soon. Enita Meyeh Yambong Tsi, wife of political prisoner  Tsi Conrad Tsi Conrad has been detained in Cameroon since 2016 for his journalistic coverage of the country’s decade-long Anglophone crisis, the violent conflict between the Francophone-dominated government and the English-speaking regions. My husband, Tsi Conrad’s imprisonment has shattered the heart of our family. He was not jailed for a crime, but for his conscience and his work as a journalist. Since his detention in Kondengui Central Prison, my children and I have been forced to leave our once-happy home in Bamenda and displaced to Yaoundé, just to remain close to him. My children have lost their home, their school, and their childhood. I have become both mother and father, carrying the trauma of separation, the constant fear for my husband’s life, and the unbearable cost of keeping him alive in prison. Every night, I face his empty side of the bed. Every morning, my children ask the same heartbreaking question, “Is Daddy coming home?” I struggle to hold our family together while watching their childhood slip away. His prison walls may hold him, but his imprisonment has imprisoned us all. Gao Pu, son of political prisoners Pastor  Gao Quanfu and  Pang Yu Pastor Gao Quanfu and Pang Yu have been detained in China since 2025 for exercising their right to religious freedom and belief. My parents’ detention has changed everything for me and my family. As their son, I have had to endure the pain of being separated from the two people who raised me, taught me about faith, and showed me what it means to live with integrity. I wake up each day wondering about their safety, health, and whether they are going to spend the rest of their days in prison. Some of my family members have experienced harassment and intimidation. There has been tremendous fear, emotional strain, uncertainty, and helplessness. Milestones and holidays gatherings have been on pause because they have become reminders of our separation. In the past 17 months, I have experienced the absolute darkest moments of my life. Yet with the unbearable despair, this time has also strengthened my resolve and faith with clarity. For the first time, I understood what “I will go to the ends of the earth for you” meant. I am proud to be my parents’ son and I am becoming the son they raised me to be. One day soon, they will see that. content: 蜂鸟 中国劳工论坛 2013年，中共官媒曾呼吁公众友善对待同性恋者、消除歧视。然而，近年中国性少数的生存空间不断收窄。LGBTQ支援中心、活动、书店、社群媒体帐号及交友应用程式，已接连遭到关闭。中共对LGBTQ权利倡议活动的「零容忍」态度，正日益扩及海外。2026年，甚至有参加泰国骄傲游行的中国性少数者回国后遭警方盘问。中共的镇压不仅针对性少数，也反映了其对一切独立社会组织的恐惧和敌视。 从历史迫害到全面收紧 毛泽东时代，同性恋者被视为「流氓」，文革期间更有人遭到批斗、羞辱和暴力迫害。1970年代后，同性恋者仍可能因「流氓罪」被捕。直到1997年流氓罪废除，同性恋行为才除罪化；2001年，同性恋才被移出中国精神疾病分类。此后，中国逐渐出现同志酒吧、网络社群和民间平权组织。然而，中共始终只容忍有限活动，并对任何可能对其控制权构成哪怕是微小挑战的事物都深感恐惧。 习近平上台后，当局进一步打压。上海骄傲节于2020年停办；2021年，多所高校LGBTQ+学生社团的微信公众号遭封禁；2023年，营运近15年的北京同志中心被迫关闭。 上海骄傲节自2009年开始举办，并于2020年宣布暂停活动。2021年，多所高校的LGBTQ+学生社团微信公众号遭到封禁。2023年，北京同志中心宣布停止营运，这个长期提供社群活动和心理健康资源的民间组织，就此结束近15年的工作。 这些组织并非以反对政府为目标，但其独立运作的性质已触碰中共红线，中共将任何不受其直接控制的事物视为「颠覆」行为。正如工人不能自由组建独立工会、学生缺乏民主组织权利，性少数也被剥夺集体维护自身权益的空间。 中国出生人口持续下降，中共除了加大压力与加强宣传传统婚姻、生育和女性的家庭责任以外，别无他法。国际研究警告，中国人口在未来十年内可能减少6,000万，这意味着劳动人口和消费者数量将减少。性少数以及拒绝传统婚育安排的人，因而更容易成为保守主义攻击的对象。但事实上，人口危机是由中共的资本主义政策所造成的：高昂的住房与育儿成本、就业不稳定、过长工时，以及女性承担的不平等家庭责任。 性少数者的存在，天然地挑战了「男婚女育、各司其职」的传统家庭模式。当政府将人口危机归咎于个人「不愿结婚生育」时，性少数者以及不愿顺从传统婚育安排的人，便成为首当其冲的攻击对象。 中共摧毁了计划经济并恢复了资本主义，从而重振并强力巩固了父权结构，以及在真正的社会主义社会中本不应存在的巨大社会与性别不平等。却试图透过宣扬传统家庭观念维持既有秩序，把社会问题转化为对个人生活方式的指责。 跨性别者一般来说因外貌、性别表达或证件资料而更难隐藏身分，面临校园霸凌、家庭排斥和就业歧视。 北京大学2017年的调查显示，约62%的受访跨性别者有激素治疗需求，但取得安全药物及医疗指导存在重大困难。另有51%希望接受性别重置手术，实际接受者却只有14.8%。 手术费用高昂，相关医疗保障不足，加上家庭反对与制度限制，使工人阶级家庭的跨性别者尤其难以获得所需治疗。 2026年的一项线上调查显示，52.1%的受访者需要在工作中隐藏身分，73.7%曾在校园遭遇负面经历，68.2%有过自伤经历。这些数字揭露了性少数以及跨性别者面对的沉重压力。 当一个人长期遭受歧视、暴力和社会排斥，又缺乏必要医疗与心理支援时，其心理困境绝不能归咎于性别认同本身，而是由于一个压迫性的体制──资本主义，为了牟利和维持「秩序」，而规定了僵化的性别角色。 团结反抗歧视与独裁 中共逐步蚕食性少数的公共空间，使许多人只能选择隐藏身分、避免公开抗争。但没有结社、集会和言论自由，性少数就难以建立持续运作的组织，更难在遭受歧视时获得集体支持。 1969年美国石墙暴动证明，性少数权利并非统治者的恩赐，而是透过群众反抗争取而来。 性少数、女性、工人和学生面对的压迫虽不尽相同，却有共同的斗争需要。右翼指责性少数破坏家庭、女性不愿生育、移工抢走工作，都是煽动分裂，并将制度危机转嫁给弱势群体的手段。 我们主张性少数有权自由建立独立组织，反对一切歧视和暴力，保障平等就业、教育及医疗权利。工人运动、女性运动与性少数运动必须相互支持，共同争取民主权利。 只有透过不受政府和财团控制的群众组织，团结反对中共独裁、资本主义剥削和父权制压迫，才能真正赢得性少数的自由与平等。■ 這篇文章 在中共的压迫与歧视之下LGBTQ+的困境 最早出現於 中国劳工论坛 China Worker 。

title: Gibo snubs China at ADMM-Plus
zh_title: Gibo在ADMM-Plus上冷落中国
source: Rappler 菲律宾（调查/南海/选举）

content:
在东南亚国家联盟（ASEAN）的任何会议中，这只是一场通常可以预见的仪式。当参加东盟防长会议的中国代表在拉普拉普市的麦克坦博览会上走过一小段红地毯时，镜头摇到了菲律宾代表的位置。然后握手并让摄像机快速暂停。不那么常规的是两位代表的级别。对于中国来说，是派驻马尼拉大使馆的武官。对于菲律宾来说，有一位副部长代表该国参加高级官员会议。就在几分钟前，国防部长小吉尔伯托·特奥多罗欢迎 ADMM Plus 合作伙伴的代表——包括级别低于他的副部长——参加会议。这是一个快照（或者也许是一个预演），展示了当一名受到有时好战的邻国马尼拉制裁的菲律宾官员同时担任某个地区集团主席时，可能会出现的尴尬和复杂情况。从快速交换中可以得到很多东西。首先，中国首次仅派出一名武官（无论如何，武官常驻菲律宾）代表中国参加东盟防务外交首屈一指的平台 ADMM。
中国共产党小报《环球时报》是这样描述的：这是“自2010年首届ADMM+会议以来中国在ADMM+中的代表级别最低”，并援引分析人士的话说，“出席率被降级应归咎于菲律宾”。这种冷落并非源自北京。 2026 年 9 月上旬，当被问及中国参加 ADMM-Plus 的情况时，特奥多罗一反常态地腼腆地回答他将如何接待中国同行。当被问及是否有可能不被邀请时，特奥多罗也表现得腼腆。到 2026 年 10 月中旬，特奥多罗承认，中国亲自参加可能会很尴尬。毕竟，中国驻马尼拉大使馆和北京本身都将特奥多罗列为问题。 2026年6月，外交部以特奥多罗及其直系亲属“多次对中国发表不负责任的言论，损害中方正当利益，破坏中菲关系”为由，对特奥多罗及其直系亲属实施制裁。  10月23日，也就是东盟及其伙伴国的国防部长和其他高级官员预计飞往宿务省参加会议的几天前，特奥多罗在新闻发布会上表示，已向中国发出参加会议的邀请。这封信由副部长伊格纳西奥·马德里加签署，他最终对这位武官表示欢迎。 10月26日，特奥多罗表示，他不知道北京是否回复了马德里加的信。
尽管一个国家——无论是东盟成员国还是其任何合作伙伴——必须得到主席或东道主的邀请才能参加这些多边活动，但这些邀请实际上是强制性的。无论双边问题如何，东道国都应该发出邀请。 27日，中国国防部宣布驻马尼拉武官杨雷大校将代表北京驻宿务。特奥多罗可能有无数的理由不欢迎杨。毕竟特奥多罗的级别明显高于高级队长。中国国防部长董军跳过 ADMM-Plus 的可能原因也有很多。但一切都以发生的事情为背景

【原文 English Original】
It was but a bit of drama in what is usually a predictable ritual in any meeting under the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN). As China’s representative to the ASEAN Defense Ministers’ Meeting made his way down a short red carpet walk at the Mactan Expo in Lapu-Lapu City, the camera panned to show the Philippines’ representative. Then a handshake and a quick pause for the cameras.  What was not so routinary were the ranks of the two representatives. For China, it was the defense attaché assigned to the embassy in Manila. For the Philippines, an undersecretary who’s been representing the country in senior officials’ meetings. Just a few minutes ago, no less than Defense Secretary Gilberto Teodoro Jr. welcomed representatives of ADMM’s Plus partners — including deputy ministers ranked below him — to the meeting.   It was a snapshot (or a preview, maybe) of the awkwardness and complications that can happen when a Filipino official sanctioned by Manila’s sometimes belligerent neighbor is also chairperson of a regional bloc.  There are a lot of things to unpack from the quick exchange. First, for the first time, China sent only a defense attaché — who is based in the Philippines anyway — to represent it in ADMM, ASEAN’s premiere platform for defense diplomacy. Chinese Communist Party tabloid Global Times framed it this way: it was the “lowest-level Chinese representation at the ADMM-Plus since its inaugural session in 2010” and that, quoting analysts, the “downgraded attendance is attributable to the Philippines.” The snub didn’t originate from Beijing.  In early September 2026, when asked about China’s participation in the ADMM-Plus, Teodoro was uncharacteristically coy when asked how he’d handle hosting his Chinese counterpart. When pressed if there was a chance they wouldn’t be invited, Teodoro played coy, too.  By mid-October 2026, Teodoro conceded that it could be awkward for China to participate in person. After all, the Chinese embassy in Manila and Beijing itself have tagged Teodoro as a problem. In June 2026, the Ministry of Foreign Affairs imposed sanctions on Teodoro and his immediate family after he supposedly “repeatedly made irresponsible remarks on China, which undermines China’s legitimate interests and sabotages China-Philippines relations.”  On October 23, or just days before defense ministers and other top officials from ASEAN and its partners were expected to fly to Cebu province for the meeting, Teodoro told a press conference that an invitation had been extended to China to participate in the meeting. The letter was signed by Undersecretary Ignacio Madriaga, who would eventually welcome the defense attaché. On October 26, Teodoro said he didn’t know if Beijing had replied to Madriaga’s letter. Although a country — be it an ASEAN member-state or any of its partners — must be invited by the chairman or host to participate in these multilateral events, these invitations are practically compulsory. The host country is expected to extend that invitation, regardless of bilateral issues. By the 27th, China’s Ministry of Defense announced that Senior Captain Yang Lei, the defense attaché to Manila, would represent Beijing in Cebu. There could be a myriad of reasons for Teodoro to skip welcoming Yang. Teodoro is, after all, ranked significantly higher than a senior captain. There are also many possible reasons for Chinese Defense Minister Dong Jun to skip ADMM-Plus. But everything is backdropped by what’s turning out to be the tensest turn yet for Philippine-China ties.  Chinese ambassador Jing Quan was summoned and widely criticized for saying the Philippines should be thankful that China does not use force in its disputes with the Philippines, as he reacted to Teodoro’s insistence that it’s Beijing that’s causing trouble in the region.  “Our functional cooperation must remain rooted in mutual respect and adherence to international law, including the United Nations Charter and the 1982 Convention on the Law of the Sea. ASEAN Member States and Dialogue Partners share the same principles, such as respect for sovereignty and territorial integrity, non-interference in internal affairs, the peaceful settlement of disputes, and the renunciation of the threat or use of force,” said Teodoro at the opening of the meeting. For years, of course, Teodoro has been among the loudest critics of Beijing in the Philippine government. Before China announced sanctions against him, Teodoro warned military and defense officials at the Shangrila Dialogue in Singapore that Beijing was not trustworthy in the context of South China Sea code negotiations.  China claims almost all of the South China Sea. It’s a claim that overlaps with claims of Southeast Asian countries, including the Philippines’.  For Manila, China’s claims have meant facing danger of harassment at sea in certain areas and features. For Beijing, it’s meant danger too — two of its China Coast Guard personnel died in a collision with its own warship, as both were trying to chase a Philippine Coast Guard ship.  – Rappler.com

title: 中共前三季處分105名省部級及以上官員

content: 中國官方媒體披露，僅在今年前三季，遭全國紀檢監察機關處分的幹部就達到68萬人。有評論者形容這是一場「黨內一場大規模運動」。 (Ng Han Guan/AP) 《中國紀檢監察報》本週二（27日）報道，今年前三季度，全國紀檢監察機關共處分68萬人，其中省部級及以上官員105人，平均每月近12人；廳局級官員3680人。 中國中央紀委國家監委此前公佈的數據顯示，2025年全國紀檢監察機關共立案101.2萬件，處分98.3萬人，其中省部級及以上官員69人。今年僅前三季度，受到處分的省部級及以上官員已比去年全年多36人，增幅約52%。 九個月處分百餘名高級官員 山西太原退休人士黃先生當天接受本臺採訪時說，中央今年多次表態，要保持高壓震懾，重點查處政治問題和經濟問題交織的腐敗案件。近期公佈的許多涉案官員已經離休、退休，或退居二線多年。他認為，如今強調終身追責，多少與明年召開中共二十一大有關：“我感覺以後會更多，主要還是當年政治敵人太多了。” 通報顯示，今年1至9月，全國紀檢監察機關共立案80萬件，其中立案調查省部級及以上官員73人、廳局級官員4203人、縣處級人員3.4萬人、鄉科級人員11.4萬人。 上述73人為同期立案調查人數，105人則為同期受處分人數，兩者不一定涉及同一批人員。通報未列出這105人的名單及具體處分情況。 評論指整肅可能進一步擴大 時事評論員胡力任接受本臺採訪時說，他預計，今年最後兩個月，中共黨內的查處行動可能進一步擴大。他認為，習近平強調全面從嚴治黨，除了查處腐敗，也有清查黨內不同意見者的意圖。 胡力任說，一名長期從事中共組織工作的高級官員曾向他透露，此輪處理可能涉及中共系統半數官員。本臺無法獨立核實這一說法。他將此次行動形容為黨內一場大規模運動：“全面是什麼？也就是說要清查所有的人，每一個人都不會放過。” 農村企業人員佔處分七成 在全部68萬名受處分人員中，縣處級人員2.8萬人、鄉科級人員9.2萬人、一般工作人員8.9萬人，農村、企業等其他人員46.7萬人。後者佔總人數約七成。 通報另列出，今年前三季度，紀檢監察機關立案調查現任或原任村黨支部書記、村委會主任7.9萬人。 按處分類型劃分，黨紀處分涉及50.5萬人，政務處分涉及22.2萬人。同一人可同時受到兩類處分，人數存在交叉。 信訪舉報累計超過三百萬 今年1至9月，中國紀檢監察機關共接收信訪舉報350.6萬件次，其中檢舉控告類信訪舉報84.7萬件次，處置問題線索214.9萬件。 同期，中國紀檢監察機關以“四種形態”批評教育和處理138.5萬人次，其中談話提醒、批評教育等佔50.2%，較輕處分及職務調整佔41%，嚴重處分及重大職務調整佔4.7%，涉嫌犯罪、移送司法機關處理的佔4.1%。 通報還稱，紀檢監察機關堅持“受賄行賄一起查”，前三季度對行賄人員立案2.9萬人，移送檢察機關3020人。 這份通報公佈之時，中共二十屆五中全會正在北京舉行。據官方媒體報道，此次會議重點研究全面從嚴治黨問題。習近平在開幕當天就《中共中央關於持之以恆推進全面從嚴治黨若干重大問題的決定（討論稿）》向全會作說明。此前，中共中央政治局討論會議文件時強調，堅持“嚴的基調不動搖”。

title: 国会中期选举结果会影响美国的对华政策吗？

content: 在德克萨斯州休斯顿的西格雷大都会多服务中心，一名女子抵达投票站，这是德克萨斯州中期选举提前投票的第一天。(2026年10月19日) 距离11月3日美国国会中期选举不到一个星期，选举结果将如何影响华盛顿对华政策，受到外界关注。两位前美国情报官员在接受美国之音采访时表示，无论国会控制权是否易手，美国对华政策预计仍将保持总体延续性，但新一届国会可能在对台军售、技术出口管制等具体议题上发挥更大作用。 美国前国防情报局代理局长戴维·谢德(David Shedd)认为，政策延续性的基础，是两党对中国所构成威胁的共同关切。布鲁金斯学会研究员、前白宫国家安全委员会中国事务主任秦江南(Jon Czin)得出了类似结论，但对华盛顿应采取哪些具体政策，他质疑两党究竟有多大共识。 两人的分析指向一个区别：国会可以增加压力、推动立法并质疑行政部门的决定，却未必能够改变一位仍然主导对华关系的总统的政策方向。 “我不认为美国对华政策会出现太大波动，”秦江南在10月22日的采访中说。 谢德在10月27日接受采访时则表示，众议院和参议院“在应对中国所代表的威胁方面，确实存在非常强烈的两党合作趋势”。 都认为政策将延续，但理由不同 特朗普的外交强调与中国国家主席习近平直接接触。白宫将习近平9月对华盛顿的国事访问描述为一次成功的访问，也是推动双边关系发展的机会。 谢德预计，总统将继续寻求与北京进行建设性互动，而国会仍会关注安全威胁。 “就选举而言，我认为总体上还是会保持不变，”他说。 秦江南则更强调特朗普本人对政策的主导作用，以及北京在稀土矿产供应上拥有的筹码。在他看来，无论哪个党赢得国会控制权，这些制约因素都会继续存在。 但他也质疑，对中国的共同担忧是否意味着对具体措施存在共识。他认为，共和党人一直不愿公开挑战特朗普总统较为缓和的对华路线，而民主党内部对于是否应该进一步强化对抗，也存在不同看法。 因此，民主党即使在中期选举中获胜，也不一定会形成要求对华采取更强硬政策的一致立场。 台湾军售是实际检验 两位分析人士都认为，对台军售是国会可能加大施压力度的领域。 谢德预计，两党议员都会继续就一项等待行政当局批准、拟议金额为140亿美元的对台军售方案，向白宫施压。 国会的关切早于此次选举。今年5月，由民主党参议员珍妮·沙欣(Jeanne Shaheen)和共和党参议员汤姆·蒂利斯(Thom Tillis)牵头的跨党派参议员小组，敦促特朗普正式向国会通报这项军售。台湾国防部长顾立雄10月初则表示，华盛顿协助台湾加强防卫能力的承诺并未改变。 “是否推进这项军售方案，最终还是由总统决定，”秦江南说。不过，他预计这方面的压力会增加。 谢德认为，国会加强对台湾的支持，与特朗普寻求同北京保持建设性互动之间，可能存在张力。 中国声称台湾是其领土的一部分，反对美国对台军售。台湾则拒绝接受北京对其主权的主张。 技术限制与知识产权保护 谢德预计，保护敏感技术仍将是两党合作基础尤其牢固的领域。 “我可以告诉你，这是一个两党都非常关注的问题，尤其涉及前沿技术时，”他说。 他预计，国会将推动加强防范知识产权被盗的措施，包括通过立法扩大调查权限。这是他对未来动向的判断，并非下一届国会已经宣布的行动计划。 出口管制是另一个潜在检验。 涉及半导体制造设备及与外国供应方协调管制措施的《硬件技术管制多边协调法案》(Multilateral Alignment of Technology Controls on Hardware Act，简称MATCH法案)，获得了共和党和民主党议员的支持。众议院外交事务委员会今年4月通过了其审议的版本。 秦江南表示，议员可能寻求加强限制，但要获得特朗普支持，可能面临困难。他认为，将相关条款附加到《国防授权法案》(NDAA)等范围更广的立法中，可能是一条推进途径，但强调这只是他的推测。 “我认为，国会要真正迫使特朗普总统改变政策方向，将面临挑战，”他说。 共和党保住国会，也不意味着没有分歧 共和党即使保住两院，也未必能够消除特朗普与部分共和党议员之间的紧张关系。 秦江南表示，关键在于共和党如何解读选举结果。如果共和党人认为特朗普险些使他们丢掉席位，可能会更愿意抵制他的政策；如果他们认为特朗普再次证明了自己的政治号召力，则可能更不愿与他分歧。 谢德则不认为，共和党继续控制国会会改变总统的基本做法。 北京可能关注什么？ 谢德预计，无论国会选举结果如何，习近平都会继续将特朗普视为美国方面的主要对话对象。他认为，削弱美国对台湾的支持，是北京在当前双边关系中的首要目标。 秦江南则认为，中国领导层已经在考虑特朗普任期结束后的局面。如果民主党赢得众议院，可能进一步强化北京的判断，即特朗普在任期最后两年将面临更大的政治制约。 政策是否改变，最明确的证据可能来自选举后的具体决定：对台军售是否推进，技术限制是否得到行政部门支持，以及国会的批评能否转化为行动。 “我认为，对台军售将是一个很有说明力的指标，”秦江南说。 美国之音记者郑裕文对本文有贡献。

|俄罗斯没有给印度尼西亚海上第三极
俄罗斯没有给印度尼西亚第三个海上极点
9 月，普拉博沃·苏比安托 (Prabowo Subianto) 在符拉迪沃斯托克举行的东方经济论坛全体会议上与弗拉基米尔·普京 (在新窗口中打开) 一起发表讲话。 《雅加达邮报》的评论将这次访问（在新窗口中打开）描述为“将俄罗斯作为第三极重新纳入 Bebas-aktif 组合”——bebas-aktif 是印度尼西亚的“自由和积极”外交政策。该专栏认为，利用普京来减少印尼对北京的依赖是“明智的战略”。
但这个第三极是没有根据的，因为俄罗斯依赖中国本身，并接受了北京在南海问题上的程序。
首先，俄罗斯在平衡中国方面处于不利地位，正如最近一篇翻译文章（在新窗口中打开）所指出的那样，它观察到与莫斯科的接触“不会自动平衡其他地方产生的限制”。此外，俄罗斯自身的对外贸易也严重依赖中国。根据卡内基基金会 (Carnegie Endowment) 2025 年 9 月发布的估计，“北京占俄罗斯出口收入的 30% 以上，并提供了俄罗斯 40% 以上的进口收入”。然而，俄罗斯在中国方面的份额“去年仅占出口的3%，进口的5%”——即2024年。
此外，两国政府在全面入侵之前于2022年2月4日发表的联合声明（在新窗口中打开）宣称，加强合作“既不针对第三国，也不受国际环境变化和第三国情况变化的影响”。换句话说，莫斯科和北京事先告诉第三国，他们的选择不会改变俄中合作。
金枪鱼的俄罗斯合作伙伴增加了制裁风险，并使雅加达无法针对中国提供保护。
其次，莫斯科支持北京处理南海争端的程序。普京和习近平于2026年5月20日签署联合声明（在新窗口中打开），表示争端应由直接当事国通过谈判协商解决。双方还坚决反对域外势力插手争端。反过来，中国外交部在 7 月向 14 个国家政府作出的答复（在新窗口中打开）中纪念 2016 年仲裁庭裁决十周年（在新窗口中打开）时也使用了相同的公式。它承诺“通过与直接有关国家谈判协商”解决争端。
翻译家在四月发表的另一篇文章询问（在新窗口中打开）当北京“重新调整自己对纳土纳群岛的态度”时会发生什么。金枪鱼天然气区块位于印度尼西亚纳土纳群岛附近的专属经济区，位于中国也对其九段线以下的海域拥有主权（在新窗口中打开）。 2020年，俄罗斯国家石油公司Zarubezhneft

|Russia gives Indonesia no third pole at sea
Russia gives Indonesia no third pole at sea
Prabowo Subianto spoke beside Vladimir Putin (Opens in new window) in September at the plenary of the Eastern Economic Forum in Vladivostok. Commentary in The Jakarta Post read the visit (Opens in new window) as “putting Russia back into the bebas-aktif mix as a third pole” – bebas-aktif being Indonesia’s “free and active” foreign policy. The same column judged that using Putin to reduce Indonesia’s dependence on Beijing was “sound strategy”.
But this third pole has no grounds, because Russia depends on China itself and has accepted Beijing’s procedure for the South China Sea.
First, Russia is poorly placed to balance China, as a recent Interpreter piece (Opens in new window) suggested when it observed that engagement with Moscow “does not automatically balance the constraints generated elsewhere”. Furthermore, Russia’s own foreign trade has come to depend heavily on China. According to an estimate published by the Carnegie Endowment (Opens in new window) in September 2025, “Beijing accounts for more than 30% of Russia’s export revenues and provides over 40% of its imports”. However, Russia’s share on the Chinese side was “just 3% of exports and 5% of imports last year” – that is, in 2024.
Furthermore, the two governments’ joint statement (Opens in new window) of 4 February 2022, issued before the full-scale invasion, declared that strengthening their cooperation was “neither aimed against third countries nor affected by the changing international environment and circumstantial changes in third countries”. In other words, Moscow and Beijing told third states in advance that their choices would not change Russian–Chinese cooperation.
A Russian partner at Tuna adds sanctions risk and gives Jakarta no protection against China.
Second, Moscow has endorsed Beijing’s procedure for South China Sea disputes. Putin and Xi Jinping signed a joint statement (Opens in new window) on 20 May 2026 in which they stated that the dispute should be resolved through negotiations and consultations between the states directly involved. They also firmly opposed interference in the dispute by forces from outside the region. China’s foreign ministry, in turn, used the same formula in July, in a reply (Opens in new window) to fourteen governments marking ten years since the 2016 tribunal ruling (Opens in new window). It pledged to settle the disputes “through negotiation and consultation with countries directly concerned”.
Another Interpreter piece asked in April (Opens in new window) what would follow when Beijing “recalibrates its own approach to the Natunas”. The Tuna gas block, in Indonesia’s exclusive economic zone off the Natuna Islands, lies in waters that China also claims under its nine-dash line (Opens in new window). In 2020, Zarubezhneft, a Russian state oil company, acquired half of the block (Opens in new window). Then, when a rig arrived on 30 June 2021, a Chinese coast guard vessel came to the scene within days, according to Reuters (Opens in new window).Chinese diplomats demanded by letter that Indonesia stop drilling in what they called Chinese territory.
Nevertheless, Jakarta refused the demand and kept the rig at work until 19 November. Throughout these months, Zarubezhneft held half of the block, with Harbour Energy as operator. Interestingly, Russia appears neither in the Reuters account of the stand-off nor in a 2023 Interpreter piece (Opens in new window) on Jakarta’s quiet handling of it, which records that “Premier Oil [renamed Harbour Energy after its 2021 merger with Chrysaor] successfully completed its exploration”. This absence is a sign that Russian ownership gave the field no protection, since Beijing pressed its claim against a block that was already half Russian.
Today, the block is being revived with the same Russian partner in place. In May 2026, Harbour Energy sold its half (Opens in new window) to Indonesia’s Prime Group, and Zarubezhneft told the deputy energy minister it was ready to resume work in June. Meanwhile, Bloomberg Technoz reported (Opens in new window) in October 2025 that sanctions imposed on the Russian company after 2022 had kept the partners from a final investment decision by making financing difficult. In addition, on 8 October the British government added Zarubezhneft (Opens in new window) to its sanctions list as a Russian government-affiliated entity.
A view reported in the South China Morning Post (Opens in new window) in July held the opposite. On this view, Beijing would probably not put its alignment with Moscow at risk to disrupt “a single offshore energy project”. However, the 2021 stand-off suggests otherwise, since Beijing demanded a halt to the drilling while a Russian state company held half of the block. And if Beijing holds back this time, the reason may well lie in its dispute with the Philippines, which the same report described as Beijing's “existing preoccupation”.
In short, a Russian partner at Tuna adds sanctions risk and gives Jakarta no protection against China. Moreover, Jakarta’s own diplomacy has weakened its position in the North Natuna Sea. Prabowo’s joint statement (Opens in new window) with Xi in November 2024 recorded a “common understanding on joint development in areas of overlapping claims”. The foreign ministry later denied (Opens in new window) that this wording meant recognising the nine-dash line.
Before the partners commit further, the government could establish whether the British listing will cut the field off from finance and insurance. It could also ask whether Zarubezhneft’s nominated oil suppliers would pass a sanctions screening. At the same time, a recent Interpreter piece (Opens in new window) noted that the new foreign minister’s first hearing before Commission I would help clarify “which commitments remain open to review”. That hearing is the place to state on the record that the 2024 joint statement does not cover Tuna.
Radityo Dharmaputra is a lecturer in International Relations at Universitas Airlangga, Surabaya, a PhD candidate at the Johan Skytte Institute of Political Studies, University of Tartu, and currently a Think Visegrad Fellow at the Centre for Eastern Studies (OSW) in Warsaw.

[Investigation No. 731-TA-1047 (Fourth Review)]
United States International Trade Commission.
The Commission hereby gives notice of the scheduling of an expedited review pursuant to the Tariff Act of 1930 (“the Act”) to determine whether revocation of the antidumping duty order on ironing tables and certain parts thereof from China would be likely to lead to continuation or recurrence of material injury within a reasonably foreseeable time.
Alexis Yim (202-708-1446), Office of Investigations, U.S. International Trade Commission, 500 E Street SW, Washington, DC 20436. Hearing-impaired persons can obtain information on this matter by contacting the Commission's TDD terminal on 202-205-1810. Persons with mobility impairments who will need special assistance in gaining access to the Commission should contact the Office of the Secretary at 202-205-2000. General information concerning the Commission may also be obtained by accessing its internet server ( https://www.usitc.gov). The public record for this proceeding may be viewed on the Commission's electronic docket (EDIS) at https://edis.usitc.gov.
Background. —On October 5, 2026, the Commission determined that the domestic interested party group response to its notice of institution (91 FR 40585, July 2, 2026) of the subject five-year review was adequate and that the respondent interested party group response was inadequate. The Commission did not find any other circumstances that would warrant conducting a full review.[1] Accordingly, the Commission determined that it would conduct an expedited review pursuant to section 751(c)(3) of the Act (19 U.S.C. 1675(c)(3)).[2]
For further information concerning the conduct of this review and rules of ( printed page 68558) general application, consult the Commission's Rules of Practice and Procedure, part 201, subparts A and B (19 CFR part 201), and part 207, subparts A, D, E, and F (19 CFR part 207).
Staff report. —A staff report containing information concerning the subject matter of the review has been placed in the nonpublic record, and will be made available to persons on the Administrative Protective Order service list for this review on January 20, 2027. A public version will be issued thereafter, pursuant to § 207.62(d)(4) of the Commission's rules.
Written submissions. —As provided in § 207.62(d) of the Commission's rules, interested parties that are parties to the review and that have provided individually adequate responses to the notice of institution,[3] and any party other than an interested party to the review may file written comments with the Secretary on what determination the Commission should reach in the review. Comments are due on or before 5:15 p.m. on January 27, 2027, and may not contain new factual information. Any person that is neither a party to the five-year review nor an interested party may submit a brief written statement (which shall not contain any new factual information) pertinent to the review by January 27, 2027. However, should the Department of Commerce (“Commerce”) extend the time limit for its completion of the final results of its review, the deadline for comments (which may not contain new factual information) on Commerce's final results is three business days after the issuance of Commerce's results. If comments contain business proprietary information (BPI), they must conform with the requirements of §§ 201.6, 207.3, and 207.7 of the Commission's rules. The Commission's Handbook on Filing Procedures, available on the Commission's website at https://www.usitc.gov/​documents/​handbook_​on_​filing_​procedures.pdf, elaborates upon the Commission's procedures with respect to filings.
In accordance with §§ 201.16(c) and 207.3 of the rules, each document filed by a party to the review must be served on all other parties to the review (as identified by either the public or BPI service list), and a certificate of service must be timely filed. The Secretary will not accept a document for filing without a certificate of service.
Determination. —The Commission has determined this review is extraordinarily complicated and therefore has determined to exercise its authority to extend the review period by up to 90 days pursuant to 19 U.S.C. 1675(c)(5)(B).
Authority: This review is being conducted under authority of title VII of the Tariff Act of 1930; this notice is published pursuant to § 207.62 of the Commission's rules.
By order of the Commission.
Issued: October 27, 2026.
Secretary to the Commission.

content:
资料照片：位于华盛顿的美国司法部总部大楼。(2026年7月27日)
美国司法部星期五(10月30日)宣布，两名男子因串谋充当中华人民共和国政府代理人以及未事先通知司法部长而充当外国政府代理人而分别被判处30个月监禁。
司法部说，40岁的赖立仁(音译，Liren “Ryan” Lai)和39岁的陈元策(Yuance Chen，音译)同意在中国国安部指挥和控制下行动，在美国境内展开秘密情报活动，包括帮助进行“秘密投放”(dead drop)式的现金支付，以换取与美国国家安全相关的信息，并收集与美国军事人员和设施有关的信息，协助从美国军中招募潜在情报人员。
根据法庭文件，赖立仁和陈元策最迟自2021年5月起便开始充当中国国安部的代理人。赖立仁招募了陈元策，起初在陈元策与国安部情报人员之间充当中间人。后来，陈元策开始直接从国安部情报人员那里接收任务。
根据美国政府向法庭提交的量刑备忘录，2022年1月，赖立仁与陈元策促成了一笔约1万美元的秘密现金交付。当时，他们两人在中国境内，与在美国的人员相配合，将一个装有现金的背包放置在加利福尼亚州利弗莫尔市的一处娱乐设施的储物柜内。这种“秘密投放”方式使情报人员能够在无需与接收方直接会面的情况下，完成资金或信息传递。
美国司法部说，被告的非法活动不仅限于协助中国国安部进行隐秘支付。司法部表示，自2022年起，陈元策在赖立仁及国安部情报人员的指使下，搜集有关美国军事设施和人员的情报，这些活动包括：获取位于华盛顿州布雷默顿的吉塞普海军基地的照片，以及在南加州某海军征兵站内拍摄新兵和现役水兵的照片与视频。此外，陈元策还搜集了一名美国海军雇员的个人履历信息，并保存多名被视为潜在情报目标的军事人员的详细个人资料。
2023年3月，赖立仁前来美国，将一部手机交给陈元策，用于与中国国安部秘密联络,陈元策将此称为“国家机密”。此后，陈元策先后于2024年和2025年前往中国，会晤国安部人员，并接受与美国军人有关的更多任务。
美国司法部说，2025年4月，赖立仁再次从中国前来美国，执行中国国安部交办的任务。次月，国安部指示他前往凤凰城，协助完成另一笔约2万美元的秘密现金支付，以推进其情报行动。
“赖立仁和陈元策长期执行旨在损害美国国家安全的阴谋，其方式是在美国境内支持中国的情报活动和招募工作来达到其目的，”美国司法部负责国家安全事务的助理部长约翰·A·艾森伯格(John A. Eisenberg)在星期五的声明中表示，“赖陈两人的这些活动是在中华人民共和国的指示下进行的，其活动范围广泛且肆无忌惮。国家安全司致力于追究任何协助或教唆此类间谍活动的人员的责任。”
加利福尼亚北区联邦检察官克雷格·H·米萨基安(Craig H. Missakian)在声明中说：“世界上有许多国家对我国怀有恶意。今天的判刑应当表明我们的决心：对于任何构成类似威胁的人，我们都将追究其责任。”
联邦调查局(FBI)负责反情报与间谍处的助理局长罗曼·罗扎夫斯基(Roman Rozhavsky)在声明中说：“中国政府渗透我国武装力量的行为，表明其为威胁美国国家安全而不择手段的程度，然而，他们低估了联调局挫败其非法活动并追究其代理人责任的决心。此次判刑应被视为一个明确的警告：如果你企图危害我们的军人、我们的公民或我们的国家的安全，逃脱不掉正义的惩罚。”
陈元策和赖立仁去年6月27日分别在俄勒冈州快乐谷和德克萨斯州休斯顿被捕，联邦大陪审团去年7月1日对他们提出起诉。赖立仁去年12月认罪，陈元策今年2月认罪。
赖立仁和陈元策都是中华人民共和国公民。根据美国司法部之前公布的信息，赖立仁具有美国合法永久居民身份，陈元策2025年4月赴美时持旅游签证。

content:
资料照片：美国众议院中国问题特设委员会主席，共和党联邦众议员约翰·穆勒纳尔(John Moolenaar)，在美国华盛顿大西洋理事会(Atlantic Council)举行的一场讨论会上发表讲话。(2026年2月12日)
美国国会众议院中国问题特设委员会主席约翰·穆勒纳尔(John Moolenaar)星期五(10月30日)发表声明，呼吁中国共产党释放中国所有的政治犯。
10月30日是国际政治犯日(International Day of Political Prisoners)。这是一个旨在声援全球因行使基本权利、表达和平信念、新闻报道或政治异见而遭受不公正监禁的政治犯的特殊日子。
“黄之锋、黎智英、陈友麟博士、敏辛、高全福牧师、古尔仙·阿巴斯(Gulshan Abbas)医生以及其他无数人的悲惨案例，充分体现了中国共产党如何利用任意拘留、非法监禁和集体惩罚作为政治筹码去压制那些为自由而奋斗的人们，”穆勒纳尔在声明中指出。
黄之锋是香港知名民主派活动人士，黎智英是香港壹传媒及《苹果日报》创始人，两人都是推动香港民主、自由和法制的知名人物；陈友麟是研究朝鲜核试验地震信号的美国地震学家；敏辛是美籍缅甸裔学者；高全福是遭中共取缔的西安市锡安之光教会牧师；古尔仙·阿巴斯则是一位维吾尔族退休医生。这些被穆勒纳尔提及的政治犯目前都被中国当局以各种罪名投入监狱。
美国及其西方盟友此前曾一再呼吁北京当局释放这些被中国拘押的政治犯。
“今天，我们向所有挺身反抗中共威权统治、却因此身陷囹圄的异见人士所展现出的勇气与胆识致敬，”穆勒纳尔在声明中指出。
美国众议院中国问题特设委员会于2023年1月设立，这是一个没有直接立法权的跨党派常设委员会，核心职能是调查、研究并向国会一个常设委员会提出有关美中战略竞争的政策建议，委员会经常聚焦美中安全、经济和人权等一系列议题。
现任委员会主席穆勒纳尔是来自密歇根州的一位共和党籍联邦众议员。
“我们必须铭记，这些人之所以被中国当局监禁，仅仅是因为他们坚信自由与民主，”穆勒纳尔在声明中表示。“我再次呼吁中国共产党释放所有政治犯。”
香港天安门烛光悼念活动三组织者遭重判；美议员：“与香港的政治犯站在一起，并呼吁立即释放他们”

content:
资料照片：位于首都华盛顿的美国联邦通信委员会(FCC)总部的主要入口。(2021年5月)
美国计划以国家安全为由，在近期作出禁止中国电信企业直接获取美国电话号码的决定，此举同时可以防范烦恼美国用户的与诈骗相关的自动拨号语音电话(robocalls)，而中国政府则对此表示反对。
美国联邦通信委员会(FCC)星期四(10月29日)表示，将于11月19日就一项禁止中国移动、中国电信、中国联通以及其他提供IP通信服务的中国企业直接获取美国电话号码的提案进行表决。
“通过这一决定，联邦通信委员会将加强我们抵御恶意行为者和非法自动语音电话拨打者的第一道防线，”美国联邦通信委员会主席布伦丹·卡尔(Brendan Carr)在一份声明中指出。
“互联网语音通话”(VoIP)是把语音转换为数字数据并通过宽带连接进行传输的一项被普遍使用的技术。
路透社指出，对于提供“互联网语音通话”的电信公司而言，“直接接入”是一种成本低得多的选择，也让它们更容易提供各类高级功能。
除了考虑禁止中国电信公司直接获取美国电话号码外，美国联邦通信委员会星期四还表示，正计划禁止那些使用被列入该机构“国家安全风险清单”企业相关设备的IP语音服务提供商开展服务。
美国联邦通信委员会还打算于2028年12月起，禁止所有中国实验室对美国智能手机等电子产品进行测试，理由是国家安全和知识产权保护方面的担忧。此外，对于被认定构成国家安全风险的中国企业，该机构还可能撤销其直接号码使用授权。
此前，美国联邦通信委员会已经下令禁止中国移动、中国电信和中国联通等电信公司向美国提供国际电信服务。
路透社指出，其他正在考虑的措施还包括直接禁止这些中国企业进入美国网络，同时禁止它们在美国境内运营数据中心。
中国政府对美国联邦通信委员会可能及即将实施的禁令表示反对。
“美方泛化国家安全概念，滥用国家力量无理打压中国企业，中方对此表示反对、强烈不满，”中国外交部发言人郭嘉昆在星期五举行的例行记者会上说。
郭嘉昆还表示，北京将“采取必要措施”，“坚定维护自身正当合法权益”。
近年来，由于与中国相关的黑客和网络窃密活动频繁，美国及其盟友担心中国窃取各自的电信数据和渗透各自的基础设施，因为这些活动可能会引发间谍活动和其他破坏性后果。
2024年下半年，华盛顿指控一个名为“盐台风”(Salt Typhoon)由中国政府支持的网络间谍组织窃取了美国消费者的通话记录及美国通话数据，并渗透进美国的电信企业和电信基础设施公司。
美国联邦调查局(FBI)今年表示，来自“盐台风”的威胁“依然十分严峻且持续存在”。
路透社说，美国联邦通信委员会今年7月将总部位于美国加州的“数字系统技术公司”(Digitalsystem Technology)列入“对美国国家安全构成风险的企业名单”，理由是该公司与中国电信企业存在关联，而且由中国公民拥有。
美众院中国问题特设委员会：中国电信企业在美监管牌照被吊销后仍留驻美国网络基础设施

title: 中国辽宁号航母打击群及大量船只在台湾东部海域活动，美智库：或演练突破第一岛链
source: 美国之音中文网 您可靠的信息来源
summary: 资料照片：美国海军公布的照片显示，两位美国海军中校罗伯特·J·布里格斯与理查德·D·斯莱2021年4月4日在阿利·伯克级导弹驱逐舰“马斯廷号”驾驶舱进行水面接触观察。照片中可见中国“辽宁号”航空母舰及其舷号。 在美国和日本举行利剑-27演习后，台湾官员说，包括辽宁号航母编队在内，超过50艘中国海军、海警和其他船只在台湾东部海域活动，对日本、台湾到菲律宾的所谓第一岛链构成威胁极其明显，台湾对此保持高度警戒。有美国智库说，解放军可能在演练未来冲突时将台湾或菲律宾孤立以突破第一岛链
content:
资料照片：美国海军公布的照片显示，两位美国海军中校罗伯特·J·布里格斯与理查德·D·斯莱2021年4月4日在阿利·伯克级导弹驱逐舰“马斯廷号”驾驶舱进行水面接触观察。照片中可见中国“辽宁号”航空母舰及其舷号。
在美国和日本举行利剑-27演习后，台湾官员说，包括辽宁号航母编队在内，超过50艘中国海军、海警和其他船只在台湾东部海域活动，对日本、台湾到菲律宾的所谓第一岛链构成威胁极其明显，台湾对此保持高度警戒。有美国智库说，解放军可能在演练未来冲突时将台湾或菲律宾孤立以突破第一岛链的行动。
台湾总统府国安会秘书长吴钊燮星期三(10月28日)在其社交媒体平台X帐号上贴文说，解放军派遣包括辽宁号打击群编队在内的船只在第一岛链东部海域演习，“我们对他们的活动保持警戒。这些活动对台湾、日本和菲律宾同时做出威胁非常明显。”
贴文也附上一张地图，显示解放军东部、北部、南部战区军舰编队、辽宁号航母打击群、中国海警、海事局及科考船等船只，在日本南部、台湾北部、东部、西南部，一路到菲律宾东、西部海域共53艘船只的分布情形，其中有34艘是军舰。
台湾国防部长顾立雄同日在立法院接受媒体联防时表示，台湾与盟友分享情资，对辽宁号及其他中国船只在台湾周边的动向都有充分掌握。
“我们当然都充分掌握辽宁号及其他各舰队、甚至公务船还有海警船等相关动态。我们不但透过联合情监侦手段，也跟友盟交换情资，所以我们都有事先掌握。那共军的军舰在这些区域的活动，我们不乐意看到它有任何要来展现威慑的企图，来影响印太区域和平稳定。”
日本自卫队在美日两年一度的联合利剑演习前发现辽宁行航母及打击群编队的踪迹。
10月14日，中国战机从辽宁号航母起飞，在台湾附近石垣岛以南约250公里处，日本紧急出动战斗机进行拦截。日本军舰和巡逻机还对从冲绳和宫古岛之间驶入太平洋的中国航母编队进行了监视。
美国智库战争研究所(ISW)与美国企业研究所(AEI)共同编写的《中国与台湾及时更新》(China and Taiwan Update)期刊，星期二在最新一期题为“中华人民共和国的军事胁迫”的文章中，刊出了辽宁号航母打击群在联合利剑演习期间的轨迹图。
轨迹图列出了10月15日日本自卫队发现辽宁号从吕宋海峡航向南中国海，一直到10月27日从卫星图见到辽宁号和打击群出现在距吕宋岛东岸500公里朝东南方航行，期间辽宁号打击群10月22日被发现位于菲律宾西南部的巴西兰海峡北边；而菲律宾武装部队也证实，辽宁号打击群10月26日行经巴西兰海峡往东朝菲律宾海航行。
“辽宁号航经巴西兰海峡是不寻常的，而且它在菲律宾海域的地点可能是中华人民共和国用来恫吓菲律宾的一个更广泛的努力。”文章说，中国可能是在加大对菲律宾的军事压力，让马尼拉为拒绝接受中国对南中国海的主权声索付出代价。解放军也可能在演练重要行动，以便在未来的冲突中将菲律宾隔绝。
文章称，辽宁号的动向可能是在“模拟突破通往太平洋的第一岛链”；辽宁号也可能在演练在一个可能的冲突中将菲律宾或台湾孤立。
文章指出，辽宁号及其护航舰艇是一支重要力量，其中055号导弹巡洋舰是解放军海军最顶级的水面战舰，而辽宁号编入了中国10艘055型战舰其中的2艘，具备强大的区域防空和反水面作战能力。
“解放军海军可以利用这支力量或类似编队来切断连接太平洋的咽喉，将南中国海隔绝起来。中华人民共和国也可以在冲突时利用菲律宾周边各种水道，像是巴西兰海峡，绕过第一岛链。这将使中国海军得以避开位于台湾与菲律宾之间的吕宋海峡，”文章说。
“台湾的反舰作战能力可用来将解放军海军限制在第一岛链内，这正是中华人民共和国极力想避免的，”文章说，控制巴西兰海峡或其他菲律宾周边水道，就能让中国海军在冲突时更有效孤立台湾。解放军可能寻求使其海军力量在重要水道的部署常态化，以便在台海冲突发生时执行这种行动。
对于辽宁号航母及其他中国军舰的动向，中国国防部发言人张晓刚星期四在国防部每月例行记者会上表示，辽宁号航母编队赴西太平洋相关海域开展训练，是中国军队组织的年度例行训练，“旨在检验和提升航母编队远海实战能力”，不针对特定国家和目标，符合国际法和国际实践。
中国视台湾为其领土一部分，从未放弃通过武力实现统一，自2022年开始不更断加大海警对台湾的海上施压；中国军舰、海警、科考及公务船在台湾周边水域的侵扰行动也日益增加。
上星期，中国骤然升级施压行动，台湾海巡署发现中国船只在台湾周边和离岛活动的“数量异常增加”，16艘中国海警、科考及渔船编队同时出现在台湾东部、南部、西南方外海及普拉塔斯群岛(Pratas Islands，台湾称东沙群岛)，并称此外对台湾的“多点齐发”及混合战；台北谴责北京意图通过此一“假执法、真扩权”手段片面改变台海现状、制造对台湾具有管辖权的假象。
张晓刚在记者会上也针对此事回应说，台湾是中国的一部分，中国相关部门在台湾以东的“中国管辖海域”开展正常活动完全正当合法，无可非议。
另外，有关美国太平洋陆军司令罗纳德·克拉克(Ronald Clark)将军星期二在夏威夷一个会议上发表演讲时称，中国解放军可能在2027年具备武力攻台能力的所谓“戴维森窗口”威胁依然存在，美军已对印太战区可能发生战争做好准备；台湾防长顾立雄星期四也对此表示，北京当局从未放弃武力“并吞”台湾的企图，台湾军方将做好战备整备一事，张晓刚则表示：“何时、以何种方式解决台湾问题，完全是中国人自己的事，外部势力无权干涉。”

content:
香港宏福苑大火调查报告公开后，特首李家超和其他官员在新闻发布会上鞠躬道歉。(2026年10月29日)
香港大埔宏福苑导致168人死亡的灾难大火发生近一年后，独立委员会的调查报告在星期四(10月29日)公布，点名多个港府部门失职，并提出改革措施。以特首李家超为首的特区政府官员公开鞠躬道歉。但受灾民众表示，有担当的政府不会在事发一年后才出来道歉。
香港行政长官李家超星期四率领相关司局长举行记者会，交代宏福苑火灾独立委员会提交的报告。李家超表示，大火造成168人死亡，影响近2000个家庭，他代表港府向灾民及广大市民道歉，与在场的七名官员鞠躬道歉。
调查报告点名房屋局独立审查组、屋宇署、消防处和劳工处失职。
李家超说，考虑到宏福苑是房屋局辖下房屋署独立审查组的管辖范围，虽然火灾不涉及房屋局局长何永贤个人犯错，但认为何永贤应承担政治责任，他已接受何永贤提出的请辞，并即时停止其职务，也已报请中国中央免除何永贤的职务。
对于四个部门失职，却只有一名局长下台，李家超解释，自己最重要的责任是带领政府解决问题。
李家超说：“在我自我检讨的过程中，我考虑到政府需要推行大量改革工作，未来也有大量工作要落实，作为政府第一责任人，其中一个最重要责任是要带领政府直视问题、解决问题，落实未来大量工作。”
杨先生是宏福苑其中一座大楼宏志阁的居民。他对美国之音表示，绝对不会接受李家超和一众高官的道歉。
杨先生说：“作为一个有担当的政府，不会在(事发)一年后才出来道歉。就好比有人一口咬定自己没错，只不过现在证据确凿，只好勉为其难出来鞠躬。。。他们只是必须做(鞠躬道歉)，而不是他们希望去做，选择去做。我不认为在没有选择情况下作出的举动是真心实意的。”
台湾香港协会理事长桑普认为，港府的做法是“刑不上司长、刑不上特首”。
“这种方法肯定是要呼应，要满足社会上怒吼的声音。一定要有人来负责，所以它要为社会消气。明摆着，独立委员会的调查报告指出了四个港府部门都有行政上的责任，甚至政治上的责任，那为什么只处分一个何永贤。‘刑不上司长、刑不上特首’。四个局长也是四挑一。其他人就请他们吸取教训，好好改革。既然何永贤辞职了，那李家超又要不要辞职呢？”
今年4月，中国中央港澳办主任、国务院港澳办主任夏宝龙公开表示，大埔火灾发生后，“一些别有用心的人把灾情政治化，妄图以灾乱港。”
身在美国的香港前民主派立法会议员单仲偕对美国之音表示，他相信，宏福苑事件被淡化处理与北京介入有关。
单仲偕说：“自从夏宝龙发表讲话后，每当有人就宏福苑事件多说几句，都会受到调查。(当局)刻意要把所有批评此事的人噤声。这次只有一名局长辞职，相信都是为了配合夏宝龙。假如连一个官员都无须问责，只会激起更强烈的议论。另一原因是，政府希望在下届特首选举之前，匆匆了事。”
宏福苑受灾居民杨先生说，过去近一年，特区政府官员对独立委员会的调查采取不合作态度，不同部门不断派人滋扰宏福苑居民，甚至透过网路群组攻击、恐吓居民。
2025年11月26日，当时正在进行大型维修的宏福苑，八幢大楼中有七幢被焚毁，香港消防当局出动超过200辆消防车、1200多名消防人员，这场大火依然烧了一整夜才受控，造成168人死亡。宏福苑逾1980户居民失去家园。至今逾4000名居民四散在不同地区的应急安置处。
去年12月，香港特首李家超成立委员会调查大火成因及提出建议，委员会取得逾百万份档案，其后举行30场听证会。
独立委员会提交的报告指责工程顾问“鸿毅”和承建商“宏业”无视投诉及安全隐患，是大火的罪魁祸首，连同其他做“橡皮图章”的专业人士持续欺瞒各规管部门，应受最严厉谴责。
这起灾难再次让公众关注香港楼宇招标工程时，承建商存在围标及反竞争的不当行为。港府29日宣布，计划修订多条法例，包括把大型楼宇维修工程围标行为刑事化。日后执法部门可行使传召问话、冻结资产等权力。
香港前立法会议员单仲偕回忆说，围标问题早已引起政界重视，无奈反送中运动导致港府搁置打击围标。这方面现任保安局局长邓炳强责无旁贷。
单仲偕说：“在（2019年）反送中运动之前，当时的香港立法会曾就反围标进行严肃讨论并制定相关议案，期望政府跟进。反送中运动发生后，港府把所有的精力、资源用于扫荡它们所指的‘黑暴运动’。保安局没有处理黑社会渗入围标事件。邓炳强是当时的警务处处长。两件事情均由他负责。谈到政治责任他是无法推卸的，但北京当然不会惩处大力执行国安路线的官员。”
港府就独立委员会调查报告提出多项改革的同时，香港时评人桑普却认为，报告根本未能掌握宏福苑悲剧的核心。
桑普说：“(宏福苑事件)表面上是失职。(报告)讲到，承包商和顾问公司不及格、不专业、监管不力，但是(报告)隐瞒了非常重要的事情：贪腐。。。专制独裁、没有民主法治自由，必然滋生贪腐。贪腐也必然滋生失职。(报告)不提贪腐是完全荒谬的。更重要的是，那些灾民怎么办？他们有合理赔偿吗？”
