summary: 朝中社图片 俄罗斯和朝鲜本周进行了弹道导弹发射，根据俄罗斯国防部周三发布的消息，俄罗斯从西太平洋向俄罗斯北极地区发射了潜射弹道导弹（SLBM），而朝鲜则发射了短程弹道导弹（SRBM），作为朝鲜领导人金正恩在无人机技术展览期间进行火力演示的一部分。核动力弹道导弹潜艇 (SSBN) RFS Generalissimus Suvorov (K-553)，分配给
content:
朝中社图片 俄罗斯和朝鲜本周进行了弹道导弹发射，根据俄罗斯国防部周三发布的消息，俄罗斯从西太平洋向俄罗斯北极地区发射了潜射弹道导弹（SLBM），而朝鲜则发射了短程弹道导弹（SRBM），作为朝鲜领导人金正恩在无人机技术展览期间进行火力演示的一部分。隶属于俄罗斯海军太平洋舰队的核动力弹道导弹潜艇（SSBN）RFS Generalissimus Suvorov（K-553）在俄罗斯西北部阿尔汉格尔斯克地区的奇扎试验场从鄂霍次克海发射了一枚RSM-56“布拉瓦”潜射弹道导弹。俄罗斯国防部周三表示：“苏沃洛夫大元帅号战略核动力弹道导弹潜艇按照作战训练计划发射了布拉瓦洲际弹道导弹。”导弹从水下位置发射，导弹弹头在预计时间成功到达指定区域。俄罗斯国防部还发布了官方媒体塔斯社转载的发射视频。尽管针对 10 月 25 日至 31 日期间进行的导弹活动发出了国际航行警告，但俄罗斯国防部并未说明发射时间。
据美国海军学院新闻报道，俄罗斯在 10 月至 11 月期间定期从俄罗斯远东地区进行潜射弹道导弹发射，苏沃洛夫大元帅于 2022 年 11 月 3 日发射了“布拉瓦”导弹，并于当年 12 月 29 日投入使用。俄罗斯上一次通过弹道导弹核潜艇发射潜射弹道导弹是在今年 5 月 21 日，当时一艘水下的 Delta IV 级弹道导弹核潜艇发射了一枚 R-29RMU Sineva 潜射弹道导弹，作为其战略核力量演习的一部分。今年仅公开披露过两次潜射弹道导弹发射，中国于 7 月从南海向南太平洋发射了一次潜射弹道导弹，法国于 10 月初进行了一次发射，从法国菲尼斯泰尔海岸向北大西洋偏远地区发射了一枚潜射弹道导弹。与俄罗斯的潜射弹道导弹在本国领土着陆和法国的潜射弹道导弹在距海岸线数百公里的北大西洋着陆不同，中国因将该地区用作潜射弹道导弹试验场而受到南太平洋岛国和其他国家的批评。朝鲜周四发射了 KN-25 600 毫米多管火箭弹（属于短程弹道导弹），作为朝鲜领导人金正恩出席的无人机技术展览期间火力演示的一部分。韩国参谋长联席会议周四表示，朝鲜于中午 12 点 30 分从元山向日本海发射了 10 枚短程弹道导弹（SRBM）。当地时间，联合参谋长联席会议还表示，短程弹道导弹的飞行距离为250公里。
日本防卫省周四报道称，朝鲜当天中午12点36分发射了一枚弹道导弹，估计弹道导弹落在朝鲜半岛东海岸附近。 JSC 和 MOD 均表示，美国、日本和韩国正在共享信息并分析此次发射。与此同时，美国太平洋司令部在声明中称发射的弹道导弹数量为两枚。周五，官方媒体朝中社报道称，金正恩周四参观了“2026年无人机技术发展”展览，该展览展示了朝鲜的无人机能力

【原文 English Original】
KCNA image Russia and North Korea carried out ballistic missile launches this week with Russia conducting a launch of a Submarine-Launched Ballistic Missile (SLBM) from the Western Pacific to Russia arctic region, according to a Russian Ministry of Defence (MOD) release on Wednesday while North Korea carried out launches of Short-Range Ballistic Missiles (SRBMs) as part of a firepower demonstration for North Korea leader Kim Jong Un during an exhibition of unmanned aerial vehicle technology. Nuclear powered ballistic missile submarine (SSBN) RFS Generalissimus Suvorov (K-553), assigned to the Russian Navy Pacific Fleet, launched a RSM-56 Bulava SLBM from the sea of Okhotsk at the Chizha test site in the Arkhangelsk region of northwest Russia. “The strategic nuclear-powered ballistic missile submarine Generalissimus Suvorov launched a Bulava intercontinental ballistic missile in accordance with the combat training plan,”the Russian MOD said on Wednesday. The missiles were fired from a submerged position and the missile’s warheads successfully reached the designated area at the estimated time. The Russian MOD also released a video of the launch that was carried by state media TASS. The Russian MOD did not state when the launch took place though international navigational warnings were issued on missile activity being carried out from Oct. 25-31. Russia has regularly carried out SLBM launches from the Russian Far East during the October to November with Generalissimus Suvorov firing a Bulava on Nov. 3 2022 prior to being commissioned on Dec. 29 that year, reported USNI News. Russia last carried out an SLBM launch by a SSBN on May 21 this year when a submerged Delta IV class SSBN launched an R-29RMU Sineva SLBM as part of an exercise of its strategic nuclear forces. There has been only two other publicly disclosed SLBM launches this year, with China carrying out a launch in July from the South China Sea into the South Pacific and France carrying out one in early October , launching an SLBM from off the coast of Finistère, France into a remote area of the North Atlantic. Unlike Russia, where the SLBM landed in national territory and France, where it landed in the North Atlantic, several hundred kilometers from any coastline, China was criticised by South Pacific island states and other countries for using the area as an SLBM test site. North Korea on Thursday conducted firings of its KN-25 600mm multiple launch rockets, which are classed as SRBMs, as part of a firepower demonstration during an exhibition of UAV technology that was attended by North Korea leader Kim Jong Un. South Korea’s Joint Chiefs of Staff on Thursday stated that North Korea launched 10 short range ballistic missiles (SRBMs) from Wonsan into the Sea of Japan at 12.30 p.m. local time, the JCS also said the SRBMs flew for a distance of 250km. Japan’s Ministry of Defense (MOD) reported on Thursday that North Korea launched a ballistic missile at 12.36 p.m. that day and it was estimated that the ballistic missile landed near the east coast of the Korean Peninsula. Both the JSC and MOD stated that the U.S., Japan and South Korea were sharing information and analysing the launches. U.S. Pacific Command’s meanwhile placed the number of ballistic missiles launched at two in its statement . On Friday, state media Korean Central News Agency reported that Kim visited the Unmanned Aeronautical Technology Development-2026 exhibition on Thursday, which showcase North Korea’s UAV capabilities and advancements. KCNA did not state the location of the exhibition though it was likely in Wonsan given the SRBM launches from the area on Thursday matched what was fired during the firepower demonstration. In his speech at the exhibition, Kim called on North Korea to seize absolute superiority in drone technology and urged North Korean scientists to go all out in obtaining miraculous results in research on UAV and Artificial Intelligence (AI) for national defence. After touring the exhibition, the North Korean leader witnessed a firepower demonstration that involved strikes on islet target by various tactical suicide attack drones, tactical cruise missiles, multi-purpose drones and a 600mm-calibre Multiple Rocket Launcher (MRL) battalion. KCNA also reported that the demonstration also involved the first publicly displayed firing of a 600mm-calibre ultra-precision MRL called ‘Sniper’. The rockets fired by North Korea’s KN-25 MRL are classed as SRBMs and North Korea has claimed they can be fitter with nuclear warheads. Imagery by KCNA, showed salvo firings by a dozen launchers. KCNA also released images showing UAVs launching missiles and loitering munitions hitting targets with some of the targets made to look like South Korean outpost and K9 Thunder Self-Propelled Howitzers and U.S. M1 Abrams tanks. KCNA images also showed Kim looking at racks of First Person View (FPV) Small Unmanned Aerial Systems (SUASs) and a new flying wing stealth design UAV not previously seen. The state media did not report or provided any details on the UAVs shown. It is unclear as to whether the flying wing UAV was an operational UAV or a model representing an actual in service UAV or one under development.

title: Party Pitches Global Governance in Xi’s Potemkin City
zh_title: 党在习近平的波将金城宣传全球治理
summary: 内容摘要：2026 年全球治理论坛由统战系统一部分的中国人民外交学会精心策划，旨在向世界其他国家展示中华人民共和国（PRC）作为技术乌托邦解决方案的仁慈提供者的形象。北京善于利用论坛等活动来增强其合法性并扩大其在国际体系中的影响力，该论坛结束了一年来令人印象深刻的共识建立，特别是在联合国，特别是在全球南方国家之间。结果包括位置
content:
内容摘要：2026 年全球治理论坛由统战系统一部分的中国人民外交学会精心策划，旨在向世界其他国家展示中华人民共和国（PRC）作为技术乌托邦解决方案的仁慈提供者的形象。北京善于利用论坛等活动来增强其合法性并扩大其在国际体系中的影响力，该论坛结束了一年来令人印象深刻的共识建立，特别是在联合国，特别是在全球南方国家之间。成果包括关于制定新领域（深海、极地和外层空间）和新兴领域（人工智能和网络空间）国际规则的立场文件。各国还共同努力塑造国际人权制度，并得到了联合国难民事务高级专员的支持。该论坛的目标明显对西方怀有敌意。外交部长王毅的讲话指责美国奉行“垄断权力、实行双重标准”的模式，而中共智库《全球治理倡议》的一份报告则将北京的做法描述为“脱离了传统上西方主导的叙事框架”。十月底的四天内，中国共产党举办了一场雄心勃勃的活动，向外界宣示其全球领导地位。
This was the 2026 Global Governance Forum, which brought together members of the “strategic, political, academic, and business communities of 97 countries and international organizations” (来自97个国家和国际组织的战略界、政界、学界、工商界等代表) to provide a sheen of legitimacy to Beijing’s attempts to refashion the international system in a way that better reflects its interests.The forum’s theme was “Rebuilding Confidence and Cooperation: Changes Unseen in A Century and Reforming and Improving Global Governance” (重建信心与合作：百年变局与改革完善全球治理) ( Xinhua , October 26). United Front Fingerprints The primary host for the event was the Chinese People’s Institute of Foreign Affairs (CPIFA; 中国人民外交学会), a “mass organization” (群团组织) that operates under the direction of the Office of the Central Institutional Organization Commission. [1] Although it does not have direct ties to the Party’s United Front Work Department, the institute functions as part of the Party’s wider united front system—as do other mass organizations, such as the All-China Federation of Returned Overseas Chinese and the Chinese People’s Association for Friendship with Foreign Countries (China Brief, May 9, 2019 , June 21, 2024 ). The involvement of CPIFA, through which the Party works to shape foreign perceptions of the People’s Republic of China (PRC), is key to understanding the forum’s messaging function.
尽管习近平总书记在论坛期间通过歌颂党的“长征”英雄并加倍强调党内普遍存在的腐败问题来煽动民族主义，但论坛试图通过投射高科技未来的愿景来消除对国家持续存在的经济问题的担忧。论坛举办地雄安新区凸显了这次活动的宣传价值。雄安是习近平的标志性项目之一，是一座位于北京郊外的规划城市。政府声称其职能是通过搬迁非必要的政府办公场所来缓解首都的拥堵，但实际上远不止于此。雄阿

【原文 English Original】
Executive Summary: The 2026 Global Governance Forum was carefully stage-managed by the Chinese People’s Institute of Foreign Affairs—part of the united front system—to present an image of the People’s Republic of China (PRC) as a benevolent provider of techno-utopian solutions for the rest of the world. Beijing is adept at using events like the forum, which capped a year of impressive consensus-building, particularly at the United Nations, and particularly among Global South countries, to enhance its legitimacy and expand its influence within the international system. Outcomes included position papers on shaping international rules for new frontiers (the deep sea, polar regions, and outer space) and for emerging domains (artificial intelligence and cyberspace). Concerted efforts were also made to shape the international human rights regime, which received support from the UN High Commissioner for Refugees. The forum’s aims are explicitly hostile to the West. Foreign Minister Wang Yi’s speech accused the United States of pursuing a model that “monopolizes power and practices double standards,” while a Party think tank report on the Global Governance Initiative described Beijing’s approach as “breaking away from the traditionally Western-dominated narrative framework.” Over four days in late October, the Chinese Communist Party (CCP) staged an ambitious event to stake its claim to global leadership to the outside world. This was the 2026 Global Governance Forum, which brought together members of the “strategic, political, academic, and business communities of 97 countries and international organizations” (来自97个国家和国际组织的战略界、政界、学界、工商界等代表) to provide a sheen of legitimacy to Beijing’s attempts to refashion the international system in a way that better reflects its interests. The forum’s theme was “Rebuilding Confidence and Cooperation: Changes Unseen in A Century and Reforming and Improving Global Governance” (重建信心与合作：百年变局与改革完善全球治理) ( Xinhua , October 26). United Front Fingerprints The primary host for the event was the Chinese People’s Institute of Foreign Affairs (CPIFA; 中国人民外交学会), a “mass organization” (群团组织) that operates under the direction of the Office of the Central Institutional Organization Commission.  [1] Although it does not have direct ties to the Party’s United Front Work Department, the institute functions as part of the Party’s wider united front system—as do other mass organizations, such as the All-China Federation of Returned Overseas Chinese and the Chinese People’s Association for Friendship with Foreign Countries (China Brief, May 9, 2019 , June 21, 2024 ). The involvement of CPIFA, through which the Party works to shape foreign perceptions of the People’s Republic of China (PRC), is key to understanding the forum’s messaging function. While General Secretary Xi Jinping spent the weeks surrounding the forum stoking nationalism by exalting the heroes of the Party’s “Long March” and doubling down on the Party’s endemic corruption issues, the forum sought to dispel fears of the country’s persistent economic problems by projecting a vision of a high-tech future. The venue for the forum, Xiong’an New Area, underscored the propaganda value of the occasion. One of Xi’s signature projects, Xiong’an is a planned city located just outside Beijing. The government argues that its functional role is to relieve congestion in the capital by relocating non-essential government offices, but in practice it is much more than this. Xiong’an is a hubristic project that, in under a decade, has sought to create a new type of digitally integrated city, incorporating the various emerging technologies that Beijing has championed in recent years. Foreign Minister Wang Yi (王毅), in his keynote speech at the forum, hit all of the propaganda points used in the Party’s messaging to describe the city. He called it “a project of millennial significance” (千年大计), “a city of the future” (未来之城), “a brand-new endeavor in exploring modernized governance” (探索现代化治理的崭新实践), and “an exemplar of high-quality development” (高质量发展样板) ( PRC Ministry of Foreign Affairs [MFA] , October 23). External observers have been more skeptical. Around the time that Wang Yi announced the Global Governance Forum earlier this year, the urban studies scholar Andrew Stokols wrote that Xiong’an “has been largely seen as a failure so far” ( Substack/Sinocities , May 20).  [2] The critique is largely based on concerns about the decision to build the city on a floodplain, the lack of demand from people wishing to relocate into the city, and the enormous investments made that are yet to realize returns. Xiong’an nevertheless has significant propaganda value. As Stokols notes, the city is a “showcase for a new ideology of the urban under Xi Jinping” (Stokols, 2025). [3] Its conceptual structure of three cities in one—the built environment above ground, an underground network of over 100 kilometers of utility tunnels below ground, and a digital twin in the cloud—is supposed to show the benefits of Chinese-style modernization and provide a model to the world. During the forum, a video pushed by a number of state media and PRC embassy accounts on Western social media platforms tried to dispel doubts about Xiong’an. But as of October 30, the short video, which is hosted by the Western, PRC-based influencer Tom Shanahan and funded by the Hebei International Communication Center, had accrued fewer than 200 views ( YouTube/iHebei , October 26). Participants literally signed on to the official narrative about Xiong’an at the forum, which the People’s Daily framed as “both a grand gathering of ideas on global governance and an important window for the world to observe China’s governance” (既是一场全球治理的思想盛会，也是世界观察中国之治的重要窗口) ( People’s Daily , October 25). After tours around the city, including to its “smart city innovation center,” all participants affirmed in the “Forum Vision Document” (论坛愿景文件) released at the event that “we … believe that the principles upheld in [Xiong’an’s] planning and construction have important reference value for reforming and improving global governance” (我们 … 认为雄安新区规划建设中秉持的理念对于改革完善全球治理具有重要借鉴意义) ( Xinhua , October 26). Xiong’an’s importance for international messaging is evident in the sensitivity about the topic within the PRC. Stokols recounts an attempt to interview officials involved in the city’s planning, but was rebuffed, with one professor declining to write a letter of introduction for fear of reprisals ( Substack/Sinocities , May 20). Blunter commentators have described Xiong’an as a “Potemkin metropolis” ( Hudson Institute , May 13). Human Rights Hypocrisy Among Forum Outcomes Beijing is adept at using events like the Global Governance Forum to enhance its legitimacy and expand its influence within the international system. Despite the fragile foundations of the event itself—echoed ironically in the choice of venue—the forum capped a year of impressive consensus-building, particularly at the United Nations, and particularly among Global South countries. Chinese experts have praised these efforts as helping the PRC “acquire the institutional capacity to coordinate positions and form a collective voice within the UN framework” (具备了在联合国框架内协调立场、形成集体声音的制度能力) ( Guangming Daily , October 26). Following Xi’s proposal of the Global Governance Initiative (GGI)—his fourth global initiative—at the Tianjin Summit of the Shanghai Cooperation Organization in September 2025, Beijing first set up a “Friends of Global Governance Group” at the UN in New York. This group has branches in Geneva and Vienna, and in May released a joint communiqué with signatories from over 60 countries ( PRC Mission to the UN , December 9, 2025; MFA , May 29; People’s Daily , May 30). In June, the State Council released a detailed white paper on “Building a More Just and Reasonable Global Governance System” (构建更加公正合理的全球治理体系), providing more detail on the specifics of Beijing’s plans to reform global governance ( SCIO , June 6; China Brief , June 26). Beijing already claims tangible results of the GGI, presenting the Hong Kong-based International Court of Mediation, the Shanghai-based World AI Cooperation Organization, and the Beijing-based World Data Organization as “vivid implementations” (生动实践) of the initiative ( Guangming Daily , October 26). Beijing’s sought to use the forum to advance its agenda in several key directions. Amid the expected advocacy for expanding the discourse power of Global South countries within the UN system, including through reforms to the UN Security Council, and reforming the global financial and trade systems, two areas of intent stood out. The first is Beijing’s desire to shape international rules in both new frontiers—such as the deep sea, polar regions, and outer space—and emerging domains—AI, cyberspace, and outer space. The clearest evidence for this was the release of a “Progress Report on the AI Capacity-Building Action Plan for Good and for All” (人工智能能力建设普惠计划〉进展报告) and a paper titled “China’s Position on Strengthening Outer Space Governance” (关于加强外空治理的中国立场) (MFA, October 23 ; October 26 ). As these and other documents released at the summit make clear, Beijing’s institutional and normative innovations are explicitly anti-Western. Wang Yi presented his audience with a “stark” (对比鲜明) choice between a model that “exalts strength, favors self-interest, monopolizes power, and practices double standards” (迷信实力地位，推行本国优先、少数垄断、双重标准) and one that “champions multilateralism, and upholds sovereign equality, mutual respect and international law” (践行多边主义，坚持主权平等、相互尊重、国际法治) ( MFA , October 23). A report released at the event by the Xi Jinping Thought on Diplomacy Studies Centre, meanwhile, lambasts the United States explicitly for “relying on self-defined legal standards such as the “effects doctrine” and “minimum contacts”, extends the reach of its domestic law infinitely across the globe, exercising jurisdiction without the consent of other states, even carrying out arrests on the territory of third countries, completely disregarding the legal sovereignty and judicial jurisdiction of the states where the conduct occurs.” It describes the GGI as “breaking away from the traditionally Western-dominated narrative framework of global governance, and avoiding the outdated discourse traps of ‘a strong country is bound to seek hegemony’ and ‘bloc confrontation,’” while criticizing the “rules-based international order” for serving as “an ideological tool for a small number of states to pursue hegemonism and construct a hierarchical order” ( Xi Jinping Thought on Diplomacy Studies Centre , October 2026). The outer space position paper, meanwhile, “opposes any country abusing its domestic laws to obstruct or impose unilateral sanctions on other countries’ external airspace activities” (反对一国滥用其国内法对他国外空活动设置障碍或进行单边制裁). Another area in which Beijing used the forum to press for material changes to the international system was in human rights. It was well placed to do so, as the event was co-organized by the United Nations Association of China, and its partners included the China Society for Human Rights Studies (中国人权研究会) and the China Foundation for Human Rights Development (中国人权发展基金会). Also in attendance were UN Under-Secretary-General for Policy Guy Bernard Ryder, the UN Human Rights Council’s Independent Expert on the Promotion of a Democratic and Equitable International Order George Katrougalos, and, most pertinently, the UN High Commissioner for Refugees Barham Salih. Remarkably, Salih praised Xi’s signature initiative, stating that the Human Rights Council “looks forward to building a close partnership with China … jointly addressing the refugee challenge within the framework of the GGI ” (期待同中方构建紧密伙伴关系，开展“以人为本”的合作，在全球治理倡议框架下共同应对难民挑战) ( People’s Daily , October 24). Such statements help fuel Beijing’s revisionist approach to the international human rights regime. As Wang Yi declared in his speech, the PRC “promotes the recalibration of global human rights governance” (推动校正全球人权治理), aiming to “place the right to development high on the multilateral human rights agenda” (将发展权置于多边人权议程突出位置)—in other words, to undermine individual human rights and censor critics of its own practices ( MFA , October 23). The report from the Xi Jinping Thought on Diplomacy Studies Centre made this unambiguous, arguing that “we must reject the misguided notion of ‘human rights above sovereignty,’ and make it clear that it is up to the people of each country to assess and improve their own human rights situation” ( Xi Jinping Thought on Diplomacy Studies Centre , October 2026). Holding the forum in Xiong’an only underscored the reality of Beijing’s approach to human rights. Not only were the homes of tens of thousands of villagers demolished to make way for the city, but the entire edifice is an exemplar of a technologically empowered surveillance state ( Substack/Sinocities , May 20). As an article in the People’s Daily lays out, the “Eye of Xiong’an” (雄安之眼)—which in English sounds unfortunately like the “Eye of Sauron”—integrates data feeds to allow for live monitoring of the entire city. And in the neighborhood of Nanwenying (南文营), which Xi inspected in 2023, “each of the more than 3,700 households has its own file” (3700多户居民‘一户一档’) that is “dynamically updated” (动态更新) every two months ( Xinhua , June 23, 2023; People’s Daily , October 24). Conclusion The success of the 2026 Global Governance Forum in Xiong’an is hard to assess. On the one hand, it was able to attract a diverse and influential international crowd: beyond the UN representatives listed above, World Economic Forum founder Klaus Schwab, former Chancellor of Germany Gerhard Schröder, the Asia Society’s John L. Thornton, and even New York Times columnist Thomas Friedman were in attendance; and prominent Western scholars, such as the political scientist David Shambaugh, sat on panels to opine on topics such as “Multilateral Solutions for Global Governance.” On the other hand, no world leaders made appearances, and Xi himself only sent a letter, which Wang Yi duly read out. The active politicians that did attend were largely those already clearly aligned with the Party (or with the Party in opposition to the West). The event itself nevertheless does appear to have advanced Beijing’s international standing. It helped show that the PRC is serious about changing the rules of the game and is building support to shape how the world approaches emerging frontiers and domains; and through its efforts to build new governance institutions and enlist other countries to endorse its initiatives and adopt its standards, it will continue capitalize on a lack of a positive vision from the rest of the world. Notes [1] Co-organizers of the event included Hebei’s provincial government, the Administrative Committee of Xiong’an New Area, United Nations Association of China, China Institute of International Studies, China Foreign Affairs University. The event’s partners included University of International Business and Economics, Renmin University of China, Red Cross Society of China, China International Communications Group, China Society for Human Rights Studies, and the China Foundation for Human Rights Development. [2] Andrew Stokols has previously written for China Brief : https://jamestown.org/analyst/andrew-stokols-100993/ . [3] Andrew Stokols, “A new city for a new era: Xiong’an as showcase of China’s evolving urban ideology,” Cambridge Journal of Regions, Economy and Society , Volume 18, Issue 2, July 2025, Pages 293–307, https://doi.org/10.1093/cjres/rsaf003 . The post Party Pitches Global Governance in Xi’s Potemkin City appeared first on Jamestown .

title: Radical AI uses autonomous labs to accelerate alloy discovery
zh_title: Radical AI 使用自主实验室加速合金发现
summary: 随着美国努力减少对中国关键矿产的依赖，总部位于纽约的 Radical AI 正在采取不同的方法来确保战略材料：利用人工智能开发需要更少供应受限金属的新合金。该公司开发了一个自动驾驶实验室平台，利用人工智能和机器人技术来设计、制造和测试先进材料，据称这一创新大大缩短了航空航天、国防和其他工业应用中使用的合金的发现过程。 9 月，Radical AI 与 Sand 合作
content:
随着美国努力减少对中国关键矿产的依赖，总部位于纽约的 Radical AI 正在采取不同的方法来确保战略材料：利用人工智能开发需要更少供应受限金属的新合金。该公司开发了一个自动驾驶实验室平台，利用人工智能和机器人技术来设计、制造和测试先进材料，据称这一创新大大缩短了航空航天、国防和其他工业应用中使用的合金的发现过程。 9 月，Radical AI 与桑迪亚国家实验室合作，开展金属-氢相互作用研究，并发现从废气流中分离氢气的新材料。 Radical AI 首席执行官约瑟夫·弗劳斯 (Joseph Frause) 在接受 MINING.COM 采访时表示，Radical AI 在布鲁克林海军造船厂的工厂中展示了一种合金发现流程，可在大约 16 周内生产出 300 种新成分。这项工作得到了 RTX 和 Nvidia 的支持，该公司表示，可以通过围绕更容易获得的元素重新设计材料，为美国制造商提供另一种解决供应链漏洞的方法。 “如果你有一个系统，可以根据你给它的限制来设计新材料，并且你现有的材料受到供应链的真正限制，我们可以帮助解决这个问题，”弗劳斯说。
“我们可以设计新材料，在考虑这些限制的同时仍然执行应用程序所需的功能或我们所说的属性集。”  围绕关键矿物进行设计 华盛顿的大部分关键矿物战略都侧重于扩大国内采矿、加工和精炼能力，以减少对外国供应商的依赖。Radical AI 进一步向下游运营，利用精炼金属开发满足特定工业性能要求的先进材料。该公司不涉及采矿或矿物加工。相反，它的技术识别出可以提供所需材料特性的元素组合，同时最大限度地减少与供应受限的金属的接触。铪就是一个例子，它是一种具有重要战略意义的元素，用于航空航天和国防应用的高温合金。 Radical AI 表示，它已成功开发出专为极端温度环境设计的高性能合金，其中铪含量极低，在某些情况下几乎不含。弗劳斯说：“铪是元素周期表中的元素之一，主要由中国供应链拥有，对战争部以及美国和我们的盟友来说都是一个风险因素。”该公司的方法允许制造商指定新材料中应排除哪些元素，同时保持所需的强度、耐用性以及耐热性和抗氧化性。
弗劳斯说：“我们正在将成分混合在一起，而不是弄乱成分。”“我们正在使用可用的成分。现在，我们能做的就是决定哪些成分应该出现在清单上。”  该技术可能有助于制造商开发含有易受出口限制、地缘政治紧张局势或国内生产有限影响的金属的合金的替代品。缩短材料发现时间传统采矿在发现过程后可能需要 10 到 15 年才能投入运营，单个材料系统的成本超过 1 亿美元。冗长且

【原文 English Original】
As the United States pushes to reduce its dependence on China for critical minerals, New York-based Radical AI is taking a different approach to securing strategic materials: using artificial intelligence to develop new alloys that require fewer supply-constrained metals.  The company has developed a self-driving laboratory platform that uses AI and robotics to design, manufacture and test advanced materials, an innovation that it says dramatically shortens the discovery process for alloys used in aerospace, defense and other industrial applications.  In September, Radical AI partnered with Sandia National Laboratories to perform research on metal-hydrogen interactions and discover new materials to separate hydrogen from waste gas streams. Working from its facility at the Brooklyn Navy Yard, Radical AI has demonstrated an alloy discovery process that produced 300 new compositions in approximately 16 weeks, CEO Joseph Frause told MINING.COM in an interview.  The work is backed by RTX and Nvidia and could, the company says, offer US manufacturers another way to address supply chain vulnerabilities by redesigning materials around more readily available elements.  “If you have a system that can design new materials based on the constraints that you give it, and you have existing materials that have real constraints from the supply chain, we can help solve that problem,” Frause said.  “We can design new materials that take into consideration those constraints while still executing on the function or what we call the property set that is required for an application.”  Designing around critical minerals   Much of Washington’s critical minerals strategy has focused on expanding domestic mining, processing and refining capacity to reduce reliance on foreign suppliers.  Radical AI operates further downstream, using refined metals to develop advanced materials that meet specific industrial performance requirements.  The company is not involved in mining or mineral processing. Instead, its technology identifies combinations of elements that can deliver desired material properties while minimizing exposure to supply-constrained metals.  One example is hafnium, a strategically important element used in high-temperature alloys for aerospace and defense applications.  Radical AI says it has successfully developed high-performance alloys designed for extreme-temperature environments that contain very little, and in some cases almost no, hafnium.  “Hafnium is one of those elements in the periodic table that is majorly owned from China’s supply chain and is a risk factor to the Department of War and just the United States and our allies,” Frause said.  The company’s approach allows manufacturers to specify which elements should be excluded from a new material while maintaining the required strength, durability and resistance to heat and oxidation.  “We are mixing up the ingredients together, not messing with the ingredients,” Frause said. “We are using the ingredients that are available. Now, what we can do is decide what ingredients should be on the list.”  The technology could potentially help manufacturers develop alternatives to alloys containing metals vulnerable to export restrictions, geopolitical tensions or limited domestic production.  Cutting years off materials discovery   Traditional mining can take 10 to 15 years to come into operations after the discovery process, and cost more than $100 million for a single material system. The lengthy and expensive process has left many aerospace and defense manufacturers relying on alloys developed decades ago.  “A lot of the advanced materials that they use, the structural metals they use, are old. 20, 30, 40, 50 years old in some of the applications,” Frause said.  The company believes autonomous experimentation can substantially shorten those timelines by integrating AI-driven material design with physical testing.  Once the system identifies a promising composition, it designs an experimental campaign to synthesize and evaluate the alloy.  The laboratory then manufactures a physical sample weighing approximately 50 to 200 grams before analyzing its chemical composition, grain structure and mechanical properties.  Testing can include hardness, tensile strength and high-temperature performance, including conditions relevant to hypersonic applications.  The resulting data is fed back into machine-learning models to improve subsequent experiments.  “We’ll take all of that data and we’ll analyze it with machine learning and then we will feed it back into that design loop,” Frause said.  “We call this the active learning loop so that the next time I make a new alloy, I am looking at the past results as I’m doing so.”  By continuously incorporating experimental results into its models, Radical AI aims to accelerate the iterative process traditionally performed by materials scientists.  The longer-term ambition is to reduce materials development timelines from decades to just a few years.  “Put simply, you take a 20-year development timeline and you shrink it down to one, two, three years,” he said.  A new model for aerospace and defense   Beyond speeding up discovery, Radical AI believes its technology could change how manufacturers design products.  Rather than selecting from existing alloys, companies could develop materials specifically engineered for the requirements of new aircraft, engines, defense systems and industrial equipment.  The approach, known as concurrent engineering, would allow materials development to proceed alongside product design.  “As I am designing my new airplane, I am designing the materials that go in my airplane,” Frause said.  “That does not happen in the alloy space today.”  The company argues that developing application-specific alloys could unlock performance improvements that are difficult to achieve using conventional materials.  It could also allow manufacturers to account for critical mineral availability at the earliest stages of product development, rather than confronting supply chain limitations after designs are finalized.  Commercial platform, not alloy production   Founded in January 2024, Radical AI has commercialized its autonomous laboratory platform and says it already has paying customers.  Unlike a conventional metals producer, the company does not manufacture commercial quantities of alloys or enter into offtake agreements.  Instead, customers use its technology to accelerate materials discovery and can retain intellectual property rights to the compositions developed through the platform.  “Our product is the platform, the self-driving lab. That’s what we’ve commercialized and that’s what we do have customers on today,” Frause said. “We don’t off-take the materials.”  The company remains focused on discovery rather than industrial-scale manufacturing, meaning promising alloys must still undergo additional development and qualification before being deployed in commercial applications.  That distinction is particularly important in aerospace and defense, where materials must satisfy stringent safety, performance and reliability requirements.  While AI-driven discovery will not eliminate the need for critical mineral mining and refining, Radical AI believes it can provide manufacturers with greater flexibility in choosing the metals used in advanced applications.  For the mining industry, the emergence of materials substitution technologies could eventually influence demand for certain critical metals, even as new industrial applications create opportunities for others.  “It’s really the way we do science that’s going to impact the entirety of the materials industry at large,” Frause said. “It’s going to be a new way to do scientific discovery.”

title: Lynas locks in price floors as revenue jumps 55%
zh_title: 莱纳斯锁定价格下限，收入猛增 55%
summary: 澳大利亚莱纳斯稀土公司（ASX：LYC；美国场外交易市场代码：LYSCF、LYSDY）已获得涵盖其一半以上产量的最低价格协议，因为制造商为中国境外的供应支付溢价。该公司周四表示，截至 9 月 30 日的三个月内，平均售价上涨 88%，达到创纪录的每公斤 102.1 澳元（合 72 美元），收入增长 55% 至 3.101 亿澳元（合 2.18 亿美元）。销量同比下降 18%。莱纳斯表示，定价上涨反映了市场价格、溢价以及轻重稀土捆绑销售的走强。 “原始设备制造商有一个真正的战略来确保部分产品的安全。
content:
澳大利亚莱纳斯稀土公司（ASX：LYC；美国场外交易市场代码：LYSCF、LYSDY）已获得涵盖其一半以上产量的最低价格协议，因为制造商为中国境外的供应支付溢价。该公司周四表示，截至 9 月 30 日的三个月内，平均售价上涨 88%，达到创纪录的每公斤 102.1 澳元（合 72 美元），收入增长 55% 至 3.101 亿澳元（合 2.18 亿美元）。销量同比下降 18%。莱纳斯表示，定价上涨反映了市场价格、溢价以及轻重稀土捆绑销售的走强。临时首席执行官 Pol Le Roux 在周四的电话会议上对分析师表示：“原始设备制造商有一个真正的战略，可以从中国境外确保部分供应。”他指的是原始设备制造商。随着制造商寻求替代供应商，这些合同为莱纳斯提供了一些保护，使其免受中国价格波动的影响。但以商业规模可靠地分离稀土对于中国以外的新兴供应链来说仍然是一个挑战。莱纳斯股价周四在悉尼上涨 4.2%，周五下跌 7.1%，至 12.10 澳元，该公司估值约为 122 亿澳元。停产压力莱纳斯本季度销售了 3,039 吨稀土氧化物，产量为 4,254 吨，同比增长 7%。用于永磁体的氧化钕镨产量创下季度记录 2,082 吨。 Le Roux 将产销之间的差距部分归因于 9 月底的强劲产量，而这些产量在季度末之前无法开具发票。
分析师敦促对钕镨销售进行细分，以区分产品结构的变化和价格上涨；他表示莱纳斯将寻求在未来的报告中提供这一细节。莱纳斯没有在季度报告中披露其底价。由于其马来西亚工厂关闭约一个月进行维护，产量预计将在 12 月份季度下降。西澳大利亚州的卡尔古利也面临着大约两周的电力网络升级关闭。 Le Roux 表示，莱纳斯的库存（包括其日本经销商持有的材料）应该能够在停工期间维持客户供应。该公司计划进行修改，以缓解加工瓶颈并提高设备可靠性，预计截至 2027 年 3 月和 6 月的季度产量将有所增加。莱纳斯正在使用镝和铽供应来帮助与购买钕和镨的磁铁制造商建立长期关系。 Le Roux 表示，将轻稀土和重稀土结合起来，可以让客户从一个供应商那里获得更多所需的材料。截至 9 月底，莱纳斯拥有 12.1 亿澳元现金和短期存款。巴西收购 本月早些时候，Lynas 同意以 9.68 亿澳元的价格收购 Meteoric Resources（ASX：MEI；US-OTC：METOF）。拟议的全股权收购将增加巴西东南部波苏斯迪卡尔达斯附近的 Caldeira 稀土项目。完成仍有待股东、法院和监管机构的批准。
莱纳斯在西澳大利亚经营韦尔德山矿，在卡尔古利加工材料，并在马来西亚分离稀土。初步计划是在卡尔代拉生产混合稀土碳酸盐，然后运往马来西亚进行分离。一项工程审查正在研究卡尔代拉如何适应莱纳斯的处理网络。勒鲁表示，首要任务是降低采矿和加工成本，并尽快将项目投入生产。

【原文 English Original】
Australia’s Lynas Rare Earths (ASX: LYC; US-OTC: LYSCF, LYSDY) has secured minimum-price agreements covering more than half its production as manufacturers pay premiums for supplies outside China. Average selling prices jumped 88% to a record A$102.1 ($72) per kg in the three months to Sept. 30, lifting revenue 55% to A$310.1 million ($218 million), the company said Thursday. Sales volumes fell 18% from a year earlier. The pricing gains reflected stronger market prices, premiums and the bundling of light and heavy rare earths, Lynas said. “There is a real strategy from OEMs to secure part of their supply from outside China,” interim CEO Pol Le Roux told analysts on a call Thursday, referring to original equipment manufacturers. The contracts give Lynas some protection from Chinese price swings as manufacturers seek alternative suppliers. But separating rare earths reliably at commercial scale remains a challenge for the emerging supply chain outside China. Lynas shares rose 4.2% Thursday in Sydney, then fell 7.1% Friday to A$12.10, valuing the company at about A$12.2 billion. Shutdown pressure Lynas sold 3,039 tonnes of rare earth oxides during the quarter while producing 4,254 tonnes, up 7% from a year earlier. Output of neodymium-praseodymium oxide, used in permanent magnets, reached a quarterly record of 2,082 tonnes. Le Roux attributed the gap between production and sales partly to strong output late in September that couldn’t be invoiced before quarter-end. Analysts pressed for a breakdown of neodymium-praseodymium sales to distinguish changes in product mix from stronger prices; he said Lynas would seek to provide that detail in future reports. Lynas didn’t disclose its floor prices in the quarterly release. Production is set to fall in the December quarter as its Malaysian plant shuts for about a month of maintenance. Kalgoorlie, in Western Australia, also faces a roughly two-week shutdown for electricity-network upgrades. Inventories, including material held by its Japanese distributor, should allow Lynas to maintain customer supplies during the stoppages, Le Roux said. The company plans modifications to relieve processing bottlenecks and improve equipment reliability, with stronger production expected in the quarters ending March and June 2027. Lynas is using dysprosium and terbium supplies to help secure longer-term relationships with magnet makers buying neodymium and praseodymium. Combining light and heavy rare earths gives customers more of the materials they need from one supplier, Le Roux said. Lynas ended September with A$1.21 billion in cash and short-term deposits. Brazil acquisition Earlier this month, Lynas agreed to buy Meteoric Resources (ASX: MEI; US-OTC: METOF) in a deal valued at A$968 million. The proposed all-share acquisition would add the Caldeira rare earths project near Poços de Caldas in southeastern Brazil. Completion remains subject to shareholder, court and regulatory approvals. Lynas operates the Mt Weld mine in Western Australia, processes material at Kalgoorlie and separates rare earths in Malaysia. The initial plan is to produce mixed rare earth carbonate at Caldeira and send it to Malaysia for separation. An engineering review is examining how Caldeira could fit Lynas’ processing network. The priorities were to reduce costs across mining and processing and bring the project into production as quickly as possible, Le Roux said.

title: 蘑菇杀手埃琳·帕特森上诉失败，使其在澳大利亚历史上留下黑暗印记
source: 澳洲唐人街 – Australia ChinaTown News 中文华人新闻
summary: Erin Patterson 不仅于周五在维多利亚上诉法院败诉，检方也成功争取到撤销其假释资格。 这使得这位 52 岁的连环杀人犯成为澳大利亚第二位被判处无假释期终身监禁的女性。 Erin Patterson 正在对其定罪和判决提出上诉。AP 在此之前，NSW 女子 Katherine Knight 因 2001 年致其准丈夫 John Price 死亡而被判刑。 这位臭名昭著的连环女杀手被定罪，因用匕首刺穿其伴侣 37 次，随后将其剥皮，并企图将煮熟的肉喂给她的孩子们。 2
content: Erin Patterson 不仅于周五在维多利亚上诉法院败诉，检方也成功争取到撤销其假释资格。 这使得这位 52 岁的连环杀人犯成为澳大利亚第二位被判处无假释期终身监禁的女性。 Erin Patterson 正在对其定罪和判决提出上诉。AP 在此之前，NSW 女子 Katherine Knight 因 2001 年致其准丈夫 John Price 死亡而被判刑。 这位臭名昭著的连环女杀手被定罪，因用匕首刺穿其伴侣 37 次，随后将其剥皮，并企图将煮熟的肉喂给她的孩子们。 2006 年，Knight 试图对其判决提出上诉，声称该刑罚对其罪行而言过于严厉，但她的上诉被驳回。 Patterson 于 2025 年被定罪，罪名是谋杀其岳父母 Don 和 Gail Patterson，以及 Gail 的妹妹 Heather Wilkinson，并企图谋杀 Heather 的丈夫 Ian Wilkinson。 NSW 女子 Katherine Knight（右），因 2001 年致其准丈夫 John Price（左）死亡而被判刑。Supplied/Andrew Forbes 2023 年 7 月，她邀请该团伙在其位于维多利亚州偏远地区的 Leongatha 家中共进午餐，期间她为他们端上了掺有死亡帽毒蘑菇的惠灵顿牛排。 四人全部入院，但只有 Ian Wilkinson 在漫长的治疗后幸存下来。 Patterson 在 Dame Phyllis Frost Centre 旁观看上诉审理，她将在该处度过余生。 这位 52 岁的女子在多个理由上败诉，其律师辩称这些理由导致了“司法不公”。 他们指出，陪审团与检方成员及案件首席调查员被关押在同一酒店，并声称 Patterson 在法庭上遭受了过度激烈和压迫性的盘问。 2023 年 7 月，她邀请该团伙在其位于维多利亚州偏远地区的 Leongatha 家中共进午餐，期间她为他们端上了掺有死亡帽毒蘑菇的惠灵顿牛排。9News Justices Stephen McLeish, Lesley Taylor 和 Peter Kidd 在周五对其重新量刑时驳斥了这种说法。 "这种犯罪极其冷酷且经过精心策划，应受到最严厉的谴责，"法官们表示。 "这是一起如此令人震惊的犯罪行为，因此不适合设定无假释期，" 法官们认定，Patterson 在长达三周的时间里都保持了谋杀意图——从她邀请客人到其家中开始，一直持续到其受害者在用餐后入院期间她所撒的谎。 法官们认定 Patterson 在长达三周的时间里都保持了谋杀意图，一直持续到其受害者在用餐后入院期间她所撒的谎。A Current Affair "[Patterson 的]行为特征是一系列精心策划的欺骗，"法官们表示。 "这种犯罪是经过仔细规划和深思熟虑的。这是对（她）扩展家庭成员残酷的背叛信任。" Patterson 将在 11 月 27 日前向高等法院提出上诉，这将是她推翻定罪的最后希望。

title: China Claims GJ-21 Naval UCAV has Flown from Type 076 Sichuan LHD
zh_title: 中国声称GJ-21海军无人战斗机已从076型四川两栖攻击舰起飞
source: 航空报 The Aviationist（战机/无人机/防空）
summary: 中国海军表示，GJ-21已在配备电磁弹射器和拦阻系统的076型两栖攻击舰上完成首次起降。据中国军方于 2026 年 10 月 30 日宣布，中国 GJ-21 海军无人作战飞机 (UCAV) 在 076 型四川两栖攻击舰上进行了首次起飞和降落。这一进展首先由官方通讯社新华社和环球时报报道，随后由国防部和官方的中国军号社交媒体公布。
content:
中国海军表示，GJ-21已在配备电磁弹射器和拦阻系统的076型两栖攻击舰上完成首次起降。据中国军方于 2026 年 10 月 30 日宣布，中国 GJ-21 海军无人作战飞机 (UCAV) 在 076 型四川两栖攻击舰上进行了首次起飞和降落。官方通讯社新华社和环球时报首先报道了这一进展，随后国防部和中国军号官方社交媒体账号进行了宣传。军方将GJ-21描述为该国“首款舰载隐身侦察攻击无人机”，并称其“最近在076两栖攻击舰‘四川’号上首次成功起降”。然而，官方媒体和军方都没有发布任何实际飞行操作的官方图像或视频。这一进展正值美国海军推进自己的 MQ-25 Stingray 无人空中加油机计划之际。 MQ-25 主要设计为舰载加油机，还将提供辅助海上情报、监视和侦察 (ISR) 能力。黄貂鱼预计将有助于成熟无人舰载航空所需的技术和操作概念，为海军未来的协同作战飞机（CCA）机队奠定基础。
空中捕获的 GJ-21 飞行中，制动钩已放下。资料来源：中国互联网，来自 Andreas Rupprecht 迄今为止，GJ-21 一直与 076 型航母联系在一起，但也有人建议未来在传统航空母舰上进行操作，有人猜测这款无人机最终会在中国最新的航母福建舰上操作。在我们之前的报告中，我们评估过GJ-21可以为两栖任务群提供无人舰载情监侦和打击能力，有可能将侦察和精确攻击选项扩展到舰艇周围范围之外。中国首架舰载隐形侦察攻击无人机“GJ-21”最近在076两栖攻击舰“四川”号上首次成功起降。 51）。这是中国两栖攻击舰发展的又一重大突破，标志着中国海军现已具备在大型海上作战平台上操作固定翼隐形无人机的能力。四川舰（舷号51）于2024年12月27日下水，是我国自主设计研发的076型两栖攻击舰首艘。它采用自动着舰引导系统、新型综合动力系统、电磁弹射助降降落技术，可搭载固定翼无人机、直升机、两栖装备等。
自2025年11月首次海试以来，四川舰按照计划稳步开展各项海上试验，顺利完成各项设备调试和整体运行稳定性试验。#GJ21 #StealthDrone #UCAV #Sichuan #Type076 #LHA #AmphibiousAssaultShip #DroneCarrier #CatapultLaunchSystem #EMALS #PLA #Navy #ChinaMilitary #ChinaMilBugle — 中国军号(@ChinaMilBugle) 2026 年 10 月 30 日第一艘配备电磁弹射系统和战斗无人机的两栖攻击舰中国军号官方帐号强调了解放军海军“操作固定翼飞机的能力”

【原文 English Original】
The PLA Navy says the GJ-21 has completed its first takeoff and landing aboard the Type 076 amphibious assault ship, which is fitted with an electromagnetic catapult and arresting system. China’s GJ-21 naval Unmanned Combat Aerial Vehicle (UCAV) has reportedly conducted its first takeoff and landing aboard the Type 076 Sichuan amphibious assault ship, the Chinese military announced on Oct. 30, 2026 . The development was first reported by state news agencies Xinhua and Global Times , and subsequently publicized by the Ministry of National Defense and the official China Military Bugle social media account. The military described the GJ-21 as the country’s “first ship-borne stealth reconnaissance and attack drone,” saying that it “recently made its first successful take-off and landing on 076 amphibious assault ship, the ‘Sichuan’.” However, neither the state press nor the military released any official image or video of the actual flight operations.   The development comes as the U.S. Navy advances its own MQ-25 Stingray unmanned aerial refueler program. Primarily designed as a carrier-based tanker, the MQ-25 will also provide a secondary maritime intelligence, surveillance, and reconnaissance (ISR) capability. The Stingray is expected to help mature the technologies and operational concepts needed for unmanned carrier aviation, laying the groundwork for the Navy’s future Collaborative Combat Aircraft (CCA) fleet. Unofficial overhead capture of the GJ-21 in flight with the arrestor hook lowered. | Source: Chinese internet via Andreas Rupprecht The GJ-21 has so far been associated with the Type 076, but future operations from conventional aircraft carriers have also been suggested, with speculation about the drone eventually operating from Fujian, China’s newest carrier. In our previous reports, we have assessed that the GJ-21 could provide an amphibious task group with an embarked unmanned ISR-and-strike capability, potentially extending reconnaissance and precision-attack options beyond the ship’s immediate surroundings China’s first ship-borne stealth reconnaissance and attack drone “GJ-21” recently made its first successful take-off and landing on 076 amphibious assault ship, the “Sichuan” (Hull 51). This is another significant breakthrough in the development of China’s amphibious assault ship, indicating that the Chinese Navy now has the capability to operate fixed-wing stealth drones from large maritime combat platforms.  Launched on December 27, 2024, the Sichuan (Hull 51) is the first vessel of Type 076 amphibious assault ships designed and developed independently by China. It incorporates the automatic carrier landing guidance system, new integrated power system, and electromagnetic catapult-assisted takeoff and arrested landing technology, and is capable of carrying fixed-wing unmanned aircraft, helicopters, and amphibious equipment, etc. Since its first sea trial in November 2025, the Sichuan warship has been steadily conducting various maritime tests as planned, successfully completing the debugging of various equipment and overall operational stability tests. #GJ21 #StealthDrone #UCAV #Sichuan #Type076 #LHA #AmphibiousAssaultShip #DroneCarrier #CatapultLaunchSystem #EMALS #PLA #Navy #ChinaMilitary #ChinaMilBugle — China Military Bugle (@ChinaMilBugle) October 30, 2026 First amphibious assault ship with EMALS and combat drone The official China Military Bugle account emphasized the PLA Navy’s “capability to operate fixed wing stealth drones from maritime combat platforms.” The statement added: “[The Sichuan] incorporates the automatic carrier landing guidance system, new integrated power system, and electromagnetic catapult-assisted takeoff and arrested landing technology, and is capable of carrying fixed-wing unmanned aircraft, helicopters, and amphibious equipment, etc. Since its first sea trial in November 2025, the Sichuan warship has been steadily conducting various maritime tests as planned, successfully completing the debugging of various equipment and overall operational stability tests.” Type 076 + GJ-21 Stealth Drone Swarm China’s Type 076 amphibious assault ship is being fitted with the GJ-21 stealth carrier-based UAV. Flying-wing design, fluidic thrust vectoring for autonomous carrier landings, electromagnetic catapult launch. Estimated 30 drones per ship, over 2-ton internal payload, ~2,000 km combat radius and 12+ hours endurance. Extremely low RCS allows deep stealth penetration to clear air defenses, airfields and anti-ship sites before troops even hit the beach. It can also act as loyal wingman with the J-35. Unlike the US “Lightning Carrier” concept of F-35B on amphibious ships, limited by vertical takeoff payload and range, plus the risk and cost of every manned jet; the Type 076 uses electromagnetic catapults and stealth UAV swarms for higher launch rate, longer reach, better endurance and zero pilot risk. This upgrades amphibious warfare from bloody beach assaults into non-contact, industrial-scale stealth suppression. China knows its priority building advanced defense capabilities for the people! Not war! #Type076 #GJ21 #StealthUAV #ChinaMilitary #PLANA #AmphibiousAssault #ElectromagneticCatapult #LoyalWingman #F35B #AmazingChina #PeopleFirst #NavalPower #DroneSwarm — GeoPaul626 (@Paull626) August 10, 2026 Global Times additionally quoted Chinese military analyst Song Zongping, who described the GJ-21’s flight operations from the Sichuan as a “global first” and compared it to the U.S. Navy’s X-47B program. “[The] US X-47B carrier-based drone program was designed for aircraft carriers, yet multiple technical constraints led to its cancellation. By contrast, the GJ-21 program has advanced steadily with an efficient development timeline,” Song told GT . However, the comparison requires some qualification: the X-47B was an experimental demonstrator that successfully completed a series of carrier-aviation milestones before the UCAS-D (Unmanned Combat Air System – Demonstrator) program concluded in 2015. The Navy subsequently redirected its follow-on unmanned-aircraft effort toward the CBARS (Carrier-Based Aerial-Refueling System) aerial-refueling role, which evolved into the MQ-25 Stingray. Song further added that the GJ-21 may also operate from China’s other EMALS carrier, the Fujian. He argued that this would help “building the technical know-how for China’s third aircraft carrier to host manned-unmanned teaming, expanding the operational modes of carrier strike groups.”   Pre-Commissioning Unit: China’s first Type 076 amphibious assault ship, PLANS Sichuan (Hull 51), has completed the deck marking, and its electromagnetic catapult system and arresting gear have been installed in place. #PLA #Navy #AmphibiousAssaultShip #Sichuan #EMALS #DroneCarrier #ChinaMilitary #ChinaMilBugle — China Military Bugle (@ChinaMilBugle) July 5, 2026 GJ-21 and Sichuan evolution The announcement provides official confirmation of a capability that had been the subject of considerable open-source speculation. Initial indications of an Electromagnetic Launch System (EMALS) aboard the Sichuan Landing Helicopter Dock (LHD) emerged from photographs taken during the ship’s construction and launch. Official images of the Sichuan’s introduction in the People’s Liberation Army Navy (PLAN) confirmed the catapult’s presence, but it was still not clear at the time whether it was meant for a drone. Open-source imagery and reporting provided further indications of progress, suggesting the Sichuan’s EMALS was tested with a sled load . Other imagery published between late 2025 and 2026 showed what appeared to be the GJ-21 flying with its arresting hook lowered , as well as a mockup of the tailless flying wing aircraft on the vessel and an image which appeared to show extended landing gear and a catapult launch bar .  Test de catapultage à charge morte du système EMALS à bord du navire d’assaut amphibie Type 076 Sichuan (51) https://t.co/lrfp5lwEDQ — East Pendulum (@HenriKenhmann) August 2, 2026 Subsequent official imagery confirmed that the Sichuan was fitted with a catapult and arresting system, with images showing the catapult being tested with trial loads . The Oct. 30 announcement now provides China’s first official confirmation that the ship has conducted takeoff and landing operations with the GJ-21. Leading Chinese military aviation researcher Andreas Rupprecht said on LinkedIn : “By late 2025, several GJ-21 aircraft were reportedly undergoing simulated EMALS launches and arrested landings at the PLAN’s land-based facility at Huangdicun. In early 2026, loading and deck-handling trials were conducted aboard the Sichuan using a mock-up.”  Type-076’nın EMALS testi https://t.co/AzCA7EuUkH — Enis Şenol (@senolenis) July 29, 2026 The GJ-21’s land-based variant, the GJ-11, had been officially unveiled in the 2019 parade. However, a section of China military watchers were still skeptical about whether the country will actually field a flying example of the GJ-11. Then, in November 2025, the GJ-11 suddenly appeared in an official video flying with a PLA Air Force J-20 and a J-16 , providing the first official visual confirmation of the drone in flight.

title: China-backed threat group used agentic AI pentesting tool to compromise 140 sensitive targets in 11 days
zh_title: 中国支持的威胁组织使用代理人工智能渗透测试工具在 11 天内入侵了 140 个敏感目标
summary: 据 CrowdStrike 称，一个中国国家支持的威胁组织正在使用 ARTEX（自动化代理 AI 渗透测试框架）在一场活动中取得了惊人的速度、规模和成功，该活动已在 11 天内入侵了约 140 个敏感目标。该安全公司在周四的威胁报告中表示，自 10 月 17 日以来，CrowdStrike 追踪的这个名为 Vapor Panda 的威胁组织已针对至少 14 个国家的 200 多个组织。目标和已确认的受害者包括外交部、欧洲国家总统府和总理办公室、国防和情报机构
content:
据 CrowdStrike 称，一个中国国家支持的威胁组织正在使用 ARTEX（自动化代理 AI 渗透测试框架）在一场活动中取得了惊人的速度、规模和成功，该活动已在 11 天内入侵了约 140 个敏感目标。该安全公司在周四的威胁报告中表示，自 10 月 17 日以来，CrowdStrike 追踪的这个名为 Vapor Panda 的威胁组织已针对至少 14 个国家的 200 多个组织。目标和已确认的受害者包括外交部、欧洲国家总统府和总理办公室、国防和情报机构；制药、半导体、国防、核能和金融领域的 19 个美国组织；以及美国、比利时和菲律宾的电信提供商。 CrowdStrike 告诉 Cyber​​Scoop，大约 70% 的 Vapor Panda 目标已被确认受到损害，或者有证据表明有一定程度的成功入侵的信心。 Vapor Panda 将 ARTEX 与 DeepSeek 配合使用，使其能够以惊人的速度完成更多任务（请求每 10 秒发生一次），并同时追求多个攻击路径。 CrowdStrike 反对手行动高级副总裁 Adam Meyers 告诉 Cyber​​Scoop：“这是我们第一次看到如此规模的代理对手民族国家威胁行为体，不幸的是，我认为我们可能会看到更多这种情况。”
CrowdStrike 在过去 15 年中跟踪的键盘操作活动通常每小时涉及多达 40 个命令。“现在，有了 ARTEX，我们可以看到每小时超过 1,500 个命令，”Meyers 说。他补充道：“如果你将目标分散到 200 个目标中，那么他们只需花费很少的成本即可开展大规模剥削活动并放弃网络销售。” “他们可以在更快的时间内击中更多目标。” Vapor Panda 的广泛访问活动仍然活跃，目标是国防、司法、金融和外交等领域的智囊团和政府机构。迈耶斯说：“我将其描述为一项多元化的行动任务，往往侧重于北京认为具有经济或政治重要性的部门和地区。” Vapor Panda 发起的活动与本月早些时候 Storm-0940 发起的 Microsoft Threat Intelligence ARTEX 活动不同，其中包括针对 ConnectWise 客户的供应链攻击。迈耶斯说，人工智能的对抗性使用相对较新，但也很快成为新常态。 “我们正在争先恐后，因为我们看到了太多这样的代理对手。”用于恶意目的的代理人工智能的使用量逐月以近三倍的速度增长。 CrowdStrike 在 9 月份观察到大约 45 起代理攻击，到 10 月份已经达到 126 起，并且还在不断攀升。
迈耶斯表示，代理人工智能的对抗性使用并不是一个棘手的问题，而是再次提醒人们，组织需要了解其端点、身份和跨域能力。这些攻击并没有展示任何新内容，“只是以我们不习惯的速度和规模进行攻击，”他说。 “这并不是绝望，但你必须采取行动。你不能把头埋在沙子里。”这个由中国支持的威胁组织使用代理人工智能渗透测试工具在 11 天内入侵了 140 个敏感目标，该组织首先出现在 Cyber​​Scoop 上。

【原文 English Original】
A China state-backed threat group is using ARTEX, the automated agentic AI penetration testing framework, to achieve remarkable speed, scale and success in a campaign that already compromised about 140 sensitive targets in 11 days, according to CrowdStrike.  The threat group, which CrowdStrike tracks as Vapor Panda, targeted more than 200 organizations in at least 14 countries since Oct. 17, the security company said in a threat report Thursday. Targets and confirmed victims include foreign ministries, a European country’s presidency and prime minister’s office, defense and intelligence agencies; 19 U.S.-based organizations in the pharmaceutical, semiconductor, defense, nuclear and financial sectors; and telecom providers in the United States, Belgium and the Philippines.  CrowdStrike told CyberScoop about 70% of Vapor Panda’s targets were confirmed compromised or had evidence indicating moderate confidence of a successful intrusion.  Vapor Panda’s use of ARTEX, paired with DeepSeek, allowed it to accomplish more tasks with shocking speed — requests occurring as often as every 10 seconds — and pursue multiple attack paths concurrently.  “This is the first time that we’re seeing an agentic adversary nation-state threat actor at this scale, and I think that this is probably, unfortunately, something we’ll see more of,” Adam Meyers, senior vice president of counter adversary operations at CrowdStrike, told CyberScoop. Hands-on-keyboard activity tracked by CrowdStrike for the past 15 years typically involved up to 40 commands per hour. “Now, with ARTEX, we could see it exceed 1,500 commands an hour,” Meyers said. “If you diversify that across 200 targets, it costs them very little to run a mass-exploitation campaign and drop a websell,” he added. “They can hit more targets in a faster period of time.” Vapor Panda’s broad-access campaign, which remains active, has targeted think tanks and government agencies spanning defense, justice, finance and diplomacy. “I would characterize it as a diverse operational mission that tends to focus on sectors and geographies that Beijing considers economically or politically important,” Meyers said. The active campaign attributed to Vapor Panda is separate from the ARTEX activity Microsoft Threat Intelligence attributed to Storm-0940 earlier this month, including a supply-chain attack targeting ConnectWise customers.  Adversarial use of AI is relatively new, yet also quickly becoming the new normal, Meyers said. “We’re scrambling because we’re seeing so many of these agentic adversaries.” Agentic AI use for malicious purposes is growing month-over-month at a rate of almost threefold. CrowdStrike observed roughly 45 agentic adversary attacks in September and it’s already at 126 for October, and climbing. Adversarial use of agentic AI isn’t an intractable problem, but rather another reminder that organizations need visibility into their endpoints, identities and cross-domain capabilities, Meyers said.  These attacks aren’t showcasing anything new, “it’s just doing it at a speed and scale that we’re unaccustomed to,” he said. “It’s not hopeless, but you’ve got to take action. You can’t put your head in the sand.” The post China-backed threat group used agentic AI pentesting tool to compromise 140 sensitive targets in 11 days appeared first on CyberScoop .

title: U.S.–PRC Competition Enters New Phase in Central Asia
zh_title: 中美竞争在中亚进入新阶段
summary: 执行摘要 美国国务卿马可·卢比奥最近对乌兹别克斯坦的访问标志着华盛顿为与北京在中亚竞争而采取的最具体的行动，特别是在关键矿产和互联互通方面。卢比奥强调，华盛顿不会强迫塔什干在美国和中华人民共和国之间做出选择，这与第一届特朗普政府更具对抗性的做法不同。美国对乌兹别克斯坦的接触仍然落后于中国的接触。就在卢比奥访问之前，中国宣布对乌兹别克斯坦投资 600 亿美元，而可能的投资额为 16 美元
content:
执行摘要 美国国务卿马可·卢比奥最近对乌兹别克斯坦的访问标志着华盛顿为与北京在中亚竞争而采取的最具体的行动，特别是在关键矿产和互联互通方面。卢比奥强调，华盛顿不会强迫塔什干在美国和中华人民共和国之间做出选择，这与第一届特朗普政府更具对抗性的做法不同。美国对乌兹别克斯坦的接触仍然落后于中国的接触。就在卢比奥访问之前，中国宣布对乌兹别克斯坦投资 600 亿美元，而美乌会议期间可能签署的交易额为 160 亿美元。同样的滞后现象也出现在美国的关键矿产优先领域。美国进口该地区约 2% 的关键矿产，而中国则进口近 50%。远离波斯湾和乌克兰的地缘政治热点，双重内陆的乌兹别克斯坦已成为美国和中华人民共和国之间竞争的新竞技场。 10月20日，美国国务卿卢比奥率200余人的美国企业代表团抵达撒马尔罕（达里奥10月14日电）。在该市历史悠久的中心广场上，卢比奥在讲话中表示，“我们现在就在这里”推进美国与乌兹别克斯坦的互联互通，就像历史上的丝绸之路通过该地区带来全球贸易一样（美国驻华大使馆，10 月 20 日）。
中国花了几十年的时间投资重振卢比奥提到的贸易路线。他在回应当地记者时承认“这是一场竞争”，但美国企业应该“有公平的机会参与竞争”（美国驻华大使馆，10 月 20 日）。北京预料到了华盛顿的示好，在卢比奥发表演讲三天前派遣总理李强前往塔什干。对于中国来说，乌兹别克斯坦是其连接欧亚大陆的重要合作伙伴。对于美国来说，该地区潜在的巨大关键矿藏提供了实现供应链多元化并减少其前沿技术行业对中国零部件依赖的机会（RFE/RL，10 月 21 日）。竞争掩盖了其他利益卢比奥的访问标志着自唐纳德·特朗普总统第一任期以来地区战略的变化。 2020 年，时任国务卿迈克·蓬佩奥 (Mike Pompeo) 提请人们注意中国虐待维吾尔人和哈萨克人的行为，认为这是中亚和中国之间潜在的隔阂（当前时间，2020 年 2 月 2 日）。最近夏天，当国务院试图迫使哈萨克斯坦在美国的 Pax Silica 计划和中国的世界人工智能合作组织之间做出选择时，对这种二元方法的担忧再次浮出水面（RFE/RL，9 月 17 日）。十月份的访问采取了一种不那么对抗性的方式。
卢比奥承认，“乌兹别克斯坦已经明确表示他们希望与所有人成为朋友”，但他表示，美国不希望强迫乌兹别克斯坦停止与其他国家对话或停止与其他国家合作（美国驻华大使馆，10 月 20 日）。这表明美国认识到中亚各国政府本身已成为更有能力的地缘战略参与者。他们现在可以有效地利用影响力，与比苏联解体以来任何时候都更广泛的参与者建立有利关系，包括他们之间的关系（《中亚时报》，9 月 23 日）。华盛顿正在寻求挑战

【原文 English Original】
Executive Summary U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio’s recent visit to Uzbekistan marked Washington’s most concrete push yet to compete with Beijing in Central Asia, especially on critical minerals and connectivity. Rubio emphasized that Washington would not force Tashkent to choose between the United States and the People’s Republic of China (PRC), unlike the more confrontational approach of the first Trump administration. U.S. outreach to Uzbekistan still trails PRC engagement. The PRC announced $60 billion in investment in Uzbekistan just before Rubio’s visit, as compared to a possible $16 billion in deals signed during the U.S.–Uzbekistan meetings. The same lag appears in the U.S. priority sector of critical minerals. The United States imports around 2 percent of the region’s critical minerals, while the PRC imports nearly 50 percent. Far from the geopolitical flashpoints of the Persian Gulf and Ukraine, double-landlocked Uzbekistan has become a new arena for competition between the United States and the People’s Republic of China (PRC). On October 20, U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio arrived in Samarkand, accompanied by an American business delegation totaling over 200 people ( Daryo , October 14). On the city’s historic central square, Rubio said in his speech that “we’re here now” to advance U.S.–Uzbekistan connectivity, just as the historic Silk Road brought global trade through the region ( U.S. Embassy in the PRC , October 20). The PRC has spent decades investing in reinvigorating the very trade routes Rubio invoked. He recognized in a response to a local journalist that “it’s a competition,” but that American businesses should “have a fair shot to compete” ( U.S. Embassy in the PRC , October 20). Anticipating Washington’s overtures, Beijing dispatched Premier Li Qiang (李强) to Tashkent three days before Rubio’s speech. For the PRC, Uzbekistan is a critical partner in its efforts to connect Eurasia. For the United States, the region’s potentially vast critical mineral deposits offer an opportunity to diversify supply chains and reduce its frontier technology sector’s dependence on Chinese components ( RFE/RL , October 21). Competition Overshadows Other Interests Rubio’s visit marked a change in regional strategy since President Donald Trump’s first term. In 2020, then-Secretary of State Mike Pompeo drew attention to the PRC’s mistreatment of Uyghurs and Kazakhs as a potential wedge between Central Asia and the PRC ( Current Time , February 2, 2020). Fears of this binary approach recently resurfaced in the summer when the State Department sought to force Kazakhstan to choose between the United States’s Pax Silica initiative and PRC’s World Artificial Intelligence Cooperation Organization ( RFE/RL , September 17). The October visit presented a less confrontational approach. Rubio acknowledged that “Uzbekistan has been clear that they want to be friends with everybody,” but said that the United States does not wish to force Uzbekistan to stop talking to somebody else or stop working with some other country ( U.S. Embassy in the PRC , October 20). This suggests a U.S. recognition that Central Asian governments have become more capable geostrategic players in their own right. They can now effectively wield leverage to gain favorable relations with a wider range of actors than at any point since the collapse of the Soviet Union, including among themselves ( Times of Central Asia, September 23). Washington is seeking to challenge Beijing’s dominance in Central Asia in critical minerals. After a regional minerals dialogue in 2024 and a White House summit in 2025, the United States signed a new investment framework with Uzbekistan in February 2026, targeting mineral exploration, extraction, and processing, along with plans for a joint investment company ( Reuters , February 18). Rubio’s visit was the next test of whether Washington could turn those ambitions into tangible investment. Nearly 300 representatives of American businesses accompanied him and announced potential deals worth around $12 billion ( Kun , October 25). Local media reports that almost 54 agreements were signed, including plans involving GE Aerospace, railway equipment manufacturer Wabtec, financial institutions such as Citigroup and BlackRock, and companies active in mineral development ( Gazeta , October 19). Surprisingly, the joint statement issued after the visit failed to mention critical minerals specifically. The statement emphasized supporting the development of Central Asian economies. It singled out the U.S. goal of helping Central Asia achieve its “export potential” by “developing innovative ways to increase value-added products within the region and [create] pathways to introduce these products to the international market” ( Department of State , October 19). It also added that the United States seeks to “foster a region where e-commerce flourishes, innovative solutions abound, and talented entrepreneurs thrive” by leveraging “secure and trusted technology, American technological excellence, and the growing technology sectors of Central Asia.” PRC–Central Asia Relations Exceed U.S. Outreach Even if realized, U.S. investments trail significantly behind the $60 billion that the PRC promised three days before the highly anticipated U.S. visit ( President of Uzbekistan , October 17). This disparity also shows up in the critical minerals sector. The United States imports just 2.1 percent of the region’s critical minerals, according to the Oxus Society’s Central Asia Resource Tracker, while the PRC imports almost 50 percent ( Oxus Society , accessed October 26). The pattern extends to broader trends in PRC–Central Asian trade, which topped $100 billion for the first time in 2025, of which Uzbekistan accounted for $16 billion ( Xinhua , January 18). In the broader region, the PRC is also the largest trade partner for isolated Iran and Afghanistan ( Ministry of Foreign Affairs , October 23, 2023). Model of the BYD Car Factory in Jizzakh Free Economic Zone displayed in the Tashkent Islamic Civilization Center (Source: Author’s photograph) Tashkent sees the PRC as being essential to its modernization. Beijing is investing in renewable energy and advanced manufacturing, and is spearheading major infrastructure projects such as the China–Kyrgyzstan–Uzbekistan railway ( Xinhua , October 18). During a recent visit to Tashkent, the authors saw how prominently these investments feature in the country’s vision for the future. Inside the lavish, marble-clad, $150 million Center for Islamic Civilization, exhibits showcase Chinese-backed projects across Uzbekistan, including a scale model of BYD’s auto factory in the southern Jizzakh region. The exhibits illustrated how much the Uzbek government is promoting the PRC’s investments as part of its broader development ambitions. During his meeting with Li Qiang on October 17, President Mirziyoyev described Uzbekistan–PRC relations as enjoying a “golden age,” a phrase he had previously used in conversations with General Secretary Xi Jinping. He also reaffirmed Tashkent’s support for the PRC’s One-China policy and Beijing’s efforts to combat what Chinese officials call the “three evil forces” of terrorism, separatism, and extremism ( South China Morning Post [SCMP] , October 18). In an interview with the South China Morning Post , Zhu Yongbiao (朱永彪), a regional specialist at Lanzhou University, emphasized the breadth of the PRC’s commercial offerings, ranging from electric vehicles and renewable energy to ordinary manufactures. He argued that Chinese firms could provide products and solutions suited to individual Central Asian markets, which is “an advantage the U.S. simply lacks” ( SCMP , October 18). Model of New Tashkent Displayed at the Center of Islamic Civilization in Tashkent (Source: Author’s photograph) Conclusion Chinese commentary on Rubio’s visit has so far combined recognition of Washington’s growing ambitions in Central Asia with skepticism about its capacity to act on them. In the lead-up to the trip, Zhang Jiadong (张家栋), a professor at Fudan University’s Center for American Studies, argued that the U.S. was merely a “distant friend” (远方朋友) to the region ( Global Times , October 19). Central Asian governments welcome Washington’s engagement because it gives them greater leverage with the PRC. Unless U.S. investment follows, though, Washington will remain a “distant friend,” lagging the PRC in influence and access.
