title: AI Lessons From Russia’s War in Ukraine
zh_title: 俄罗斯乌克兰战争中的人工智能教训
summary: 摘要：研究人工智能（AI）在俄罗斯乌克兰战争中的应用的中国军事作家得出的结论是，其决定性价值在于缩短杀伤链，而不是完全自主的武器。在他们的解读中，人工智能扮演着四个角色：将传感器数据转化为目标，加速规划和指挥，在干扰切断链路时使无人机保持在目标上，以及大规模生产宣传和深度伪造。这些角色都依赖于中国希望在国内控制的战斗数据、计算能力、芯片和人工智能模型。星链的战时限制
content:
摘要：研究人工智能（AI）在俄罗斯乌克兰战争中的应用的中国军事作家得出的结论是，其决定性价值在于缩短杀伤链，而不是完全自主的武器。在他们的解读中，人工智能扮演着四个角色：将传感器数据转化为目标，加速规划和指挥，在干扰切断链路时使无人机保持在目标上，以及大规模生产宣传和深度伪造。这些角色都依赖于中国希望在国内控制的战斗数据、计算能力、芯片和人工智能模型。星链的战时限制和俄罗斯对美国芯片的依赖都是警告。中国人民解放军 (PLA) 正在将这些经验教训转化为人工智能规划系统、无人部队以及国产大语言模型 (LLM) 的采购。一些人承认解放军的人工智能仍然主要用于辅助任务，这些作者承认这种学说落后于技术进步。编者注：本文是詹姆斯敦中国研究研究员 Sunny Cheung 撰写的关于俄罗斯乌克兰战争中中国教训的系列文章中的最新一篇。 8月2日，中央电视台播出了建军节系列纪录片《制胜》一集，展示了中国人民解放军空军的“智能打击计划系统”，使100多个战术单位能够进行同步打击（环球时报，8月3日）。
10月初，解放军中部战区部队开始从俄罗斯多国中心2026演习返回，无人机群向地面作战群提供精确的目标信息（环球时报，10月3日）。10月12日，国防大学联合作战学院的作者在《解放军报》上撰文称，人工智能（AI）已经“从作战辅助工具跃升为指挥保障系统的核心赋能引擎” （从作战保障辅助工具跃升为指挥系统的核心赋能引擎），以乌克兰的Delta和俄罗斯的Svod战斗管理系统为证（《解放军报》，10月12日）。这些事态发展表明，中国军事专家一直从俄罗斯乌克兰战争中汲取教训，他们认为这是对“智能化”战争（解放军的术语，即人工智能渗透到指挥和武器系统的战争）的首次重大考验。过去两年在军事期刊上发表的中国研究论文明确指出，人工智能对军事胜利的主要贡献是压缩杀伤链中从最初命令到执行打击的时间滞后。它通过协助完成四项主要任务来实现这一目标：寻找目标、做出决策、在干扰下进行打击以及发动认知战。
将数据转化为打击 中国研究人员对乌克兰作家所说的“滴滴打车”模式印象深刻，该模式以中国的 Uber 同类产品命名，在该模式中，小型部队通过战术应用程序接受零碎的打击命令，并报告执行情况。 2024 年 9 月，乌克兰国防部报告称，其“复仇者人工智能”平台通过分析无人机视频和固定目标，每周自动检测到约 12,000 个俄罗斯装备目标。相机，这给国防科技大学的研究人员留下了深刻的印象（乌克兰国防部，2024年9月23日；Zhang和Liang，2025年）。 [1] 华中科技大学教授、启元拉原首席战略研究科学家房超主导论文

【原文 English Original】
Executive Summary: Chinese military writers studying the use of artificial intelligence (AI) in Russia’s war in Ukraine have concluded that its decisive value lies in shortening the kill chain rather than in fully autonomous weapons. In their reading, AI plays four roles: turning sensor data into targets, accelerating planning and command, keeping drones on target when jamming cuts the link, and mass-produced propaganda and deep-fakes. Each of these roles rests on the combat data, computing power, chips, and AI models that the PRC wishes to control domestically. Starlink’s wartime restrictions and Russia’s reliance on U.S. chips serve as warnings. The People’s Liberation Army (PLA) is turning these lessons into AI planning systems, unmanned units, and procurement of domestic large language models (LLMs). Some concede that PLA’s AI is still used mainly for auxiliary tasks, with these authors acknowledging that doctrine lags technological advancements. Editor’s note: This article is the latest in an occasional series by Jamestown China Studies Fellow Sunny Cheung on Chinese lessons from Russia’s war in Ukraine. On August 2, China Central Television (CCTV) aired an episode of Zhisheng (制胜; “Victory”), an Army Day documentary series, showing a People’s Liberation Army (PLA) Air Force “intelligent strike-planning system” that enabled more than 100 tactical units to conduct synchronized strikes ( Global Times , August 3). In early October, troops from the PLA Central Theater Command began returning from Russia’s multinational Center 2026 exercise, where drone swarms fed precise target information to ground combat groups ( Global Times , October 3). And on October 12, authors from the National Defense University’s Joint Operations College wrote in the PLA Daily that artificial intelligence (AI) has “leapt from a combat auxiliary tool to the core enabling engine of the command-support system” (从作战辅助工具跃升为指挥保障体系的核心赋能引擎), citing Ukraine’s Delta and Russia’s Svod battle-management systems as proof ( PLA Daily , October 12). These developments show that Chinese military experts have consistently learned from Russia’s war in Ukraine, which they see as the first major test of “intelligentized” (智能化) warfare—the PLA’s term for war in which AI pervades command and weapons systems. Chinese research papers published in military journals over the last two years make clear that AI’s principal contribution to military victory is in compressing the time lag in a kill chain from the initial order to executing a strike. It does this by assisting with four primary tasks: finding targets, making decisions, striking under jamming, and waging cognitive warfare. Turning Data into Strikes Chinese researchers are impressed by what Ukrainian writers call the “Didi ride-hailing” (滴滴打车) model, named after the PRC’s Uber equivalent, in which small units accept piecemeal strike orders via tactical apps and report back when they have been carried out. In September 2024, Ukraine’s Defense Ministry reported that its “Avengers AI” platform automatically detected roughly 12,000 Russian equipment targets per week via analysis of video from drones and fixed cameras, something that impressed researchers at the National University of Defense Technology ( Ministry of Defense of Ukraine , September 23, 2024; Zhang and Liang, 2025).  [1] A paper led by Fang Chao (房超), a professor at Huazhong University of Science and Technology and former chief strategy research scientist at Qiyuan Laboratory (启元实验室), contends that the GIS Arta artillery app, a Ukrainian targeting app that matches artillery units with targets reported by drones and spotters, has slashed the time between receiving a fire order and striking a target from 20 minutes to just 30 seconds (Fang Chao et al., 2025).  [2] Researchers point to the whole process—from sifting through enormous volumes of drone and satellite feeds, to decoding intelligence gathered from intercepted communications and civilian tips, to the speed of target acquisition—as a model to emulate. Experts from the National University of Defense Technology believe that the PLA should treat private sector AI and big data capabilities as part of its arsenal, cataloguing them as “potential resources” (潜力资源) for conversion into military uses (Zhang and Liang, 2025).  [3] Li Chen (李晨) of Renmin University is more measured in his assessment, noting that although information-network operations and electronic warfare have figured heavily in the Ukraine conflict, they have not “paralyzed either side’s operational system” (未导致任何一方作战体系瘫痪) (Li Chen, 2025).  [4] Ultimately, he argues, the advantage from faster target identification has not been decisive. AI Making Decisions in the Command Post Several experts believe that AI will be instrumental in improving decision-making processes in future wars. An article in the journal Military Digest (军事文摘), for example, argues for the creation of “joint operations intelligent computing centers” (联合作战智算中心) and specialized large models trained on joint operations scenarios to deliver “dimension reduction strikes” (降维打击). This refers to attacks from a level of capability so far above the opponent’s that it cannot respond in kind, which could be used against “the U.S.-allied intelligentized combat system” (美盟智能化作战体系). In a future high-end conflict, the author writes, “what is fought over is information, what is fought with is algorithms, and what is contested is intelligence” (斗的是信息，打的是算法，争的是智能) (Li Zhongqiang, 2025).  [5] The PLA has made progress in using gathered intelligence in the decision-making process. The Global Times reported that the Air Force strike-planning system seen on CCTV can coordinate targets, formations, and successive waves of attack far more quickly than conventional planning ( Global Times , August 3). An aerospace editor at state-affiliated China Aerospace Daily reported the next day that intelligence gathered from PLA Air Force drones can be fed into an open-architecture system that relies on AI to evaluate it and “generate optimal operational plans in seconds or tens of seconds” ( Global Times , August 4). According to procurement records, PLA entities have issued tenders that explicitly call for tools based on DeepSeek and other domestically developed AI models, while university researchers use DeepSeek to examine battlefield scenarios and to improve drone-swarm targeting decisions ( Reuters , October 27, 2025; China Brief , October 27, 2025). However, members of the People’s Armed Police (PAP), the paramilitary police force under the command of the Central Military Commission, have acknowledged that PLA AI applications remain limited to auxiliary support functions such as answering queries and generating content, and lag foreign models in performance considerably. The application of AI in offensive combat remains at an exploratory stage (Li, Wu, and Wang, 2026).  [6] Experts at the PRC’s National Defense University see militaries moving toward a hybrid approach in which AI assists with various functions but humans make the final call (AI辅助推演、人类最终定夺)—something also referred to as “humans in the loop, machines speeding up” (人在回路、机在提速) ( PLA Daily , October 12). Ukraine’s new decision-support system Marichka is an early version of this kind of system. The same PLA Daily article voices fears, however, that if AI is integrated too deeply into decision mechanisms, “human-machine authority will be eroded in the pursuit of efficiency in war” (人机权责在战争中被效率侵蚀) ( PLA Daily , October 12). Mixed Views on Autonomy’s Decisiveness Autonomy addresses the problem of communications jamming. As Yang Zhen (杨震) of the China Electronics Standardization Institute wrote for the defense industry publication China Defense Conversion (中国军转民), “the core lesson of the Russia–Ukraine battlefield is that the electronic warfare environment determines the technology route” (俄乌战场的核心教训是电子战环境决定了技术路线), but fully autonomous use of lethal force is still far from being mainstream (Yang Zhen, accessed October 30, 2026).  [7] Autonomy is nevertheless widely understood to be potent, and Chinese defense-industry researchers have been quick to take note of the use of autonomy in Ukraine. An engineer at the 54th Research Institute of the China Electronics Technology Group Corporation (CETC) mentioned that Ukrainian forces now routinely use “last-mile” autonomy, in which a drone can identify a target, hone in on it, and make impact after communications with the operator are jammed. “Last-mile” autonomy boosts hit rates in a strike mission from 10–20 percent to 70–80 percent, and troops can learn to use the technology in under 24 hours (Hao Yunfeng, April 2025).  [8] Some PLA writers see autonomy as fully decisive. One author in the Military Digest urged the PLA to build forces around algorithms, stating that “algorithms are king, the system wins” (算法为王、体系制胜), and using Ukraine’s June 2025 Operation Spiderweb as evidence that “human-out-of-the-loop” (人在回路外) operations are increasingly common. Despite the piece’s enthusiasm, however, it makes unsupported claims about AI swarm coordination, and PLA doctrine lags behind its proposals (Liu Zhenggang, 2026).  [9] As authors from PLA Unit 63893 wrote in 2025, drone attack-and-defense theory in general “has not yet formed valuable combat guidance manuals or regulations” (尚未形成有价值作战指导手册、作战条例等) and called deeper research “a real and urgent task for us” (对我们来说是一项现实而紧迫的工作) (Liu Zhengtang et al., 2025).  [10] The PLA is instead focusing on building unmanned ground units and counter-drone capabilities. At the September 2025 military parade in Beijing, unmanned ground formations were described as capable of “remote control, autonomous action, and flexible grouping” (远程操控、自主行动、灵活编组) (Xinhua, September 5, 2025). In an exercise the following month, a PLA brigade trained counter-drone tactics, using equipment that could detect drones’ radio frequencies and match them to a catalog of more than 800 commercial drone models ( CSIS , October 7). Cognitive Warfare Offers Cheap Offensive Measures The fourth PLA use case for AI is deception. Military researchers have worked on deepfake technologies with the aim of deceiving, persuading, and shaping the cognitive battlefield. Deepfake technology is cheap—researchers at a Chinese military academy note that they can create a voice clone by using just a ten-second audio sample and that the cost of creating deepfakes has collapsed to the point that “the side defending against deepfakes always pays more than the side using them” (防御深度伪造技术的一方付出的代价总是要多于应用它的一方) (Gu Junwei et al., 2025).  [11] Rather than curbing deepfakes through detection, the paper recommends “offense as defense” (以攻代守), or the pre-emptive creation of deepfakes by the defensive side. By creating a flood of its own deepfakes, an army can seize the “cognitive high ground” (抢占认知域的高地). Doing so, the authors argue, will save money and prove effective. Another paper cites an example of Russian attempts to create low-quality websites that, when scraped for data to train large language models, pollute the dataset (Wang Ling et al., 2026).  [12] In this way, the authors argue, AI can be used to deceive the enemy, just as it is already used to deceive consumers. There is some debate about how effective these techniques can be. Writing in the PLA Daily earlier this year, an academic from the Academy of Military Sciences argued that AI enables more granular targeting of propaganda, turning propaganda wars from “flood irrigation” (漫灌) into more precise “drip irrigation” (滴灌) ( PLA Daily , April 13). By contrast, civilian scholars note that AI propaganda may not pay off. In Ukraine, they say, the sheer volume of AI-generated material led to massive fatigue and mistrust, and ultimately limited its influence (Shi and Huang, 2025).  [13] Fears of Hardware Dependencies The AI technologies empowering modern military capabilities rely on an array of software and hardware supply chains that are vulnerable. Chinese experts treat control of these resources as an essential military requirement. First, AI needs combat data for training. According to a Military Digest assessment of Russian military AI, Moscow started collecting combat data from unmanned combat systems in mid-2025 to train its AI models, which cannot be substituted by laboratories. Li Zhongqiang (李忠强), a PLA researcher, has called for “an all-army mechanism for reporting military training data samples” (全军军事训练数据样本上报机制) (Li, 2025).  [14] Second, AI needs hardware. The same Military Digest assessment notes that Nvidia’s Jetson Orin Nano, an edge AI computer, is used in Russia’s long-range Shahed drone, the MS001, while more than half of the key AI components in Russia’s unmanned systems are supplied by U.S. firms (Yuan Li et al., 2026).  [15] Third, AI needs networking. As Peking University researcher Pang Xun (庞珣) points out, SpaceX can unilaterally control the coverage area and functional scope of a sovereign state’s critical wartime infrastructure by deciding where its Starlink system is available (Pang and Qu, 2026).  [16] Gao Jixiang (高际香), a researcher at the Chinese Academy of Social Sciences, draws the conclusion from Russia’s experience of Western sanctions that only self-controlled AI can ensure the continuation and iteration of a nation’s AI system in the face of a blockade (Gao and Liu, 2026).  [17] Moscow has thus turned to its Chinese partners for assistance, with Sberbank cooperating on the “joint improvement and adaptation of open-source large language models” (开源大语言模型的共同改进和适配) ( S&T Daily , September 25, 2025). This assistance would be in conflict with Russia’s draft AI law, however, which excludes foreign software or components from its definition of “sovereign” models (Gao and Liu, 2026).  [18] Clearly, sovereignty is easier to claim than to achieve. Conclusion Chinese military writers interpret Russia’s war in Ukraine as one in which AI matters most as an accelerator—of targeting, planning, and strikes under jamming—and as a cheap amplifier of propaganda. They also observe that all of these innovations rest on data, chips, and networks that must be brought under national control. They are divided, however, on some of the other takeaways from the conflict. Some argue that the PLA should develop AI planning systems, unmanned formations, and domestically-produced large language models, while others argue that the PLA should focus instead on developing “upstream capabilities” (上游能力建设) such as intelligence, navigation, communications, and command-and-control, as well as operator training, arguing that these are better investments than drones (Huang and Yan, 2026).  [19] The establishment of a system-wide method for collecting training data, formation of special units to employ unmanned systems, and exercises designed to test unmanned systems in heavily-jammed environments are all worth watching out for in the coming months. After all, PLA officers are aware of the shortcomings of PLA doctrine, performance of AI models, and lack of combat experience, and Beijing wants to understand the war in Ukraine before having to fight its own. Li is vice dean of Renmin University’s School of International Studies. [5] Li Zhongqiang [李忠强]. “The Use of AI Algorithms in Joint Operations and Reflections” [人工智能算法在联合作战中的运用与思考]. China Defen s e Conversion [中国军转民], no. 14 (2026): 45–46. The authors are with the PAP Shandong Corps and the PAP Engineering University. title: PRC Escalates Political Warfare Against Philippines
zh_title: 中国升级针对菲律宾的政治战争
summary: 内容摘要：北京正在加紧针对菲律宾的政治战争。自2022年小费迪南德·马科斯政府上台以来，北京方面的紧张局势升级可能是因为它认为马尼拉在海上的自信和围绕台湾海峡的言论有所增强。中国政府于六月制裁了菲律宾国防部长吉尔伯托·“吉博”·特奥多罗，这是针对与其保持外交关系的国家的内阁官员采取的前所未有的举措。制裁阻止了任何降级的可能性，至少在特奥多罗离开他的职位之前是这样。是
content:
内容摘要：北京正在加紧针对菲律宾的政治战争。自2022年小费迪南德·马科斯政府上台以来，北京方面的紧张局势升级可能是因为它认为马尼拉在海上的自信和围绕台湾海峡的言论有所增强。中国政府于六月制裁了菲律宾国防部长吉尔伯托·“吉博”·特奥多罗，这是针对与其保持外交关系的国家的内阁官员采取的前所未有的举措。制裁阻止了任何降级的可能性，至少在特奥多罗离开他的职位之前是这样。北京的政治战也瞄准了菲律宾国内政治。菲律宾当局指责中华人民共和国（PRC）干涉选举，并与菲律宾副总统萨拉·杜特尔特（Sara Duterte）存在不当的财务联系。北京的回应是在菲律宾参议员弗朗西斯·托伦蒂诺提出中国干预选举的证据后对其进行制裁。中国行动的效果似乎有限。相反，这种影响力运动可能会煽动菲律宾民族主义，并推动该国与美国、日本和台湾走得更近。中华人民共和国正在升级针对菲律宾的政治战运动，以抹黑亲美派的名誉。总统小费迪南德·马科斯 (Ferdinand Marcos Jr.) 的政府，并促使一位更加包容主义的领导人在马尼拉 2028 年 5 月的总统选举中获胜。
马科斯于 2022 年当选，受到本国宪法的限制，任期为六年（《菲律宾共和国宪法》，1987 年 2 月 2 日）。近几个月来，中华人民共和国口头攻击菲律宾高级官员，制裁菲律宾国防部长，声称菲律宾巴丹群岛属于中国主权，并放大了支持马科斯政治对手之一的宣传言论。北京出于对马尼拉海上自信的愤怒而采取的策略可能会适得其反。它的行动将加剧该国已经面临的高度不信任，同时促使马尼拉与美国、日本和台湾走得更近。打制裁牌 长期以来，中国和菲律宾在南海主权争议问题上存在分歧。值得注意的是，中华人民共和国拒绝遵守 2016 年南海国际法庭做出的有利于马尼拉的裁决（中华人民共和国外交部 [MFA]，2016 年 7 月 12 日）。然而，两国历来都试图防止这些紧张局势破坏更广泛的双边关系。然而，近几个月来，中国对菲律宾采取了更强硬的态度，因为菲律宾采取了更加积极主动的防御姿态。马尼拉拒绝在南海问题上让步，深化与美国和日本的安全合作，并更加直言不讳地表达其对两岸和平的利害关系。
北京对国防部长吉尔伯托·“吉博”·特奥多罗保留了最严厉的待遇，认为他是马尼拉挑战其所谓“核心利益”的策划者。 6 月，特奥多罗在新加坡年度安全论坛香格里拉对话会上批评北京在其领海的侵略行为后，北京禁止他和他的家人进入中国领土并与中国实体开展业务（外交部，6 月 11 日）。 10 月，网易的一篇文章嘲笑特奥多罗是一位“可怜的支持率”的“代总统”，试图通过“创造一个低劣的支持率”来破坏总统府。

【原文 English Original】
Executive Summary: Beijing is ramping up its political warfare targeting the Philippines. Beijing’s escalation since the Ferdinand Marcos Jr. administration came to power in 2022 is likely due to what it perceives as Manila’s increased maritime assertiveness and comments surrounding the Taiwan Strait. The Chinese government sanctioned Philippine defense minister Gilberto “Gibo” Teodoro Jr. in June, an unprecedented step against a cabinet official of a country with whom it maintains diplomatic relations. The sanctioning forecloses any deescalation, at least until Teodoro leaves his position. Beijing’s political warfare is also targeting domestic Philippine politics. Philippine authorities have accused the People’s Republic of China (PRC) of election interference and of improper financial links with Philippine vice president Sara Duterte. Beijing’s response has been to sanction Philippine senator Francis Tolentino after he presented evidence of PRC electoral interference. The efficacy of the PRC’s actions appears limited. Instead, the influence campaign is likely stoking Philippine nationalism and pushing the country closer to the United States, Japan, and Taiwan. The People’s Republic of China (PRC) is escalating its political warfare campaign against the Philippines in a bid to discredit the pro-U.S. government of President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. and enable the victory of a more accommodationist leader in Manila’s May 2028 presidential election. Elected in 2022, Marcos is limited by his country’s constitution to a single six-year term ( Constitution of the Republic of the Philippines , February 2, 1987). In recent months, the PRC has verbally attacked senior Philippine officials, sanctioned the Philippine defense minister, claimed that the Philippines’ Batanes archipelago is under Chinese sovereignty, and amplified propaganda narratives that support one of Marcos’s political rivals. Beijing’s gambit, driven by anger with Manila’s maritime assertiveness, is likely to backfire. Its actions will aggravate the high levels of distrust it already faces in the country while pushing Manila closer to the United States, Japan, and Taiwan.   Playing the Sanctions Card The PRC and the Philippines have long been at odds over conflicting South China Sea claims. Notably, the PRC has refused to abide by a 2016 South China Sea international tribunal ruling in favor of Manila ( PRC Ministry of Foreign Affairs [MFA] , July 12, 2016). Yet both countries have historically sought to prevent those tensions from undermining the broader bilateral relationship. In recent months, however, the PRC has taken a hard line against the Philippines for its more proactive defense posture. Manila has refused to yield in the South China Sea, deepened security cooperation with the U.S. and Japan, and become more outspoken about its stake in cross-Strait peace. Beijing has reserved the harshest treatment for Defense Secretary Gilberto “Gibo” Teodoro Jr., whom it sees as the architect of Manila’s challenges to its so-called “core interests.” In June, after Teodoro criticized Beijing’s aggressiveness in its territorial waters at the Shangri-La Dialogue, an annual security forum in Singapore, Beijing banned him and his family from entering PRC territory and doing business with PRC entities ( MFA , June 11). In October, a NetEase article mocked Teodoro as an “acting president” (代总统) with “pitiful approval ratings” (可怜的支持率) trying to undermine the Presidential Palace by “creating a separate policy towards China” (制定另一套对华政策) ( NetEase News , October 15). While largely symbolic, the sanctions are still significant. They marked the first time Beijing has targeted a sitting cabinet official of a country whom it diplomatically recognizes. By defining the Philippine defense secretary as a direct geopolitical adversary, Beijing has closed off a key de-escalation ramp with Manila until he leaves his position.  [1] The PRC, meanwhile, may double down on the sanctions tool. In October, Chinese-language Philippine media, citing “well-informed sources,” warned that Beijing is “running out of patience” (失去耐心) with Manila. Among measures to punish the Philippines being considered is sanctioning a group of Filipino politicians considered “anti-China.” The article further stated that if the Philippines allows Taiwan to open a representative office in Cebu, Beijing could demand that Manila close some of its consulates in the PRC, including the one in Hong Kong ( Chinese Commercial News , October 21).  Claiming the Batanes In some cases, the PRC aims to pressure the Philippines through lower-level unofficial channels. For instance, at a June 30 academic symposium in Guangzhou, academics from Jinan University, Nanjing University, and the Chinese Academy of Social Sciences argued that the northernmost Philippine island province of Batanes, which is about 88 miles from Taiwan, belongs to the PRC. To support this argument, they claimed that the archipelago is a natural geographic extension of Taiwan that was governed by the Ming and Qing dynasties. The academics said that the symposium was convened in direct response to the launch of maritime delimitation negotiations between the Philippines and Japan ( South , July 2).   The National Historical Commission of the Philippines swiftly refuted the Chinese scholars’ claims about the Batanes, noting that Spanish records from 1687 show no Chinese governance, that Spain claimed the archipelago in 1783, and that the islands have long been considered part of the Philippines ( Philippine Daily Inquirer , July 10). PRC media commentaries suggest the Batanes claim is not just a response to maritime delimitation discussions Beijing opposes, but also reflects more deeply-seated security anxieties. Highlighting recent U.S.-Philippines military cooperation in the Batanes, a July commentary published by the Jiangxi provincial government said, “Holding a knife to China’s doorstep and calling it ‘defense’—that’s Manila’s real intention” (把刀子架在中国家门口，还说是“防御”。这就是马尼拉的真实算盘) It further accused the Philippines of using the Batanes as “a springboard for intervening in the Taiwan Strait” (干预台海的跳板) ( Sohu , July 15). Political Interference Arguably Beijing’s most aggressive political warfare moves against the Philippines are its direct interference in Manila’s domestic politics. In April 2025, Senator Francis Tolentino presented evidence during a Senate hearing linking the Chinese embassy in Manila to online disinformation campaigns against the Philippine government ahead of midterm elections the following month ( Philippine Daily Inquirer , April 24, 2025). That prompted President Marcos to order an investigation into the alleged election interference. The PRC’s foreign ministry spokesperson rejected these claims, insisting that it “adheres to the principle of non-interference in the internal affairs of other countries” (一贯奉行不干涉内政原则) ( PRC MFA , April 24, 2025). It subsequently sanctioned Tolentino, barring him and his family from entering the PRC and any business dealings with Chinese entities ( PRC MFA , July 1, 2025). New allegations have emerged that suggest deepening PRC meddling in Philippine politics. In October 2026, Manila’s National Security Council said that it would investigate reports of remittances totaling Philippine Peso (PHP) 319 million ($4.8 million) sent from the PRC to a company linked to the husband of Vice President Sara Duterte ( Daily Tribune , October 8). Duterte, the daughter of former president Rodrigo Duterte, is a political rival of Marcos, despite serving as vice president in his administration (In the Philippines, the offices of president and vice president are elected separately.) After the allegations surfaced, Sara Duterte was accused of improperly amassing wealth and impeached. Her trial is expected to run through December ( Philippine News Agency , October 27). Duterte denies the allegations, claiming the Marcos administration is using them to sideline a political rival ( Davao Today , October 7). Duterte’s public comments suggest, at a minimum, that she favors a more accommodating PRC policy than Marcos. She has consistently advocated for a less assertive stance on maritime sovereignty issues. At a recent press conference, she said that the Philippines is “becoming a troublemaker in Southeast Asia,” echoing PRC propaganda ( ABS-CBN , October 14). When Marcos warned that the allegations against her could constitute a grave national security threat, she said that the president’s statement “is a bold and dangerous challenge to China” ( OneNews , October 13). Chinese media has been supportive of Duterte. A Chinese scholar quoted by Global Times said “she holds relatively pragmatic stances,” in contrast to the Marcos administration’s “increasingly radical China policy” ( Global Times , October 13). Conclusion The PRC has intensified its political warfare campaign against the Philippines in recent months to undermine the Marcos administration, underscore its sweeping maritime territorial claims, and lend support to Filipino politicians it sees as friendlier to its interests. Yet thus far, Beijing’s strategy has failed to bear fruit.  Instead, the PRC’s heavy-handed tactics have stoked Philippine nationalism, allowed Manila to strengthen its alliance network, and exposed the vulnerability of Marcos’s Beijing-friendly political rivals. Even if Sara Duterte is found not guilty in her impeachment trial, her alleged close ties to the PRC and accommodationist approach to Beijing will be heavily scrutinized if she runs for president in 2028. Notes [1] The PRC has sanctioned other politicians, such as Tom Tugendhat in the United Kingdom and Marco Rubio in the United States, but only before they were promoted to cabinet-level positions. And since sanctioning Teodoro Jr., Beijing has also sanctioned two more cabinet-level politicians: Francis Fonseca, Belize’s foreign minister, and Gustavo Villate, Paraguay’s minister of information and communication technologies. However, the PRC lacks official diplomatic relations with Belize and Paraguay due to their official recognition of Taiwan. content: Binance，全球最大的加密货币交易所，在黑客入侵其数字钱包并盗取约 60 亿美元（89 亿美元）后，已暂停提现服务，这似乎是迄今为止最大的加密货币盗窃案。 该交易所周五表示，已开始追回受影响的资产，并继续与执法机构和区块链情报公司合作，以追踪更多资金。 Binance，全球最大的加密货币交易所，遭到疑似朝鲜黑客袭击，成为世界最大规模的盗窃案。Adobe Stock 初步调查显示，此次黑客攻击是通过一名工程师的笔记本电脑进行的，“这使得攻击者能够访问服务容器并提交未经授权的提现交易”，Binance 周四晚间表示。 根据多家加密货币追踪公司的区块链证据，此次黑客攻击起源于朝鲜。 一支由加密货币公司组成的团队成功冻结了约 30 亿美元（43 亿美元）的被盗赃款，并在与黑客的激烈争夺中努力寻找和控制这些数字资金。 Binance 联席首席执行官 Richard Tend 在 X 上表示，此次攻击并非“一键”操作，而是一个复杂的过程。调查尚未将责任归咎于任何个人，也未发现任何钱包私钥泄露的证据。 Binance 表示将用公司资金和紧急资产基金覆盖所有损失，并强调“用户资金是安全的”。 Binance 联席首席执行官 Richard Tend 在 X 上表示，此次攻击并非“一键”操作，而是一个复杂的过程。AP 该加密货币交易所表示，已暂时暂停存款和提现服务，以便完成安全检查，并让区块链情报合作伙伴追踪和追回资金。该加密货币交易所预计周日早晨恢复提现服务。 比特币和以太币，即交易量最大的两种加密货币，在 Binance 泄露消息公布后暴跌，但在周五中午前后于香港市场恢复部分跌幅，交易价格较此前下跌约 2%-3%。 而在华尔街，加密货币行业股票在黑客袭击后暴跌，比特币价格从本月早些时候的 8.6 万美元以上跌至接近 7.7 万美元。 Coinbase Global 股价下跌 13%，尽管其最新一季度的业绩强于分析师预期。Strategy 公司表示其持有比特币总供应量的约 4%，股价下跌 7.5%。该公司也表示其最新一季度的利润强于分析师预期，同时表示其首席财务官将于下周因个人原因辞职。 多家情报机构指向朝鲜 加密货币追踪公司 TRM Labs 根据“强大的链上和链下情报”将此次盗窃案归因于一个精英朝鲜黑客单位，并指出“此次攻击的多个特征与之前的朝鲜关联盗窃案相符”。 另一家总部位于新加坡的区块链追踪公司 Pangolin Intelligence 也表示，认为此次盗窃案是由一个朝鲜黑客单位所为。 一位不愿透露姓名的 Pangolin Intelligence 分析师表示，通过分析与此次黑客攻击相关的链上活动，并结合此前已知事件收集到的信息，得出了这一结论。 Pangolin Intelligence，另一家总部位于新加坡的区块链追踪公司，也表示认为此次盗窃案是由一个朝鲜黑客单位所为。Getty Images/iStockphoto Pangolin Intelligence 的一位分析师告诉 CNN，表示“我认为猫鼠游戏才刚刚开始”，并补充称朝鲜可能正准备利用一个洗钱组织网络，试图变现被盗资金。 另一家加密货币追踪公司 Chainalysis 表示，正在监控被盗资金“在多个区块链上流动”，包括比特币和以太坊。Chainalysis 的一位发言人告诉 CNN，该公司对朝鲜是此次黑客攻击的幕后黑手“非常有信心”。 CNN 已联系朝鲜驻联合国代表团寻求评论。平壤此前曾否认黑客指控。 ‘将他们绳之以法’ 与股票交易平台不同，加密货币交易所往往代用户持有数字资产，这使得它们更容易受到黑客和盗窃的侵害，尤其是在该行业监管尚不完善的背景下。 在过去对大型加密货币盗窃案的调查中，FBI 曾有一支待命的分析师团队，负责冻结部分资金。 FBI 周五发表声明称，它“已了解此事，并与相关的公共和私人合作伙伴合作，以了解活动范围、评估潜在影响，并协调适当的调查步骤”。 美国联邦调查局（负责调查网络犯罪）的一位发言人表示，该机构的“调查人员正与我们的私营部门合作伙伴彻夜工作，包括 Circle[公司推出的美元挂钩稳定币 USDC]，以识别、冻结、追踪和追回周四从 Binance 被盗的资金。我们还在与美国哥伦比亚特区检察官办公室和执法合作伙伴密切协调，以识别负责的网络犯罪分子并将其绳之以法。” 朝鲜黑客此前被指控犯下创纪录的加密货币盗窃案，当时他们涉嫌从另一家主要加密货币交易所 Bybit 盗取 15 亿美元。nna\april.glover 如果朝鲜被证实是罪魁祸首，美国执法官员和私人专家对此都不会感到意外。 朝鲜黑客此前被指控犯下创纪录的加密货币盗窃案，当时他们涉嫌从另一家主要加密货币交易所 Bybit 盗取 15 亿美元。 在那次事件中，攻击者在几分钟内盗取的金额相当于朝鲜报告年度国内生产总值的很大一部分。 根据现任和前任美国及韩国官员的说法，朝鲜强大的黑客团队是该受制裁、遭受制裁的政权的重要收入来源。 根据联合国和私营公司的报道，朝鲜关联黑客在过去几年内从银行和加密货币公司盗取了数十亿美元。 Binance 重回聚光灯下 Binance 于 2017 年由加拿大籍人士 Changpeng Zhao 共同创立，在推出后一年内成为世界上最大的加密货币交易平台。 Changpeng Zhao，Binance Holdings Ltd 联合创始人但已辞去 CEO 职务，他表示用户资金将免受此次黑客攻击影响。Chan Long Hei/Bloomberg/Getty Images via CNN Newsource 然而，Zhao 于 2023 年在承认违反美国反洗钱法后辞职。 他被判处四个月联邦监禁，并于去年 10 月获得前总统唐纳德·特朗普的赦免。 Zhao 不再管理该平台，但仍是其最大股东，他在 X 上表示，用户资金将完全由交易所覆盖，并反驳了与此事相关的任何相反说法，此前他与 Elon Musk 在 X 上发生争执。 由 CNN 和美联社报道。

title: 24 岁中国留学生遭男友毒手身亡，生前曾资助其生活，遗体发现 41 处伤痕，此类悲剧频发

content: 在海外留学，感情往往是生活中很重要的一部分。 离开熟悉的家庭和朋友圈，来到一个陌生的国家，身边能说得上话的人不多。一段感情带来的陪伴，有时会让人觉得终于有了依靠。 但当亲密关系开始出现控制、威胁甚至暴力，原本的陪伴也可能变成危险。 2016年，24岁的中国女生毕习习在英国卡迪夫遭男友殴打致死。她身上共有41处损伤，长期遭受暴力的痕迹也出现在尸检报告中。 十年过去，类似的悲剧仍在发生。2026年10月，英国伦敦法院又对一起中国女性遭前男友杀害的案件作出判决。 在异国他乡，一旦亲密关系演变成持续的控制和暴力，受害者可能面临比想象中更复杂的困境。 24岁中国留学生遇害，身上41处伤痕 毕习习出生于南京，她精通四门语言，语言天赋与学习能力令人钦佩。15岁那年，她便凭借自身努力与优秀，远赴牛津开启求学之旅。 大学毕业后，她又毅然前往卡迪夫大学，攻读国际商务硕士学位，那时的她，未来之路铺满了希望与可能，前途一片光明璀璨。 2015年，她在当地酒吧找了一份兼职，当是体验别样生活的一种途径，就是这段经历，却断送了她年轻的生命。 在打工期间，酒吧里的保安马修斯对她持续不断的热情，以及始终如一的坚持，渐渐攻破了她的心防，两人随后发展为恋人并开始同居。 马修斯的经济状况并不稳定。交往期间，毕习习承担了两人的房租和日常开销，也经常为男友支付其他费用。 但一味地付出，反而让这段关系逐渐失去了平衡。 马修斯对小毕的依赖与日俱增，甚至到了理直气壮伸手向她索要金钱的地步。 一旦小毕因为繁重的课业压力或者自身经济上的捉襟见肘而拒绝他的要求，他便会瞬间变脸，用暴力来宣泄自己的不满。 第一次遭受暴力，仅仅是因为她上课时，没能及时回复马修斯那句“你帮我买个饭”的消息。 据案件审理期间披露的信息，马修斯长期对毕习习实施身体暴力和言语羞辱。 她的亲友注意到，她的状态与过去相比发生了明显变化，脸上的淤青也曾引起旁人怀疑。为了遮掩伤痕，她开始化浓妆。 但这段关系并没有因此结束。 2016年8月，马修斯要求毕习习向家里要钱为自己购买宝马汽车。遭到拒绝后再次对毕习习施暴，最终导致她死亡。救援人员赶到时，她已经没有生命体征。 尸检显示，毕习习全身有41处损伤，包括下颌骨骨折、多根肋骨断裂以及大面积瘀伤。 部分伤势处于不同的愈合阶段，表明她此前可能已经遭受过多次暴力。 案件审理期间，马修斯试图以过失杀人等说法为自己辩解，还声称毕习习使用约会软件，引发了他的愤怒。 但警方调查后发现，根本没有任何小毕出轨的证据，反而看到小毕在这段关系里，不管是经济上还是情感上，都一心一意地付出，从来没有背叛过。 2017年2月17日，英国法院做出了最终判决：马修斯谋杀罪成立，判无期徒刑，最低得服刑18年。 这场“爱情”最后变成了一场悲剧。 十年后的今天，又发生一次类似案件 2026年10月，英国伦敦中央刑事法院对中国女性柯晓清遭杀害一案作出判决。 39岁的柯晓清在国内独自抚养两个孩子，赴英后曾在南安普顿生活，之后搬到伦敦。 她与24岁的印度籍男子迪帕克·桑杜交往后，逐渐发现对方存在欺骗和侵占财物等问题。 庭审信息显示，桑杜曾偷走她的钱财，并有控制其手机、护照等行为。 2025年8月，柯晓清提出分手，并要求对方归还欠款。 但分手没有让骚扰停止。 2025年12月，桑杜以归还欠款等理由接近柯晓清，随后持刀袭击她，造成38处刀伤。 行凶后，他更换手机卡并购买机票，试图离开英国，最终在前往机场的途中被警方抓获。 2026年10月，陪审团裁定桑杜谋杀及妨碍司法公正罪名成立。法院判处其终身监禁，最低服刑28年后才可申请假释。 每当类似案件发生，外界很容易把注意力放在受害者身上，追问她们为什么没有早点离开。 但长期处于暴力关系中的人，往往面对着比旁人想象中更复杂的处境。 一段关系开始时，未必就伴随着明显的暴力。对方可能先表现得体贴、热情，随后逐渐干涉日常生活，要求随时回复消息，限制与朋友来往，甚至通过贬低和威胁，让另一方不断怀疑自己。 当控制越来越严重，受害者可能已经习惯了为对方的行为找理由，也可能担心分手后遭到报复。 对留学生而言，异国生活还会增加一些现实困难。 语言不熟练、不清楚当地法律和求助渠道、身边缺少可以立即联系的亲友，都可能让人更难应对突发状况。有些人担心把感情问题告诉家人，会引发争执；也有人害怕报警后影响学业、签证或个人生活，于是选择暂时忍耐。 留学生遭遇到类似情况一定要保护自己 此前一项针对澳大利亚女性国际学生的研究访谈了30名来自16个国家的学生，其中23人表示曾经历亲密关系暴力。研究指出，社会孤立是受访者寻求帮助时面临的突出障碍之一。 跨国恋爱本身没有问题。不同国家、不同文化背景的人建立感情关系，是再正常不过的事。真正需要关注的，是一个人在相处过程中如何对待伴侣。 尤其需要记住，第一次出现暴力时，不必等到下一次发生，才证明这段关系有问题。 推搡、扇耳光、威胁伤害，以及以自伤相逼迫，都不应该被当成普通的情侣争执。 如果已经出现危险信号，优先考虑安全，比试图改变对方更重要。 在澳大利亚，遇到紧急危险时可以拨打000；在英国，紧急情况下可以拨打999。身处其他国家时，应提前了解当地的紧急求助号码。学校的学生服务部门、国际学生支持团队，以及所在地区的相关援助机构，也可能提供实际帮助。 如果担心语言沟通困难，可以提前了解当地的翻译服务。不要因为英语不够流利，或者不确定事情是否严重，就放弃寻求帮助。 对于身边的人来说，发现朋友突然变得沉默、频繁遮掩伤痕，或者明显与原有社交圈疏远时，也可以主动关心。与其急着批评她的选择，不如先让她知道，自己愿意倾听，也愿意在她需要时提供帮助。 毕习习案已经过去近十年，柯晓清案也有了法院判决。 但刑罚无法挽回逝去的生命，更无法消除留给家人的伤痛。 对在海外学习和生活的人而言，感情可以慢慢了解，关系也可以随时重新评估。无论对方来自哪个国家，都不应该以爱为理由限制你的自由，更不应该让你生活在恐惧之中。 如果一段关系已经让你感到害怕，离开并不是失败。 保护自己，也不需要向任何人证明理由。

title: Hanwha Philly Shipyard to Build Navy Landing Ship Mediums

content:
据船舶建造经理周五发布的公告称，LST-100 韩华费城造船厂已赢得价值 2.69 亿美元的合同，用于建造海军陆战队中型登陆舰。 TOTE Services 在 7 月份赢得了价值 22 亿美元的合同，担任 LSM 船舶建造经理，并在 7 月份提出征求建议书后将合同授予韩华。 TOTE 新闻稿中写道：“韩华防务美国公司 (HDUSA) 是通过该流程选出的第一家造船商，因为其具有竞争力的定价以及对 TOTE Services 分包合同条款和条件的接受。” “该合同涵盖在韩华费城造船厂 (HPSI) 建造一艘价值 2.69 亿美元的 LSM，并可选择另外建造三艘船舶。”位于墨西哥湾沿岸的 Bollinger Shipyards 已签订建造第一艘 LSM 的合同。威斯康星州的 Fincantieri Marinette Marine 公司今年早些时候赢得了一份为四艘船提供长铅项目的合同。据该公司称，TOTE 的 LSM 合同涉及多达八艘船。新闻稿中写道：“TOTE Services 继续与 Bollinger Shipyards 和 Fincantieri Marinette Marine 进行富有成效的合同讨论，这两家船厂都根据 VCM 合同指导造船厂，预计将在建造 LSM 船队方面发挥有意义的作用。”这是海军第一次选择使用船舶建造经理来代表海军运行该计划。
USNI 新闻图片 由于海军和海军陆战队就该舰的设计和生存能力展开争论，LSM 项目多年来一直面临着需求波动。该平台是海军陆战队当前在西太平洋对抗中国战略的重要组成部分，较小的海军陆战队部队将在岛屿和海岸线之间移动，建立临时基地，从那里可以发射反舰导弹。 LSM基于Damen LST-100概念，这是一种出口导向型坦克登陆舰设计，目前在尼日利亚海军服役，也计划在澳大利亚皇家海军服役。据 USNI News 此前报道，海军以 1700 万美元的价格购买了该设计包。 TOTE 已经在管理韩华费城造船厂正在建造的另一个项目——美国海事管理局的国家安全多任务船只。去年，唐纳德·特朗普总统访问韩国后，白宫宣布了与韩国的贸易协议概要。该协议包括韩国承诺向美国造船业投资 1500 亿美元。

【原文 English Original】
LST-100 Hanwha Philly Shipyard has won a $269 million contract to build the Marine Corps’ Landing Ship Medium, according to a Friday announcement from the program’s vessel construction manager. TOTE Services, which won a $2.2 billion contract in July to function as the LSM vessel construction manager, awarded Hanwha the contract after putting out a request for proposals in July. “Hanwha Defense USA (HDUSA) is the first shipbuilder selected through that process, based on its competitive pricing and acceptance of TOTE Services’ subcontract terms and conditions,” reads a TOTE news release. “The award covers construction of one LSM, valued at $269 million, at Hanwha Philly Shipyard (HPSI), with options for three additional vessels.” Gulf Coast-based Bollinger Shipyards is already on contract to build the first LSM. Fincantieri Marinette Marine out of Wisconsin won a contract earlier this year for long lead items for four ships. TOTE’s LSM contract is for as many as eight ships, according to the company. “TOTE Services continues productive contract discussions with Bollinger Shipyards and Fincantieri Marinette Marine, both directed shipyards under the VCM contract, which are expected to play a meaningful role in building the LSM fleet,” reads the release. This is the first time the Navy has opted to use a vessel construction manager, which runs the program on behalf of the service. USNI News graphic The LSM program has faced years of requirements churn as the Navy and Marine Corps debated the ship’s design and survivability. The platform is a crucial component of the Marine Corps’ current strategy for countering China in the Western Pacific, where smaller units of Marines would move around between islands and shorelines to set up ad-hoc bases from which they could fire anti-ship missiles. The LSM is based on the Damen LST-100 concept, an export-oriented tank landing ship design currently in service with the Nigerian Navy and also planned for the Royal Australian Navy. The Navy bought the design package for $17 million, USNI News previously reported. TOTE is already managing another program under construction at Hanwha Philly Shipyard – the U.S. Maritime Administration’s National Security Multi-Mission Vessel. Last year, the White House announced the outlines of a trade deal with South Korea following President Donald Trump’s visit to the country. That deal included a pledge from South Korea to put $150 billion into American shipbuilding.

title: 刘建超被开除党籍：比秦刚重，却不说他做了什么

content: 茉莉花深度报道 文 / 孙亦然 中国政情撰稿人 中共二十届五中全会10月29日闭幕，公报第一次证实前中联部部长刘建超出了事：中纪委认定他严重违纪违法，中央政治局此前已开除他的党籍。他做了什么，公报没有说。 原始文件 网页 中国共产党第二十届中央委员会第五次全体会议公报 news.cn 打开 网页 中国共产党章程 news.cn 打开 网页 中华人民共和国公职人员政务处分法 npc.gov.cn 打开 要点 查明 刘建超去年7月30日在阿尔及利亚公开露面以后，再没有出现；9月底，中联部官网显示刘海星已接任部长。 查明 按中共党内的规定，开除中央委员的党籍要由全会三分之二以上多数决定；刘建超的党籍是政治局先开除、五中全会再追认，政治局作出时没有宣布。 查明 五中全会追认开除33人，比四中全会多19人；出席的中央委员和候补中央委员只有279人，是二十大选出人数的74%。 还不知道 刘建超到底做了什么，有没有被降为处级——公报只写了严重违纪违法，没有说是泄密、转移资产、贪腐还是别的问题。 我们的判断 到2027年6月30日，官方不会公布刘建超的具体违纪违法事实。这是因为，政治局开除他时没有宣布，全会追认时也只列了名字。 2024年7月，中共二十届三中全会「接受秦刚同志辞职申请」，免去这位前外长的中央委员职务，公报里他仍是「同志」。两年多以后，五中全会公报写到前中联部部长刘建超，用的词换成了「严重违纪违法问题」和「开除党籍处分」：中纪委关于他的审查报告获得通过，中央政治局此前开除他党籍的决定得到确认。从去年7月底他不再公开露面算起，官方沉默了一年多，这一次究竟交代了多少？ 只交代了结论。开除党籍是党内的最高处分，按官方记录，刘建超受到的处理比秦刚重得多；可是政治局哪一天作出这个决定、他做了什么、会不会被追究刑事责任，公报一个字也没写。外界知道的他被查的原因，全部来自未经证实的说法。 从外交部、中纪委到中联部 1964年2月出生的刘建超是吉林德惠人，资深外交官出身。2008年北京奥运期间，他以外交部发言人的身份开始受到注意；2009年3月中菲关系高度紧张之际，他由外交部新闻司司长调任驻菲律宾大使，之后改任驻印度尼西亚大使，2013年11月升任外交部部长助理。 2015年8月，他离开外交部进入纪检系统，任国家预防腐败局副局长（专职，副部长级）和中央纪委国际合作局局长，并担任中央反腐败协调小组国际追逃追赃工作办公室负责人，中央社形容这次任命「出人意料」。2017年4月，他出任浙江省委常委、省纪委书记，同年7月兼任浙江省监察委员会主任。2018年3月，他回到外事系统，任中央外事工作委员会办公室副主任；2022年5月接替宋涛出任中联部部长，同年10月进入二十届中央委员会。中央社、美国之音和香港01都报道过，他是下任外长的热门人选；美国之音还说，他也有望接替杨洁篪出任中央外办主任。 刘建超最后一次出访是在7月下旬：7月23日至24日在新加坡，25日至27日在约翰内斯堡出席解放运动峰会，28日至30日在阿尔及利亚。据中央社报道，他最后一次公开露面是7月30日在阿尔及利亚会见该国国家总体战略研究院院长穆贾希德。9月30日，中联部官网「部领导」一栏更新，显示原中央国家安全委员会办公室副主任、1963年4月出生的刘海星已经接任部长。 时间线：刘建超：从外交部发言人到被开除党籍——2008年，北京奥运期间任外交部发言人，开始受到注意；2009年3月，由外交部新闻司司长调任驻菲律宾大使，之后改任驻印尼大使；2013年11月，任外交部部长助理；2015年8月，调入纪检系统，任中央纪委国际合作局局长、国际追逃追赃工作办公室负责人；2017年4月，任浙江省委常委、省纪委书记，7月兼任省监察委员会主任；2018年3月，任中央外事工作委员会办公室副主任；2022年5月，接替宋涛任中联部部长，10月进入二十届中央委员会；2025年7月30日，在阿尔及利亚会见该国国家总体战略研究院院长，此后没有再公开露面；2025年9月30日，中联部官网显示刘海星已接任部长；2026年10月29日，五中全会公报确认中央政治局此前开除他党籍的处分。 政治局先开除，全会再追认 按中共党内的规定，给中央委员、候补中央委员撤销党内职务、留党察看或开除党籍的处分，必须由中央委员会全体会议三分之二以上的多数决定；全会闭会期间，可以先由中央政治局作出决定，等召开全会时追认。刘建超的党籍就是这样先由政治局开除、再由五中全会追认的。 公报确认开除党籍的共33人，刘建超是其中之一，名单上还有前中央军委副主席张又侠、前政治局委员马兴瑞。美国之音和香港01都指出，这个人数创下改革开放以来历届中央全会的最高纪录。党员的纪律处分有五种：警告、严重警告、撤销党内职务、留党察看、开除党籍；同一份公报给金监总局原局长李云泽的是撤销党内职务。一年前的四中全会确认开除何卫东、苗华等14人，这次多了19人，两次全会合计47人；再往前，2024年7月的三中全会确认开除的是李尚福、李玉超、孙金明3人。 出席全会的人也在减少。二十大选出中央委员205人、候补中央委员171人，共376人；这次出席的只有中央委员162人、候补中央委员117人，合计279人，比四中全会少了36人。香港01按官方公开资料计算，74%的出席比例是1978年改革开放以来最低的。全会同时按党章把卢东亮、包钢等10名候补中央委员递补为中央委员，四中全会递补的是11名。全会还决定，中共二十一大于2027年下半年在北京召开。 表：二十大选出的人数和一中、三中、四中、五中全会：出席的少了，开除的多了——二十大选出（2022年）：中央委员 205人，候补中央委员 171人，追认开除党籍 —；一中全会出席（2022年）：中央委员 203人，候补中央委员 168人，追认开除党籍 —；三中全会出席（2024年7月）：中央委员 199人，候补中央委员 165人，追认开除党籍 3人；四中全会出席（2025年10月）：中央委员 168人，候补中央委员 147人，追认开除党籍 14人；五中全会出席（2026年10月）：中央委员 162人，候补中央委员 117人，追认开除党籍 33人。 由正部级降为处级：只有明报这样说 香港《明报》引述消息说，刘建超被认定严重违纪违法，由正部级贬为处级；消息还说，他的问题比在三中全会「辞去」中央委员的前国务委员、外交部长秦刚严重很多，秦刚据悉被降为副部级（中央社在全会开幕第二天转述，未经证实）。中央社转述的报道还说，中纪委大约在今年初已经完成对他的审查报告（未经证实）。两天后的公报对他的职级没有任何说法。 从正部级降到处级，降了多少？按官方规定，公务员的领导职务从国家级正职、国家级副职、省部级正职一直排到乡科级副职，共10个层次。部长属于省部级正职，处级属于县处级，两者之间隔着省部级副职、厅局级正职、厅局级副职三个层次。按香港01的解释，县处级正职包括各县四套班子的正职领导。被撤职的人要按规定降低职务、职级和级别，同时降低工资和待遇。有中国媒体把这种连降多级的处理称为「断崖式降级」。2018年底，甘肃省人大常委会原副主任李建华、河南省人大常委会原副主任王铁被政务撤职，降为副处级非领导职务。 最接近的先例是前工信部长肖亚庆。2022年12月，他被开除党籍，由国家监委给予政务撤职处分，降为一级主任科员，办理退休手续。香港01的解释是，肖亚庆犯了错，但没有严重到要开除公职，所以按规定降低职级。如果刘建超被降为处级，他受到的就是和肖亚庆一样的处理：开除党籍，保留公职，按降低后的职级领工资和待遇。 为什么是他：几种说法 公报给中纪委和中央军委两份审查报告点到的每一个人，用的都是同一句「严重违纪违法问题」，从这几个字看不出刘建超的问题和名单上的其他人有什么不同。 《华尔街日报》去年8月引述知情人士报道，刘建超7月底结束海外工作返回北京后被带走，被拘留的原因尚未明朗（中央社转述，未经证实）。据中央社当时报道，中国网络上从8月8日起盛传他被带走，说法不一，有的说他可能涉及泄密，有的传他居间协助中国富豪把资产搬到海外（未经证实）；到去年10月，中央社又提到他传出涉贪腐被查，下落不明（未经证实）。 另一种说法与他访美有关。据中央社报道，刘建超2024年1月选在台湾总统大选的同时访美5天，见了美国国务卿布林肯，「国际能见度宛如中国外长」。据香港01转述的一篇报道，有消息指，他那年访美时，在官方正式宣布之前就以候任外长的姿态示人，这种不合政治规矩的举动引起了北京注意（未经证实）。 学者谈的是这一轮开除高层党籍的范围和代价。据中央社报道，淡江大学两岸关系研究中心的张五岳在一场解读二十届四中全会的座谈会上说，那时有中共高层、军方「反习」的传言，有的话应该只是习一派独大之下的成员彼此竞争、甚至相互举报，习基于零容忍不分亲疏一并处理，这在军事和外交上造成人才断层；以二十大时的外事系统看，属于外事系统的中央委员只有5个，到那时只剩下3个。10月29日，张五岳又对中央社说，五中全会强调「全面从严治党关键在从严治吏」，查有没有贪腐只是「基本款」，更重要的是政治忠诚与政治纪律，「21大前还会继续再反（贪腐），会继续从严治党」。三立新闻网去年8月综合外电报道，新加坡南洋理工大学助理教授骆明辉说，若刘建超真的被免职，可能影响中国外交部的士气，并进一步削弱北京高层外交政策的专业。 能和官方记录对上的，只有明报说的他的问题比秦刚严重很多。我们认为，其余几种说法里，访美时以候任外长的姿态示人这一说依据最多，泄密、帮富豪转移资产和涉贪腐几种说法依据最少。这是因为，前者出自一篇报道引述的消息，后者到现在都只是中央社报道的传言。不过，这条消息也只说那次访美引起了北京注意，没有说他是因为访美被查。张五岳说比查贪腐更要紧的是政治忠诚与政治纪律，这一点访美和泄密两种说法都对得上，分不出哪一种依据更多。本文的判断不取决于哪一种说法属实，因为不管是哪一种，官方都没有说。 不同意本文的人会说，公报本来就不是交代案情的地方，案情要等审判：2024年6月27日，中共中央政治局会议决定开除李尚福的党籍，把他的涉嫌犯罪问题移送军事检察机关；将近两年后的2026年5月7日，军事法院一审以受贿罪、行贿罪判处他死刑，缓期二年执行，期满减为无期徒刑后终身监禁。他们还会指出：据中央社报道，长期行踪不明的中央军委办公厅原主任方永祥，也是到这份公报才第一次被官方证实涉及严重违纪违法。我们同意这两点，刘建超的案情以后也可能写进起诉书或判决书。但上面李尚福那一次，开除的日期和移送都有记录；四中全会开幕前三天，国防部发言人张晓刚就宣布何卫东、苗华等9名将领被开除党籍。刘建超的处分，政治局作出时没有宣布。 接下来看什么 如果官方接下来公布刘建超的具体违纪违法事实，北京就只是把交代放在了全会之后，本文说的只公布处分、不公布理由就站不住。 第一，检察机关会不会对刘建超提起公诉，会不会有中央纪委国家监委的通报写明他的职级：若提起公诉，说明他涉嫌犯罪，要像李尚福那样被追究刑事责任；若通报写明职级，明报说的降为处级就有了答案；若到明年年中两样都没有，说明官方对他的交代就停在五中全会公报上。我们判断，到2027年6月30日，官方不会公布刘建超的具体违纪违法事实。这是因为，政治局开除他时没有宣布，全会追认时也只把他的名字列进名单，两次可以交代的时候官方都没有交代。 第二，二十一大召开前的全会还会追认开除多少人：若仍在两位数，说明到换届前中共还在大批开除中央委员会成员的党籍；若只有个位数，说明这类开除在换届前已经基本停下。我们判断，从现在到二十一大开幕，二十届中央委员会的全会还会再追认开除至少10人的党籍。这是因为，全会追认开除的人数从三中全会到五中全会一次比一次多；五中全会强调从严治吏，张五岳也认为二十一大前还会继续从严治党。 2022年，同样被开除党籍的前部长肖亚庆有一份通报，写明他能在较短时间内如实说明违纪违法事实、认错悔错、全额退缴违纪违法所得，所以「可予从宽处理」；刘建超的案子，官方至今只给了33人名单中的一个名字，和「严重违纪违法」这几个字。 茉莉花深度报道独立调研、撰写。 参考报道：世界新闻网（10月27日） · 德国之声中文网（10月28日） · 中央通讯社（台湾）（10月28日） · 新华社（10月29日） · BBC中文网（10月29日） · 纽约时报中文网（10月29日） · 法国国际广播电台 RFI 中文（10月29日）
