content: 安东尼·阿尔巴尼斯表示，峰会是与亲密伙伴共同应对“共同挑战”的机会。（ABC 新闻：马特·罗伯茨） 总理将在本周与安提瓜和巴布达的英联邦领导人会晤时，推进澳大利亚争取联合国安理会席位的竞选，而同事们则需面对周二广泛预期的利率上升带来的后果。 随着工党成员指责安东尼·阿尔巴尼斯“飞往”加勒比海地区，而澳大利亚人正为生活成本挣扎，总理表示，他出席英联邦政府首脑会议（CHOGM）是查尔斯国王的个人请求。 “[CHOGM] 为澳大利亚提供了一个机会，与一些最亲密的伙伴共同应对共同挑战，包括气候变化、保护我们的海洋、贸易和投资，以及人工智能的兴起，”阿尔巴尼斯先生表示。 “这也是澳大利亚推进 2029-30 年争取联合国安理会席位竞选的重要机会。” 来自 56 个国家的领导人出席也将为阿尔巴尼斯先生提供机会，在峰会季节之前与关键谈判集团进行对话，因为 COP 31、APEC、G20 和东亚峰会都在 11 月举行。 总理将与英国讨论贸易和背包客 阿尔巴尼斯先生将与英国首相安迪·伯纳姆和加拿大总理马克·卡尼举行场外会谈，预计还将与几位太平洋和非洲领导人会面。 虽然阿尔巴尼斯先生和伯纳姆先生在 9 月联合国大会的场外短暂会面过，但他们首次正式会议将聚焦于人工智能、中东战争期间的燃料安全以及英国背包客人数的激增。 根据 2021 年莫里森时期的自由贸易协定，一项迫使英国背包客在澳大利亚农村和地区工作的规定被废除，导致英国工作假期制游客人数几乎翻倍。 政府已经下令对英国工作假期签证的处理“放缓”，每年约 8 万人，但仍将允许英国公民绕过农村和地区工作。 工党还引入了背包客签证抽签制度，将第二年和第三年签证分别限制在 4.5 万和 5 千。 该协议已被部分归咎于加剧了澳大利亚农村地区的劳动力短缺和净海外移民水平持续居高不下。 英联邦的“未开发的潜力” CHOGM 是少数几个没有美国或中国参与的多边论坛之一，但地缘政治仍然将在峰会上占据重要地位。 在过去的二十年中，中国向该地区投入了数十亿美元，资助了加勒比海地区的主要基础设施项目，包括安提瓜的主要港口、机场和板球场，CHOGM 活动将在此举行。 上周，特朗普政府宣布将在 15 个加勒比国家投资超过 3.4 亿美元（4.84 亿美元），重点在于数字基础设施、医疗保健和地区安全。 美国总统唐纳德·特朗普正在加大对加勒比海国家的投资。（路透社：乌米特·贝克塔斯） 在 CHOGM 之前的演讲中，英联邦秘书长 Shirley Botchwey 呼吁英联邦国家之间进行更大规模的贸易合作和社会流动性，这些国家的经济体总量价值近 30 万亿美元。 “我坚信英联邦的潜力能够造福其成员及其人民，无论是今天还是未来。而且，这种潜力仍未被充分开发，”她说。 Botchwey 女士还呼吁在国际体系“新的分裂时代”中采取“大胆而紧迫的变革”。 “很清楚的是，国际事务中的常规做法将不再奏效，”她说。 板球、气候与殖民主义 尽管安提瓜远离该地区，但加勒比海和太平洋领导人本周希望讨论许多相互交织的问题，包括气候变化、殖民主义的遗产，以及对太平洋地区程度较轻的奴隶制影响。 上升的海平面对低洼的加勒比海国家构成了生存威胁，这些国家更容易遭受自然灾害，且经济高度依赖旅游业。 澳大利亚矿业大亨安德鲁·“Twiggy”·福雷斯特也计划乘坐“福雷斯绿先锋号”驶入安提瓜的港口，这是世界上第一艘能够运行绿色氨的双燃料船舶。 在 2024 年萨摩亚举行的 CHOGM 上，领导人承认了“共同的历史经历”，包括殖民主义、原住民被剥夺土地和奴隶制，并承诺进行“包容性对话”以解决这些遗产带来的伤害。 阿尔巴尼斯先生将黑人板球（导致数万名太平洋岛民被强迫或绑架从事契约劳动）的做法描述为“澳大利亚历史上令人遗憾的一章”，但表示他的重点是未来。 目前的伯纳姆英国政府，就像之前的斯塔默政府一样，已排除支付奴隶制赔偿。 然而，加勒比海和非洲领导人本周将继续讨论赔偿正义问题。 CHOGM 预计将于周日在圣约翰斯的维维·理查兹体育场举行领导人板球赛，该体育场以传奇安提瓜板球运动员命名，他是峰会的官方大使。 总理将不会参赛，但会出席比赛。

content: 习近平预计将在 2027 年寻求担任中国共产党总书记的史无前例的第四任期。(路透社：王廷书) 本周，中国共产党（CCP）高层的权力更迭发生了令人震惊的转折。在高级将领清洗之后，中国中央军事委员会的七名成员中仅剩两人，其中包括国家主席习近平。 通过留下五个空缺职位，最高军事指挥体系出现了重大空白，引发了关于中国雄心勃勃的军事扩张与其核心决策者仍不稳定的问题。 这一转变是习近平最新一轮旨在全方位执行党纪的扫荡行动的一部分。 如今已进入第 14 年，习近平标志性的反腐运动，针对“老虎和苍蝇”，已对至少 790 万名涉嫌腐败的中共成员和官员进行了惩处。 在本周中共二十大第五次全体会议上，33 名成员和候补成员被开除出党，其中包括 16 名军人。 此次清洗的规模在近半个世纪中前所未有，创下了空缺席位的纪录，使委员会规模小于往常。 这提出了一个习近平必须面对的重大问题：这是系统性的力量还是失败？ 党的建设 中共被广泛认为是世界上最大的政党之一，拥有高度复杂的组织结构。 建设和管理一个拥有超过 1 亿名成员的政党是一项棘手的任务；这是毛泽东将其视为政党成功关键之一的“三把法宝”之一。 中国共产党（CCP）本周在北京举行了第五次全体会议。(路透社：王廷书) 今年的全会进一步巩固了习近平在党内的核心地位，将严格纪律与其政治意志联系起来。 人们普遍预计，习近平将在 2027 年下半年党的下一次代表大会上寻求担任中共总书记的史无前例的第四任期。 自他掌权以来，中国观察家经常将其反腐运动视为清除其对手的工具。但这次运动也波及到他身边的人，包括前外交部长秦刚，以及像高级军事领导人张又侠这样的权贵人物。 即使清洗波及到他自己的圈子，也有助于习近平强化其权威，使其继续掌控权力的合法性得以确立。 “如果用绝对化的话说，我会说他的下一任期是 100% 的，”前中共党报编辑邓玉文说。 尽管该党在威权体制下运作，但它有着长期的内部竞争历史，这几十年来帮助塑造了权力平衡。 中国领导层在党建全会上开会 习近平的最新举措表明，他正在进一步集中权力，以控制风险并确保其成员牢牢处于控制之下。 “反腐只是方程的一部分，”悉尼大学中国政治副教授陈明禄说。 “这也是关于党的治理能力、它与人民的关系，以及确保中央政府政策得以实施。” 目前尚不确定的是，这种集中化将如何重塑中共长期存在的省际官员竞争以及政治局内部竞争，后者是国家政治机构。 本周该党驱逐了三名前政治局成员。它在高层创造了空缺，为低层人才提供了晋升的机会。 习近平可能利用这一点，允许政党更新其领导层，而无需挑战其权威，这意味着在国家的政治体系中更难表达反对意见。 武装斗争 这是毛泽东的“三把法宝”之二。 习近平的军事使命已从夺取政治权力转变为维护国家安全并捍卫中共的统治。台湾，当然，在这个背景下是政治上最重要的目标之一。 对于习近平来说，实现国家统一不仅关乎中国的领土主张，而且与他所倡导的中国梦——即“民族复兴”的实现——密切相关。 中国人民解放军（PLA）由中国共产党控制。(路透社：王廷书) 全会强调加快中国人民解放军（PLA）的现代化，并继续党在台湾的工作。 然而，习近平对军事人物的持续清洗提出了一个实际问题：加强政治忠诚是否以牺牲军事有效性为代价。 随着 2027 年 PLA 迎来 100 周年，其指挥结构中的权力真空也引发了关于军队是否准备好实现习近平雄心的问题。 “习近平将致力于解决台湾问题。这并不意味着在他离任前台湾将统一，但方向已明确，”邓说。 如果这一评估属实，邓补充道，本周的清洗也可能旨在确保该体制在未来任何冲突中在政治上与习近平的目标保持一致。 至少，习近平正在表明他决心确保军队对党的政治目标的长期服从。 然而，风险在于体制对他人的依赖日益增加。 统一战线 法国足球明星基利安·姆巴佩本周在将毛泽东称为“中国独裁者”后道歉，意外地将党的第三把法宝——统一战线——置于现实世界的考验之中。 该事件恰逢全会，重新引发了人们对毛泽东近 27 年统治及其在一年中中国政治最敏感时期对党的权威影响的问题。 这一争议显示了该党如何将对其政治叙事的批评描绘成对中国人民的“侮辱”，从而团结公众情绪反对外部批评者。 对于中共来说，维护党的权威和控制其叙事不仅关乎国内稳定，而且塑造了中国在国际舞台上的形象。 尽管姆巴佩的言论是随意的，但它触动了中国最敏感的神经。对毛泽东的批评可能会引发对习近平无限期总统任期的审查。 这导致姆巴佩被中国商业合作伙伴、国有广播公司和体育平台取消合作。这显示了该党的影响力如何超越中国国界，中国市场成为对国外个人和机构施压的来源。 由毛泽东倡导的统一战线，原本是中共赢得国内社区支持并团结政治盟友的关键策略。 近年来，西方对这种努力是否也能用于在国界之外施加政治影响表示担忧。 “统一战线的根本原则是团结一切可以团结的力量。中国越来越认识到结交朋友而非制造敌人的重要性，”陈说。 北京中南海领导层大楼外有一块写着“万岁，伟大的中国共产党”的标牌。(美联社：Ng Han Guan) 然而，寻求认可并要求遵守特定的政治叙事是两个截然不同的目标。 当对毛泽东的批评被视为对中国人民的对抗性言论时，正如中国外交部本周所说，北京正在模糊党、中国和中国人民之间的界限。 这使得该党能够利用政治压力和公众情绪作为维护立场的工具。 全会强调全面严格的党的治理和坚持习近平的集中领导，反映了中共管理风险和维持政治秩序的方向。 它不太可能解决党、中国人民和国际社会之间的信任问题。

title: 吴国光：中国政局的斯大林逻辑

content: 吴国光 VOA 【国事光析】20230925 近来中国高层政局"大瓜"供应丰富，甚有戏剧性、刺激性的消息与传言接二连三。先是外交部长秦刚下台，接下来国防部长李尚福也因"健康原因"缺席外事活动。这两个副国级领导都是在习近平手下得到加速提拔的政坛新贵。随后，传言涉及中央军委纪律检查委员会书记张升民，乃至中央军委副主席张又侠。"二张"是习近平过去十年来一直倚重的重量级军头；张又侠更是习近平掌军的头号辅佐，当下职务最高的职业军人。这还不够，有说中共第三号人物、全国人大委员长赵乐际也面临政治麻烦。至于中共火箭军高层前些时日被一窝端，那个新闻与上述大人物的遭际相比简直上不了档次呢。全世界的舆论都在惊讶并追问：中国高层政局究竟发生了什么事情？ 中共制度溃败的加速征兆 舆论的惊讶首先在于：在习近平已经于中共二十大上空前地巩固了权力、组成了几乎清一色亲信与喽啰组成的高层班子的背景下，为什么仍然出现这样的事态发展？ 如果事情果如中共所宣称的那样，原因在于当事人生活作风腐化或牵涉腐败案件，那么，习近平作为最高领导人的眼光也好，中共官员选拔过程中的审查机制也好，岂不是出了很大的毛病，根本无法达到选拔出合乎习本人和中共组织所设标准的领导干部？ 当然，人们知道，中共的腐败和腐化是制度性的，并在过去三十几年中蔓延到了官员个体无法洁身自好、可以称为"普遍腐败"的程度。因此，习近平上台以来的所谓反腐败，必然是选择性的，甚至也只能是选择性的。所谓选择性反腐，就是反腐目标的确定不是按照官员腐败程度来决定的，而是按照另外的标准、为了另外的目的所选择的。那个目的就是清洗异己，巩固权力。因此，谁成为反腐的靶子，不在于此人是否腐败或是否腐败严重，而在于此人是习近平为了巩固自己的权力所必须拿掉的。 一句话，中共官员个个腐败，但跟对了上级就无所谓腐败，没有跟对嘛，那就很可能会被揪出来。所以，反腐在中共官员中的政治效应，就是所有官员不论原来是什么门路升官的，都赶快向习近平效忠，拼命显示其对习近平是如何地绝对忠诚。就这样，习近平才能够从一个权力基础薄弱、能力平庸昏聩的地方官员，上台伊始即迅速巩固权力，直至建立起习本人定于一尊的超级独裁。 但是，秦刚、李尚福不都是习近平的亲信吗，为什么现在也成了"反腐"目标？有这样一种解释，说习近平尤其不能容忍在他上台之后仍然"不收手"的腐败行为，因此秦、李腐败或腐化案一旦被揭出，习就不会饶了他们。这样一说，那就很难说习近平的反腐是选择性的了吧？可是，栗战书、王岐山等的腐败、腐化，不是早就有多个信息源的确凿报道了吗？怎么习近平却一直优容他们呢？如果习近平真的想从根源上限制腐败，他为什么不去限制公权力、不搞司法独立、也不容许舆论监督呢？如果秦、李真的是因为腐败而下台，那只能说，中共政权的制度溃败已经到了无法满足这个制度本身保持正常运转的起码要求了。如此高级别的官员新上台几个月就下台，可见这种制度溃败正在加速。 斯大林逻辑：杀的就是"亲信" 其实，把秦刚、李尚福或者栗战书、王岐山说成习近平这个独裁者的亲信，这个说法本身在政治上是个悖论。所谓亲信，意味着受到信任——那个"信"字是很重要的。但是，如果独裁者能够真的信任手下的人，那他/她恐怕也会至少在一定程度上放手让手下的人去做事，也就说不上是完完全全的"独裁"了。至于那个"亲"字更是未免讽刺。中国古人即有"伴君如伴虎"的说法——谁来想象一下和一头老虎保持亲密关系的图景？ 现在西方媒体也有借助中国古代宫廷政治来理解中共高层政局的了，应该说这是中国政局观察的一种进步。不过，单用王朝政治的权术来理解中共，还是不够的。要从制度上更深地理解中共，更多地还是要读一读苏联共产党的历史。毛泽东自比秦始皇，其实有点避重就轻；田家英说毛像斯大林晚年，毛可就大怒而要置田于死地了。习近平要当毛二世，这从国际眼光来看也就是斯大林三世。最近中共政局的这些事情，显示习近平已经在走往斯大林1930年代中期的"大清洗"那个方向了。 有人会说：习近平不是一直在搞清洗吗？怎么能说现在才往那个方向走？这就需要解释一句：斯大林1930年代中期的"大清洗"，是一连串的特定历史事件，不等同于"清洗"作为一个通用词汇的含义。是的，习近平上台之后一直在搞政治清洗，这和毛在文革前也没断了搞政治清洗是一样的，也和斯大林在1936年之前一直在搞政治清洗是一样的。但是，到了文革，毛要清洗的对象，从刘少奇到林彪，那可都是曾经帮助他获得至高权力的曾经的"亲信"了。斯大林1930年代中期的"大清洗"也是这样，用曾经长期任职苏联内务人民委员会（后来以"克格勃"著称于世）、写了《斯大林肃反秘史》一书的奥尔洛夫的话来说，那就是：斯大林"决心在1937年除掉所有亲信"。 可以说，共产党的当权者上台之初，清洗的是政敌，那正是过去十年习近平反腐的逻辑；一旦成为权力无可匹敌、无所制约的独裁者，清洗的就是亲信，那就是二十大之后观察中共高层政局的看点。人们容易理解前者，但往往难以理解后者，而恰恰后者才是共产党政治的深层逻辑——这里我把它称为"斯大林逻辑"。 吴国光 美国之音特约评论员，任 斯坦福大学中国经济与制度研究中心 高级研究员，并兼任 美国亚洲协会政策研究所 中国分析中心高级研究员，试图以学术研究透视政治现实。 ——新世纪20230924转发 附： 【國關Talk專題演講精華】習近平政治的史達林邏輯 二十大後中共政局深度解讀 feat. 史丹佛大學 吳國光教授 Institute Of International Relations, NCCU

title: 吴国光 | 独裁与恶政的螺旋效应：再谈“斯大林逻辑”
summary: 吴国光 VOA 【国事光析】20231016 前次拙文谈 中国政局的"斯大林逻辑" ，以苏联1930年代中期斯大林进行的大清洗为历史对照，来理解近期中共不断有高官落马的现象，试图解释为什么二十大后习近平已经高度集中权力但却仍然对基本都是自己亲信的官员持续进行政治清洗。文短未能展开，留下不少疑问。其中一个疑问是：为什么要进行这样的持续清洗？本文即尝试回答这个问题，并进一步揭示"斯大林逻辑"的制度本质。 资料照：1930年11月21日，苏联领导人斯大林和苏共政治局委员布哈林（右）
content: 吴国光 VOA 【国事光析】20231016 前次拙文谈 中国政局的"斯大林逻辑" ，以苏联1930年代中期斯大林进行的大清洗为历史对照，来理解近期中共不断有高官落马的现象，试图解释为什么二十大后习近平已经高度集中权力但却仍然对基本都是自己亲信的官员持续进行政治清洗。文短未能展开，留下不少疑问。其中一个疑问是：为什么要进行这样的持续清洗？本文即尝试回答这个问题，并进一步揭示"斯大林逻辑"的制度本质。 资料照：1930年11月21日，苏联领导人斯大林和苏共政治局委员布哈林（右）在莫斯科。 灾难之后的政治整肃 斯大林1922年当上苏共总书记，1924年列宁死后他开始不断清洗政敌并高度集中权力。到1935年开始的新一轮大清洗，其间大约11年时间。无独有偶，习近平清洗政敌并高度集中权力的历程，如今也有11年了。斯与习，在那11年当中的作为，都是很成功的，也就是实现了个人高度集权的目标。 斯大林在这一段高度集权的过程中，逐步地抛弃了列宁的"新经济政策"，转而在工业化和农业集体化上采取冒进政策，试图加速建设苏共版本的所谓社会主义。特别是在农村，斯大林强力推行"全盘集体化"。这一过程充满暴力，包括以武装力量镇压那些抵抗集体化的农民，甚至出动了轰炸机。接下来的恶果，就是包括以"欧洲粮仓"著称的乌克兰在内的苏联各地发生的大饥荒。据估计，当时饿死的民众，至少有500万到700万。 资料照：中国前领导人毛泽东1949年访问苏联期间与苏联领导人斯大林出席会议。 这样的巨大灾难，不仅引起了民众对于斯大林专制的憎恶，也导致苏共内部对斯大林的不满四处蔓延。我想，了解到这种历史背景，再来看斯大林1930年代中期的大整肃，应该就不是那样地不可理解了。简单地说，斯大林不是个疯子；他在高度集权之后仍然持续清洗，有他的理由和逻辑。 对于这种理由和逻辑，中国人应该不陌生，因为类似的灾难在中国也曾经发生，因为毛泽东以同样的理由和逻辑做过同样的事情。1958年毛泽东推行"大跃进"，也是要加速工业化，并在农村强力建立人民公社，恶果也是大饥荒。这场人为的、也是人类历史上最大规模的大饥荒，夺走了数千万中国人的生命。毛自知"闯了大祸"，但他绝不肯因此哪怕削减一点点自己的权力，反而变本加厉推行个人崇拜，接下来就发动了所谓文化大革命，也就是毛版本的十年大整肃，不仅全民遭难，就是那些曾经为树立毛的领袖地位立下汗马功劳的中共领袖们，也一个接一个被关进监狱乃至死于非命。 理由是什么？斯大林和毛泽东都曾经摆出了很多理由要进行这样的清洗，从苏联有所谓"白卫分子"、"托派分子"等等，到中共上上下下都有所谓"走资本主义道路的当权派"，名目不一而足。但是，背后的真正理由，放在大饥荒的背景下，人们应该就可以看得比较清楚了，那就是 最高专制者在制造了巨大的社会灾难之后对于自己权力地位受到质疑、削弱、乃至挑战的担心。为了应对已经或可能出现的对于自己权力地位的质疑、削弱和挑战，不仅要加强对于民众的社会控制，而且要在共产党内部进行持续的政治清洗；在政敌已经清洗殆尽、全是自己亲信掌权的情况下，清洗的对象也就必然是所谓亲信了 ——这就是所谓"斯大林逻辑"。 请同时参阅： 国事光析：中国政局的斯大林逻辑 独裁出恶政，恶政促独裁 习近平现在正在制造上述历史的第三版。与他的斯爷爷和毛爸爸所处的时空不同，习版本的故事情节当然不会完全重复上述种种，但其中的逻辑是相同的。因为共产党最高专制者这么做始自斯大林，所以我将之称作"斯大林逻辑"。 但是，"斯大林逻辑"的出现，首先不是因为有斯大林这么个人，而是因为斯大林是苏联共产党的最高领袖，是因为共产党有那样一种专制制度。共产党的组织特性和意识形态，决定了其最高领袖实行个人专制。这里的个人专制与共产党对于整个国家的专制统治是相互表里的，不可分割开来。一般讲所谓"独裁"，容易偏于只讲个人的专制，这一点我在本专栏以前的文章中谈过。现在，我们就在这个意义上用"独裁"这个词来专指共产党最高领袖的个人专制。"斯大林逻辑"是独裁者的逻辑，而"斯大林们"则是共产党专制的产物。"斯大林逻辑"在今天的中国政局中重现，也正是因为共产党制度过去十年间成就了习近平的独裁。 独裁必然带来治理上的恶果。过去几年中，从对于新冠肺炎的"动态清零"，到无预警放开的"疫情海啸"，制造了巨大的人命牺牲和人道灾难。反市场和敌视民营经济的经济政策，加剧了中国经济增长的放缓，直接、负面地影响了上亿民众的就业、收入和消费。习近平的这些恶政与斯大林、毛泽东当年制造大饥荒的恶政是一脉相承的，因此，在灾难之后进行政治整肃的权力逻辑也是一以贯之的。 这里，可以发现在独裁与恶政之间存在一种螺旋效应，二者相互之间推动升级。就独裁领导人来说，越是个人集权，就越是没有制约；决策越是任性，越是造成治理上的 灾难，也就是造成恶政；而越是出现治理的灾难，独裁者也就越发感到已经高度集中在自己手里的权力还是不够用。地位不安全，于是越发要进一步强化个人权威，进一步实行政治清洗，进一步压制乃至消灭可能的不满，首先是出现在精英阶层的不满。共产党的整个权力体系作为独裁体制，恰恰为这种个人集权和政治清洗提供了足够的、强大的制度手段，也由于不向民众负责而必然走向恶政。因为独裁而形成恶政，因为恶政而愈发独裁，这才是深层的"斯大林逻辑"。 吴国光 美国之音特约评论员，任 斯坦福大学中国经济与制度研究中心 高级研究员，并兼任 美国亚洲协会政策研究所 中国分析中心高级研究员，试图以学术研究透视政治现实。 ——新世纪20231016转发

title: 2026 年马自达 CX-6e 电动 SUV 行驶中
source: 澳洲唐人街 – Australia ChinaTown News 中文华人新闻
summary: 一款粗口不断的马自达病毒视频现已抵达澳大利亚道路。 新款马自达 CX-6e 配备了一项“外部公告”功能，该功能通过安装在车头的大喇叭向外界广播信息。 其中包括预录的留言，例如礼貌地建议行人停止看手机并关注周围环境。 当我们发布该功能演示视频时，它吸引了 Nova FM 主持人 Ricki-Lee 和 Tim 的注意，他们对汽车能够用数字合成的声音大喊“滚开”和“快点，***头”感到震惊。 “我从未想过生活中有什么比这更令人渴望的，”Ricki-Lee 说。 The Mazda
content: 一款粗口不断的马自达病毒视频现已抵达澳大利亚道路。 新款马自达 CX-6e 配备了一项“外部公告”功能，该功能通过安装在车头的大喇叭向外界广播信息。 其中包括预录的留言，例如礼貌地建议行人停止看手机并关注周围环境。 当我们发布该功能演示视频时，它吸引了 Nova FM 主持人 Ricki-Lee 和 Tim 的注意，他们对汽车能够用数字合成的声音大喊“滚开”和“快点，***头”感到震惊。 “我从未想过生活中有什么比这更令人渴望的，”Ricki-Lee 说。 The Mazda CX-6e electric car represents a bold departure for the brand. Picture: Supplied 驾驶员可以通过屏幕键盘将其编程为说出任何他们想要的话，该键盘会原样转达您的消息，没有任何审查。 这是我体验过的第一款会像那样对人们大喊大叫的马自达，这可能会让您被罚款、打架或被指指点点。 品牌那些严谨且一丝不苟的日本工程师绝不会制造出那样的东西。但这不是一辆马自达。不完全是。 由长安在中国制造，CX-6E 看起来像马自达，但其硬件和软件与 Deepal 和 Nevo 等新品牌共享。这意味着它比同等级的汽油动力马自达更便宜。 马自达 CX-6E 的起价为 56,990 美元（落地价），低于中档马自达 CX-5，也低于特斯拉、极氪或比亚迪等电动车竞争对手。 您还获得了大量标准配置，包括全景天窗、加热和冷却的仿皮座椅，以及一个巨大的 26.45 英寸中央屏幕，连接着 23 个扬声器的立体声系统。 客户可以升级至高配 Azami 版本，额外支付 3000 美元，以获得漂亮的 21 英寸轮毂和数字侧视镜。我们不会这么做，因为数字侧视镜缺乏传统玻璃侧视镜的深度感知和易于调整的功能。 The Mazda’s massive touchscreen lets people broadcast messages. Picture: Supplied 虽然顶配版的合金轮毂看起来很漂亮，但这并不意味着这辆车是一只需要华丽修饰的丑小鸭。 它在我们眼中看起来很棒，细节也很可爱，例如前大灯之间隐藏的空气动力学扰流板。 仔细查看的马自达粉丝会发现，它没有马自达通常用于营造展厅内家族相似感的按键布局、菜单布局，甚至屏幕字体。 与 MX-5、Mazda2 或 Mazda3 等车型以及较新的但源自五十铃的 BT-50 皮卡相比，内饰显得格外陌生。这是因为它有一个真正巨大的 26.45 英寸屏幕，从乘客膝盖延伸到驾驶员指关节，占据了仪表盘上近 70 厘米的空间。 The CX-6e is a handsome-looking car. Picture: Supplied 它巨大无比。 在嘲笑屏幕令人震惊的向骑自行车的人广播时尚评论的能力（紧身裤不错，超人！）后，我们坐在副驾驶座上实验其功能，发现它 surprisingly 功能有限。 显示器的乘客侧可以在蓝牙、AM 或 FM 收音机之间切换——就这些了。您无法用它来流媒体电影——即使停车时——玩游戏、与导航交互或折腾 Apple CarPlay 或 Android Auto 连接。 The car’s touchscreen has more features in China than Australia. 这些功能未来可能会更新，但目前，这个巨大的屏幕在乘客侧利用率不高。 而在驾驶员侧，它却被过度使用，因为大显示器必须用于开启前大灯、调节空调或与各种安全系统协商，这些系统在其他安静的驾驶体验中发出各种蜂鸣声。 这很遗憾，因为马自达 CX-6E 相对容易驾驶。 其 190kW 和 290Nm 后置电动马达产生的扭矩调节良好，配有经过精心校准的油门映射和牵引控制系统，受益于马自达的技术。 悬挂系统也是如此，能够平滑处理道路坑洼的边缘。 2026 Mazda CX-6e electric car. Picture: Supplied 尽管如此，它似乎没有马自达 6 天生的运动感，方向盘的反馈不足，这与方向盘上的标志不符。 马自达 CX-6E 代表了一个试图应对完美风暴的品牌努力，这场风暴包括电动化、大量新品牌以及日益注重成本的买家群体。 只需几次软件更新，它就能成为马自达家族的优秀一员。特别是如果它能学会注意自己的言行。 MAZDA CX-6E 价格：从 56,990 美元（落地价）起 动力：后置电动，190kW 和 290Nm 保修：5 年，不限里程 续航：484 公里 备胎：维修套件 后备箱：468 升 后备箱：468 升

title: 华人女子自制梯子翻越美监狱铁丝网越狱，45 分钟后被抓获
source: 澳洲唐人街 – Australia ChinaTown News 中文华人新闻
summary: 康涅狄格州联邦检察官办公室10月28日宣布，现年32岁的中国公民严小琴（Xiaoqin Yan，音译），因从联邦监狱越狱，被法官追加判处10个月监禁。 根据美国司法部公布的资料，严小琴原本因纵火和非法持有枪支罪，在康州丹伯里联邦惩教所（FCI Danbury）的一处低设防设施服刑。 2024年12月10日晚上7点左右，她实施了越狱计划。 根据检方提交的量刑备忘录，严小琴并不是临时起意，而是事先进行过观察和准备。 监控画面显示，越狱前一天，她曾来到监狱围栏附近，研究周围环境。行
content: 康涅狄格州联邦检察官办公室10月28日宣布，现年32岁的中国公民严小琴（Xiaoqin Yan，音译），因从联邦监狱越狱，被法官追加判处10个月监禁。 根据美国司法部公布的资料，严小琴原本因纵火和非法持有枪支罪，在康州丹伯里联邦惩教所（FCI Danbury）的一处低设防设施服刑。 2024年12月10日晚上7点左右，她实施了越狱计划。 根据检方提交的量刑备忘录，严小琴并不是临时起意，而是事先进行过观察和准备。 监控画面显示，越狱前一天，她曾来到监狱围栏附近，研究周围环境。行动当天，她将多件运动衫和外套穿在身上，戴好手套，还准备了一条毯子，打算用来覆盖围栏上的带刺铁丝网。 当晚，她先躲在监狱建筑外一处车库门旁的黑暗角落，等待狱警完成围栏巡逻。等狱警离开后，她迅速利用院子里的材料搭建起一架简易梯子，并不断调整高度。 随后，她爬上梯子，借助毯子越过带刺铁丝网，最终成功落地，逃出了监狱范围。 整个过程虽然惊险，但她确实突破了联邦监狱的防线。 然而，真正的问题才刚刚开始。 成功越狱后，严小琴并没有接应车辆，也没有能够迅速离开当地的交通工具。她只能跑到附近道路上，试图寻找愿意帮助她逃离的人。 根据检方披露的情况，她先后向加油站附近的人、亚马逊送货司机，以及夜间待在家中的居民求助，希望有人能够开车载她一程。 但她的行为引起了周围人的警觉。 面对这些陌生人，严小琴不断重复一句话：没有警察！（No police!）她显然不希望任何人联系警方。 然而，事情并没有按照她的计划发展。被她拦下的人不仅拒绝提供帮助，其中两人还直接拨打电话报警。 当地警方很快赶到现场。最终，警员发现严小琴躲在一辆亚马逊送货车辆后面。 看到警方出现，她还不断质问司机：“你报警了？你报警了？” 但一切已经来不及了。 从成功翻越监狱围栏，到再次落入警方手中，严小琴仅仅获得了约45分钟的自由。 随后，她被重新拘押，并被转移至马萨诸塞州西部一处安全级别更高的监狱设施。2025年4月，联邦大陪审团正式以越狱罪对她提出起诉。 2026年4月10日，严小琴承认越狱罪。10月28日，康州联邦地区法官Kari A. Dooley正式判处她额外10个月监禁。 这意味着，她不仅没有通过越狱获得自由，反而因为这次行动延长了自己的刑期。 事实上，严小琴之所以被关进联邦监狱，与一起发生在阿拉巴马州的严重纵火案有关。 2021年9月29日晚，严小琴出现在阿拉巴马州蒙哥马利市中心的第一浸信会教堂（First Baptist Church Montgomery）。这是一座拥有悠久历史的教堂，也是当地具有代表性的宗教建筑之一。 根据此前庭审证据，严小琴当时携带多个行李袋进入教堂，参加周三晚间的宗教活动。但教堂工作人员此前已经多次注意到她的异常举止，甚至曾因为她的行为而要求她离开教堂。 然而，9月30日凌晨2点刚过，监控再次拍到了她的身影。这一次，她从随身行李袋中取出多个容器，开始在教堂内部不同位置纵火。火势迅速蔓延，教堂多个区域遭到严重破坏。 蒙哥马利消防部门接到报警后赶到现场，最终将大火扑灭，但建筑已经遭受重大损失。调查人员随后通过监控录像、嫌疑车辆及车牌信息，锁定了严小琴。 2021年10月4日，执法人员在蒙哥马利一处住所将她逮捕。搜查过程中，警方发现了与教堂监控画面中相同类型的行李袋和衣物，以及燃料容器、引火木、打火机等物品。 警方还发现了一把手枪。调查显示，严小琴此前持非移民签证进入美国，但在纵火案发生时已经逾期滞留。按照联邦法律，她当时的移民身份不允许她合法持有枪支。 2024年3月22日，联邦法官正式判处她102个月监禁，同年7月，法院还裁定她必须向遭受火灾损失的教堂支付约1,828万美元赔偿。 检方在2026年10月28日宣布最新判决时确认，严小琴自2024年12月10日被重新抓获后，一直处于羁押状态。至于她当初为什么要纵火烧毁教堂，以及为什么在服刑期间决定冒险越狱，现有司法部公告并未给出完整的动机解释。

国务卿马可·卢比奥 (Marco Rubio)，佐治亚州亚特兰大 洛斯亚特兰大 国务卿马可·卢比奥 (Marco Rubio) 在 2026 年 10 月 31 日新闻发布会上的讲话 主持人：谢谢大家。美国国务卿马可·卢比奥。卢比奥国务卿：谢谢。这有点奇怪。我想你们知道我是谁。如果你不知道我是谁，你就不会在这里。所以——但是谢谢你。嗯，我要感谢亚特兰大市。他们本周接待我们做得很好。它是美国伟大的商业和创新中心之一，它是我们不仅展示我们的国家，而且关注当今世界面临的关键经济政策问题的理想地点。在特朗普总统的领导下，美国为G20确立了明确的使命，即回归本源，聚焦于论坛创立之初的核心目的。因此，本周在亚特兰大，我们在外交部长级别上执行了该指令。我们专注于核心经济、能源、技术和供应链挑战。我们提出了切实可行的解决方案和真正的成果，不仅使今天在座的各国公民受益，而且使全世界的公民受益。目前世界上存在许多复杂、相互关联的问题，这些问题对我们各国产生集体影响，我们必须共同努力找到这些问题的解决方案。
这就是为什么让这个小组聚集在一起召开一次认真、集中的会议很重要，我很高兴地说，本周我们讨论了很多内容。如果还没有发布的话，你会在即将发布的主席声明中找到我们讨论的所有内容。当然，我们解决的主要问题之一是航行自由。船只在国际水域的安全通行对于世界的生计至关重要，我们看到了袭击——事实就是如此。让我理解——我在评论中强调了这一点；我现在就和大家一起强调一下。我们现在生活在一个伊朗政权积极、公开地以商船为攻击目标的世界，而不是海军舰艇；我们不是在谈论海军舰艇，我们不是在谈论潜艇。我们谈论他们时说：这是一艘载有货物、石油、天然气的商船，我们将尝试击沉它。我们将尝试——他们公开攻击船只作为治国工具。这就是我们生活的世界。我认为中央司令部和美国在保护这艘船方面做得非常出色。如今，通过那里的燃料量与冲突前的燃料量相当，但尽管如此，我们几乎每晚都必须保护这些船只免受无人机和导弹的袭击。
我们现在不仅在曼德海峡看到袭击，而且在曼德海峡也看到袭击，当然，我们在南海和台湾海峡以及其他地方看到的敌对胁迫——也许不是那么激烈，但肯定仍然令人担忧——这也使经济处于危险之中。海上通道受到攻击或胁迫的最严重后果之一是粮食安全问题的上升。当能源、化肥和农产品无法到达目的地时，就会威胁到我们每个国家以及世界所有国家最重要的必需品。我很感激这个小组能够就这个主题举行有目的的会议，但显然——而且我们至少在我们的目标、我们的理解上是一致的。

【原文 English Original】
Marco Rubio, Secretary of State Atlanta, Georgia Loews Atlanta Secretary of State Marco Rubio at a Press Availability Remarks October 31, 2026 MODERATOR: Thank you, guys. The Secretary of State of the United States, Marco Rubio. SECRETARY RUBIO: Thank you. It’s kind of strange. I think you guys know who I am. You wouldn’t be here if you didn’t know who I was. So – but thank you. Well, I want to thank the city of Atlanta. They did a great job hosting us this week. It’s one of America’s great business and innovative hubs, and it’s been an ideal location for us to not just showcase our country, but to focus on critical economic policy issues that are facing the world today. Under President Trump’s leadership, the United States has established a clear mission for the G20 to get back to basics and to focus on the core purpose for why this forum was created in the first place. So this week in Atlanta, at the foreign ministers’ level, we executed on that directive. We focused on core economic, energy, technology, and supply chain challenges. And we addressed practical solutions and real outcomes that benefit the citizens not just of the countries represented here today, but of the world. We have a lot of complex, interconnected problems in the world right now that impact our countries collectively, and we have to work together to find solutions to those problems. That’s why it’s important to get this group together to have a serious, focused meeting, and I’m happy to say that this week we covered a lot of ground. And you’ll find everything we talked about in my chair statement that will be coming out, if it hasn’t come out already. One of the main issues we addressed, of course, was freedom of navigation. Safe passage of vessels in international waters is vital to the livelihood of the world, and we see the attacks – and that’s what they are. Let me understand – and I underscored this in my comments; I’ll underscore it with you now. We now live in a world where the Iranian regime actively and openly targets commercial vessels for attack – not naval vessels; we’re not talking about naval vessels, we’re not talking about submarines. We are talking about them saying: Here’s a commercial vessel with cargo, oil, natural gas, and we are going to try to sink it. We are going to try – they are openly attacking vessels as a tool of statecraft. That’s the world we live in. And I think Central Command and the United States has done a phenomenal job of protecting this shipping. And today, the amount of fuel getting through there is comparable with what was coming out before the conflict, but nonetheless we’ve had to defend these ships from drones and missiles almost every single night. And we’re also seeing attacks not just in the straits now, but also in the Bab al-Mandeb, and the hostile coercion, of course, that we see – maybe not as kinetic but certainly still concerning – in the South China Sea and the Strait of Taiwan and elsewhere that also puts economies in danger. One of the most severe consequences to sea lanes being under attack or under coercion is the rise of food security problems. When energy and fertilizer and agricultural products can’t reach their destinations, it threatens the most vital necessity for each and every one of our nations and for all the nations of the world. And I’m grateful that this group was able to have purposeful meetings on this subject, but obviously – and that we are aligned at least in our goal, in our understanding that it’s a serious problem, although I cannot say we are aligned on how to solve it. My closing comments on critical minerals really could have applied to this as well, and that is that we all agree there’s a problem, but obviously there’s work to be done to find agreement on – collectively on solutions. I’m also glad that on the sidelines of this G20 gathering, we were able to get the Quad group together again and discuss a myriad of topics, a myriad of issues. The Quad is something we’ve invested a lot of time in. I think this year alone we’ve met four or five times. It was my first meeting as Secretary of State when I took over in January of 2025. And we’re going to continue to work in that forum as it’s gone from a place where we just meet and talk about problems to a place where we identify areas to work together on, and are actually being able to act on that. And hopefully we’ll be announcing very soon, if we haven’t already, that we will have a Quad leaders’ meeting in Manila in the – I guess today is the 31st – next month. So those – these are the issues that are important to the United States and to all the countries here today. We have a great relationship with all the members of the Quad, and our partnership enables us to address these challenges in an effective, unified way that benefits the shared national interests of our respective countries. I also had great bilateral meetings. For example, we had a trilateral meeting with Japan and South Korea. We’ve done that a number of times as well. We signed a memorandum of cooperation on transnational Arctic-Pacific partnership with them. And together we’ll ensure that the Arctic remains a region free of dominion or coercion, and that it instead remains a place of peaceful relations and commerce. We’re grateful for all of the invited participants who came to Atlanta here this week. I want to recognize the Polish delegation in particular. Poland as a country is making great strides economically as well as in the security domain because they put their national interests and their citizens first. They are stronger; they are more robust as a nation. And America, as an ally and a partner of Poland, therefore, is stronger as well. President Trump believes very strongly that Poland deserves a seat at this table of global leaders, and we very much hope to see them – and other strong nations on the rise – invited back next year. As we prepare for the summit in Doral, which is coming up now in December, I want to give my thanks and praise to my fellow cabinet members who have led extremely successful ministerials across the country leading up to this one. The U.S. presidency of the G20 has been one of the many highlights of the America’s – America’s 250 – 250th birthday celebration. We’ve successfully used this platform to build global initiatives that truly benefit the American people, which is ultimately our primary obligation. So we are looking forward to another great G20 meeting that will be led by President Trump in Florida in December, and that will be a capstone to this year of American leadership. All right, let’s go. Right here. We’ll start here. We’ll move around. I can’t get everybody. There’s a game, guys. All right. QUESTION: Is there a mike? Hi – hello? I can’t tell if it’s on. SECRETARY RUBIO: Yeah, it’s on. QUESTION: Is it? Okay. Thank you, Mr. Secretary. SECRETARY RUBIO: I can barely see him with this damn podium. Go ahead. QUESTION: (Laughter.) Recognizing that it is difficult enough to get 20 people to agree on any one subject let alone the variety of issues that you were going for here, talking about here, I’m wondering if there is – what you’re most concerned, or not – maybe concerned is the wrong word, but what you’re – what is the biggest obstacle to consensus on the most important issues that remains after this meeting? SECRETARY RUBIO: Well, the first obstacle – any – is to identify what the problems are. If you can’t even agree on what the problems are, you can’t make progress. So I do think that what you saw in this meeting over the last day and a half and what I hope you’ll see in the leaders’ meeting is a universal recognition that on issues like critical minerals and supply chains and freedom of navigation and – these are issues that all of us should be – food security – these are issues that every nation on Earth should be concerned about. Now, what you saw on the back and forth, of course, is that nation-states argue about what are the causes that are creating those problems, and they’re arguing about how to solve them. But I think the first step is at least some universal acknowledgment that freedom of navigation matters, that critical minerals matter, that supply chains matter, that food security matters, not just to the countries at the table but to countries around the world, and I do think we have that. Now, obviously there’s going to be a lot of work that goes into determining how we solve some of these problems, and some of them, frankly, are being challenged by very acute challenges like the war between Russia and Ukraine, like the conflict in the Middle East, like unrelated conflicts but nonetheless ones we see, for example, like in Sudan and the one between the Democratic Republic of Congo and Rwanda. So there are some regional conflicts as well. But at least coming to an understanding about what the problems are is important, because at least it lays the predicate for what you seem to be – or want to be – talking about. Of course, I wouldn’t pretend to you today that we are close to finding universally accepted solutions to these problems, but I do think that among the G20 represented here are countries that are working together to solve some of them, particularly in the realm of supply chains and critical minerals. Yes. QUESTION: Thank you, Mr. Secretary. When it comes to Iran, what was your message to the G20 on diplomatic efforts, and how much time are you giving these Qatari-backed talks with Iran an opportunity to succeed before you might resume military operations? SECRETARY RUBIO: Well, I mean, the message is simple. Iran is blowing up ships, including ships that have, for example, Indian sailors on them, including ships that have energy that’s destined for countries represented at that table. We live in a world in which a country is openly – a regime is openly – saying: We will blow up commercial ships. Think about that, okay? Think about the world we now live in. It sounds like something from a hundred years ago or 80 years ago. It’s happening, and every country there is challenged. As far as the talks are concerned, I don’t know if there’s a time frame. It’s up to the President to make decisions with regards to those sorts of things. There are multiple talks; talks have actually never stopped. There’s been active conversations going, both – in some cases directly but often through intermediaries. And the President’s preference in any challenge around the world is to try to solve it diplomatically and peacefully, if possible. He recognizes there are some issues in the world that cannot be solved peacefully – unfortunately, sadly. But we would prefer to solve it in that manner. So I’m not going to characterize neither the progress on those talks nor any time frame on it, other than to tell you that if there is a diplomatic solution we would be open to it. But obviously, it can’t be one that endangers our national security or one that doesn’t meet our core concerns that we have that brought us into that in the first place. And that is primarily that Iran not – not only has shown that they clearly have ambitions to be a nuclear weapons power – and that can never be allowed to happen – but this is also a country and a regime that’s at the center of all of the instability in the Middle East. In Lebanon, there’s instability because they support Hizballah. In – Saudi Arabia is under attack because Iran supports the Houthis. In Iraq – is a country that’s feeling challenged because Iranian-backed militias are challenging the state there. So anywhere you turn, what you find is some Iranian proxy that’s undermining the peace and stability of the Middle East. That’s a fundamental threat that we have to confront – on top of the fact that they want nuclear weapons. This is a regime that’s massacred its own people. You can only imagine what it would do to others if they possessed weapons of mass destruction, which will never be allowed to happen as long as President Trump is in the White House. Yes, second row, right – I guess you in the – yes, sir. I have no science for picking people. And part of it, I can’t see you, so, like, don’t feel discriminated against. I’m just — QUESTION: (Off mike.) SECRETARY RUBIO: Yeah, I will. Don’t worry, I’ll try to get as many people as I can. Go ahead. QUESTION: Usually, when people see my face they don’t pick on me. Mr. Secretary, thank you for doing the briefing. Mike Wagenheim with i24NEWS. When it comes to freedom of navigation and the communication here this week, is it more – would you characterize it as America is laying out the ideas and asking for everybody else to follow, or are other countries contributing their own ideas here? Is it more of a collaborative process? SECRETARY RUBIO: Well, freedom of navigation – there’s different challenges in different places, all right? So when you talk about the Black Sea, obviously you saw a lot of countries speak up and provide a willingness to – both Türkiye and India have come to the table with some ideas about how we can get grain shipments movement, because this is threatening the world’s food security, and some energy security as well. In the case of the straits, it’s more challenging, of course, because many countries around the world don’t have the ability to project power in the region. The President has, of course, repeatedly asked for countries to join us in the endeavor of predicting global – protecting global shipping through the Straits of Hormuz. So far we’ve had some very limited cooperation but not much; it primarily has fallen on the United States to protect shipping. So – and obviously, in the Indo-Pacific, we don’t have, like, active kinetic things going on like what you see in the straits or even in the Black Sea. But you do have some challenges, some territorial claims that we do not recognize. And that’s why you see us not just continue to have a presence in that part of the world, but also to operate jointly and cooperatively with our partners to continue to make clear that we do not accept illegitimate territorial claims on waterways that are either international or not territorial waters of any single nation. Okay. Yes, ma’am. Yes. QUESTION: Andrea Shalal with Reuters. Thank you. I wanted to ask you about the Quad statement that you put out. You don’t exactly call out China in that statement, although it’s clear that the – due to the concerns raised about economic coercion and arbitrary export restrictions seem to apply. So could you clarify whether that was, in fact, the thought? SECRETARY RUBIO: Yeah, well — QUESTION: And then I wanted to ask about you – these ideas about the Black Sea. So are you thinking that there is sort of growing momentum for a ceasefire, at least partially, to govern the Black Sea grain shipments and ensure food security? SECRETARY RUBIO: So I think on the second point, there is – I wouldn’t call it momentum; I think there’s growing interest from the international community to serving as either guarantors and/or facilitators of some sort of agreement that allows – because of the threat it’s posing not just to energy, but primarily to food and grain. So I wouldn’t call that momentum, but I think there’s long – I think there’s been renewed interest in serving a role; and we are examining proposals, for example, that were forwarded to us maybe a couple weeks ago, maybe a week ago, from Türkiye in that regard. And we’ll continue to explore that. We’d like to achieve it; it doesn’t solve the war, but at least it solves a unique aspect of it. In the case of the Quad, look, the Quad is not an anti-anybody. It’s not a format that exists to be against any country; it’s a – to the extent we express concern about things in the Quad, it’s concern about behaviors. It’s concern about activities. Now, those activities or behaviors are coming repetitively from one country; that’s going to be obvious to everybody. But it is not an anti-China or anti-anybody coalition. The Quad is a cooperative agreement between four countries with – that share a common interest, and common opposition to behaviors. And that’s what we’ll continue to point to. All right, third row, right here, this gentleman. QUESTION: Thank you, Mr. Secretary. Lalit Jha from IANS, an Indian news agency. What role do you see for — SECRETARY RUBIO: Did you guys cover my trip when I was there a couple weeks ago? QUESTION: Yes. SECRETARY RUBIO: You did? QUESTION: Yes, we did. SECRETARY RUBIO: Good. Did I get a lot of coverage, or a little coverage? (Laughter.) QUESTION: You are quite popular there. (Laughter.) SECRETARY RUBIO: Oh, good. Popular in India; that’s good to know. QUESTION: Among Indian Americans as well. SECRETARY RUBIO: All right. Go ahead; I’m sorry. QUESTION: What role do you see for India in G20, and Quad as well? What eludes – what’s the next step do you see for Quad coming or going forward in the leadership summit? SECRETARY RUBIO: What’s the next step? QUESTION: Next steps in Quad. SECRETARY RUBIO: Oh, we have – so, I mean, look, the challenge anytime you put together a format like the Quad is you can sit, and you can meet, and you can say we have all these things we want to work together on; you actually have to do it. So on many cases it’s going from talking about it to doing it. So we’ve had some success, some infrastructure projects in Palau and other places like that. We want to continue to build on that, which we are hoping to put together a business forum so that the businesses of the four countries can meet and identify unique opportunities to work together. So the forum is both a facilitator of nongovernmental cooperation, but also areas of cooperation – as an example, one of the areas that I think we’ve made substantial progress in for – to actually have concrete actions, is in humanitarian relief and disaster response. We want to be in a situation where the next time there is a humanitarian and/or – a crisis or a national – natural disaster in the region, that we can pool our resources to quickly provide assistance to a country that’s been hurt by a typhoon, or an earthquake, or a mudslide, or whatever it might be. And I think we’ve had some nascent success in that regard, but we want to be able to do more. Maritime awareness is another area where I think we can pool our resources to better understand not just what’s happening at the surface, but also under the water; any threats to freedom of navigation that are present, having awareness about the domain. So I think really the challenge for the Quad is we can have meetings and we’ve – but turning those meetings and the things we talk about into concrete actions, and I think we’re building really good momentum. And I think, hopefully, when our leaders meet in November, they will be able to announce some more concrete steps. So – and each one of these build more and more momentum for the Quad to be a forum that doesn’t just say these are four countries that get along with one another and work together, but actually doing things together. The best way to make a forum useful and important is to make sure that it does something – not just talks about it, but does it. And I think we’ve made good progress in the last 12 months. We want to build on it. This row here. Yes, sir. Just because you’re leaning forward. You guys need to lean forward. He was leaning forward, coming at me. QUESTION: Thank you. SECRETARY RUBIO: Yes, sir. QUESTION: My name is Abdel Elbardisi, and I’m from Al Araby TV. SECRETARY RUBIO: Okay. QUESTION: What makes the U.S. administration confident that the new strikes on Iran will be brief and quickly, as President Trump suggested, and also without accounting the retaliation from Iran? SECRETARY RUBIO: Yeah. First of all, I’m not going to comment about what the U.S. may or may not do militarily, so – nor is it – am I going to be up here and broadcast that any decision in that regard has been made. I think the President’s observation is the United States remains the most highly capable military power on Earth. We can achieve military objectives if we seek to. He hasn’t made a decision. I have no announcement in that regard with you today, and nor do we take any of it lightly. The President prefers not to do it that way. If he did, he would have done it weeks ago, months ago. He’d prefer to solve it diplomatically, but I think what the President expresses to you is the incredible confidence that if we needed to do something militarily, we would have the ability to do it and we really – we have everything we need to be successful, but we would prefer to do it peacefully. The next, right behind, right there, the gentleman. Yeah. QUESTION: Thank you. SECRETARY RUBIO: See, I’m just going row by row and just, like, I don’t know how. I’m not really – there’s no rhyme or reason to it, guys. My apology. QUESTION: Thank you, Secretary. SECRETARY RUBIO: He’s complaining. You get questions all the time. You’re with me all the time. Go ahead. QUESTION: Thank you, Secretary. My name is Steffen Wurzel. I’m with German broadcaster Deutschlandfunk. Do you think there’s a possibility for Mr. Zelenskyy, the Ukrainian president, to travel to take part in the G20 summit in Florida later this year? And secondly, was the topic of climate change discussed in the past days? Thank you. SECRETARY RUBIO: Well, it wasn’t one of the topics on the agenda, but of course a number of countries raised it. Brazil and others have raised it, and it comes up. But it wasn’t on our agenda in regards to that. But countries raise it in their statements, yes. And the first question about Zelenskyy, look, that’s a leaders-level meeting. That would be up to the President to decide. I wouldn’t rule it out. I think the President – especially if something positive could happen as a result of him attending. But I don’t have an announcement on that today. All right. Yes, sir. Right there. Leaning into the – you. Right? Yes. QUESTION: Thank you. My name is Jiha Ham with Voice of America’s Korean Service. So President Trump has expressed an interest in engaging with Kim Jong-un. So what concrete step is the administration taking to bring North Korea back to the negotiating table? Also, there have been some concerns in South Korea about possible strains in the U.S.-South Korea relationship, including recent visa issues involving South Korean lawmakers. So how would you characterize the current state of the relationship? SECRETARY RUBIO: Yeah. Well, we’ll work through the visa issues. I think there was one particular visa individually that there was an issue about regarding behavior perhaps a couple decades ago, but we’ll work through that at a bilateral basis, not in a press conference. And on your first question about North Korea, I mean, the President has repeatedly said, as he did in his first term, he’ll talk to anybody. The President doesn’t view talks, doesn’t view meeting with someone, as a concession. I know in traditional foreign policy, meeting with someone or inviting someone to something is viewed as a concession that somehow legitimizes them. I think the President’s perspective is if North Korea and Kim Jong-un is prepared to talk with the United States about issues that are of concern to us and concern to our allies like South Korea, he’d be open to doing it. Nothing has been scheduled. I don’t have anything to announce in regards to that today. I think that the gist of it is what he has said publicly and repeatedly, that he’s prepared for such a meeting. They had two such meetings in his first administration. I think if something productive could come from such talks, he’d be open to doing it again. But we don’t have any announcement on that. Nothing’s been scheduled in that regard. The last row. Are you guys journalists or are you just here? Okay. I know they’re not journalists because they work for me and they’re not getting any questions. All right, we’re going to go through this one more time and then we’re going to leave. Okay. QUESTION: One question. QUESTION: Secretary? SECRETARY RUBIO: Okay. Hold on. Go ahead. Did you already get a question? Okay, go. QUESTION: Thank you very much. SECRETARY RUBIO: Did he? Let me know if somebody’s cheating, because if they already had a question and I don’t remember, then you guys will all tell me. You’ll turn on them. Go ahead. QUESTION: Thank you very much. My name is Tom Watkins with The National . You’ve been asking Gulf countries to support the U.S. position on Iran, but they’re the ones that are facing the prospect of Iranian retaliation. What concrete security guarantees are you prepared to give allies like Saudi Arabia, the UAE, and other Gulf partners if a decision is made for the U.S. to resume strikes? SECRETARY RUBIO: Well, let me first say we’re there doing it now. I mean, it’s not our oil and natural gas that’s flowing through the Straits of Hormuz; it’s theirs, and it’s the lifeblood of their economies. And our – CENTCOM is there now protecting it. Virtually every day, every other day, we shoot down a drone or a missile that’s aimed at a ship that’s shipping, either coming in or leaving, with cargo from those countries or for those countries or their energy shipments. They’re already doing that. The United States also has an extensive presence in air defense, and we provide that and have done so in the past along with other – along with their own capacities. They’re using American equipment to do much of that. So no, we fully recognize the threat that’s posed, but think about it again. Just I want everybody – because sometimes we lose perspective here. Think about what we’re saying here. What the Iranian system, the Iranian regime is basically arguing is, unless we get what we want, not only will we blow up ships, but we will destroy the energy infrastructure of our neighbors in the entire region. Just think about that, because I think we skip over that like that’s some sort of normal behavior. That’s not normal behavior. That’s not – but we are there to help protect against it. But just imagine if Iran had a nuclear weapon. Imagine if Iran had a nuclear weapon. Imagine if Iran had weapons of mass destruction of any kind, be they chemical, biological, or nuclear – all three. Imagine if they had that. What would they threaten their neighbors with then? Then they wouldn’t be threatening to blow up pipelines. Then they’d be threatening to kill tens, if not hundreds, of thousands of people. That’s who we’re dealing with. So I think the fact that you even have to ask that question is a reminder of the nature of the regime that we’re dealing with in Tehran that’s been waging war, not just against the United States, but against its neighbors in the region since 1979, exporting their revolution. And so the next time that a Houthi strike reaches into Saudi territory, it’s a reminder that the Houthis would not have the weaponry they have now were it not for Iranian support. And the next time that Iranian – Shia-backed militias in Iraq either threaten the nation-state of Iraq or threaten the neighbors, it’s a reminder that Iran has been a destabilizing force against their neighbors and Iraq all of these years. The next time that an Iranian missile strikes a target in Bahrain or in Kuwait or anywhere else in the region, it’s a reminder of the threat that these people pose. By the way, the next time Hizballah fires a bunch of rockets and invites aggression coming back in their direction from Lebanon, not to mention threaten the Lebanese state, it’s a reminder that Hizballah would not exist, much less have the capabilities it has now to threaten its neighbors and launch rockets and missiles, were it not for Iranian support. Yes. You in the blue. Yeah, I know who you – that’s a nice blue color there. It’s almost Gator blue. Go ahead. QUESTION: Thank you, Secretary. I wanted to ask you about the participation of Sergey Lavrov in this week’s ministerial meetings. Your EU counterpart, Kaja Kallas, said today that hosting President Putin at the G20 in Miami in December would risk regularizing his war crimes. Some of your counterparts from other countries have been critical of the inclusion of Minister Lavrov this week. Why is it important to have Minister Lavrov here and to potentially include President Putin in Miami in December? SECRETARY RUBIO: Yeah. Well, I don’t have any announcement. I don’t even know if President Putin is going to come to Miami. They haven’t announced that and they haven’t confirmed that. So I thought the President thought it was important that Russia be a part of the G20 conversation because in the end, everything people ask about all the time is: What can you do to end the war in Ukraine? Well, just think about this for a moment. In order to end the war in Ukraine peacefully, you’re going to have to have a negotiated settlement. Who is that negotiated settlement between? Russia and Ukraine. How can you have a negotiated settlement between Russia and Ukraine if you don’t have the ability to talk to both Russia and Ukraine? How can you talk to both Russia and Ukraine unless you interact with them? And so I think today is just one more opportunity to continue to interact with the Russian system. As I’ve said to you earlier in my conversations, the President does not view meeting with someone or talking to someone as legitimizing everything they do or everything they stand for. What he does from a practical perspective, because he’s a person that comes from the common-sense world of business, not from a traditional foreign policy or traditional and archaic political class, is that what he doesn’t accept is the idea that somehow meeting with someone legitimizes them or makes you agree with everything that they do. It’s very simple. Everybody wants there to be a deal that brings about an end to this war. How can you do a deal unless you’re meeting with them, unless you’re talking to them, unless you’re interacting with them? And that – apart from that is the fact that Russia possesses a large number of nuclear weapons. Perhaps people don’t remember that, but we would remind you that I think it is important. No matter what, putting everything else aside, it is always important that the United States and Russia have communications at some level because of the danger of escalation in the future if, God forbid, something were to go wrong. So look, our position on it remains clear, and that is if we can play a role in mediating an end to that conflict, the United States is prepared to play that role. And to play that role, we have to have the ability to communicate with both sides. We talk to the Ukrainians plenty. We talk to them as much, if not more, than we talk to the Russian side. But we have to be able to talk to the Russian side. And one of the ways to do that is to invite them to forums like this, where they’re not just hearing from us, but potentially hearing from other countries that are there as well. On the next row. Oh wait, I went this side. Okay. All right, this guy’s not going to stop. Go ahead.. QUESTION: Thank you so much, Mr. Secretary. Alex Raufoglu, Radio Free — SECRETARY RUBIO: This better be a good question, because I wasn’t going to call on him. Go ahead. Okay. QUESTION: Just to follow up on what you just said on Lavrov, can you give us a better sense of your interaction with Lavrov this time? SECRETARY RUBIO: My what? QUESTION: With – your interaction with Lavrov, the interaction that — SECRETARY RUBIO: Well, we didn’t have a meeting. We spoke. I mean, we spoke about – but we didn’t have a meeting. We spoke just briefly about the opportunity for our leaders to potentially interact at APEC next month, and we spoke about – there was no firm commitments about G20. And that was – but we didn’t have any – we didn’t have a meeting. QUESTION: He did speak to his own pool, and he mentioned that the position on Ukraine has not changed. Given that position, what makes you believe that a negotiated peace is achievable? Thank you so much. SECRETARY RUBIO: Well, I don’t know if a negotiated peace is achievable in Ukraine. That’s what we’re trying to find out. But I don’t think anyone here is claiming that we’re on the verge of a negotiated settlement. I think what I can say to you is that the United States – we have people that basically – Jared and Steve as an example – work on this portfolio almost full-time between that and Iran; that’s all they focus on. They don’t focus on the Quad, they don’t focus on Western Hemisphere, they don’t – they focus on that, and we’ve invested – to say we’ve invested a lot of high-level attention to that topic. But we’re going to continue to try and see if we can reach an agreement, but I’m not here to tell you we’re on the verge of one, but hopefully we are. But today, we didn’t have any meetings about that at this G20 gathering. Okay, in this row right here. QUESTION: Thank you, Mr. Secretary. I wanted to ask you if – did the United States help Flávio Bolsonaro flee Brazil? And if you had any engagement with the foreign minister of Brazil here in Atlanta. SECRETARY RUBIO: Yeah. Yeah, I saw him here today. We talked yesterday as well. I think we’ll see each other in France. I think he’s attending the – Brazil’s an observer at the G7. They were there, so we’ll see them in France in a few weeks. We didn’t facilitate anything. I mean, we had word that he arrived at – in the United States. He had previously held a visa, and the President made the decision to allow him to enter the country, which we did. But we were not involved in any of the arrangements he made in terms of leaving. At least the U.S. Government was not involved directly in any of the moves that were made. But the President made clear that if he arrived in the United States in a port of entry, that he would be paroled into the country, and he was. Okay. Back row, right there. Yes, ma’am. You, yeah. You sound surprised, but it’s a press conference. QUESTION: Yes. SECRETARY RUBIO: You ready? Okay, let’s go. QUESTION: Thank you so much, Mr. Secretary. Thank you. Do you think a limited ceasefire, regarding Black Sea shipping and grains, is more likely now than before following this conference? SECRETARY RUBIO: Yeah, I’m not an odds-maker. I wouldn’t say more or less likely. I would say there’s interest in facilitating it. And by the way, it’s not new. Like, Türkiye, for example, has been consistently and at one point did have an agreement in place in the past, that then of course fell apart. So I wouldn’t say it’s – I don’t want to put or prognosticate the chances of it. I do think it’s having an impact on many countries around the world; you heard that expressed today. The African continent in particular is paying a high price for it, and there’s an energy component to it as well. So I really hate to put, like, odds, because in foreign policy in particular odds are a hard thing to set. But I do think there’s an incredible amount of interest in facilitating something, that we have nation-states that are involved, and India has also expressed an interest in perhaps floating some ideas. And so we’re open to that. We’ve been talking to countries. But I can’t give you odds as to how likely it is to happen. We’d like to see it happen. It doesn’t solve the war problem, but at least it diminishes some of the impact – spillover impact that it’s having on the food security of vulnerable countries. Okay, yes. Did I already get you? QUESTION: No. SECRETARY RUBIO: No, okay. Can we start putting, like, a little sticker on people when I call them? Because – (laughter) – I can’t – like, I’m – the lights make it hard for me to see you. Go ahead. QUESTION: Marco Valerio from RAI, Italian national TV. SECRETARY RUBIO: Ah, Italy. QUESTION: Yeah. My question is: In your speech in Athens, you called for a revival of Western democratic values. SECRETARY RUBIO: Yes. QUESTION: And I was wondering, when it comes to food crisis or Ukrainian crisis, is there any of those values that the U.S., along with the Europeans, is trying to uphold in finding a solution on the Ukrainian conflict? SECRETARY RUBIO: Well, I think – look, obviously, but I mean at the end of the day I think the Ukrainian-Russian issue is pretty singular right now, which is we’re trying to stop a very deadly war in which, on the one hand, Kyiv every single night is facing devastating attacks against its energy infrastructure, but also increasing number of civilians being killed; and even on the Russian side, you’re seeing 20,000 Russians killed a month. It’s a very deadly and destructive war, and every month that goes by you’re just adding – I mean, think about how long it’s going to take. When this stops, how long is it going to take Ukraine to rebuild its economy, rebuild its energy grid? We also think it’s very costly for Russia as well. So right now, I mean, yes, I mean, ultimately we would – I think embedded in all of this is values that we care a lot about. But the primary value we care about is – it’s not really very complicated. There’s a very nasty war going on, very destructive war, what appears to be in some ways of a stalemate that has the threat of escalation and spreading into other places. We already see some of the ancillary effects of this crisis – as an example, the Black Sea; as an example, some of these irregular efforts at sabotage that have spread into other countries; drones that are being launched that are being intercepted by electronic means, and so they wander into the airspace of a NATO country. There’s a lot of danger involved in that as well. So from us, the singular focus is: How can we – is there an opportunity for the United States, because we talk to both sides, to be able to facilitate a negotiated end to a very deadly, very costly, and very destructive war? And that’s really what we’re focused on. I think once – and that’s a pretty ambitious desire. Everyone has encouraged us. In every meeting we have, no matter what – be it the Europeans or others – we are encouraged to remain involved and engaged in this. And so we’ve remained involved and engaged, but that’s really what we’re focused on there. I don’t know how that ties into the speech I gave. Yes. Behind – well, go ahead. I feel bad; I pointed at you. Go ahead. We need to have more than one mike, guys. This is – go ahead. QUESTION: Thank you, Mr. Secretary. SECRETARY RUBIO: Yes. QUESTION: Paris Huang, Voice of America. Did you get a chance to convey the U.S.’s commitment to Taiwan and Ukraine to your Chinese and Russian counterparts? Also, did you also get a chance to talk to them the potential bilateral meeting in APEC or even in Miami? Thank you. SECRETARY RUBIO: The – which bilateral? I’m sorry. QUESTION: Between President Trump, President Xi, and President Putin. SECRETARY RUBIO: Well, there’ll most certainly be a bilateral meeting at both. I mean, they’ll meet in addition to being a part of these forums. I’m certain that we’ll meet with regards to that. So we really – we didn’t discuss it, those brief conversations about arrangements for both the attendance at G20 and at APEC. So we talked about that, but that was the gist of it. I mean, ultimately the point of this gathering, as I said, is we want – it’s not that geopolitical issues wouldn’t be discussed at G20 because I’m sure they are, and there were a lot of other bilateral meetings going on that we were not involved in between the different countries who were here. And it’s why we structured the agenda the way we did, to leave plenty of time for some of these countries to interact with one another. So I can’t speak to all of those meetings. But the core of this meeting and the core of what the President’s vision has been for G20 is to bring the G20, which is primarily an economic forum, back to its core principle and purpose, and that’s what we tried to address in the agenda we outlined today. That doesn’t mean that geopolitical issues weren’t discussed on the sidelines by different countries, but that’s what we focused on in both our agenda and in our engagements. Okay, right here in the middle. QUESTION: Thank you, Mr. Secretary. Majid Sattar from Allgemeine Zeitung , Germany. I was wondering whether you fear that your job will become more difficult come January when you have to deal with a Democratic Congress. SECRETARY RUBIO: Do I fear it? QUESTION: Yes. SECRETARY RUBIO: Well, first of all, we haven’t had an election yet so we don’t know what Congress will look like. So second of all, no. I mean, look, the foreign policy – Congress has a role to play in foreign policy; I played it for a very long time as a member of the Senate. So I understand what Congress can and cannot do with regards to foreign policy. But when it comes to issues of national security and foreign policy, the Executive Branch – and I learned this both ways; I learned it when we were in the majority and in the minority. I learned it when Republicans had the White House and didn’t have the White House, that the majority – our foreign policy is largely directed by the Executive Branch. Now, Congress has a role to play, primarily in the funding and the appropriations and in their oversight function. But that’s just a normal part of our system. I’ve been a part of it. I’ve been a part of it on both sides. I’ve been in the minority; I’ve been in the majority. I’ve had a Democratic White House and I’ve had a Republican White House. It won’t influence or change the President’s directives in terms of what he was elected to do. The President was elected to execute the foreign policy of the United States. That is a function of the Executive Branch. It obviously will have oversight from the congressional branch and it will have funding from the congressional branch. But that’s normal; administrations have played that in the past, with the president – the previous president, Biden, had a Republican Senate to deal with at one point. President Obama had to deal with a Republican majority at some point as well during his – so it’s not unique to have divided power in our system, and we’ve always had a foreign policy. And to my great frustration, when I was a member of the Senate, I realized that while there are things we could do, ultimately the foreign policy decisions are made by the Executive Branch and Congress plays a role. There’s no doubt about it. But the central role belongs to the Executive Branch. It’s something I learned when I was in the Legislative Branch, and it’s something I know now. But we’ll see how things play out. All right. I got a couple more questions. Go ahead. She – you. QUESTION: Thank you. Mirtha Donastorg from The Atlanta Journal-Constitution . So you’ve been – SECRETARY RUBIO: Oh, we have to go – you have to. QUESTION: Thank you. You’ve been lauding the city. Last night at the reception you praised Atlanta and the region’s vibrant economy, calling it the economy of the future. But when I talk to business owners and workers here, they’re struggling under high inflation and increased uncertainty from the administration’s economic policies. So given the priorities of this meeting, did any concrete solutions come from your discussions that will help ease the economic burden people in this city and state and across the country are feeling? SECRETARY RUBIO: Yeah, look, I think the way to cover the G20 is a little different than that. And it’s the G20 is a gathering of the 20 – theoretically the 20 largest economies in the world that collectively represent 80-something percent of global GDP. And the things we talked about today most certainly will have an impact, not just on Atlanta, not just on the United States, but the entire world; and not just next week or next month. Some of these are long-term issues – as an example, supply chains; as an example, energy. If access to energy is impeded or in any way we can’t generate sufficient energy, you can’t power your economy. Energy costs are imbedded in the cost of everything we buy and everything we pay for, which is why the U.S.’s energy dominance and it’s self-sustainability policies are so important. But none of these are magic elixirs that happen overnight. Likewise in the case of supply chains, and I think we learned sort of the first inklings of – supply chains was something you just talked about in the business world but it really wasn’t widely discussed politically or in society until COVID. And in COVID, people realized things we used to buy all the time are suddenly in short supply and you couldn’t get them because we realized that these supply chains are interlinked across the world, and if there’s a disruption halfway around the world, it could ultimately disrupt either how much you have to pay for something or how much access you have to it. So I think the way to cover G20, it is not a forum in which you are going to come up with solutions that you are going to feel tomorrow or next week or solely in the United States. It is a place where we are discussing issues that are going to impact and define the global economy – and Atlanta’s role in it, but the country’s role in it – for the next 20, 30, 40 years. So these are big-picture things that we’re talking about long term. Suffice it to say that whether it’s access to critical minerals necessary for technology, whether it’s access not just to energy to power what we do now but energy to power the things we need to do for a 21st century economy, or whether it’s supply chains across the board, these things are going to have a huge impact not just on what Atlanta looks like today but what Atlanta’s going to look like and how much it’s going to cost to live here and work here 10, 15, 20, 30 years down the road. That really is what the G20 focuses on. All right, I have time for two more questions. One way in the back, the gentleman right there. And then — QUESTION: You can take a question from me, sir. SECRETARY RUBIO: Huh? QUESTION: It’s my first time attending your press conference. SECRETARY RUBIO: Oh, it is? Who are you with? QUESTION: Voice of America. SECRETARY RUBIO: Good, but that would be, like, the third Voice of America question. All right. Well — QUESTION: Thank you very much, Mr. Secretary. SECRETARY RUBIO: I’m going to think about it while I answer his question. QUESTION: Some time ago, an agreement was made between the U.S., Denmark, and Greenland regarding Greenland and the Arctic up there. And for the last couple of weeks, the President has been very active in – on the campaign trail, saying that he was very glad that Denmark gave Greenland to the U.S. And that is being perceived a little differently in Denmark and in Greenland. So has the President misunderstood the agreement that was made, or has the people of Denmark and Greenland misunderstood? SECRETARY RUBIO: Yeah, I’m not sure what comments you’re referring to, and I certainly haven’t followed how it’s been covered in Denmark. Suffice it to say we have a very good deal, one the President is fully apprised of, he understands, and is very supportive of. And it builds on what we’ve done there for a long time. But one of the most important things that it does is it ensures that never do we have to worry about – irrespective of the decision Greenland makes to – if they one day go independent or stay, continue to be a part of the Kingdom of Denmark, it will never have to worry about it being a place where a potential adversary – through commercial means – can gain access to things that would be harmful to any of our countries. I think just from a strategic standpoint and where it is geographically, which was what the President has always focused on when it comes to Greenland, is national security. It has always played a critical role in national security. It is more pronounced now, not just because of defenses against missiles but because of the Arctic. And you now have a place that is not – we now have an agreement in place that will exist in perpetuity that ensures not just the equities of North America, meaning the United States and Canada, but all of our partners in NATO as well. And so it’s very solid in that regard, and we think it’s a very positive deal and one that I think gave us what the President was most interested in, and that is protecting not just the national security of the United States but the security of our Allies in NATO and in North America. Okay, I’m going to do your question, and then one more and then we’ve got to go. Yes, sir. QUESTION: Thank you, Mr. Secretary. U.S. is deporting dozens of Afghans back to their country. It’s the first time that the U.S. is deporting a large number of Afghans. How is this plan moving? And then do you — SECRETARY RUBIO: Well, I can’t comment on – I mean, we don’t – the State Department – I’m not avoiding your question. I’m just telling you it would not be – you’d have to direct that to the Department of Homeland Security. QUESTION: Sure. And in regards to the region, Pakistan and the de facto government in Afghanistan are at war. Now, the Russians stepped in to mediate between two countries. President Trump has ended many wars in many countries. How do you see these tensions in the region? SECRETARY RUBIO: Well, we share – look, Pakistan is concerned about terrorist attacks that are being sponsored from the territory of Afghanistan. They feel as if the Taliban has not done enough to constrain those attacks, and they’ve taken action against it. We obviously have heard those concerns on their part. We obviously don’t want them to be targeted for terrorism. So if there’s a productive role for us to play, we would play it. We don’t necessarily have the closest relationship with the Taliban, as you can imagine. So – but in the end, I mean, we’ve heard the concerns that Pakistan has raised, and we’ve seen some of those attacks that they point to. We’re against terrorism no matter where it emanates from and who it targets. Okay, final question. Yes, ma’am. QUESTION: Thank you, Mr. Secretary. You mentioned the Houthis and Bab al-Mandeb, but there’s a perception in the Middle East that the U.S. has downplayed the Houthi threat. How do you respond to that? I – you designated the Houthis as a terrorist organization, but the President himself said they are firing at one country. How do you respond to this perception? And at what point – or is there a red line the U.S. will join the Saudi strikes against the Houthis? SECRETARY RUBIO: Well, I won’t comment on that part of – those military objectives are always a decision for the Commander-in-Chief and the President. Suffice it to say that we have defense agreements with Saudi Arabia. We’ve lived up to those commitments and we’ll continue to live up to those commitments, particularly those that are defensive in nature. Beyond that, those are decisions for the President to make. We are in regular and continuous contact with our partners in Saudi Arabia, not just here today but on the phone and in conversations, including between the crown Prince, his highness, and the President, very recently and multiple times over the last month. So we’re tracking all that very closely. But the statement I would make is we have a defense cooperation agreement. We have defense understandings with Saudi Arabia. We intend to continue to live up to those commitments that have been made, and we’re happy to see that other countries have also participated and joined in helping defend the kingdom against these attacks. And we would remind everybody that, at the end of the day, the Houthis certainly – and the capabilities they have today – would not exist, they would not have the capabilities they have today, had it not been for the support – direct support – of the Iranian regime that allowed them to grow in their capabilities and continue to destabilize the region. Okay, thank you, guys. Thank you.

台湾骄傲游行参加者呼吁可见度、自由和结束耻辱 - 聚焦台湾
台湾骄傲游行参加者呼吁可见度、自由和结束耻辱
要激活文字转语音服务，请首先同意以下隐私政策。
周六，多家公司的团队参加了在台北市政府广场举行的第24届台湾骄傲游行。中央通讯社照片2026年10月31日
中新社台北10月31日电 周六，估计有15万名来自台湾和海外的参与者聚集在台北，参加一年一度的台湾LGBT+骄傲游行，庆祝表达自己的自由，同时呼吁更多理解和结束歧视。
游行组织者台湾彩虹民事行动协会主席戴佑勋表示，2019年同性婚姻合法化保障了婚姻权利，但并不意味着台湾社会充分理解LGBTQ+人群或在日常生活中公平对待他们。
“我们需要重新倾听，这样我们才能理解他人的差异，超越标签并理解这些问题，”戴在游行前告诉记者。
台湾彩虹公民行动协会主席戴裕勋在周六台北举行的台湾 LGBT+ 骄傲游行前向记者发表讲话。中央通讯社照片2026年10月31日
他说，10 月 3 日，警方搜查了台北万华区的一家同性恋酒吧，这让人们重拾了国家对 LGBTQ+ 空间的压迫的记忆，并会激发人们表达他们的愤怒。
尽管市政府已道歉并对人员进行纪律处分，但戴呼吁进行透明的调查并制定具有约束力的警务准则。该市周四表示，检察官正在调查此案，并将根据社区意见制定指导方针。
戴还敦促进一步努力消除艾滋病毒/艾滋病的耻辱，并表示恐惧和偏见阻碍了检测。他补充说，台湾的长期护理系统还需要做好准备，以支持感染艾滋病毒的老年人。
19岁的国立清华大学人文社会学院本科生潘丽丽(Alice Pan)继去年参加旧金山游行后，于周六首次参加台湾骄傲节。
潘回忆道，人们在旧金山自信地表达自己的想法。与台北的同学一起，她说自己是异性恋，但希望支持各种性取向的人。
“每个人都应该有爱和被爱的权利，”她说，并鼓励人们参加骄傲活动，挑战网上恐同言论背后的误解。
周六，在台北举行的第 24 届台湾骄傲游行期间，身着皮卡丘服装的日本参与者在台北市政府摆姿势拍照。中央通讯社照片2026年10月31日
24 岁的香港游客梁薇薇 (Verena Leung) 回国参加第二次台湾骄傲节，并被包容的氛围所吸引，邀请了一位朋友加入。
梁说，香港 LGBTQ+ 活动的取消让她感觉越来越受到限制，并希望在台湾体验自由。
她不穿胸罩，穿着与扭结相关的绳索，她将自己的服装描述为身体自主的表达，并呼吁人们不受歧视地表达自己。
来自台北的 33 岁保险销售员蔡威廉 (William Tsai) 正在参加他的第五次游行。此前，他曾亲自参赛，今年他代表一个 LGBTQ+ 友好的英语俱乐部担任主席。
蔡说，每年重返街头有助于人们了解 LGBTQ+ 社区并减少冲突。国际

Taiwan Pride parade attendees call for visibility, freedom and an end to stigma
To activate the text-to-speech service, please first agree to the privacy policy below.
Teams from several companies join the 24th Taiwan Pride parade at Taipei City Hall plaza on Saturday. CNA photo Oct. 31, 2026
Taipei, Oct. 31 (CNA) An estimated 150,000 participants from Taiwan and abroad gathered in Taipei for the annual Taiwan LGBT+ Pride parade on Saturday, celebrating the freedom to express themselves while calling for greater understanding and an end to discrimination.
Legalizing same-sex marriage in 2019 guaranteed marriage rights but did not mean Taiwanese society fully understood LGBTQ+ people or treated them fairly in everyday life, said Tai Yu-hsun (戴佑勳), chairperson of parade organizer Taiwan Rainbow Civil Action Association.
"We need to return to listening so we can understand others' differences, move beyond labels and understand these issues," Tai told reporters before the march.
Taiwan Rainbow Civil Action Association chairperson Tai Yu-hsun speaks to reporters ahead of the Taiwan LGBT+ Pride parade in Taipei on Saturday. CNA photo Oct. 31, 2026
An Oct. 3 police search of a gay bar in Taipei's Wanhua District had revived memories of state oppression of LGBTQ+ spaces and would motivate people to voice their anger, he said.
Although the city government had apologized and disciplined personnel, Tai called for a transparent investigation and binding policing guidelines. The city said Thursday that prosecutors were investigating the case and that guidelines would be developed with community input.
Tai also urged further efforts to combat HIV/AIDS stigma, saying fear and prejudice discouraged testing. Taiwan's long-term care system also needed to prepare to support aging people living with HIV, he added.
Alice Pan (潘), a 19-year-old undergraduate studying at National Tsing Hua University's College of Humanities and Social Sciences, attended Taiwan Pride for the first time Saturday after participating in San Francisco's parade last year.
Pan recalled people confidently expressing themselves in San Francisco. Joining classmates in Taipei, she said she was heterosexual but wanted to support people of every sexual orientation.
"Everyone deserves the right to love and be loved," she said, encouraging people to attend Pride to challenge misunderstandings underlying homophobic comments online.
Japanese participants in Pikachu costumes pose for photos at Taipei City Hall during the 24th Taiwan Pride parade in Taipei on Saturday. CNA photo Oct. 31, 2026
Hong Kong visitor Verena Leung (梁), 24, returned for her second Taiwan Pride and invited a friend to join her, drawn by its inclusive atmosphere.
Cancellations of LGBTQ+ events in Hong Kong had left her feeling increasingly restricted and wanting to experience freedom in Taiwan, Leung said.
Going without a bra and wearing ropes associated with kink, she described her outfit as an expression of bodily autonomy and a call for people to express themselves without discrimination.
William Tsai (蔡), a 33-year-old insurance salesperson from Taipei, was attending his fifth parade. Previously participating for himself, he was this year representing an LGBTQ+-friendly English-speaking club as its chair.
Returning to the streets each year helped people understand LGBTQ+ communities and reduced conflict, Tsai said. International visitors made the annual gathering feel like an extended family, offering freedoms some could not experience at home, he added.
"Today is our gay Christmas day," he said.
The 24th Taiwan Pride parade sets off from the plaza in front of Taipei City Hall on Saturday, with organizers inviting participants to help unfurl a giant rainbow flag. CNA photo Oct. 31, 2026
Before the march, Tai estimated at least 150,000 people would attend the 24th parade, themed "Our Voices, Our Journey," with more than 180 groups registered.
The march was scheduled to depart Taipei City Hall Plaza at 2:05 p.m. along two loops.
The northern route follows Ren'ai, Dunhua South, Zhongxiao East and Yixian roads before returning via Ren'ai Road. The southern route takes Ren'ai, Guangfu South, Xinyi and Dunhua South roads before returning along Ren'ai Road.
Both finish at the plaza. The second stage program was scheduled to begin at 4:25 p.m., the rainbow market to close at 6 p.m., and the event to end at 6:40 p.m.

中新社台北10月31日电 据主办方台湾同知热线协会称，周五晚上估计有3800人走上台北街头，表达对跨性别群体的支持。
台湾跨界大游行以“跨界·同心”为主题，从和平公园228号出发，向西穿过西门町商圈部分区域，返回公园。
该协会表示，该主题呼吁打破社会对性别的二元期望，缩小跨性别者与更广泛社区之间的差距。
该热线还强调了世界各地的跨性别问题，呼吁人们跨越国界，与跨性别者站在一起，共同反对污名和歧视。
参与者挥舞着跨性别旗帜和彩虹旗，并举着写有“跨性别权利就是人权”和“敌人是父权制，而不是跨性别女性”等口号的横幅。
他们还呼吁台湾政府废除强制手术改变身份证件性别标记的要求。

“变性人权利就是人权，”她说。

【原文 English Original】
3,800 march in Taipei in support of transgender community - Focus Taiwan
LGBTQ RIGHTS/3,800 march in Taipei in support of transgender community
To activate the text-to-speech service, please first agree to the privacy policy below.
Participants in the Taiwan Trans March hold up a transgender flag at the head of the march. CNA photo, Oct. 30, 2025.
Taipei, Oct. 31 (CNA) An estimated 3,800 people took to the streets of Taipei on Friday night to show their support for the transgender community, according to the organizer, the Taiwan Tongzhi (LGBTQ+) Hotline Association.
Themed "Crossing Boundaries, Standing Together," the Taiwan Trans March began at 228 Peace Park, proceeded west through part of the Ximending shopping district and then returned to the park.
The theme calls for breaking down society's binary expectations around gender and bridging the gap between transgender people and the wider community, the association said.
The Hotline also highlighted transgender issues around the world, calling on people to cross national borders and stand in solidarity with transgender people in the fight against stigma and discrimination.
Participants waved transgender and rainbow flags and carried banners bearing slogans such as "Trans Rights Are Human Rights" and "The Patriarchy Is The Enemy, Not Trans Women."
They also called on the Taiwanese government to abolish the requirement for mandatory surgery to change gender markers on identification documents.
Taiwanese concert pianist Huang Yi-chung, who came out as transgender in September. CNA photo, Oct. 30, 2025.
Among the marchers was Taiwanese pianist Huang Yi-chung (黃顗中), who told CNA that she had experienced gender dysphoria for 12 years before coming out as transgender in September. She said she had been in extreme emotional distress because she no longer wanted to live as a man.
"Trans Rights Are Human Rights," she said.
Alex, who is from South Africa and identifies as nonbinary, poses with a transgender flag. CNA photo, Oct. 30, 2025.
Another participant, Alex, who identifies as nonbinary, said they and their partner had come to Taiwan for the Pride events in Taipei. Originally from South Africa and now living in Vietnam with their partner, Alex said the march was meaningful because they had never seen so many transgender people gathered in one place.
"It's really nice to feel seen, to feel like I'm not alone, ... I'm so happy to be here," they told CNA.
Now in its eighth year, the Taiwan Trans March is one of the few marches in Asia dedicated to transgender issues, the Hotline said.
Saturday will mark the 24th Taiwan LGBT+ Pride. The parade is scheduled to begin at Taipei City Hall Square at 2 p.m.
Taiwan floats join New York, San Francisco Pride parades
Taiwan-themed floats were part of the New York City (NYC) Pride March and the San Francisco (SF) Pride Parade on Sunday, featuring Taiwanese drag performers in New York and Taiwan's mascot Oh Bear in San Francisco.
Taiwan launches gender equality week in New York ahead of U.N. session
Taiwan's Ministry of Foreign Affairs (MOFA) and various non-governmental groups on Sunday launched a series of gender equality events in New York to coincide with the 70th session of the United Nations Commission on the Status of Women (CSW70).
150,000 join Taiwan Pride as organizers urge understanding
Around 150,000 people attended Taiwan Pride on Saturday, with organizers and participants expressing hope that the parade would help build understanding amid a growing global backlash against diversity, equity and inclusion (DEI).

（中央社記者廖漢原華盛頓3日專電）美國選民今天前往投票所，投票決定下屆國會席次與多州下任州長。今年期中選舉結果攸關總統川普未來執政是否跛腳，2028年總統大選候選人動態，及民主黨左派勢力能否在國會掌握實質影響力。
美國選民3日前往各地投票所，投票選出435位聯邦眾議員、35位聯邦參議員及36個州的州長等。選後兩黨國會版圖變化攸關總統川普（Donald Trump）第2任期未來2年，內政、外交、經濟政策等能否順利上路，及2028年總統選舉兩黨人選的動態。
除了國會議員及州長選舉，各州同步舉行包括墮胎權、同志權益、富人稅、投票權認定與保障移民等多項公投。
美國領土跨越多個時區，從東岸到西岸及阿拉斯加州，各州投票時間約在當地早上6時至晚間9時間，投開票時間都較長。全美約有6000萬選民已提前及郵寄完成投票，創下期中選舉新紀錄。由於多州聯邦參眾議員選情膠著，選舉整體結果可能在數日之後才會明朗。
選前美國多數民調顯示，選民較關注通膨、油價等經濟議題，反對陷入伊朗戰爭。民主黨在選戰中主打「可負擔」生活，環境對執政的共和黨較不利。部分民調指民主黨甚至有機會拿下眾院238至241席，取得遠高於218席過半的穩定多數。
聯邦參議員改選的35席中，多數民調指包括德州、密西根州、愛荷華州、俄亥俄州、阿拉斯加州、堪薩斯州等，約有6到9州選情膠著，候選人支持度長期未見超越民調誤差領先差距，難以預料共和黨能否繼續維持參院過半優勢。
華府一處投票所上午開放選民進入投票。中央社記者廖漢原華盛頓攝 115年11月4日
此外，民主黨內左派及民主社會主義聯盟（Democratic Socialists of America，DSA）近期聲勢走高，約有5名DSA支持的全新候選人可能進入眾院，加上現任眾議員歐加修-寇蒂茲（Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez，AOC）等，屆時可能有能力影響國會動向。
支持DSA華盛頓特區市長候選人路易斯．喬治（Janeese Lewis George）的布勞納（Joanna Brauner）向中央社記者表示，許多人對民主社會主義聯盟候選人有興趣，因為他們講出了大部分民眾日常生活要面對的問題，包括可負擔生活、日常用品、住房、租金、家庭照護、工作、福利、家庭成員醫療假及個人病假等，這些都是民眾想要的生活品質。
她說，因為華盛頓特區重視誰掌控國會，及國會是否友善對待華府的自治自主，希望選民也能思考最高法院、女權及健保的未來，不再捲入不必要的戰爭及氣候變遷等。（編輯：洪啓原）1151104

（中央社華盛頓3日綜合外電報導）美國聯邦當局起訴一名來自奧克拉荷馬市的男子，指控他在2024年與2026年選舉前，寄送數以百計含有白色粉末的信件給公職人員，信內並附有關於叛國罪的不祥警告。
美聯社報導，美國聯邦調查局（FBI）在今天公開的法庭文件中表示，這些粉末最後發現沒有危害，成分是酵母或麵粉，但並非所有信件都完成檢驗。
馬丁（Robin Martin）遭控傳播虛假訊息並郵寄具威脅性的信件。他於昨天遭到逮捕，預計今天將在奧克拉荷馬市（Oklahoma City）聯邦地區法院出庭。
FBI表示，這起調查可追溯至2024年，當時多個州的選務官員通報收到內含白色物質的郵件，裡面還放了一封長達3頁、宣稱要發動戰爭的信件。其中一些信件含有透過紫外線才能看到的警告字句，像是「站在歷史正確的一邊！你的生命可能取決於此！！」
寄件者在回郵地址欄寫上「美國叛國者剷除軍（U.S.T.E.A., United States Traitor Elimination Army），馬里蘭州塔科馬帕克市（Takoma Park）」。
調查人員認為，今年秋天寄出的700多封郵件似乎與同一名寄件者有關，但使用不同的回郵地址。FBI探員柯爾（David Cole）在宣誓書中指出，這些郵件寄給選務官員、國會議員、民調機構、新聞媒體與聯邦執法機構。
在2024年與2026年寄出的郵件中，常見的訊息是警告收件者，他們將因叛國罪「或更嚴重的罪名！！」遭到逮捕。
柯爾說：「這封信件的寄件人描述他所認為的2020年選舉問題，聲稱總統川普贏得2020年大選，並擔憂部分相同問題可能在即將舉行的2024年選舉中再次浮現。」
聯邦當局上月宣布，正在調查寄往全美各地國會與選舉辦公室、內含「可疑物質」的信件，並呼籲收件者將這些信件視為可能具危險性。（編譯：張曉雯）1151104

（中央社記者廖漢原華盛頓3日專電）美國晶片大廠超微（AMD）今天公布第3季財報，營收較去年同期成長45%，執行長蘇姿丰指出，有信心未來幾年延續強勢成長。另一家台裔業者美超微（SMCI）今天也公布業績，營收大幅超前去年同期表現。兩家AI設備業者盤後交易價均走高。
美國晶片業者超微（Advanced Micro Devices，AMD）3日公布第3季業績，在大數據中心設備銷售額接近去年一倍的強勁增長，及毛利率維持在54%高水準等營運表現支撐下，上季營收達133.8億美元，較去年同期成長45%，每股盈餘2.09美元，均優於市場預期。
超微董事長暨執行長蘇姿丰在新聞稿中指出，公司創下破紀錄季度業績，營收超過財務指標設定的上限，大數據中心部門銷售額較去年同期成長近一倍。
她表示，市場對超微AI晶片系列Instinct和CPU處理器EPYC等產品需求持續增加，AI機櫃系統Helios和第6代處理器Venice全面進入量產，預期第4季成長將進一步加速。超微擁有領先市場的產品組合及與客戶、供應鏈的深厚關係，有信心未來幾年延續強勢營收成長，擴大獲利能力。
超微近期面臨AI類股遭投資人拋售的挑戰，過去3個交易日股價走低，不過上季強勁業績表現扳回一城。英特爾（Intel）因個人電腦市場持續萎縮及未來展望不佳，股價在10月30日大跌近3成。
在AI設備強勁需求下，伺服器業者美超微（Super Micro Computer, Inc.）3日公布正式財報表現驚人，營收超過去年同期的3倍，達199億美元，調整後每股盈餘1.81美元，均大幅超過分析師預期。
美超微董事長暨執行長梁見後在新聞稿指出，美超微持續加速轉型為全方位AI與IT數據中心供應商，上季創下199億美元高營收。
他表示，美超微資料中心建構模組解決方案（Data Center Building Block Solutions, DCBBS）為各種客戶，從百萬瓩級的資料中心到小型單一貨櫃式模組化架構POD，都能創造龐大價值。（編輯：陳慧萍）1151104

（中央社記者林尚縈柏林3日專電）美俄烏將展開新一輪和平談判，烏克蘭總統澤倫斯基今天在德國呼籲，歐洲應在美國可能縮減安全投入之際，承擔更大責任。德國總理梅爾茨則強調，歐洲不能被排除在和平談判之外，宣布兩週後在柏林召開援烏峰會，強化對烏克蘭支持。
美國、烏克蘭與俄羅斯預計10日至11日在阿拉伯聯合大公國首都阿布達比舉行新一輪三方磋商，由美方居中斡旋，討論停火、烏克蘭戰後安全等議題，目前尚未宣布是否有歐洲代表參加。
澤倫斯基（Volodymyr Zelenskyy）今天訪問柏林，在與德國總理梅爾茨（Friedrich Merz）舉行聯合記者會後，現身柏林安全會議（BSC）發表演說。
他在演說中以今天美國國會期中選舉為切入點指出，過去美國提供的安全保障「就像空氣一樣」，讓盟友習以為常、不必擔心失去。澤倫斯基認為，未來美國即使不退出北約等既有安全合作機制，也可能更加專注國內事務，減少對歐洲及其他盟友安全的關注。
澤倫斯基指出，世界上已有其他國家開始將歐洲視為安全保障的來源，儘管歐洲目前仍有許多潛力尚待發揮，但具備成為強大安全力量的條件。他強調，美國在世界上的角色可能進一步縮小，歐洲就必須扮演更重要的角色，而德國在其中不可或缺。
日前有媒體曾引述美方高層報導，川普（Donald Trump）政府正探索將俄國天然氣重新輸往歐洲，包括重啟德俄間北溪天然氣管線（Nord Stream）作為和平協議一環。
澤倫斯基以中國為例指出，俄羅斯經濟離不開中國市場，同樣也需要與歐洲維持經濟往來。他呼籲歐洲全面落實對俄制裁，對莫斯科施加更大壓力，迫使俄方停止戰爭。
他並表示，美國總統川普對俄羅斯總統普丁具有影響力，但僅靠外交對話不足以迫使俄羅斯停戰，歐洲也必須展現更強大的力量，在和平談判中發揮作用。
另一方面，梅爾茨在稍早與澤倫斯基舉行的聯合記者會上表示，俄烏戰爭的結果將長期影響歐洲安全，支持烏克蘭不僅是援助遭受侵略的國家，也符合德國自身安全利益。
梅爾茨說，任何涉及對俄制裁及歐洲未來安全架構的和平協議，都不能缺少歐洲參與。歐洲不僅承擔對烏克蘭的軍事與財政援助，也握有對俄羅斯實施制裁的經濟籌碼，因此必須在和平談判中發揮作用。
德國目前是烏克蘭最大的歐洲軍事援助國，但梅爾茨強調，維護歐洲安全不能只由德國承擔，其他歐洲國家也必須履行援助承諾。
梅爾茨進一步宣布，19日將與法國、英國共同在柏林召開「志願聯盟」（Coalition of the Willing）峰會，邀集多國領袖協調2027年對烏克蘭的軍事及財政援助，並討論停火後的烏克蘭安全保障與和平進程。（編輯：陳慧萍）1151104
