On October 28, Taiwanese media reported that the Secretary for Relations with States of the Holy See, Archbishop Paul Richard Gallagher, addressed the progress of negotiations regarding a Vatican office in China at an event with journalists in Rome. When a reporter asked about the status of these talks, Monsignor Gallagher responded: “The idea is to have some type of cultural presence in Beijing. But, as with everything in a negotiation, there would be a price to pay and, for the moment, we are not willing to pay that price.”
The report drew significant attention in Taiwan and Hong Kong media. This was partly because it cited earlier reporting by the Italian daily Corriere della Sera that, during the tenure of the late Pope Francis, the Vatican’s Secretariat of State repeatedly expressed a long-standing desire to establish a “permanent office” in China. Corriere della Sera also noted that Beijing proposed a precondition, demanding that the Vatican first sever diplomatic ties with Taiwan.
The Taiwanese news outlet ETtoday followed up, using the headline, “Beijing Proposes ‘Severing Ties with Taiwan’ in Exchange for an Office? Vatican Foreign Minister: Not Prepared to Pay the Price for Now.” Meanwhile, Hong Kong’s TVB provided an in-depth report headlined, “Vatican Foreign Minister: Sino-Vatican Bishop Agreement Flawed, Holy See Has No Intention of Setting Up Office in Beijing.” Archbishop Gallagher’s remarks about establishing an office have undoubtedly struck a sensitive nerve in cross-strait relations.
However, while Archbishop Gallagher mentioned that “there would be a price to pay,” he did not explicitly state what that “price” entails. A report by INFOVATICANA simply noted, “The archbishop did not wish to specify what the demands would be to reach such an understanding. Currently, the Holy See maintains diplomatic relations with Taiwan and has a study mission in Hong Kong, but does not have official diplomatic representation in the People’s Republic of China.”
Reuters’ reporting focused solely on Gallagher’s admission of the provisional agreement’s flaws, quoting him as saying: “It’s not easy, the dialogue is not easy. The imperfections of the agreement are evident, but there is a commitment to persevere in dialogue… and that is what will continue to happen.”
Comparing Chinese and English media reports, the assertion that the “price” the Holy See must pay – but is currently unwilling to – involves severing ties with Taiwan seems to be an interpretation by Chinese-language media of past Italian reporting, which in turn reflected the Chinese Communist Party-led government’s stated position.
Beyond the political maneuvering between Taiwan and China over formal Vatican recognition, what is the Holy See’s real motive for establishing an office in China? Is it to forge diplomatic relations, or is it a procedural step in negotiating the agreement on the appointment of bishops?
I believe it is necessary to clarify the significance of this “office” through the lens of the Holy See’s pastoral mechanism for China – specifically, the appointment of bishops. The Vatican’s effort to establish a presence in Beijing should not be oversimplified as “the Holy See rejecting China’s demand to break ties with Taiwan” or “the Holy See currently having no intention of opening an office in Beijing.”
As to whether this issue will return to the Sino-Vatican negotiating table, some scholars believe that the issue of setting up an office is unlikely to be discussed in near-term negotiations, now that the policy position is clear. I disagree; establishing an “office” will almost certainly remain an active topic of discussion. My primary argument is that an on-the-ground presence is necessary to properly implement the Sino-Vatican agreement. A Papal delegate’s presence in Beijing is necessary for good governance over the episcopal appointment process. Beijing is deliberately misinterpreting the purpose of this “office” as a matter of diplomatic negotiation over cross-strait relations, masking its true reluctance to loosen its control over the Catholic Church’s religious freedom.
While traveling in a devoutly Catholic European country, I had the privilege of attending its National Day reception. During the event, I met a senior Holy See diplomat assigned to that nation. Out of curiosity, I asked, “Father, what does your daily work entail? Being in such a devout Catholic country, is your work fairly smooth?” The diplomat replied, “Not exactly. 90 percent of my work involves investigating bishop appointments. I need to understand the backgrounds of so many clergy members to determine who is suitable to become a bishop.” This Holy See diplomat’s statement truthfully outlined the core mission of a papal diplomat. Fulfilling pastoral care in a local Catholic Church includes vetting candidates for the episcopacy as a primary task.
The Holy See and the People’s Republic of China signed a provisional agreement on the appointment of bishops in 2018, and renewed it in 2024 for another four years, until 2028. Since the signing of the agreement, the Pope has appointed several bishops in China, resulting in an increasingly rejuvenated Chinese Catholic episcopate. However, the process by which China selects bishop candidates remains a black box. Because there is no true religious freedom in China, the Catholic Church remains under severe control of the Chinese Communist Party’s United Front Work Department.
Scholars note that, even without a formal Holy See-Vatican office in China, certain civic organizations operated by religious orders may play intermediary roles. Yet these unofficial mechanisms are far less institutionalized than establishing a direct, official office in Beijing. Regarding the Holy See’s process for selecting bishop candidates, a significant concern is whether the background of every episcopal candidate can be vetted in a diverse and transparent manner. If the Holy See does not have an official delegate in China – and if that representative cannot investigate freely while possessing completely uncontrolled personal liberty – then establishing a Holy See-Vatican office in Beijing is a false proposition, one that merely falls into the CCP’s diplomatic narrative of coercing the Holy See over whether to sever ties with the Republic of China (Taiwan).
In the article “Diplomacy and Divided Nations: The Holy See’s Approach to China and Taiwan,” published in the journal Issues & Studies, Yun Wang and I analyzed the distinction between a Papal Delegation and an Apostolic Nunciature. The core differences lie in the presence of “Diplomatic Recognition” and whether the primary counterpart for engagement is the “local government” or the “local church.” These two terms represent entirely different tiers of diplomatic tools the Vatican uses across varying political environments and historical periods. Whether the Holy See-Vatican is pushing to establish a Papal Delegation or an Apostolic Nunciature in Beijing becomes clearer when we look at another Asian communist state the Holy See engages with: Vietnam.
The office in Beijing is truly intended to be a Papal Delegation, an ecclesiastical rather than diplomatic office. However, the CCP cleverly conflates the two. When the Holy See proposes a Papal Delegation to China, Beijing counters that establishing an Apostolic Nunciature requires “first severing ties with Taipei.” This is a malicious interpretation to disguise China’s basic lack of religious freedom.
This year marks the 400th anniversary of Catholicism’s arrival in Taiwan. The Chargé d’Affaires of the Apostolic Nunciature to China (Taipei), Monsignor Stefano Mazzotti, has attended multiple events marking the anniversary. “This year marks the 400th anniversary of the arrival of the first Catholic missionaries in Taiwan to evangelize,” he said in one such speech. “Today, the Catholic Church has taken deep root and become an indispensable part of Taiwan’s diverse society. The Holy See will work hand in hand with the international community, including Taiwan, to continue to develop and consolidate the Church’s mission within the framework of ‘security and freedom,’”
As my previous article “Taiwan-Vatican Ties: The Dynamic Interplay Under Pope Leo XIV” indicated, amid shifting Sino-Vatican dynamics, Taiwan has no reason to worry. In the eyes of the Holy See, Taiwan remains an undeniably “precious” presence. I firmly believe Taiwan can be decoupled from the Sino-Vatican negotiation narrative, and indeed, it must be. Neither Taiwan nor the Holy See should fall into the narrative trap maliciously set by the Chinese Communist Party.

title: ACM Research Announces Shipment of Its First 310 × 310 mm Ultra ECP ap-p Panel-Level Horizontal Electroplating Production Tool
zh_title: ACM Research 宣布发货其首款 310 × 310 mm Ultra ECP ap-p 面板级水平电镀生产工具
summary: 半导体和先进封装应用晶圆加工解决方案供应商 ACM Research, Inc. 今天宣布向中国大陆以外的亚洲客户发货其首个 310 × 310 mm Ultra ECP ap-p 面板级水平电镀生产系统。此次发货标志着 ACM 核心面板级技术的又一重大进步，也是在拓宽其多产品平台和扩大全球客户影响力方面向前迈出的重要一步。随着先进封装技术的不断发展，面板级加工越来越受到关注
content:
半导体和先进封装应用晶圆加工解决方案供应商 ACM Research, Inc. 今天宣布向中国大陆以外的亚洲客户发货其首个 310 × 310 mm Ultra ECP ap-p 面板级水平电镀生产系统。此次发货标志着 ACM 核心面板级技术的又一重大进步，也是在拓宽其多产品平台和扩大全球客户影响力方面向前迈出的重要一步。随着先进封装技术的不断发展，面板级处理因其适应更大基板的能力而在整个行业中受到关注。电镀是先进封装制造中最关键的步骤之一，其中设备稳定性、镀层厚度均匀性和一致性对于成功的工艺集成、产品良率和制造效率至关重要。新发货的工具专为 310 × 310 mm 面板级应用而设计，展示了 ACM 根据客户要求快速推进产品开发的能力。在此之前，ACM 首款 515 × 510 mm 研发工具于去年发货，突显了 ACM 将技术突破快速商业化至规模生产的能力。 “这是 ACM 先进封装工作的一个重要里程碑，标志着我们向亚洲客户交付了世界上第一个 310 × 310 毫米面板级水平电镀生产工具，”ACM 博士说。
ACM Research 总裁兼首席执行官 David Wang 表示：“我们相信，我们专有的水平电镀技术具有独特的优势，能够实现跨多种面板尺寸和新兴封装架构的下一代先进半导体封装。随着人工智能推动日益复杂的封装要求，我们看到了 ACM 在这个快速发展的市场中发挥推动作用的重要长期机会。” Ultra ECP ap-p 系统采用 ACM 专有的水平电镀技术，支持铜 (Cu)、镍 (Ni)、锡银 (SnAg) 和金 (Au) 电镀工艺。其铜电镀室采用专为高铜柱应用设计的高速电镀桨，能够在高电镀速率下为 300 微米铜柱实现良好的芯片内均匀性。该系统还具有四面密封干接触吸盘，可提高可靠性；单元内冲洗功能可最大限度地减少不同电镀单元之间的化学交叉污染；水平电镀设计采用 ACM 正在申请专利的技术，使吸盘的旋转与旋转矩形电场同步，从而实现卓越的沉积均匀性。除了设备交付之外，ACM 还致力于通过提供高质量设备、支持可靠的批量生产和提供可靠的技术支持来建立长期的客户关系。
ACM将继续推进技术进步，拓展多产品平台，扩大全球客户群。ACM旨在通过与全球合作伙伴的合作，支持人工智能行业的发展，并以其差异化的半导体设备技术为客户创造更大的价值。 ACM Research 宣布其首款 310 × 310 mm Ultra ECP ap-p 面板级水平电镀生产工具发货的消息首先出现在《半导体文摘》上。

【原文 English Original】
ACM Research, Inc. , a supplier of wafer processing solutions for semiconductor and advanced packaging applications, today announced the shipment of its first 310 × 310 mm Ultra ECP ap-p panel-level horizontal electroplating production system to a customer in Asia outside mainland China. The shipment marks another significant advance in ACM’s core panel-level technologies and represents an important step forward in broadening its multi-product platform and expanding its global customer presence. As advanced packaging technologies continue to evolve, panel-level processing is gaining traction across the industry for its ability to accommodate larger substrates. Electroplating is one of the most critical steps in advanced packaging manufacturing, where equipment stability, plating thickness uniformity and consistency are essential to successful process integration, product yield and manufacturing efficiency. The newly shipped tool is designed for 310 × 310 mm panel-level applications, and demonstrates ACM’s ability to quickly advance product development per customer requirements. This follows last year’s shipment of ACM’s first 515 × 510 mm R&D tool, highlighting ACM’s ability to rapidly commercialize technical breakthroughs into scale production. “This is an important milestone for ACM’s advanced packaging efforts, and marks shipment of what we believe is the world’s first 310 × 310 mm panel-level horizontal electroplating production tool to a customer in Asia,” said Dr. David Wang, President and Chief Executive Officer of ACM Research. “We believe our proprietary horizontal plating technology is uniquely positioned to enable the next generation of advanced semiconductor packaging across multiple panel sizes and emerging packaging architectures. As AI drives increasingly complex packaging requirements, we see a significant long-term opportunity for ACM to play an enabling role in this rapidly evolving market.” The Ultra ECP ap-p system features ACM’s proprietary horizontal electroplating technology and supports copper (Cu), nickel (Ni), tin-silver (SnAg) and gold (Au) plating processes. Its copper plating chamber incorporates a high-speed plating paddle specifically designed for tall copper pillar applications, capable of achieving good within-die uniformity for 300-micron copper pillars at high plating rates. The system also features a four-sided sealing dry contact chuck for improved reliability, in-cell rinse functionality to minimize chemical cross-contamination between different plating cells, and a horizontal electroplating design that uses ACM’s patent-pending technology to synchronize the rotation of the chuck with a rotating rectangular electric field for superior deposition uniformity. Beyond equipment delivery, ACM is committed to building long-term customer relationships by providing high-quality equipment, supporting reliable volume production and delivering reliable technical support. ACM will continue to advance its technologies, expand its multi-product platform and grow its global customer base. Through collaboration with partners worldwide, ACM aims to support the growth of the AI industry and create greater value for customers with its differentiated semiconductor equipment technologies. The post ACM Research Announces Shipment of Its First 310 × 310 mm Ultra ECP ap-p Panel-Level Horizontal Electroplating Production Tool appeared first on Semiconductor Digest .

title: North Korean fake job interview led to $6.3B Binance heist
zh_title: 朝鲜虚假面试导致币安价值 6.3B 美元被盗
summary: 在上周破纪录的 63 亿美元盗窃案之前，朝鲜加密货币窃贼在一次虚假的面试过程中，诱骗币安软件工程师将恶意软件下载到他们的工作电脑上。在周二发布的一份事件报告中，该加密货币交易所表示，多种技术导致了 10 月 29 日的安全漏洞，其中包括通过虚假面试进行的社会工程、恶意软件下载、受损的内部人工智能工具、端点接管和“高级交易授权方法”。 “我们目前的调查表明，这是一次复杂的
content:
在上周破纪录的 63 亿美元盗窃案之前，朝鲜加密货币窃贼在一次虚假的面试过程中，诱骗币安软件工程师将恶意软件下载到他们的工作电脑上。在周二发布的一份事件报告中，该加密货币交易所表示，多种技术导致了 10 月 29 日的安全漏洞，其中包括通过虚假面试进行的社会工程、恶意软件下载、受损的内部人工智能工具、端点接管和“高级交易授权方法”。事件报告称：“我们目前的调查表明，这是一场复杂的、多阶段的活动。” “这不是一次孤立的违规行为或简单的网络钓鱼事件。”周末，联邦调查局将这起盗窃案归咎于 TraderTraitor，这是一个与 Lazarus Group 有关联的朝鲜黑客组织，该组织以将间谍活动与大规模加密货币抢劫相结合而闻名。平壤支持的团队也非常擅长就业市场诈骗——他们既冒充 IT 工人，然后受西方公司雇用，又冒充潜在雇主，引诱软件工程师下载恶意软件并感染公司设备。在最近的币安攻击中，挪威人使用了后者。攻击准备工作早在 6 月份就开始了，当时一名工程师下载了恶意的 Homebrew 安装，引发了供应链攻击。
报告称，虽然安全团队检测到了恶意软件，但设备被更换，所有受影响的凭证也被轮换，“工程师 A 的角色和他在我们钱包基础设施团队的相关同事都暴露给了黑客。”三个月后，攻击的社会工程部分发生了。 9 月，一名自称项目总监的人通过“合法求职平台”联系了另一名软件工程师，该人为币安工程师与这家假冒公司安排了一系列工作面试。报道称，在第一轮对工程师和假人力资源代表的现场视频面试中，面试官“与他分享了一个社交媒体帐户，包括在平台上发布的个人照片和视频，以建立信任”。 “这比以前看到的社会工程方法更先进、更具欺骗性。”对自称是该冒牌公司首席执行官的某人的第二次采访是在“流行的社交聊天应用程序”上进行的，最后，首席执行官指示工程师下载包含恶意软件代码存储库的“作业”。该代码在安装过程中在他的工作计算机上执行，从而引发了一系列未经授权的活动。据币安称，该恶意软件用恶意版本替换了合法的开发工具组件，该版本执行命令并与攻击者控制的外部服务器建立通信。
攻击者还采取了隐藏恶意脚本并逃避检测的措施，并且这种方法奏效了。币安的端点安全工具没有立即检测到恶意软件。脚本如下： CREATE /opt/homebrew/Cellar/pyenv/2.8.0/libexec/pyenv_ MODIFY pyenv_ → 3,414 B DELETE .../libexec/pyenv (3,344 B) ← 删除有效的 pyenv RENAME pyenv_ → pyenv (3,414 B) ← 将其替换为恶意版本 DELETE /opt/homebrew/bin/pyenv (3,414 B) ln（创建新的符号链接）+spawn zsh 然后，在 10 月 20 日，不法分子使用受感染的计算机和内部 AI 工具来访问钱包 DevOps 工程师 A 和另一位钱包软件开发人员工程师 C 的计算机。

【原文 English Original】
North Korean cryptocurrency thieves tricked a Binance software engineer into downloading malware onto their work-issued computer during a fake job interview process before last week's record-breaking $6.3 billion heist . In an incident report published on Tuesday, the cryptocurrency exchange said several techniques - including social engineering via fake job interviews, malware downloads, compromised internal AI tooling, endpoint takeover, and an “advanced transaction-authorization method” - led to the October 29 security breach. “Our current investigation indicates that this was a sophisticated, multi-stage campaign,” the incident report said. “It was not a single isolated breach or a simple phishing incident.” Over the weekend, the FBI attributed the theft to TraderTraitor, a North Korean hacking operation linked to Lazarus Group , known for combining espionage with massive cryptocurrency heists . The Pyongyang-backed crew is also highly adept at job market scams - both posing as IT workers , who are then hired by Western companies , and as potential employers to lure software engineers into downloading malware and infecting corporate devices . With the recent Binance attack, the Norks used the latter. The attack prep began back in June with a supply chain attack when one of its engineers downloaded a malicious Homebrew installation . While the malware was detected by the security team, the device was replaced, and all affected credentials rotated, “Engineer A’s role and his related colleagues on our wallet infrastructure team was exposed to the hacker,” the report says. Three months later, the social engineering part of the attack happened. In September, another software engineer was contacted via a “legitimate job-hunting platform” by someone purporting to be a project director who arranged a series of job interviews for the Binance engineer with the fake company. During the first round - a live video interview with the engineer and a fake HR rep - the interviewer “shared a social media account with him, including personal photos and videos posted on the platform, in order to build trust,” according to the report. “This was more advanced and deceptive than previously seen social engineering approaches.” The second interview with someone purporting to be the CEO of the phony company was conducted on a “popular social chat app,” and toward the end, the CEO instructed the engineer to download an “assignment” containing a malware-laced code repository. The code executed on his work computer during the setup process, which kicked off a series of unauthorized activities. According to Binance, the malware replaced a legitimate development tool component with a malicious version, which executed commands and established communication with an attacker-controlled external server. The attackers also took steps to hide the malicious script and evade detection, and it worked. Binance’s endpoint security tools did not immediately detect the malware. Here’s the script: CREATE /opt/homebrew/Cellar/pyenv/2.8.0/libexec/pyenv_ MODIFY pyenv_ → 3,414 B DELETE .../libexec/pyenv (3,344 B) ← remove the valid pyenv RENAME pyenv_ → pyenv (3,414 B) ← replace it with a malicious version DELETE /opt/homebrew/bin/pyenv (3,414 B) ln (create a new symlink) + spawn zsh Then, on October 20, the miscreants used the compromised computer and an internal AI tool to gain access to the computers of wallet DevOps engineer A and another wallet software developer, Engineer C. Engineer A had a container deployment permission token on his computer, which the Norks soon discovered. On October 29, the attacker accessed Engineer C's computer, used the stolen credentials from Engineer A to deploy a container, and triggered a script to launch the cryptocurrency-stealing attack. As of Tuesday, Binance said it has rebuilt the compromised wallet system and internal AI tool, and replaced all of the affected devices. It also decommissioned all credentials and tokens assigned to the compromised engineers, and is working with law enforcement, blockchain intel firms, and security researchers to trace and freeze the assets. The crypto exchange has also hired independent cybersecurity experts to conduct a cybersecurity review of the incident, and recommend additional protective measures. Binance said it’s also working to establish a security research fund and initiatives with AI companies and security shops to focus on AI security in blockchain environments.®

title: Official Assessments Argue Beijing Has Strategic Initiative
zh_title: 官方评估认为北京拥有战略主动权
summary: 内容提要 中国共产党内部人士似乎正在达成共识，预示着在 2026 年底领导人峰会之前，华盛顿将采取更加自信的外交政策方针。北京认为，美国明显接受“战略稳定的建设性关系”，这是一项重大外交成就，也是中华人民共和国相对于美国持续衰落的地位有所改善的证据。中国正在将其外交政策方针从利用机遇转变为积极塑造其对外政策
content:
内容提要 中国共产党内部人士似乎正在达成共识，预示着在 2026 年底领导人峰会之前，华盛顿将采取更加自信的外交政策方针。北京认为，美国明显接受“战略稳定的建设性关系”，这是一项重大外交成就，也是中华人民共和国相对于美国持续衰落的地位有所改善的证据。中国的外交政策方针正在从利用机遇转向积极塑造外部环境和寻求战略主动权。这一转变可能会让北京在与美国的谈判中提出更高的要求。目前尚不清楚这种转变如何转化为未来的军事侵略或机会主义。 2026年10月16日，中国现代国际关系研究院院长傅小强在中央党校颇具影响力的期刊《学习时报》（10月16日）上发表了对未来中美关系的政策处方。 [1] 傅的文章与中国外交部长王毅详细宣读习近平2026年9月中旬对华盛顿进行国事访问并与唐纳德·特朗普总统会晤的情况密切相关（新华社，9月26日）。王强调，习近平已经巩固了中美关系的新框架。
中美关系：“建设性战略稳定关系”。傅的文章认为，新的关系设定了竞争边界，支持了中华人民共和国的核心利益，并促进了未来的合作（《学习时报》，10月16日）。在习近平和特朗普 11 月和 12 月的会议之前，这篇 2026 年 10 月的文章可能有三个重叠的目的。对外，它传达了北京对中美可持续发展的构想。与华盛顿的关系。在国内，它向中国决策者解释了如何运作新型大国关系。从战略上讲，它使中国和美国处于平等地位，使美国未来对中国利益的迁就变得必要且可以实现（《学习时报》，10 月 16 日）。十月份的文章是一系列文章中最新的一篇，展示了中国外交政策处方的明显趋势。 2026年5月习近平与特朗普峰会的前一天，CICIR研究小组发表了一份题为《世界大变局与中美共处之道》的报告。这篇文章与傅的最新文章非常相似，并描述了中美关系。中美关系进入长期“战略相持”阶段。它主张稳定的中美关系建立在相互尊重、和平共处、合作共赢基础上的关系（《中国外交》，5月13日）。
在王毅宣布双边关系新方向之后，傅的文章为解释、鼓励或挑战美国未来的行为建立了一个总体框架。 [2] 傅：习近平指导关系，新标签“重新调整战略认知” 王毅外长描述了扩大后的中美关系将两国关系确定为习近平九月访问华盛顿的重要政治成果。他解释说，两国同意建立基于三项原则的“战略稳定的建设性关系”：“尊重”，即“尊重彼此的主权和领土完整、社会制度”。

【原文 English Original】
Executive Summary Chinese Communist Party (CCP) insiders appear to be developing a consensus that portends a more confident foreign policy approach to Washington ahead of leadership summits in late 2026. Beijing regards the United States’ apparent acceptance of a “constructive relationship of strategic stability” as a significant diplomatic achievement and evidence of an improving position for the People’s Republic of China (PRC) relative to the ongoing decline of the United States. The PRC is evolving its foreign policy approach from exploiting opportunities toward actively shaping its external environment and seeking strategic initiative. This shift will likely make Beijing more demanding in negotiations with the United States. It remains unclear how that shift might translate into future military aggression or opportunism. On October 16, 2026, Fu Xiaoqiang (傅小强), president of the China Institutes of Contemporary International Relations (CICIR), published a policy prescription for future relations between the United States and the People’s Republic of China (PRC) in the influential Central Party School journal Study Times ( Study Times , October 16).  [1] Fu’s article closely tracks with PRC Foreign Minister Wang Yi’s (王毅) detailed readout of Xi Jinping’s mid-September 2026 state visit to Washington and his meeting with President Donald Trump ( Xinhua , September 26). Wang underscored that Xi had solidified a new framework for PRC–U.S. relations: a “constructive relationship of strategic stability” (建设性战略稳定关系). Fu’s article argued that the new relationship sets boundaries for competition, supports the PRC’s core interests, and promotes future cooperation ( Study Times , October 16). The October 2026 article likely serves three overlapping purposes ahead of Xi and Trump’s November and December meetings. Externally, it communicates Beijing’s conception of a sustainable PRC–U.S. relationship to Washington. Domestically, it explains to Chinese policymakers how to operationalize the new great power relationship. Strategically, it presents the PRC and the United States as equals, making future U.S. accommodation of PRC interests both necessary and achievable ( Study Times , October 16). The October article is the latest in a series of writings showing a distinct trend in Chinese foreign policy prescriptions. The day before Xi’s May 2026 summit with Trump, a CICIR research group published a report titled “World Transformation and a Way for China and the United States to Coexist” (世界大变局与中美共处之道). The article closely resembled Fu’s latest piece and described PRC–U.S. relations as entering a prolonged period of “strategic stalemate” (战略相持). It argued for stable PRC–U.S. relations based on mutual respect, peaceful coexistence, and “win-win” cooperation ( China’s Diplomacy , May 13). Following Wang Yi’s declaration of a new direction for bilateral relations, Fu’s article establishes an overarching framework for interpreting, encouraging, or challenging future U.S. behavior.  [2] Fu: New Label ‘Recalibrates Strategic Perceptions,’ With Xi Steering Relations Foreign Minister Wang described the expanded PRC–U.S. relationship designation as an important political achievement of Xi’s September visit to Washington. He explained that both countries agreed to establish a “constructive relationship of strategic stability” based on three principles: “respect” (尊重), which entails “honoring each other’s sovereignty and territorial integrity, the social systems and development paths chosen by each side, and each other’s core interests and major concerns” (尊重彼此主权和领土完整，尊重各自选择的社会制度和发展道路，尊重对方核心利益和重大关切); “fairness” (公平), which implies “engaging in mutually beneficial cooperation, addressing differences through consultation, avoiding zero-sum games where one side wins at the expense of the other, and eschewing the pursuit of unilateral, absolute advantage” (开展互利合作，协商处理分歧，不搞你输我赢的零和博弈，不追求单方面的绝对优势); and “reciprocity” (对等), which signifies that “both nations are sovereign equals—with neither being superior or inferior to the other—rejecting hegemonic or bullying behavior, addressing each other’s concerns on an equal footing, and fostering balanced cooperation across all areas” (两国主权平等，没有高低之分，不搞霸道霸凌，对等解决各自关切，平衡发展各领域合作) ( Xinhua , September 26).  [3] Fu’s article is aligned with Wang’s explanation, but he goes considerably further in his analysis. He argues that the designation has fundamentally “recalibrated strategic perceptions” (战略再校准) away from conflict and confrontation, even amid competition. Fu may be attempting to influence the internal American debate by praising what he called the pragmatic approach of those in the U.S. administration who sought to avoid the costs of confrontation, contrasting them with U.S. policymakers “shackled by a Cold War mentality” (深陷冷战思维桎梏) who cast the PRC as an enemy ( Study Times , October 16). The article argues that the PRC and the United States should set clearer national security boundaries, distinguishing between activities that directly affect sovereignty and other core interests that should remain outside competition. Fu further argues for decoupling security issues from trade and economic issues, strengthening crisis communication mechanisms, and expanding cooperation across areas ranging from people-to-people exchanges to transnational crime to artificial intelligence risk assessments. In effect, Fu asserts that the new constructive relationship should prompt U.S. restraint on the PRC’s core interests while preserving the benefits of commerce and cooperation in other areas. According to a 2025 State Council white paper on “China’s national security in the New Era” (新时代的中国国家安全), the country’s core interests principally include “state political power, sovereignty, national reunification and territorial integrity, the well-being of the people, and sustainable economic and social development” (国家政权、主权、统一和领土完整、人民福祉、经济社会可持续发展) ( State Council Information Office , May 12, 2025). The language that the PRC’s core interests “principally include” (主要包括) these elements allows Beijing to add additional items if necessary. Fu appears to view agreement on the constructive relationship as committing Washington to Beijing’s red lines—which Xi delineated in his 2024 meeting with President Biden as Taiwan, democracy and human rights, the PRC’s development path and political system, and the PRC’s development rights—thereby empowering it to steer the relationship ( PRC Ministry of Foreign Affairs [MFA] , November 17, 2024). The Changing Character of Opportunity The 2026 shift in Chinese foreign policy, especially toward the United States, aligns with how leadership has recently characterized the country’s external environment. Since 2002, Beijing has assessed that an “important period of strategic opportunity” (重要战略机遇期) would facilitate its development. The United States was distracted by the Global War on Terrorism while the PRC enjoyed unfettered access to markets, technology, and capital, along with a relatively accommodating security environment. The optimistic assessment of the strategic environment survived the 2008 financial crisis and the rise of PRC–U.S. competition into this decade. Xi’s work report to the 20th Party Congress in 2022 replaced the 20-year window of strategic opportunity with a more sober judgment: the PRC faced a period in which “strategic opportunities, risks, and challenges coexist, with an increase in uncertain and unpredictable factors” (战略机遇和风险挑战并存、不确定难预料因素增多) ( People’s Daily , October 26, 2022). However, this did not end the PRC’s opportunities. A Work Report study guide explained that the resulting task was to “discover opportunities, seize opportunities, and shape opportunities” (发现机遇、抓住机遇、塑造机遇), while simultaneously preparing for consequential risks ( CCP Member Net , December 15, 2022). The 2022 shift from exploiting opportunities to actively shaping the international environment marked a significant evolution in the country’s foreign policy approach. The 15th Five-Year Plan (2026–2030), published in March 2026, reaffirmed the coexistence of opportunity and risk while asserting that the PRC possesses favorable conditions to “actively manage international space and shape the external environment” (主动运筹国际空间、塑造外部环境) ( National Development and Reform Commission , March 18; China Brief , April 4). A Chinese Academy of Social Sciences (CASS) interpretation of the five-year plan presented this new formulation as evidence that the country is moving from adapting to the international system toward exercising greater initiative and shaping its external environment ( CASS , January 27). A consistently invoked planning maxim, “time and momentum are on our side” (时与势在我们一边), connects the period of “strategic opportunity” to the present-day period of “strategic opportunity with greater risks.” That optimistic assessment has shaped Beijing’s foreign policy behavior over the past quarter-century. In an October 9 Study Times essay, Gao Zugui (高祖贵), dean of the Central Party School’s graduate school, invoked the phrase and presented “时” (time or the historical moment) and “势” (momentum or trend) as key variables in an analytic framework asserting that both the current historical moment and the underlying trajectory of the international system strongly favor the PRC ( Study Times , October 9). Party-Aligned Assessments Herald American Decline The evolution of Chinese foreign policy in 2026 also aligns with Beijing’s official perception of a shift in the strategic balance of power. A number of Chinese policy analysts and influential academics have framed the PRC’s rise against a rapid decline in the relative power and influence of the United States. In mid-2025, CICIR vice president Zhang Jian (张健) assessed the growing fractures among Western powers caused by aggressive U.S. policies ( Contemporary World , July 2025). By October 2026, Gao’s Study Times article described the United States as having fallen from the world’s sole superpower to the strongest power in an emerging multipolar order. Gao’s article assessed U.S. weakness in Washington’s strategic retrenchment to a “Western Hemisphere fortress” (西半球堡垒), deepening conflicts with allies, and growing military and economic costs of the ongoing confrontation with Iran ( Study Times , October 9). Analysts writing in Party publications have seen the U.S.–Iran conflict as accelerating the decline in U.S. international influence that Beijing has long anticipated. Chen Wenxin (陈文鑫), director of CICIR’s American Studies Institute, argued in April in the authoritative Party journal Qiushi that the war is exhausting American strategic resources, damaging its international credibility, worsening alliance relations, and exposing a growing mismatch between U.S. ambitions and capabilities. The article further asserted that the Iran conflict’s impacts exceeded U.S. expectations, exacerbating political polarization and social fragmentation within the United States ( Qiushi , April 16). An August 2026 PLA Daily article authored by Renmin University academics concluded that the Iran conflict is accelerating the erosion of U.S. dominance in the Middle East and creating opportunities for other countries to fill the power vacuum ( PLA Daily , August 21). Beijing is keen to step into the gap: in late October, Wang Yi praised Xi’s “series of proposals to maintain and promote peace and stability in the Middle East” (维护和促进中东和平稳定的系列主张) ( MFA , October 23). Official publications also cite the ongoing Iran conflict as a conspicuous example of how Beijing might turn international disruption into diplomatic and commercial advantage. The joint statement from the ASEAN-China foreign ministers meeting envisaged an opening for the PRC to engage in practical energy security cooperation throughout Southeast Asia, born out of the Iran conflict ( MFA , July 24). In a more recent People’s Daily commentary, Lu Ruquan (陸如泉), president of the China National Petroleum Corporation Research Institute, argued that the country’s energy reserves, diversified supplies, and growing exports of clean energy technologies could help stabilize global energy markets disrupted by the Iran conflict ( People’s Daily , September 30). These assessments of U.S. diplomatic decline and the limits of U.S. military power exposed by the Iran conflict do not necessarily portend Chinese military aggression in the Taiwan Strait or elsewhere in Asia. Several analysts have expressed concern about improving U.S.-led security arrangements in the Pacific, even amid the perceived U.S. decline. The China Institute of International Studies (CIIS) has described such arrangements involving Japan, the Philippines, Australia, and South Korea as a “nested, multi-layered, grid-like Indo-Pacific mini-multilateral mechanism” (圈层嵌套的复合型、网格化“印太”小多边机制) ( CIIS , March 5, 2025).  [4] Even without U.S. military capabilities and regional security guarantees, Chinese military planners have likely drawn lessons from the Iran and Ukraine conflicts about the consequences of becoming trapped in a prolonged military campaign, which likely serves as an even greater deterrent against military overreach. While most nations appear to accede to requests to define their relationship with the PRC on Beijing’s terms, the United States has had a tortured history with these labels.  [5] Even as different presidential administrations were seduced into “partnerships” or “relationships,” the bilateral labels would inevitably atrophy. By 2018, the Clinton- and Bush-era “constructive strategic partnership” and “constructive cooperative relationship,” along with the Obama-era “new-type great power relationship,” had been eclipsed by “great power competition,” a label Beijing has rejected as unhelpful ( China Brief , June 5). The current U.S. administration apparently embraced the May 2026 return to a mutually agreed label for the bilateral relationship ( White House , May 17). Chinese accounts describe the “constructive relationship of strategic stability” as a “new orientation” (新定位) intended to provide strategic guidance for relations for at least the next three years ( MFA , May 14). After Xi’s September visit, the White House again confirmed that the two nations would build a constructive relationship of strategic stability “on the basis of respect, fairness, and reciprocity,” mirroring the Chinese read-out ( White House , September 25; MFA [English] , MFA [Chinese] , September 26). Conclusion The next tests for PRC–U.S. relations will be scheduled meetings between Xi and Trump at the November 18–19 APEC leaders’ meeting in Shenzhen and the December 14–15 G20 summit in Miami. American policymakers should pay close attention not only to material agreements but also to Chinese readouts and the language Beijing uses to explain them. This includes whether Beijing invokes the “constructive relationship of strategic stability” to request or expect changes in U.S. policy toward Taiwan or regional alliances, or whether it translates claims of American decline to seek concessions on economic issues like tariffs or technology controls. Answers to these questions may offer insights into Beijing’s perceptions of the PRC’s relative strength and potential leverage against the United States. Chinese leaders do not believe dominance over the United States is imminent. Rather, they currently assess that their external environment increasingly favors the PRC. American policymakers and legislators should be sensitive to the possibility that consensus will continue to shift and calls for increased assertiveness may grow within the PRC’s foreign policy establishment. In the near term, Beijing may pursue a seemingly benign initiative to test the limits of the newly established “constructive relationship of strategic stability.” Beijing may also act quickly on its perceptions of a narrowing power differential with the United States and leverage its interpretation of the new bilateral relationship to seek advantages and concessions from Washington. The United States may understand “stability” within the new relationship designation as managing risk while continuing to compete. Based on Wang and Fu’s recent interpretations, however, Beijing expects the new framework to limit competition in ways that benefit the PRC’s core interests. Conflating these two differing interpretations could increase, not reduce, strategic miscalculation between the PRC and the United States. Notes [1] On October 29, 2026, Michael Kovrig, Thomas Shipley, and Patricia Xavier observed in China Brief that Beijing is using its proposed framing of the relationship to constrain U.S. behavior. In early June, Christopher Nye discussed the history of the framing, suggesting similarly that Beijing sought to curtail U.S. interference in what it claims are its internal affairs (China Brief, June 5 , October 29 ). [2] The China Institutes of Contemporary International Relations (CICIR) is the in-house think tank of the Ministry of State Security (MSS), China’s principal external intelligence agency. CICIR is also known as the MSS 11th Bureau. In a 2026 interview, Fu Xiaoqiang explained that CICIR served the CCP Central Committee and was responsible for integrating its research with domestic and international strategic communication (“研宣融合”) ( Xinhua Think Tank Research , May 27). [3] The MFA’s English-language press release following the summit states the two leaders “agreed to build a constructive relationship of strategic stability based on respect, fairness and reciprocity.” However, in Chinese-language versions of the release, the word used is not “reciprocity” or “reciprocal” (互惠). Instead, MFA uses “对等”, which may mean “reciprocity” in certain contexts, but is more commonly translated as “equal in status; on an equal footing; or of equal standing (especially between two parties). [4] The China Institute of International Studies (CIIS) is the official research institution and think tank administered by China’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs (MFA). [5] The PRC has organized virtually all external relations into a complex hierarchy of either “relationships” or “partnerships,” and appends a combination of adjectives to these categories to define different levels of diplomatic engagement. Chinese diplomatic “partnerships,” in particular, are widely misunderstood as akin to business partnerships with shared risks and rewards. Instead, the PRC’s relationship and partnership labels define the nature and scope of the relationship, identifying areas of overlapping interest for engagement, even when the two sides disagree on certain issues (China Brief, September 20, 2024 ). The post Official Assessments Argue Beijing Has Strategic Initiative appeared first on Jamestown .

title: Beijing Uses Mbappé Controversy to Export Censorship
zh_title: 北京利用姆巴佩争议输出审查制度
summary: 摘要：法国足球运动员基利安·姆巴佩 (Kylian Mbappé) 出人意料地发现自己成为中华人民共和国 (PRC) 政治争议的对象，此前他在一次采访中讨论了一个将他与毛泽东相比较的模因。这场争议起源于球迷社区平台东球地，并因姆巴佩被认为蔑视中国人民和国家而蔓延至全国范围内针对姆巴佩的“取消”运动。中国正在利用这一争议和随之而来的公众愤怒向世界表明，进入中国市场是有条件的
content:
摘要：法国足球运动员基利安·姆巴佩 (Kylian Mbappé) 出人意料地发现自己成为中华人民共和国 (PRC) 政治争议的对象，此前他在一次采访中讨论了一个将他与毛泽东相比较的模因。这场争议起源于球迷社区平台东球地，并因姆巴佩被认为蔑视中国人民和国家而蔓延至全国范围内针对姆巴佩的“取消”运动。中国正在利用这场争议和随之而来的公众愤怒向世界表明，进入中国市场取决于遵守党国的政治敏感性，从而有效地将其政治正确性偏好和审查制度全球化。中国中央电视台和浙江省委宣传部等党政机关已关注到这一争议，并发表声明谴责姆巴佩、他的俱乐部皇家马德里和西班牙足球联赛西甲。中央电视台已暂停在中国境内所有西甲比赛的转播，姆巴佩的中国商业合作伙伴也已撤回支持。分析人士推测，由于直接提及毛泽东，中共感到有必要对这一争议做出回应。与之前其他被指控“侮辱中国”的个人和企业事件相比，党和国家机关并不总是得到类似程度的回应。
10月26日，社交媒体平台X上的一个粉丝账户上传了法国足球运动员基利安·姆巴佩4月份采访的片段。当被问及他觉得自己的哪一个表情包最有趣时，姆巴佩提到了一个将他的脸贴在“中国独裁者”身上的表情包。该视频随后显示了一个将他描绘成毛泽东的表情包（澳大利亚广播公司，10 月 27 日）。当晚，中华人民共和国最大的足球新闻和球迷社区平台“懂球帝”发表声明，声称姆巴佩的言论“伤害了中国球迷和中国人民的感情”，但拒绝翻译（《东球帝》，10月26日）。蒙牛和东鹏特饮等中国品牌很快宣布终止与姆巴佩的商业合作关系（彩联出版社，10 月 27 日）。中央电视台还宣布暂停播放姆巴佩的西甲联赛以及任何有关他的广告。要求球员本人、他的球队皇家马德里和西甲公开道歉（新京报10月27日）。一次在中国境外进行的旧采访出人意料地让这名球员、他的俱乐部和他的联盟受到了来自北京的商业和政治压力。这场争议也迅速蔓延到中华人民共和国以外的地区，成为一场所谓“辱华”的全球奇观。这场争议首先是通过东秋地的积极介入而引起关注的。
在声明宣布姆巴佩的言论“不能接受的”后不到20分钟，社区里就已经充斥着针对姆巴佩和皇马的攻击。这种愤怒很快蔓延到其他中文社交媒体平台。关于这段视频发布几个月后出现的时间一直存在猜测，东秋地在一份声明中解释说，其中一名编辑只是在晚上上网时看到了这段视频（东秋地，10 月 31 日）。两种解释 第二天早上，当中央电视台宣布暂停 L 节目时，中国官方媒体进行了干预。

【原文 English Original】
Executive Summary: French soccer player Kylian Mbappé has unexpectedly found himself the subject of a political controversy in the People’s Republic of China (PRC) following the resurfacing of an interview in which he discussed a meme that compared him to Mao Zedong. The controversy originated on fan community platform Dongqiudi and spread into a nationwide “cancellation” campaign against Mbappé due to his perceived slight against the Chinese people and nation. The PRC is leveraging this controversy and its ensuing public anger to show the world that access to the Chinese market is contingent on adherence to the political sensitivities of the Party-state, effectively globalizing its political correctness preferences and censorship. Party-state organs such as China Central Television (CCTV) and the Zhejiang provincial propaganda department have latched onto the controversy and issued statements condemning Mbappé, his club Real Madrid, and the Spanish soccer league La Liga. CCTV has suspended all broadcasts of La Liga matches in the PRC, and Mbappé’s Chinese commercial partners have withdrawn support. Analysts have speculated that the Party felt compelled to respond to this controversy due to its direct reference to Mao Zedong. A comparison of other previous instances of individuals and corporations accused of “insulting China” have not always been met with a similar level of response from Party-state organs. On October 26, a fan account on the social media platform X uploaded a clip from an April interview featuring French soccer player Kylian Mbappé. Asked which meme of himself he found the funniest, Mbappé mentioned one with his face put onto the body of a “Chinese dictator.” The video then showed a meme depicting him as Mao Zedong ( Australian Broadcasting Corporation , October 27). That evening, the biggest football news and fan community platform in the People’s Republic of China (PRC), Dongqiudi (懂球帝), issued a statement claiming that Mbappé’s remarks had “hurt the feelings of Chinese fans and the Chinese people” (伤害了中国球迷和中国人民感情), though it declined to translate them ( Dongqiudi , October 26). PRC brands including Mengniu (蒙牛) and Eastroc Beverage (东鹏特饮) soon announced that they were ending their commercial partnerships with Mbappé ( Cailian Press , October 27). CCTV also announced it was suspending broadcasts of Mbappé’s league, La Liga, along with any advertisements featuring him. It demanded public apologies from the player himself, his team Real Madrid, and La Liga ( Beijing News , October 27). An old interview conducted outside the PRC had unexpectedly subjected the player, his club, and his league to both commercial and political pressure from Beijing. The controversy also quickly spread beyond PRC, turning into a global spectacle over an alleged “insult to China” (辱华). The controversy first gained traction through the active intervention of Dongqiudi. Less than 20 minutes after its statement declared Mbappé’s remarks as “unacceptable” (不能接受的), the community was already awash with attacks on the player and Real Madrid. The anger soon spread to other Chinese-language social media platforms. There has been speculation about the timing of the clip surfacing several months after its release, Dongqiudi explained in a statement that one of its editors simply saw the clip while browsing online at night ( Dongqiudi , October 31). Two Explanations PRC state media intervened the following morning when CCTV announced the suspension of La Liga broadcasts and demanded public apologies from Mbappé, Real Madrid, and the league. Two explanations for its decision. One is that Beijing may have viewed the emerging calls to boycott Mbappé as an opportunity: Responding forcefully to a foreigner could demonstrate to domestic audiences that it was defending national dignity, while simultaneously using public pressure to constrain the words and actions of individuals and entities abroad. This geopolitical reading is not fully supported by the evidence. Several senior soccer journalists at Titan Sports Weekly (体坛周报), a PRC sports newspaper, privately offered a different explanation. They said Beijing was displeased that Dongqiudi had stirred up the controversy without permission, but found it difficult to remain silent because Mao Zedong’s name was implicated (Author’s interview, October 28).  [1] According to these journalists, once Dongqiudi’s statement provoked a strong reaction among some netizens, the political instinct to defend Mao’s legacy increased the cost of silence for Beijing. These opposing explanations, however, remain unreconciled. Similar past controversies show that grassroots accusations of “insults to China” do not necessarily prompt the same response from Beijing. In 2019, for instance, some nationalists accused the fashion retailer Zara of “insulting China” by featuring a Chinese model with visible, natural freckles, claiming that the advertisement portrayed Chinese people as unattractive and that the brand had failed to observe Chinese beauty standards. Some official media, however, did not support the accusations. China Youth Daily (中国青年报) publicly rejected it, warning against abusing the label “insult to China”; the Global Times, meanwhile, praised the model’s appearance as “iconic” ( The Paper , February 17, 2019; BBC , February 18, 2019). The preceding year, Italian fashion house Dolce & Gabbana was likewise embroiled in controversy for creating a promotional video for a Shanghai show that featured a model eating Italian food with chopsticks. At the time, despite online outrage, the Ministry of Foreign Affairs explicitly stated that it “did not want it elevated to a diplomatic issue” (不希望它上升为外交问题) ( People’s Daily , November 22, 2018). These cases show that Beijing is often inclined to avoid diplomatic escalation, but the involvement of Mao in Mbappé’s case made such restraint unsustainable. Officials who choose to let the matter quietly subside are highly likely to be accused in future political struggles of failing to uphold the Party’s own political principles. Exporting Censorship Whether Beijing initially sought to exploit the controversy or felt compelled to respond, its subsequent handling followed a familiar pattern. Beijing has long exploited foreign individuals’ and firms’ dependence on the PRC market to force them to submit to its political will.  [2] This approach brings the censorship faced by PRC citizens to foreign nationals, wherever they may be. Mbappé’s income from commercial deals in the PRC, Real Madrid’s sponsorship, and La Liga’s broadcasting partnership all provide channels for such a pressure campaign. Raising the economic cost of refusing to yield allows Beijing to make non-PRC citizens heed its standards of political correctness even when speaking outside PRC.  [3] Beijing’s previous pressure campaigns have gone beyond sports. In 2018, German auto manufacturer Mercedes removed an advertisement quoting the Dalai Lama and publicly apologized, but the People’s Daily still criticized its apology as lacking in sincerity. The following day, Daimler’s top executives wrote to the PRC’s ambassador to Germany to apologize again ( People’s Daily , February 6, 2018; Xinhua , February 8, 2018). That same year, international hotel chain Marriott apologized repeatedly over a Tibet-related controversy, but was still ordered to shut down its Chinese-language website and app for a week. It subsequently announced the dismissal of employees involved, tighter reviews of political-sensitive content worldwide and additional staff training ( Xinhua , January 11, 2018; Shanghai Observer , January 17, 2018). That same year, Versace, Coach, Givenchy, Calvin Klein, Asics, Gap, and Swarovski all issued similar public apologies to the PRC, but these are only a small number of commercial entities that have been pressured into making such statements.  [4] Conclusion Mbappé, Real Madrid, and La Liga president Javier Tebas have all apologized to the PRC for Mbappé’s remarks, but as of November 3, CCTV still had not resumed La Liga broadcasts ( Lianhe Zaobao , November 3). CCTV’s most recent stance has been to demand that Mbappé “mend his ways” (痛改前非) and said it would “listen to his [future] words and watch his [future] actions” (听其言更观其行) ( CCTV , October 27). Beijing’s demands for obedience can extend from requesting a public apology to requesting changes to an entity’s internal management. On October 29, Zhejiang provincial propaganda department criticized Real Madrid even after its formal apology for offering “no internal accountability and no commitment to corrective measures” (没有内部追责，也没有整改承诺). It described this as evidence of the club’s “dismissive and perfunctory attitude” (轻慢与敷衍), demanding that a Spanish club incorporate the PRC’s political standards into its management ( WeChat/Zhejiang Propaganda , October 28). Once someone crosses the red line to “insult China,” Party organs feel that they retain the power to decide on the requisite concessions for punitive actions to end. What is clear from recent history, however, is that a public apology has yet to prove a reliable guarantee against further political interference from Beijing. Notes [1] In a speech in 2013, Xi Jinping explicitly linked a repudiation of Mao to whether the Party and PRC’s socialist system could survive. He also identified the rejection of Soviet Communist Party history and its leaders as an important cause of the Soviet Union’s final collapse ( Qiushi , March 31, 2019). Article 28 of the Regulations on Party History Study and Education (党史学习教育工作条例), issued by the CCP Central Committee in 2024, further required units (单位) at all levels to implement the “responsibility system for ideological work” (意识形态工作责任制) and actively oppose misconduct such as “vilifying Party and state leaders” (诋毁党和国家领导人) ( Cyber Administration of China , February 19, 2024). [2] The most prominent example came in 2019, when PRC authorities enacted similar restrictions on the U.S. National Basketball Association following a tweet from the Houston Rockets’ general manager Daryl Morey that voiced support for pro-democracy protestors in Hong Kong. [3] W. D. O’Connell, “Silencing the Crowd: China, the NBA, and Leveraging Market Size to Export Censorship,” Review of International Political Economy 29, no. 4 (2022): 1112–34, https://doi.org/10.1080/09692290.2021.1905683 . [4] These cases are documented in Hoffman, Samantha, China’s Mobilization State , The Jamestown Foundation, 2026, p.77. title: Fifth Plenum Breaks Personnel Records

内容提要 中国共产党二十届五中全会创下了后毛泽东时代出席率低、纪律处分规模大的纪录。张胜民被增选为政治局委员，但没有晋升为中央军委委员。在清洗过程中，军队几乎从中央委员会中消失：44名军人中只有五人正式出席。这次全会，中央委员会的空缺没有全部填补。它只填补了 24 个空缺的正式成员席位中的 10 个，并跳过了 5 个候补成员。中国共产党二十届五中全会首次公开公布党的领导层最新人事决定。会议于 10 月 29 日结束，共有 162 名正式成员和 117 名候补成员出席。这不到 2022 年 376 名当选议员的四分之三，是毛泽东时代以来出席人数最低的一次（美联社，10 月 29 日）。 [1] 全会确认了文革以来规模空前的纪律处分。它针对24名正式委员和10名候补委员，开除33名委员，并剥夺李云泽的党内职务（新华社，10月29日）。 [2] 党的二十大以来，全会共罢免了51名正式委员和候补委员（人民网，2024年7月18日、2025年10月24日；新华社，10月29日）。
全会允许习近平总书记对这次整肃进行盘点，既赋予了整肃的合法性，也是在党的二十一次代表大会上继续执政的前提。除了打破人事记录外，全会还通过了《全面从严治党的决定》。只有五名军人参加全会 张升民加入政治局是全会最突出的举措。张是继1994年黄菊之后第一位中期增补的政治局委员（南华早报，10月29日）。张自2017年起担任中央军委纪律检查委员会书记，负责监督当前的军队清洗工作。他的晋升可以被视为习近平对他这项工作的奖励。这也是实际的需要。政治局是事实上的最高权力机构，按照惯例，军事代表参与国家重大事务的决策（《电讯报》，10 月 30 日）。时任中央军委副主席张又侠一月份接受调查后，政治局就没有了在职的军事代表（国防部，1月24日；中央社，10月29日）。鉴于政治局的许多决定都与军队有关，一个在没有任何士兵在场的情况下举行会议和投票的机构对于将武装力量团结在习近平周围几乎没有什么帮助。张的晋升并不能掩盖军队在党的高层中的缺席。
中央委员会的44名军人中，有25人已被确认开除党籍（布鲁金斯学会，10月23日；新华社，10月29日）。只有五人正式出席十月全会：张、国防部长董军；被免职或退休的三名军官分别是原军事科学院院长杨学军、原南部战区副政委兼南海舰队政委杨志亮、原空军副司令员俞庆江（X/@cnpoliwatch，10月29日）。 [3] 剩余的m中

【原文 English Original】
Executive Summary The Fifth Plenum of the 20th Central Committee of the Chinese Communist Party (CCP) set records for low attendance and large-scale disciplinary measures in the post-Mao Zedong era. Zhang Shengmin was added to the Politburo, but there were no promotions to the Central Military Commission. Amid the purge, the military has all but vanished from the Central Committee: only five of its 44 military members formally attended. Central Committee vacancies were not fully filled at this plenum. It filled only ten of 24 vacant full-member seats and skipped five alternate members. The Fifth Plenum of the 20th Central Committee of the Chinese Communist Party (CCP) announced the Party leadership’s latest personnel decisions publicly for the first time. The meeting, which closed on October 29, was attended by 162 full and 117 alternate members. This constituted fewer than three-quarters of the 376 elected in 2022, making it the lowest attendance since the Mao Zedong era ( Associated Press , October 29).  [1] The plenum confirmed disciplinary measures on a scale unprecedented since the Cultural Revolution. It targeted 24 full members and 10 alternates, expelling 33 while stripping Li Yunze (李云泽) of his Party posts ( Xinhua , October 29).  [2] Since the 20th Party Congress, plenums have removed 51 full and alternate members (People’s Daily Online, July 18, 2024 , October 24, 2025 ; Xinhua , October 29). The plenum allowed General Secretary Xi Jinping to take stock of the purge, both to give it legitimacy and as a precondition for staying in power at the 21st Party Congress. Beyond breaking personnel records, the plenum adopted a Decision on comprehensively and strictly governing the Party (全面从严治党). Only Five Military Members Attend Plenum The addition of Zhang Shengmin (张升民) to the Politburo was the plenum’s most prominent move. Zhang is the first Politburo member added mid-term since Huang Ju (黄菊) in 1994 ( South China Morning Post , October 29). As secretary of the Central Military Commission (CMC) Commission for Discipline Inspection from 2017, Zhang oversaw the current military purge. His promotion can be seen as Xi rewarding him for this work. It was also a practical necessity. The Politburo is the de facto highest body of power, and by convention it includes military representatives in decisions on major national affairs ( The Telegraph , October 30). After then-CMC Vice Chairman Zhang Youxia (张又侠) was placed under investigation in January, the Politburo had no functioning military representative ( Ministry of National Defense , January 24; Central News Agency , October 29). Given that many Politburo decisions bear on the military, a body that meets and votes without a single soldier present does little to rally the armed forces around Xi. Zhang’s promotion cannot mask the military’s absence from the Party’s upper ranks. Of the Central Committee’s 44 military members, 25 have been confirmed as expelled from the Party ( Brookings Institution , October 23; Xinhua , October 29). Only five formally attended the October plenum: Zhang; Minister of National Defense Dong Jun (董军); and three officers who have been removed or have retired, namely former Academy of Military Science President Yang Xuejun (杨学军), former Southern Theater Command Deputy Political Commissar and South Sea Fleet Political Commissar Yang Zhiliang (杨志亮), and former Air Force Deputy Commander Yu Qingjiang (俞庆江) ( X/@cnpoliwatch , October 29).  [3] Among the remaining military members, only Zhang still holds real power. The CMC has yet to gain any new members beyond Xi and Zhang. Neither Dong, defense minister since late 2023, nor the four officers promoted to general since the purge began, have been elevated to the body (Xinhua, December 22, 2025 , July 3 ).  [4] Xi would be expected to rebuild the high command before the People’s Liberation Army’s (PLA) centenary in 2027, but he is clearly in no hurry and instead may plan to overhaul the CMC at the 21st Party Congress ( Nikkei Asia , August 6). Zhang Shengmin will likely remain, however. Xi still needs a veteran general to help him control the military, and his entering the Politburo greatly improves his chances of staying on. Promotions of Alternates Break with Convention This plenum did not follow the constitutionally mandated procedure for filling vacancies. When a full member’s seat falls vacant, whether for political reasons or through death, the Party Constitution requires that it be “filled by alternate members of the Central Committee in order of the number of votes they received” (由中央委员会候补委员按照得票多少依次递补) ( People’s Daily Online , October 26, 2022). The number of full members should thus stay constant, but this time was different. First, not all vacancies were filled. Plenum communiqués show that, since 1989, seats vacated through disciplinary action have always been filled at the same plenum. The 20th Central Committee’s Third Plenum filled all three vacancies, and its Fourth Plenum filled all eleven (People’s Daily Online, July 18, 2024 , October 24, 2025 ). This time, however, only ten of 24 were filled, leaving 191 full members on the books. The shortfall was not for lack of alternates. Promotions stopped at Liu Qiang (刘强), 38th on the list, with more than 100 names below him ( People’s Daily Online , October 22, 2022). Second, promotions skipped a number of alternates instead of strictly following the vote order. This practice began at the 18th Central Committee’s Seventh Plenum in 2017, which passed over Liu Xuepu (刘学普), Zhu Yanfeng (竺延风), Zheng Qunliang (郑群良), and Zhao Jin (赵金) (Xinhua, November 14, 2012 , October 14, 2017 ). Those skipped have likely run into political trouble, which makes the practice a leading indicator of the purge. Fang Yongxiang (方永祥) and Fang Hongwei (方红卫), passed over at the Fourth Plenum, were expelled from the Party at this one ( People’s Daily Online , October 24, 2025; Xinhua , October 29). Others were skipped because poor health leaves them unfit to serve. This time, five alternates were skipped: Fu Wenhua (付文化), Cong Liang (丛亮), Ji Lin (吉林), Zhu Wenxiang (朱文祥), and Zhu Hexin (朱鹤新) ( Lianhe Zaobao , October 30). Fu and Zhu Wenxiang both come from the People’s Armed Police and have likely been caught up in the military purge (Caixin, July 11, 2014 , March 14, 2025 ). Ji, a Communist Youth League veteran, was removed early as Party secretary of the Central Institute of Socialism in September 2024 and has long been sidelined ( China Economic Net , September 27, 2024). Cong, a former subordinate of Vice Premier He Lifeng (何立峰), moved in 2024 from deputy head of the National Development and Reform Commission to deputy director of the State Council’s Development Research Center, a posting he was likely given for health reasons ( The Paper , July 5, 2024). Finally, Zhu Hexin missed the plenum and was skipped, yet on October 30 he chaired a Party group meeting on the plenum as head of the State Administration of Foreign Exchange. His situation is unclear ( State Administration of Foreign Exchange , October 30). Conclusion Xi’s main political goal now is to secure another term at the 21st Party Congress. That requires not only a firm grip on power but also a case that his continued rule is legitimate and natural. The Fifth Plenum is the last plenum before the congress that can take stock of the term.  [5] Xi had to use it to resolve the problems of legitimacy created by the purge, and personnel changes were central to that effort. The Fifth Plenum has not ended the purge. Minister of Agriculture and Rural Affairs Han Jun (韩俊), Navy Commander Hu Zhongming (胡中明), Western Theater Command Political Commissar Li Fengbiao (李凤彪), Air Force Political Commissar Guo Puxiao (郭普校), and others missed the plenum, yet no action against them has been announced. Dozens of members are in the same position. Li and Guo were removed as deputies to the National People’s Congress in June ( Xinhua , June 26). The Sixth Plenum, which will be convened ahead of the 21st Party Congress, will almost certainly deal with another batch. Notes [1] Among plenums since the end of the Cultural Revolution that published attendance figures, the previous low was 84.4 percent, at the Third Plenum of the 11th Central Committee in 1978 ( People’s Daily Online , December 22, 1978). At the 12th Plenum of the Eighth Central Committee in 1968, during the Cultural Revolution, only 40 full members attended. Together with 10 members added on the spot and 9 alternates, the attendees made up about 30 percent of the members elected at the Eighth Party Congress ( Institute of Party History and Literature of the CCP Central Committee , December 25, 2012). [2] The previous record was 15, at the 18th Central Committee’s Seventh Plenum in 2017 ( Xinhua , October 14, 2017). [3] Central Committee members are elected for a five-year term, and stripping a member of Party posts requires a two-thirds vote at a plenum ( People’s Daily Online , October 26, 2022). Retirement or removal from a military post during the term does not affect membership. [4] The four include: Eastern Theater Command Commander Yang Zhibin (杨志斌), Central Theater Command Commander Han Shengyan (韩胜延), Air Force Commander Wang Gang (王刚), and CMC discipline chief Zhang Shuguang (张曙光). [5] A Sixth Plenum will be held before the 21st Party Congress, but it will effectively be a preparatory meeting for the congress. Such plenums are usually held a few days before the congress opens to review the work report and the draft amendments to the Party Constitution, and they do not serve as interim reviews. The Seventh Plenum of the 19th Central Committee, for example, closed on October 12, 2022, four days before the 20th Party Congress opened on October 16 ( Xinhua , October 12, 2022).
